author: youyou5202
quoted_text:
Surprise 1: Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech
.
.
.
Surprise 2: that person is me
Surprise 3: I’m here to tell you all about it

Yes, this is what you think it is; after 6 yrs of increasingly loose anonymity: the Professor Oak reveal post

…and yes, it has gotten so boring around here that I’m literally doxxing myself to spice up the timeline

-------
Ok, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Cody Tranbarger. I mostly tweet, but occasionally find time to dabble in drug dev & starting/building biotechs. My past lives span the VC, crossover, startup continuum; Prof Oak has been my way of keeping a digital foot in those worlds, despite having my physical feet planted elsewhere.

The past 18 mo, ‘elsewhere’ was Mithril Medicine, a co. I founded to develop bsAbs for LAMA2-CMD & other ECM-related genetic diseases.

Mithril was born out of hands-on building with @MikeNGladstone, @JasonPaulRhodes, @LifeSciVC, & team @atlasventure. Somehow, I made enough half-decent calls along the way (even a broken clock is right twice a day, eh?) to convince them Mithril/I warranted a small seed. While I can hardly rationalize such an outrageously cavalier bet, I’m grateful for it, & I'd partner with Atlas again in a heartbeat.

In typical AV fashion, Mithril’s primordial form was virtual, decentralized, & ultra-lean. This stage tends to be short-lived, but for Mithril, it worked surprisingly well, for surprisingly long, thanks in part to the rapid maturation of the AI tools I used liberally.

Eventually, Mithril became a bit of an experiment itself - to find the upper bound of how far it could scale as a single operator + a bunch of Claude (+ a stellar bench of part-time consultants).

In parallel, I started spending time with @nc_frey, @an1lam, & @CoefficientBio team; and promptly experienced, for the 1st time, AI at the frontier. Soon thereafter, Mithril stopped looking like an experiment, & started looking like a preview of an entirely new operating model.

From that spark came “Pipeline-in-a-Person.” The idea immediately resonated when we shared it here back in April; and it was central to the shared vision that led to Anthropic’s acquisition of Mithril, & my joining the team.

Why join Anthropic? Three reasons.
(1) For Mithril, the programs continue, with more resources & infrastructure behind them, and as much Claude as I can put to work.

(2) For me, the chance to start several more programs, & find out how many one person can actually run in parallel - an almost unprecedented luxury for a curious drug hunter.

(3) For our mission, a path to institutionalize & scale this new way of working, then put it in the hands of all of biopharma, all over the world - which, candidly, I find the most energizing.

Will AI x Bio cure diseases? Unequivocally yes, imo… but not by the route that gets the most airtime. Rather than timeline acceleration & compression, I see orchestration & parallelization as today's low-hanging fruit.

Most drug hunters see a handful of go/no-go calls in a career, & spend entirely too much of the rest trading emails (my inbox can attest).

Give them the bandwidth to run several programs at once, and the time to focus on scientific judgment, and I’m willing to bet they’ll make better calls. And at scale, better calls translate to more drugs, higher hit rates, broader patient impact, & likely, a disease or 10 or 100 cured. I couldn't be more excited to build toward that future @AnthropicAI.

Finally, a heartfelt thank you to BioTwitter/X. The end of anonymity is bittersweet, but if anyone’s earned a proper introduction, you all have.

It’s difficult to overstate how much this app has done for me: a decade of education, plenty of friends, many job opportunities, several mentors, a few investors, even a co-founder (fmr). It was the generosity of this community that inspired me to start posting 6 years ago, after just as many years lurking. I hope I’ve been able to pay it forward, in my own small way.

But, to be clear, Prof Oak isn’t going anywhere. Same beat, same themes, and now, a front-row seat to drug development at the frontier. Stay tuned for dispatches from the trenches; and remember...

Gotta Cure 'Em All

quoted_text:
最近推上聊 @predictdotfun 的人多了不少，很开心能被这么多人看到和了解到。不过有几个点被反复提起，我觉得多少有点误解，这里也和大家讨论下

1️⃣ TVL 为什么没别人高

我们的协议 TVL（OI）长期在 $10M 上下，有三个原因：用户主要交易的是加密货币短时涨跌、体育和电竞比赛这类短周期事件，平均持仓和结算时间都很短；我们的积分基本没往持仓上倾斜；再加上我们直接接入了币安的交易所和钱包，用户拿交易所余额就能下单，钱不用趴在协议里

反观友商之前的高 TVL，大量积分分给了持仓，又没有短期市场，撸毛用户只能拆分仓位长期拿着来刷积分，TVL 自然被推上去了

我自己的看法是，预测市场的 OI 远没有 perps 那么关键。perps 要卷 OI，是因为刷交易量成本太低，光看交易量给分培养不出用户习惯，也转不起增长飞轮，所以才要求大量持仓，预测市场不存在这个问题

2️⃣ 交易量是不是刷分刷出来的

这个误解最大。预测市场最重要的是订单簿流动性，所以我们把大部分积分给了流动性提供者，付手续费拿到的积分并不多。举个例子：现在纯靠刷交易量和手续费拿积分的用户，成本大概 0.3u 一分，而场外某老 x 的最新报价是 0.1u 一分。谁会花三倍的钱在我们这刷量撸分？哈哈哈

3️⃣ 29M 手续费撑不撑得起 1.6B的盘前市值

也有人说我们今年累计手续费 $29M，撑不起盘前 1.6B 的估值。但预测市场这个赛道还在高速增长，还非常早期。Kalshi 这个月的交易量和手续费收入是去年同期的十倍以上，我们现在的单日手续费也是今年一月的十倍多。炒过股的朋友都懂，高成长赛道从来都是给高 PE 倍数来估值的，拿静态收入去算没什么意义

最后再给大家分享两个很有意思的数据也能很好地说明我们在大量虹吸 Polymarket 的市场份额和用户，从下面两张图上可以看到 Crypto 涨跌全市场的交易用户数和交易量总数在过去半年都是变化不大的，但是 Polymarket 的用户数和交易量都在大幅下滑，同时这个下滑数量基本和我们的增长量是一致的，这个说明什么就懂得都懂啦～

有问题欢迎大家在评论区直接问我们哦 @dingalingts @yuexiaoyu @TC8880

text:
回望过去两个月，TapeOut社区里萌生过许许多多想法。难得的是，所有美好的构想，都没有止步于纸上空谈、停留在空想阶段。大家沉下心，摒弃浮躁，一件一件拆解目标，一步一步落地执行。没有急于求成的喧嚣，只有持续不断的耕耘，从机制打磨到社区共建，从共识凝聚到生态迭代，每一小步，都走得扎实、笃定。我们就这样，稳稳地向着更大的舞台走去。

曾经很多看起来遥不可及的目标，当初遥想时，仿佛隔着万重山。路上不乏质疑的声音，也有迷茫焦虑的时刻，有人匆匆路过，选择转身离开；也有人守住初心，选择留下来踽踽前行。我们深知，TapeOut从来不是一场短期的狂欢， $BEM也不是追逐快进快出的筹码，它是一场关于设计、创造与长期主义的漫长修行。

PoD设计证明的赛道本就小众，没有现成的捷径可以复刻。一次次调试电路，一遍遍优化方案，在画布上反复试错，打磨每一个逻辑单元，只为拿到更高的设计质量。每一枚BEM的收获，都来自实打实的思考与创造，而非单纯算力的堆砌。这份机制本身，就在筛选同频的人：耐得住寂寞，扛得住起伏，看得懂底层逻辑，愿意把时间交给时间。

潮起之时，不被浮华迷眼；潮落之际，不被恐慌裹挟。我们不去迎合市场短暂的热度，不随大流追逐转瞬即逝的风口。社区伙伴彼此守望，有人钻研电路，有人分享心得，有人默默坚守，把零散的共识拧成一股力量。种子的成长，本来就需要静待天时，厚积才能薄发。

前路依旧漫长，风雨或许还会再来。但这颗已经破土的种子，扎根越深，就越有抵御风浪的力量。我们继续踽踽前行，守住共识，持续深耕，静待生态慢慢绽放。时间会见证所有安静的付出，那些日复一日的打磨与坚守，终会在某一天，开出意料之外的花，奔赴我们共同期许的远方。
#长期主义 #学会和时间做朋友

说实话，我是真不建议年轻人用仅有的几万块炒币

有这钱出去玩一趟、认识几个新朋友
或者拿去折腾个自己的小项目
都比天天盯 K 线强。这是我自己的内心看法

不过要是你真在做交易，AI 目前的能力确实越来越强
让它帮我查资料，新闻、项目背景、历史行情
以前要自己翻半天，现在问一句就有了

开单的时候我也会问它
大概就是"你觉得现在这个位置能不能开"

它说能，我就小仓位试一下
它说不行，我会反过来让它挑毛病
它说的理由如果认为是没毛病的，这单就不开了
但也就到这一步了。最后点下单的那个人，一直是我

前几天翻了 MEXC 和 Hacken 一起出的《AI 交易安全手册》

里面有个说法我挺有共鸣：提示词不是风控

道理其实很简单。你跟 AI 说"小心点""别亏太多"，它听不听，你控制不了

手册的意思是，限制得做在系统里，比如单笔最多多少钱、杠杆最多几倍、亏到多少就停，超了的单直接下不出去，AI 自己想绕也绕不过去

我看到 MEXC 的调研里还有个数，3,145 个用过 AI 的人里
有 20% 让 AI 不用自己确认就直接下过单。说实话这数据有点夸张了

我还看到有人用Grok bot晒 100U 做到 1000U
你也不知道他之前亏了多少次才有这一回

毕竟亏了钱，心疼的是自己，不是AI

quoted_text:
There have been three key critiques in regards to the @prlnet  raise, but they are largely overblown in my view:

(1) The lab sells AI for dollars and keeps any PEARL it mines, so its investors can profit even if pearl-2:native falls. 

But PEARL is meant to be a SoV like Bitcoin, so buybacks would start a classic fight over how much of the lab’s revenue goes to shareholders vs token holders. The lab raised its own money to build a business that earns separately. That is the separation the SoV narrative actually needs, and the raise allows the lab to not sell the PEARL it may have for funding.

(2) The lab has written every fork and therefore controls the network and would cater to itself. 

But a fork only sticks if the majority of hashrate runs it and the lab’s $75M fleet would add only 2% to 3%. More importantly, the network won’t survive unless someone actually proves useful mining works, so the lab pushing to prove it outweighs the risk of its control.

(3) The lab has never disclosed how much PEARL it holds and the whitepaper says the low starting difficulty was partly meant to fund the team behind it. 

But the raise was cash for shares and not a token sale, and while we can’t tell which addresses are the lab’s, 98% of the coins mined in launch week have never moved. Although more transparency around their current holdings would help the market give more confidence around the entity.

If you agree or disagree let me know...

Robinhood CEO：美代币化监管不确定，大额资产难入场

Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev 在周二第三季度财报电话会议上表示，美国代币化规则能否长期延续存在不确定性，可能阻碍投资者将大额资产投入代币化市场。

他称 SEC 于 9 月授予的五年期创新豁免是“非常积极的一步”，但强调仍需进一步规则制定或立法，才能带来长期监管确定性。

Tenev 称，与客户沟通时，五年后规则走向的不确定性很可能成为把大额资产配置到该技术上的障碍。

代币化股票此前已遭传统发行方抵制，微软、Alphabet 和 Goldman Sachs 等 16 家公司反对其股票在拟议的 OKXICE 平台上线，AMC 首席执行官 Adam Aron 亦公开批评 Robinhood 的代币化股票产品。

quoted_text:
宝子们同一个 fxSAVE 到了 Pendle 上被拆成三种玩法，数字从 6.7% 到 64%，跨度拉得很大。

还是那句话这个数字第一眼确实容易上头，但先别急着选，越是夸张越要冷静！把底层看清楚，再决定往哪边站。
 
先看收益从哪来。

fxSAVE 本身是自动复利加 Delta Neutral 策略，连接 fxUSD/USDC 稳定池，收益来源主要是 xPOSITION 相关费用和储备收益，不承担传统方向性交易敞口。

换句话说，它不是靠赌行情方向赚钱，而是靠策略结构和协议运转产生回报。

当然，Delta Neutral 不等于没有风险，智能合约漏洞、稳定币脱锚、市场机制失效，都在需要评估的范围内。
 
这次的新市场，是 @protocol_fx 在 Pendle 上开的 fxSAVE 池，到期日 2027 年 4 月 29 日，LP 和 YT 都加了 FXN 激励。

同一个底层资产，被做成了三种不同预期的产品。
 
PT 显示 6.7% 固定回报，持有到到期日，拿的是市场隐含的确定收益，适合对收益有明确预期、不想承受波动的资金。

它的风险主要来自底层协议和市场本身。
 
YT 显示 28.45%，最高能拿到 31 倍收益敞口，本质是押注 fxSAVE 未来收益超过市场预期。

预期兑现，收益被放大；收益或者激励不及预期，买入的 YT 也会亏损。

倍数越高，这个赌注越重。
 
LP 显示 64%，做市赚取交易手续费，叠加 FXN 激励，数字最漂亮，但承担的东西也最多：流动性变化、价格波动、收益波动，都要一起扛。

而且这个 64% 要拆开看——里面有多少来自 FXN 奖励，激励能持续多久，市场成交量撑不撑得住，才是决定实际回报的关键。
 
还有一点要记住：页面上的 APY，是按当前条件估算出来的年化数字，不代表接下来半年都能保持这个水平，更不等于最终到手的利润。

激励会变，利率会变，市场也会变。
 
所以赚 6.7% 还是冲 64%，表面是收益选择，实际是对风险的判断。

选之前，把收益来源、激励结构、市场变差时自己要承担多少回撤，这三件事想清楚，再决定站哪边。@quipnetwork

text:
Silicon Valley billionaires are calling Bitcoin dead again.

Jason Calacanis said the same thing when $BTC was $3,700. Now the argument is that AI makes Bitcoin irrelevant.

I think they've got it completely backwards.

AI could create millions of autonomous economic actors that need to transact, settle payments, and store value without relying on traditional banking infrastructure.

Stablecoins solve the payments problem. Bitcoin offers something different... It's scarce, neutral digital capital.

The irony? The same people betting on AI replacing everything are dismissing the financial infrastructure AI could actually need.

I think we're still incredibly early.

(1/5) 225 consecutive Baoding ball rotations. One less finger. Zero cameras. Over 5 minutes without a drop.

We humans can manipulate objects in our hands with our eyes closed, relying on touch and a sense of how our fingers move. Can a robot hand do the same, with two balls that keep colliding with each other?

We trained a four-fingered Shadow Hand Lite in simulation to perform blind Baoding ball rotation, then deployed it on real hardware with no fine-tuning. We provide no vision, no depth and no motion capture. Just proprioception and 16 binary touch signals.

Announcing 3 Critical vulns for hundreds of millions of IoT, Firewalls, OT, and Military devices including: Palo Alto Networks, Comcast, D-Link, HP, Canon, Honeywell, GE, Oracle, Siemens, Rockwell, Digi, Lockheed Martin, Boeing... 

The vulns are with GoAhead Web Server which is a backend library used by these devices. There's a patch available from GoAhead but that doesn't mean there's a patch available for the devices yet -- that's up to the manufacturer.

- TLS traffic over DHE ciphers have a 1-byte secret, "04", meaning anyone can decrypt connections to these devices and steal login credentials and session tokens if the client negotiated with DHE ciphers like the latest TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, which is extremely likely.

- LibreSSL mTLS has been completely bypassed, meaning anyone can connect over mTLS. If you have one of these devices listening on the internet and are expecting mTLS to protect it from attackers, take it offline or patch asap.

- OpenSSL Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) are not enforced, meaning if a user device is stolen or compromised, and you revoke that mTLS cert, nothing actually happens. There are a lot of other attacks this can be used for.

These are critical because these types of devices run our world. Water systems, electricity, military, firewalls, critical infrastructure.

https://t.co/AYUgNsrA0f

text:
Available compute and productive compute aren’t the same thing.
A GPU can sit idle because demand isn’t there. It can also sit idle because the workload is waiting on data: another copy, another sync job, another environment to stage.
The fixed-cost maths looks the same either way. The fix doesn’t.
author: shelbyserves
quoted_text:
Idle GPUs can still produce an expensive AI bill.

In VentureBeat Intelligence’s Q3 survey, 79% of respondents reporting GPU use said their GPUs were busy half the time or less. Yet 70% of that low-use group planned a new, additional or replacement AI platform.

A platform change can mean moving workloads, replacing an inefficient stack or buying access to a different model. It does not automatically mean ordering more GPUs.

An enterprise can also pay twice: once for owned or reserved compute, then again for a hosted model API. Spare capacity on its own hardware does not automatically offset the API invoice. Moving that work requires a suitable model and a functioning deployment.

The fixed-cost arithmetic is unforgiving.

At 20% busy time, each busy GPU-hour carries 5x the fixed capacity cost of a fully used hour. At 50%, that falls to 2x. At 80%, it is 1.25x.

Moving from 20% to 50% cuts fixed cost per busy hour by 60%, with no change in hardware prices. The total fixed bill stays the same; more work shares it. This is an illustrative model, not a measured saving.

The return still needs proving. In September, 58 of 64 respondents planning a platform change lacked finance-reviewed ROI figures. That means unverified returns, not necessarily losses.

For investors, follow three different tests:

• Hardware suppliers: orders converting into collected cash.
• GPU clouds: utilization alongside realized pricing and contract costs.
• Enterprise buyers: cost per successfully completed task.

A busy GPU can run an unprofitable workload. An idle enterprise GPU does not establish a shortage of demand everywhere else.

Survey caveat: self-selected respondents, not a representative census of the world’s GPUs.

20% DONE. EXACTLY WHAT I SAID I WAS GOING FOR. 📈

Even before I passed the evaluation, I had already set a target for myself: 20%.

I told a few friends about it, and one advised me not to put a figure on it because it could put me under pressure and make me start forcing trades. 
His advice was simple: make whatever you can, protect the account, and withdraw.

He genuinely meant well, but I stood by my target. That even almost caused an argument between us 😂
Still, his words planted a little doubt in my mind.

But I knew what I had set out to do.

Honestly, it wasn’t easy. 
My first trade took me straight to 12%, then I pushed to 16%, only to fall back to 5%. 🤣🤣

THAT 5% humbled me! Fear crept in, and I remembered my friend’s warning. I told myself, “If I can just get back to 10%, I’ll be done.”

But God had other plans.

At some point, I had to remind myself: You’ve done this before. Why are you doubting yourself now?

And here we are. 20% achieved. ✅

The goal was always 20%, but if I had been offered less along the way, I would have considered taking it. I’m not going to pretend otherwise. But if I could achieve what I set out to do, why not?

Now, I’m done trading this account. No more trades. I’m protecting what I’ve built and waiting for November 2nd to come around.

Next step: withdrawal.

Now we wait for @EquityEdgeUK to come through. 🇳🇬🤝💙

以为是个王者，原来只是个青铜。

Peer OTC原理就是卖家锁USDC→买家向卖家支付宝转人民币→Peer的TEE验证付款→合约释放USDC。

这里面有两个风险：

1.支付宝封控风险很高

支付宝公开禁止账户用于虚拟货币交易。Peer自己的教程也承认无法保证账户不受风控，并建议卖家每天最多接3名买家，每个挂单只接1单。

这已经说明团队知道支付宝会把此类收款识别为异常交易。所谓“支持支付宝”，只代表技术上能验证支付宝转账，不代表支付宝允许这项用途。

2.收到涉诈资金的风险

卖USDC时，你收到的是陌生买家的人民币。一旦买家资金与诈骗、洗钱或跑分有关，支付宝账户和银行卡都可能被限制，甚至需要配合调查。链上USDC在证明通过后已经交给买家，后续人民币被冻结时，很难把币追回。

现在大多数交易所已经实行冻结包赔了，所以Peer这个台子在没有兜底的情况下，谁会选择在它这里出金呢？

路透和彭博近期披露了 DeepSeek 的上市路径与时间表，目标选在上交所科创板，计划 2026 年底递交招股申报材料，2027 年上半年正式挂牌，保荐机构确定为中信证券。

在组织架构与合规层面，高瓴创投前合伙人严文韬已在九月下旬正式出任 CFO。中信证券团队目前配合推进的核心工作，是协助梁文锋梳理早年幻方量化背景下的股东持股架构，调整私募基金备案方式，处理境内上市关于股东穿透和两百人上限的合规红线，并确立管理层在上市后的控制权与特别表决权机制。

冲刺上市前的这轮私募融资最初目标为 500 亿元，最终超募至约 1000 亿元人民币（折合约 150 亿美元），对应的投前估值在 5000 亿元人民币左右。出资方涵盖了产业资本与国资引导基金，除腾讯追加投资外，宁德时代、美团、吉利汽车产业基金以及芯片设计公司兆易创新均在出资名单内。

不同于以往依赖巨额补贴、缺乏造血能力的大模型初创团队，DeepSeek 推进科创板进程具备实质性的财务指标支撑。凭借极低的推理成本优势，其企业级 API 调用业务快速放量，目前的年化经常性收入（ARR）已经跨过 10 亿美元门槛，这构成了其对标科创板第五套上市标准的基本盘。

本轮 1000 亿元融资的核心去向是算力基础设施储备。在高端芯片禁运与供应链外部限制下，单纯依赖海外算力卡路线不可持续。DeepSeek 正在把大笔资金投向国产算力集群的适配与采购，底层重点推进华为昇腾芯片集群的模型训练与大规模推理联调。投资方中的宁德时代对应能源供给与工业场景，吉利对接智能汽车座舱，兆易创新协同存储与芯片生态。

放弃赴美选择科创板，根本原因在于规避海外跨法域审计与 CFIUS 审查风险，把模型底座、国产芯片、能源与下游工业场景的利益彻底锁在同一张资产负债表内。从量化对冲基金孵化出的极客团队，到建立规范财务与合规体系、绑定本土硬科技产业链，DeepSeek 正在正式转轨为公众科技公司。

中肯一点讲，这放在美国顶尖竞赛圈里，这份履历并不足够强，也并不传奇。

三年入围 USAMO说明达里奥稳定在全国前几百名，但没进 IMO 国家队；高中去 Berkeley 修实分析、抽象代数，在竞赛生里，也其实并不算罕见。
就我周围的CMO竞赛的朋友，有金牌、集训队，国家队虽然没有（其实本来是有的，but此人后来高二对数学失去兴趣转攻IOI了），但是基本在数学方面可以干翻这个履历，更不要说什么湾区数学奥赛第二名。

当然，有人会说这是做题家。可是，哪里不需要做题呢？做题是理解的必要步骤，至少是作为人类筛选天赋的过程当中。我们只能这样来说：竞赛成绩只衡量一个很窄的维度，限时、有标准答案的题，你能解得多快多准。后来拉开差距的，往往是另一些东西，比如选题、方向、是否长期扛住没有答案的研究。Dario 从生物物理再转到 AI，每一步看的方向都很早，这跟奥赛分数，关系确实是不大的。

至于我身边那些天赋绝顶的CMO朋友们，十几年后会走到哪里，就要看后面那些最难量化的部分了。不过，我相信他们都有机会成为各个领域天骄般的存在。

text:
The fundamentals of $PRIORS have clearly strengthened.

0xedbf91223639800bcd5756815caf908df3b890be 

The most important change this time is not simply the addition of a few product features.

Priors is gradually evolving from an on-chain credit protocol for AI Agents into infrastructure integrating credit records, credit lines, a job marketplace, payments, and agent discovery.

I believe the most promising bullish thesis is that Priors could become the credit layer of the AI Agent economy. As Agents begin hiring one another, calling tools, purchasing services, and settling transactions, they need more than just payment capabilities. They also need working capital and reliable ways to assess whether their counterparties can fulfill their obligations. Priors is attempting to solve both problems simultaneously.

There are several reasons why its fundamentals have strengthened.

The product is expanding from a credit protocol into a complete set of use cases.

The core thesis of my previous analysis was that Agents can borrow USDG to pay for tools, APIs, inference costs, or to take on jobs. After repaying their loans, their records remain permanently on-chain, forming a public credit history and score. Other applications can then query these records to decide whether an Agent should be trusted. Recent updates have made this thesis more concrete.

Go Mode is beginning to connect with actual job demand. The interface lists 50 paid jobs that Agents can take on using their credit lines, five of which were live at the time. Users can also assign jobs to Agents running on OpenClaw, Hermes, or ElizaOS, pay for tool usage through Priors MCP, and confirm the borrowing before it happens.
Borrowing and repayment records are beginning to connect with job income. The update states that loans repaid using income from jobs are recorded in an Agent's credit history, with Score V2 increasing the weighting of such repayment records by up to 25%.
The user experience continues to improve. Go Mode supports Google login, removes the need for users to manage seed phrases themselves, and has the protocol handle gas fees. It also supports one-tap stock purchases using USDG, subject to platform eligibility and availability.
Credit information is becoming standardized and accessible. Every account can now have a public profile, while each Agent's card shows its credit level, exactly what it needs to reach the next level, and how its credit tree is progressing.

The significance of these features is that Priors is no longer simply waiting for Agents to come and borrow money. It is connecting borrowing, completing jobs, paying for tools, and repaying debt into a single workflow.

I particularly value the connection between job income and credit scoring. If an Agent can use the income it earns from each completed job to repay its loans and improve its credit history, credit becomes more than a static metric. It becomes an asset that can accumulate value through real economic activity.

However, 50 listed jobs, with five live at the time, only demonstrate that the product has begun connecting to a job marketplace. They do not prove that substantial job demand has already developed. The next things to watch are completed job volume, actual borrowing by Agents, and repayment rates.

PRIORS is expanding from an individual credit product toward a credit network between Agents. This is the upgrade I consider most promising.

Priors' latest product direction is to allow Agents to assess one another using historical borrowing, repayment records, overdue payments, and credit scores, rather than relying solely on their owners or a single platform to determine creditworthiness.

For example, a trading Agent may want to buy a token but first needs another Agent to check its holder distribution. The Agent performing the check wants to start working immediately and get paid later, so it needs to know whether the other party has the ability to pay.

When such a transaction takes place between two Agents that have never worked together before, it is difficult to establish trust based solely on names, scores, or subjective assessments. Actual borrowing and repayment records provide another basis for making that judgment.

Priors has already advanced public profiles and credit history displays, and plans to further establish a unified ERC-8004 Agent directory. The project mentioned in its tweets that there were approximately 8,800 ERC-8004 Agents on Robinhood Chain. Agents without credit histories can also list their identity information first and gradually build their credit profiles as they begin accumulating records.

This means Priors is targeting not only Agents that already need to borrow, but the entire population of Agents that could become borrowers, counterparties, or service providers in the future.

This creates a potential positive feedback loop: more Agents conduct transactions → more Agents need to check their counterparties' credit → more Agents have an incentive to establish their own credit histories → more real borrowing and repayment records further improve the usefulness of the credit system.

Priors has also proposed that Agents should be able to retain their credit histories when ownership changes. If implemented, this would further strengthen the significance of credit records as identity assets belonging to Agents, because their credit profiles would no longer be merely data held within their original owners' accounts.

However, product development stages need to be distinguished. A unified Agent directory, the transfer of credit records alongside an Agent's identity, and reducing the process of opening a credit line in Go Mode to a single step were still under development or planned for the future in the screenshots. They should not all be treated as already launched features.

x402 makes Priors' positioning more meaningful.

My previous research focused on the lack of working capital available to Agents. The development of payment infrastructure further reinforces the importance of this problem.

The project update mentioned that Priors x402 0.8.0 had been released, designed to enable a single USDG payment to support payment flows on Robinhood Chain and pay service sellers on Base. The project also stated that its credit-checking API now supports OpenAPI and x402 Discovery, allowing other Agents to discover the API and pay per call.

These two directions are important when combined: x402 addresses how Agents initiate and complete payments on demand, while Priors attempts to address whether Agents have the funds to use these services and whether their counterparties are trustworthy.

If the Agent economy continues shifting from human-operated workflows toward autonomous transactions, Agents may frequently purchase APIs, call analytical tools, take on paid jobs, and settle transactions with other Agents. Credit infrastructure could then become an important layer built on top of payment rails.

One of the project's tweets also cited ecosystem figures at the time, including more than 230 million settlements across Base and Solana through x402, as well as Robinhood's reported figures of more than 150,000 Agentic Trading accounts and nearly 30 million tool calls per day. These are claims cited by the project in its materials and should not be directly interpreted as users or transaction volume already acquired by Priors. However, they show that the project is targeting a market much broader than lending alone.

Expanded collateral options and improved risk controls are making the credit model more complete.

Priors recently announced that Agents can use Pendle's PT-USDG as collateral to borrow USDG. This further expands the range of eligible assets beyond the previously available collateral options, including USDG, Robinhood stock tokens, and PRIORS.

A broader collateral range could allow more asset holders to access credit lines and improve the utilization of idle assets. However, PT-USDG carries specific risks involving maturity, price discounts, and liquidity. The addition of a new collateral type alone does not mean that lending capacity will increase proportionally.

Another update worth recognizing is the improvement in risk controls for stock collateral. Priors stated that before issuing loans against stock tokens, it now checks every round of Chainlink price-feed records over the previous 14 days. This is designed to prevent a 25% price jump occurring between two sampling points from going undetected.

This reflects the real problems that a credit protocol must address: collateral pricing cannot rely solely on the quoted price. It must also guard against sudden price fluctuations and valuation manipulation.

Meanwhile, Priors has made its GitHub code public and established a bug bounty program. It has also been listed on DefiLlama, allowing the public to track its credit pools. The project previously stated that TVL and loan data would gradually become available for tracking, and subsequently announced that its pools could be tracked through DefiLlama.

These updates help improve transparency and confidence in its risk controls. However, what will truly demonstrate the viability of its credit model is actual loan volume, collateral ratios, bad debt, and repayment performance, rather than the existence of risk-control rules alone.

However, whether the value proposition of the PRIORS token has strengthened remains the most critical question in the entire thesis, and one that still requires further validation.

According to my previous research, PRIORS is not merely a governance token. It is a credit-guarantee asset:

Agent owners can stake PRIORS to obtain larger credit lines for their Agents.
If a default occurs, approximately 75% of the associated staked tokens are burned.
The protocol plans to use a portion of its revenue to purchase PRIORS and use it as protocol collateral backing high-performing Agents.
A portion of revenue is used to increase liquidity in PRIORS/USDG pools.
Holders can guarantee their own Agents and share a portion of the fees generated by those Agents.

If these mechanisms can operate as designed, the value of PRIORS would no longer need to depend solely on market expectations for the broader AI Agent sector. Instead, it could gradually become connected to credit demand, the expansion of credit lines, default risk, and protocol revenue.

This is the main reason I am bullish on PRIORS: it attempts to make the token part of how Agents obtain credit and expand their operations, rather than merely a token generating trading volume through an AI narrative.

Going forward, I will divide the potential catalysts into three layers.

First layer: Real lending activity and data transparency

TVL and loan data on DefiLlama become more comprehensive, while jobs and credit lines through Go Mode begin generating sustained borrowing activity. Public data shows continued growth in loan balances, utilization, and repayment records. If these metrics continue improving, the market will find it easier to move from seeing Priors as a project with a product to recognizing it as a protocol with real economic activity.

Second layer: The formation of an Agent credit network

Go Mode continues expanding its job marketplace, making it easier for Agents across ecosystems such as OpenClaw, Hermes, and ElizaOS to integrate with Priors MCP. The credit directory gradually opens up, allowing ERC-8004 identities and credit histories to be discovered and queried by other applications. If Agents begin actively checking their counterparties' credit, Priors could evolve from a lending protocol into credit infrastructure that can be called upon by multiple applications.

Third layer: Token demand and a revenue flywheel

If the expansion of Agent credit lines begins generating greater demand for PRIORS as collateral, while protocol revenue can actually be allocated to token backing, liquidity, and related economic mechanisms, PRIORS may achieve more direct value capture. In particular, it is worth tracking the scale of staking demand, protocol revenue, and token burns resulting from defaults, as well as whether they are significant enough relative to the circulating supply.

In addition, Priors has proposed a credit-level dashboard, the transfer of loan records alongside Agent identities, further simplification of the process for opening credit lines, and privacy features designed for Agents. These are all potential future catalysts.

The privacy solution remains an area of exploration. The project hopes that, in the future, it will be possible to prove an Agent's credit level or absence of defaults without disclosing the details of every transaction, while keeping the underlying debt itself public. This is not a product feature that has been completed at the current stage.

If product usage, the credit-record network, and PRIORS' collateral mechanism can ultimately reinforce one another, Priors' long-term potential could be far greater than that of an ordinary AI Agent concept project. This is the core thesis that I believe makes it most worth being bullish on at this stage.

Priors is an on-chain protocol specifically providing credit to AI Agents.

The core logic: AI Agents can borrow USDG to pay for tools, APIs, inference costs, or take on jobs. After repaying, the repayment record is permanently written on-chain, forming a public credit file and score. Any other application can query this record for free to decide whether to trust the Agent.

AI Agents can already take on tasks, call tools, and pay each other using the x402 protocol, but they lack "operating capital." Many jobs are "pay first, get paid later." Traditional ratings or reviews are easy to fake, but "borrowing real money and paying it back" is very hard to fake. Priors solves the Agent's credit and liquidity problems: Agents with repayment records are easier to trust, can get larger credit lines, and better pricing, while lenders' risk remains controllable.

The project's main product is Go Mode:
- Log in with Google, no need to remember seed phrases, protocol pays for gas.
- Agents can borrow USDG.
- Can use Robinhood stock tokens as collateral to open credit lines.
- Can also use their own PRIORS as collateral to open credit lines.
- Also has MCP tools, SDK, paid API, letting Agents borrow, repay, and check others' credit on their own.
- Idle USDG can be deposited into Morpho to earn interest.
- Has an assistant like agent001 to help you operate.

The PRIORS token is not purely a governance token. Its core use is as a credit guarantee asset:
- Agent owners can stake PRIORS behind them to open larger credit lines. On default, about 75% is burned.
- The protocol uses a portion of revenue to buy PRIORS and place it behind well-performing Agents as protocol guarantees.
- A portion of revenue is also used to increase PRIORS/USDG liquidity pools.
- Holders can guarantee their own Agents and share a portion of the fees generated by that Agent.

text: Recent user data leaks at hardware wallets and exchanges. Watch for phishing, social engineering, and SIM swap attacks 👇👇
author: GoPlusSecurity
quoted_text:
4 data leaks reported today:

1. Coinbase's vendor Amplitude exposed some users’ contact data (funds unaffected).
2. Bithumb (Korea) had user data leaks.

In TradFi, two securities firms in Korea leaked data: 
3. Mirae Asset
4. Daishin Securities

You can't prevent a leak, but you can protect yourself.

Leaked exchange data (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ID documents, transaction history) is mostly used for phishing, SIM swapping, and social engineering.

Reduce info you share
- Use a unique email alias for each exchange (SimpleLogin, Apple Hide My Email, etc). A leak then can't be linked to your other accounts, and you can spot which service leaked.
- Share only what's required. Don't add optional profile details.
- Use a dedicated phone number (a VoIP or secondary SIM) for exchange accounts if you can, since leaked numbers are the main route to SIM swaps.

Lock down the account
- Use a unique, long password from a password manager.
- Turn on hardware security keys (YubiKey) or passkeys, or at least an authenticator app.
- Avoid SMS 2FA.
- Enable withdrawal address whitelisting and a withdrawal time lock if the exchange offers them.
- Set up an anti-phishing code, which puts a code you choose in every legitimate email from the exchange.
- Review active sessions and API keys regularly. Delete any API keys you don't use.
- Restrict API keys to withdraw-disabled and IP-whitelisted.

Defend against
- SIM swapping: Ask your carrier to add a port-out PIN or number lock.
- Phishing and impersonation: Assume anyone who contacts you about your account, "security issues," or "refund recovery" is a scammer, even if they know your name, balance, or recent trades.
- Exchange support staff don't ask for your password, 2FA codes, or seed phrase.
- Never click links in emails or texts. Go to the site yourself.

- "Wrench attacks": Leaked addresses plus holdings data have led to real-world extortion and robberies. Don't publicize your holdings, and keep large balances out of anything tied to your home address if you can.

If a breach is announced
1. Change the exchange password and any other account that reused it.
2. Check https://t.co/qtIGFkbaPO for your email address.
3. Revoke API keys and active sessions.
4. Review recent withdrawals and security settings.
5. Watch for phishing emails and texts that reference the breach, because scammers move fast after one.

Stay SAFU! 🙏

text:
$microduck is beginning to gain a kind of exposure that sets it apart from ordinary AI projects.

0xd5f1afea47b1a9eab414d2ee740cf1d6d039e725 

Jensen Huang first interacted with the robots in person at GTC, then mentioned the ducks on X, and Elon Musk also joined the conversation.

Individually, none of these posts seems sufficient to change the project's long-term value.

But when a real product repeatedly enters the public spotlight through high-profile figures, the market has reason to reassess its potential reach.

Of course, I would not treat Jensen Huang mentioning Microduck once, twice, or three times as a linear increase in bullishness. His latest post still revolves around the previous GTC demonstration. It was not a new product launch, and it does not mean that either Jensen or Elon endorses the on-chain token. However, it has given a moment from the original demonstration another opportunity to circulate rather than fade away over time. A single interaction can be a coincidence; repeated mentions can make the market pay attention to the character itself. What ultimately determines the narrative's ceiling is whether it can continue generating content without the help of high-profile figures.

My bullish view on Microduck was never based on the possibility that another prominent person might mention it. It was based on the fact that there is a real physical AI product behind it. Priced at $399, the robot is compact and comes with an open SDK and training framework. Users can teach it to walk, dance, roller-skate, or even perform entirely different movements. It is not limited to following a fixed script in a promotional video. Different users have the opportunity to produce different behaviors with the same robot.

This is what distinguishes Microduck from many projects that attract attention purely through the AI narrative. Ordinary AI Memes often need to keep producing new images, videos, or trending topics to maintain interest. Microduck, by contrast, has a physical product that can continuously generate new material. The movements the robot performs, unexpected outcomes during training, and new ideas developed by users can all become independent pieces of content. The GTC demonstration showcased precisely this potential: the ducks did not execute every instruction perfectly, and their unpredictable reactions made the demonstration more entertaining.

From this perspective, Jensen Huang's exposure changes Microduck's distribution opportunities rather than its underlying product proposition. Previously, it relied mainly on product launches, developer communities, and technology media for attention. Now, the character has an opportunity to reach a much broader social media audience. Elon's interaction added another layer of momentum to the circulation of that content, potentially introducing Microduck to people who otherwise might never have paid attention to Physical AI.

However, the first wave of traffic generated by celebrity attention and the long-term distribution potential of a product are two different things. If the discussion ultimately remains focused on Jensen and Elon interacting with the ducks, the market is still trading a short-term event. If this exposure introduces Microduck to new audiences who then continue following the product and user-generated content, the event could become the starting point of a much longer narrative.

The physical product's sales data also provides some support for this thesis. Earlier reports indicated that Microduck had surpassed 15,000 pre-orders in September, generating more than $6 million in sales. On October 23, TechCrunch reported that pre-orders had subsequently exceeded 20,000 units. It is important to distinguish pre-orders from robots already delivered, and from actual active users. Nevertheless, these figures confirm that Microduck already had a real product and existing pre-order demand before receiving this additional exposure. It is not an empty concept waiting for a celebrity to give it a story.

What matters next is what happens after the first batch of robots reaches customers. If the previously announced delivery schedule proceeds as planned, users could start posting unboxing videos, interactions at home, newly trained movements, and all kinds of unexpected use cases. Some people will teach their ducks to dance; others might put them through gaming challenges, while others will share their training failures. These pieces of content will be created independently, yet they will all revolve around the same recognizable character. Compared with waiting for Jensen to post again, this form of distribution has a better chance of producing a sustained stream of content.

I believe this is the most compelling long-term direction for MICRODUCK: evolving from a physical AI product that has attracted attention into an AI pet that users want to train, showcase, and share. If it really makes its way into more people's lives, Microduck could evolve from a product passively waiting for exposure into a character that actively generates new content. At that point, its distribution would no longer depend entirely on official releases or require an external celebrity to provide every new catalyst.

From the token's perspective, the market has clearly started trading this narrative. The previous rally shows that investors are willing to assign a premium to the combination of a physical AI product, celebrity exposure, and the potential for user-generated content to spread. However, I would not conclude that the fundamental value of MICRODUCK has changed dramatically simply because Jensen mentioned it again and Elon subsequently interacted with the post. There is currently no evidence that the on-chain token entitles holders to a share of the physical product's revenue, commercial rights, or official endorsement. Strong product sales do not automatically mean that customers will buy the token. The connection between the two remains primarily driven by market attention and narrative.

Therefore, I am watching two main catalysts going forward. The first is whether Microduck can generate substantial amounts of authentic user-created content after the first deliveries, allowing the ducks to appear in more than just demonstrations involving a handful of prominent figures. The second is whether Jensen Huang or other high-profile figures mention Microduck again in new contexts, expanding its reach further. The first determines whether the narrative can sustain itself; the second could create another window of exposure. If these two forces begin reinforcing each other, the market will have a stronger reason to reassess the project's potential reach.

Overall, I believe MICRODUCK's narrative fundamentals have strengthened compared with before. Jensen's renewed public mention, Elon's interaction, and growing attention toward the physical product have all increased the likelihood that Microduck will be discovered by a broader audience. However, it still needs to prove that external exposure can translate into sustained user participation, and that these developments can ultimately generate real, lasting demand for the on-chain token.

I am not simply betting on whether Jensen Huang will publish a third post. What I really want to observe is whether people continue making content about Microduck after the current excitement fades. If the answer is yes, it has a chance to evolve from a robotic duck that attracted attention at a technology conference into a recognizable character capable of sustained distribution in the Physical AI space. If all the discussion ultimately returns to the same demonstration video, then even with both Jensen Huang and Elon involved in spreading the content, this rally could still turn out to be a short-term event trade with unusually high visibility.

Took another look at $microduck recent price action.

0xd5f1afea47b1a9eab414d2ee740cf1d6d039e725 

Is the rally just because Jensen Huang interacted with the robots?

I think the more important factor is timing:

Microduck already had a real product and existing pre-order demand when the exposure hit.

The prominent figure's attention is just the catalyst.

What determines how far this narrative can go is whether this robotic duck can evolve from a physical AI product into a character that users want to continuously train, create content around, and share.

On October 21, Jensen Huang interacted with four Microduck robots during his NVIDIA GTC Berlin keynote. He asked them to sit down, stand up, take a nap, and even attempted to get them to perform a backflip. The robots did not follow every instruction perfectly. Some fell over, while others kept moving, making the demonstration particularly entertaining. Clips of the interaction subsequently began circulating online.

I believe the value of this footage goes beyond Microduck appearing in Jensen Huang's keynote. It presents a contrast that is highly suitable for internet distribution: a real AI robot attempting to understand and follow human instructions, yet producing unpredictable responses. Compared with polished promotional videos in which every movement is carefully choreographed, these genuine interactions are more likely to evoke an emotional response and be edited into standalone content for wider distribution.

Moreover, the demonstration was not simply about putting four cute robotic ducks on stage. NVIDIA also showcased a Physical AI workflow built around Microduck: creating a simulated environment with Isaac Sim, training in the cloud, and then bringing the trained policy back to physical devices for evaluation and deployment. This made Microduck more than just an appealing product on stage. It also became a concrete demonstration of embodied robotics, reinforcement learning, and AI Agent technology.

This reinforces my earlier thesis on Microduck. Many Physical AI projects focus on efficiency, productivity, industrial automation, or how many complex tasks humanoid robots can perform. Microduck takes a different approach. First and foremost, it is an AI pet that can enter people's homes, be trained and modified, and be shared with others.

Its significance does not necessarily lie in being more capable than other robots, but in being easier for ordinary people to understand and engage with. Priced at $399, it is compact and comes with an open SDK and training framework. Users can try teaching it to walk, dance, roller-skate, or perform entirely new movements. Different users may end up with different behaviors, creating opportunities for continuous content creation.

If these robots eventually reach a large number of households, content generation will no longer depend entirely on official releases. Some people may share new movements they have trained, others may challenge their robots to perform unusual tricks, and some may turn the training process, failures, and successful results into videos. Other users can then imitate, modify, and retrain them, gradually developing their own ways of interacting with Microduck.

The core reason I was bullish on microduck in the first place was this potential transition from a physical product to user-generated content. Jensen Huang's demonstration created a new distribution opportunity, bringing attention that had previously come mainly from product launches, developer communities, and technology media onto NVIDIA's global technology stage and into a broader public audience.

The data surrounding the physical product is also changing. Reports in September indicated that Microduck had surpassed 15,000 pre-orders, generating more than $6 million in sales. On October 23, TechCrunch reported that pre-orders had subsequently exceeded 20,000 units. This increase coincided with the viral spread of videos following Jensen Huang's demonstration, suggesting that product attention and pre-order demand were both expanding during this period. However, we cannot attribute every additional order to this single interaction, nor can we equate pre-order figures directly with the number of robots already delivered or active users.

To me, the significance of these figures is that Microduck is no longer just a concept waiting for market validation. It already has a real product, actual pre-order demand, and additional exposure from NVIDIA's technology showcase. What needs to be verified next is whether these orders can be converted into successful deliveries and whether the robots will generate sustained usage and content once they reach customers.

This is why I am particularly interested in the delivery window around Christmas. According to the project's previously announced plans, the first batch of robots is expected to be delivered to North America, Europe, and the UK before Christmas. If deliveries proceed as planned, another wave of content could emerge, distinct from Jensen Huang's demonstration: unboxing videos, interactions in home environments, newly trained movements, and developers sharing their training strategies. If this content continues to appear, Microduck's attention will no longer be limited to demonstrations by a handful of prominent figures. It could gradually shift toward content created by users themselves.

Of course, an announced delivery schedule does not mean deliveries have already been completed. Product experience, delivery timelines, and user retention will all influence whether this path succeeds. If users only experiment with the robot briefly after receiving it and do not continue training or sharing content, even high pre-order numbers may fail to translate into lasting cultural relevance. Conversely, if the robots can continually develop new behaviors and provide new ways to interact with them, Microduck could gradually become a recognizable character in the Physical AI space.

Looking at the chart, microduck previously consolidated in the market-cap range of approximately $1.7M–$2M before experiencing two sharp rallies, briefly reaching around $7.2M. It has now pulled back to approximately $4.97M. This shows that the price action has been significantly influenced by event-driven attention, but the roughly 31% retracement from the peak also indicates that some short-term traders have taken profits. Going forward, we need to watch whether the price can stabilize and reclaim the MA10 rather than simply assuming that exposure from a prominent figure will keep driving the price higher.

I also want to emphasize an important distinction: progress in the real Microduck product does not automatically translate into revenue or value for the on-chain microduck token. Jensen Huang showcasing the robots at an NVIDIA event does not mean he endorses this token, and growing pre-orders do not mean people purchasing the physical robots will buy the token. At this stage, the relationship between the two is primarily through narrative and market attention, rather than direct economic rights.

Therefore, I am bullish on microduck not because Jensen Huang might interact with it again, but because this exposure has given an existing Physical AI product a much larger opportunity to reach new audiences. A high-profile demonstration can generate the first wave of attention, actual deliveries could create a second, and the behaviors trained by users and the content they continuously produce will determine whether the narrative can sustain itself over a longer period.

If Microduck can evolve from a robotic duck showcased by Jensen Huang into an AI pet that thousands of users independently train, demonstrate, and share, its narrative will no longer depend on a single external event. Instead, it will have the ability to continuously generate new content. This is what I believe makes the long-term thesis for microduck most compelling.

quoted_text:
The Fed decides rates tomorrow. Everyone's asking "hold or hike?"

Wrong question. The real one: is the Fed fighting inflation, or fighting oil?

September CPI: 3.7% headline. Core: 2.6%.

That 1.1-point gap is mostly energy, up 20% in a year. Gasoline alone was over half of September's increase.

Strip out oil and the Fed isn't far from target. So the December hike markets are pricing would be a hike into a supply shock.

Rate hikes don't pump more oil. They just slow everything else.

The last major central bank to try it: the ECB, July 2008. It hiked with oil near $145. Within three months it was cutting.

Now look at bonds. The 10-year fell from above 5.3% to ~4.99% this month, with hikes still priced. The bond market is leaning toward slowdown, not inflation.

And Brent just slipped under $115 on Iran talks. If Hormuz reopens, the case for Dhikedecember goes with it.

Tomorrow I'm listening for one word from Warsh: "core" or "headline."

Core = he looks through oil. Risk breathes.

Headline = he's chasing oil. December is live, and BTC at $80K isn't priced for that.

text:
今天海力士最新财报，能回答8月份关于存储这三个思考框架么？海力士三季度营收104.62万亿韩元，营业利润83.33万亿韩元，营业利润率接近80%，确实很强。但如果担心的是2027年以后会怎样，单季利润再高，也解决不了全部疑问。大家的是这笔利润还能赚多久，之后会掉到哪里。

看完今天的财报和电话会，个人倾向于把本轮高景气持续的时间看得更长。下一轮底部抬高也有了更具体的依据。至于现在这些利润有多少能够长期保留下来，还需要持续观察。

1、关于周期顶部，今天给出的增量相当明确。 
海力士已经完成与主要客户的2027年HBM供货量和价格协商。与此同时，长期供货协议LTA覆盖了2027至2028年总产能的50%以上，签约客户增加到14家，协议通常以五年为期。

关于明年电话会上更吸引眼球的一句话，是DRAM和HBM到2029年基本售罄。这里要看清口径：它包括已签LTA，也包括正在与客户具体洽谈的需求。后者有明确采购计划支撑，但尚不能全部算成已经锁定的订单。

再往远看，公司判断供不应求可能持续到2030年。这是管理层对供需的预测。把它和已经谈妥的明年交易条件放在一起，确实能提高对景气持续性的信心

需求也在向更多产品扩散。三季度服务器DDR5出货环比增长超过40%，AI基础设施对存储的拉动已经延伸到系统内存和企业级SSD。长上下文与Agent应用需要保存和反复调用更多数据，容量与成本约束又会推动部分数据转移到SSD。海力士的产品组合因此有机会覆盖更广的需求。

从这个角度看，把2027年直接设定为盈利终点，显得过于机械。至少今天的披露支持我们把时间周期再往后延。

2、下一轮周期底部能不能抬高，我认为这次有了更值得重视的证据。
今天海力士披露，LTA会在双方约定的价格区间内反映市场变化，同时加入保证金等履约安排。合同开始承担一部分稳定采购和定价的作用，这有助于减轻需求调整对公司的冲击。

客户愿意为远期供给承担一定的约束，对原厂当然有价值。公司也更容易按照相对确定的采购安排规划生产，减少一边扩产、一边猜需求的成分。

但这里还缺一些决定底部有多高的细节。价格区间的下沿在哪里，能不能覆盖下一代产品的全部成本？保证金有多少，客户推迟采购需要承担什么代价？这些条件，比协议写了几年更重要。

供给端也有一个积极变化。海力士表示，新厂房可以先建，设备投入和量产扩张则分阶段推进，根据需求和盈利情况调整。这样能保留一部分扩产弹性，不过一家公司的资本纪律，还需要放到全行业供给里检验。

因此，下轮盈利回落得幅度小一些，是有商业依据的判断。但这个只算是定性而非定量的判断。

3、最后是正常化利润，这会直接决定海力士应该值多少钱。
今天电话会上有一个细节很有意思：公司预计明年HBM与普通DRAM的盈利差距会缩小。结合管理层对HBM交易条件和盈利改善的说明，普通DRAM当前的价格景气对利润贡献有多大，就值得单独拿出来看。

三季度DRAM出货环比增长约10%，平均售价上涨幅度达到百分之二十几的后段；NAND出货略有下降，平均售价仍上涨百分之二十几的中段。这里包含产品组合改善的影响，但也足以说明当前业绩对价格环境相当敏感。

如果未来普通存储价格不再大涨，海力士能留下多少利润，才是正常化估值的主要依据。HBM确实有机会提高盈利质量。它与客户芯片和系统的协同更深，定制化也在增加，技术领先和稳定量产能力可能带来更强的客户黏性。

对海力士，更有用的做法是分别估算HBM、服务器DRAM和其他存储业务的持续盈利能力，再把它们加起来。

对长期估值来说，接下来很关键的一步，是新产能陆续投产、普通存储涨价放缓以后，海力士还能不能保持较好的利润和现金流。如果能做到，市场就有更多理由接受一个高于过去的盈利中枢。当然最终还是要看需求增长能持续多久？这是一切估值的起点，未来两年最下游token的消耗大概率还是高速增长，但说实话再往后我也看不清。

随意简单说，根据今天披露的信息，可以得出：
1）景气持续时间比市场想象的要长；
2）下一轮下行幅度相比之前大概率大幅收窄；
3）长时间维持正常化利润这点，长协已经给出了有价值的起点，未来的交付、价格和资本回报会继续给出证据。

整体来说，今天海力士财报能给市场更大的信心，也能支持一波向上的走势。也是周一这里https://t.co/EJK02ZdFdL聊到的、Anthropic路演开始之前应该有一波行情。

quoted_text:
存储板块从6月之前最热的板块，经过一轮调整现在已经是争议最大的板块了，核心市场现在也弄不清到底把存储当做周期还是成长来看。之前行情好认为有成长的迹象，现在一股脑又归为周期，要万劫不复才行。高盛最新这份关于存储的报告，还是很值得看看，它梳理了当下市场八大核心疑虑，也给了我们一个去看待存储的框架。下面图片是高盛报告对市场八大疑虑的分析。 说说我的理解：
1、这八项之中，哪些最有说服力，哪些假设最激进？
最有说服力的三项
1）LTA结构确实发生了实质变化
五年合同、take-or-pay、价格底线和大额预付款都已有公司公开披露，这是本轮周期最不同于历史周期的地方。

2） 原厂库存仍然偏低
2—4周库存明显低于历史下行周期水平，且三星和海力士均公开表示客户需求仍超过供给能力。

3）HBM扩张会挤压普通DRAM供给
HBM trade ratio上升、先进封装约束、洁净室空间不足和新厂建设周期较长，使得“HBM扩产”和“普通DRAM同步扩产”难以同时快速实现。

最激进、最需要验证的两项
1）2027年HBM可比产品涨价约60%
方向上有逻辑，但幅度对：GPU出货、HBM4良率、客户议价、LTA价格上限、三家供应商扩产纪律等这几点非常敏感。

2）长鑫影响长期局限于中国本土
在未来一年可能成立，但放到三至五年维度，这个判断明显偏乐观。除非存储供应链因为政治原因出现明显东西分化。长鑫真正的风险未必是立刻争夺HBM，而是压低普通DRAM长期价格中枢。

2、高盛这份报告最的价值，在于提出了一个可能的框架：
市场仍然用上一轮“现货主导、供应商盲目扩产、库存快速累积”的存储周期，去估值一个越来越由AI服务器需求、先进封装约束、长期同、预付款和价格底线主导的新周期。

其中，最扎实的多头依据是：
LTA条款明显强化；
原厂库存极低；
HBM扩产挤压普通DRAM；
NAND资本开支不足；
服务器存储需求仍在增长。
最需要保持警惕的是：
2027年HBM涨价幅度可能过于激进；
长协既保护底部，也可能限制顶部；
海力士“二季度一次性miss”必须在三季度兑现修复；
长鑫的全球影响短期有限，但中长期绝不能忽视。

3、需要思考的几个点：
1）周期顶部会不会比市场预期更晚？
只要AI服务器、HBM、服务器DRAM和企业级SSD需求持续增长，2027年未必就是盈利终点。

2）下一轮周期底部是不是会显著高于过去？
LTA、预付款、价格底线和低库存，会降低过去那种“价格暴跌—库存爆仓—巨额亏损”的概率。

3）估值逻辑需要从峰值利润转向正常化利润
未来会长时间维持正常会利润（而非峰值利润）么？
 
一个思考点是：如果把dram、nand当做周期品来看可以理解，但是hbm其实是跟gpu高度绑定的，封装在一起，把hbm当做周期品看的前提是得把英伟达GPU也当做周期品来看（显然gpu并非周期品）。

对于存储企业来说，现在有新周期影子和迹象，但还需要进一步证明，核心还是看需求，未来几年新产能陆续落地后，需求是不是在持续快速增长。

text:
Miden mainnet is live (partner phase).

Programmable privacy by default, and imo the most quantum-paranoid design that has shipped so far.

Went through @bobbinth's launch piece.

Three things worth knowing:

1) There's nothing onchain to decrypt

Most privacy chains put your data onchain in encrypted form. Miden only posts a 32-byte hash. Your actual account data stays on your device, backed up by your Guardian.

Why does that matter?

If an encryption scheme breaks in 10 years (quantum, AI, a leaked key), every encrypted ledger becomes readable in hindsight. A hash gives an attacker nothing to collect in the first place.

Add a core protocol that only relies on hash functions, plus ECDSA keys that never leave your device, and users can move to quantum-safe keys at their own pace instead of in a panic.

2) Compliance is built in, with a few doors

- You can prove one balance or one time window to someone, without opening up the rest of your account

- Issuers can bake rules into their asset (viewing rights, freezes, blocklists)

- Guardians can limit who they secure (e.g. one country, an age group, accredited investors). Every tx needs your keys plus their signature, but they can only pause you, never spend. Spending limits cap the damage if a key leaks (e.g. $1,000 a day), and you can always rotate them out

- In extreme cases (think large hacks), a threshold of validators can decrypt specific txs

That's what a regulated issuer needs before shipping a private dollar. ZEC never needed any of that, it's just money.

3) Today's chain is a rehearsal

Before public mainnet, which Bobbin puts "within a few months":

- The hash function switches from Poseidon2 to a Blake3-based one, which means a migration

- Fees are flat rn and get a proper resource-based model

- Block proofs are still partial, so validators enforce security for now

The guardrails also stay on through both phases. Validators see your private inputs and keep threshold-encrypted tx details for emergencies. Bobbin is upfront about it: once the protocol is battle-tested and formally verified, they come off and users "seamlessly get Zcash-level privacy".

What you can already use today, all through Bread:

- <3s proving on mobile
- USDCx for fees
- Bridges via Circle's xReserve, AggLayer, NEAR Intents and Epoch
- An in-protocol DEX for simple swaps

The real test is public mainnet, and whether those guardrails ever come off.

Watching closely (but NFA ofc).

text:
There are 62,445 resting orders on Hyperliquid's BTC book rn, from 6,919 wallets.  

The public API can't tell you whose any of them are. By default it shows you 20 price levels a side (just totals per price).  

That's the gap @Alchemy's new L4 stream closes, giving you every resting order in the book, incl. the wallet that placed it.

So I built a page that shows both views of the same block, side by side: https://t.co/crpEc9ylST

A few interesting things that stood out:

1) At full precision the public view is ~1.7% of the BTC book

$14.5M of size in a $46 window around mid, vs $849M actually resting (most of it way off mid, but still).

2) HIP-3 books are way more concentrated than you'd think

In 52 of 164 builder-deployed markets, one wallet holds more than half the size within 1% of mid. And just 4 wallets are the biggest quoter on 89 of the 164.

Makes sense for new markets, someone has to seed them. But if you trade size on HIP-3, worth knowing who's actually on the other side.

3) Most of the size near mid on BTC never trades

In a 30s sample, 79% of the size placed within 10bp of mid got pulled within 10s without a single fill. Median order life: 0.34s.

Doesn't mean spoofing, fast MMs requote constantly. But a big chunk of what you see near mid is gone before you can click.

What else?

There's also a live liquidation feed on my lil page. Every liquidation on every market as it hits a block, with the wallet that got liquidated. It starts counting when you open the page, so leave a tab open on a volatile day if you want to witness some action lol.

And the same Alchemy key also reads HyperEVM btw, so the page checks the BBO precompile against the stream on every load (0.00bp apart rn) and matches the L4 book to the public one level by level before showing the book.

Honestly pretty wild what you can build on HL data in an evening now with infra & tooling like this in place.

text:
Should you be on Reddit to drive LLM recommendations?

One of Discuss GTM’s chat members shared an unreviewed preprint study I just finished reading. It looks at whether Reddit shapes which brands AI tools recommend – even when the tools don’t cite Reddit.

Sample and methodology:

The author pulled 12K posts and 100K+ comments from 60 subreddits via Reddit’s API.

Brand mentions were scored by upvotes, placement (title, body, comment), and comment depth.

Those scores were then ranked against brand recommendations from ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini across 50 product queries, each asked three times. The correlation analysis spans 12 consumer categories.

A second test compared Reddit citations in 60 API calls (15 queries) vs. 100 web UI queries per platform, collected via browser automation in February 2026.

Key findings:

• Reddit brand rankings and AI brand rankings lined up fairly strongly.
• Web UIs cited Reddit in 44% of queries on Google AI Mode, 20% on Perplexity, and 17% on ChatGPT.
• APIs returned 0% Reddit citations on every platform.
• Opinion and comparison queries pulled in Reddit most often: 70.8% on Google AI Mode and 45.8% on Perplexity.
• Claude cited Reddit zero times in both channels, but it cited any source in only 19% of web UI queries.

Now, how I read it.

Reddit may influence LLM recommendations even when it’s not cited.

The big implication: citation tracking alone may underestimate Reddit’s role. If brand rankings on Reddit correlate with brand recommendations from LLMs, Reddit may function as a background reputation / consensus layer – not just a direct source.

Remember my post about fan-out queries? Here’s the answer for getting into an LLM’s pre-search association brain.

So “being cited” and “shaping the answer” are two different things.

Reddit also seems especially relevant for high-consideration / opinion-heavy queries. So if you’re in a very competitive field and switching costs are high—yeah, you have to think about building a presence on Reddit.

Shilling is also not the answer.

Engagement quality > raw mention volume.

Because the Reddit score included upvotes, title/body placement, and comment depth, the implied signal is a brand showing up in substantive, highly engaged discussions.

Reddit = reputation channel.

I definitely need to research more guerrilla tactics on Reddit. For now, I’m just passively growing karma—but I’m not sure how to inject brand discussions without it becoming shilling / spam.

Feel free to share your ideas.

PS: This study is an unreviewed preprint from a consultancy with a stake in GEO advice, and it’s co-written with Claude folks.

text:
we got a new 4

a typo in goahead's tls configuration passes sizeof(dhm_g) instead of sizeof(dhm_p), reducing a 2048-bit diffie-hellman modulus to just 1 byte, the size of the generator.

the first byte happens to be 255. not only is it tiny, it's not even prime (3×5×17).

with g=2, the powers of 2 modulo 255 cycle through just 8 values: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128.

that's just 3 bits of possible shared-secret entropy. an attacker can try all 8 possibilities to decrypt an affected tls session.

the typo has been there since 2018.

important caveat: this only affects tls 1.2 dhe with clients that accept the tiny modulus, using the optional mbedtls backend. goahead uses openssl by default.

You can't prevent a leak, but you can protect yourself.

Leaked exchange data (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ID documents, transaction history) is mostly used for phishing, SIM swapping, and social engineering.

Reduce info you share
- Use a unique email alias for each exchange (SimpleLogin, Apple Hide My Email, etc). A leak then can't be linked to your other accounts, and you can spot which service leaked.
- Share only what's required. Don't add optional profile details.
- Use a dedicated phone number (a VoIP or secondary SIM) for exchange accounts if you can, since leaked numbers are the main route to SIM swaps.

Lock down the account
- Use a unique, long password from a password manager.
- Turn on hardware security keys (YubiKey) or passkeys, or at least an authenticator app.
- Avoid SMS 2FA.
- Enable withdrawal address whitelisting and a withdrawal time lock if the exchange offers them.
- Set up an anti-phishing code, which puts a code you choose in every legitimate email from the exchange.
- Review active sessions and API keys regularly. Delete any API keys you don't use.
- Restrict API keys to withdraw-disabled and IP-whitelisted.

Defend against
- SIM swapping: Ask your carrier to add a port-out PIN or number lock.
- Phishing and impersonation: Assume anyone who contacts you about your account, "security issues," or "refund recovery" is a scammer, even if they know your name, balance, or recent trades.
- Exchange support staff don't ask for your password, 2FA codes, or seed phrase.
- Never click links in emails or texts. Go to the site yourself.

- "Wrench attacks": Leaked addresses plus holdings data have led to real-world extortion and robberies. Don't publicize your holdings, and keep large balances out of anything tied to your home address if you can.

If a breach is announced
1. Change the exchange password and any other account that reused it.
2. Check https://t.co/qtIGFkbaPO for your email address.
3. Revoke API keys and active sessions.
4. Review recent withdrawals and security settings.
5. Watch for phishing emails and texts that reference the breach, because scammers move fast after one.

Stay SAFU! 🙏

text:
一年赚了1400多万美元的美国交易员Dan Zanger，最喜欢找放量突破的股票，用的是他自己开发的工具ZVR。

不过想用这个工具，每个月都要花几十美金订阅费😢

TradingView 上有大善人，照着这个思路做了一个免费版，搜索 Zanger Volume Ratio，直接添加就可以使用🤣🤣

它能在盘中告诉你，今天到现在的成交量，是平常同一时间的几倍。  

开盘头一个小时，通常就要成交全天三成左右的量，光看成交量柱子，几乎天天开盘都像在放量。 
ZVR 拿今天到现在的累计成交量，和过去 20 天同一时刻的平均值比，10 点半就跟平常的 10 点半比。  

图表下方会多出一排柱子，100% 就是和平常一样。超过 200%，也就是平常的 2 倍以上，柱子变红，正常的量是灰蓝色。  

真放量的突破，比如图中的 CrowdStrike。
9 月 14 日到美东时间 10 点半，它的成交量已经有平常一整天的九成，ZVR 是 253%，柱子一片红。 
10 点 50 分，股价冲过 8 月 31 日的高点 233.85，之后一个月都收在这条线上方，9 月 23 日比突破那天又涨了 11.4%。  

AMD 那次正好相反。
10 月 2 日开盘十来分钟，它冲过 9 月 25 日的高点 639，创了 52 周新高。 
冲过去那一下，ZVR 只有 88%。到 10 点半，它也成交了平常一天将近四成的量，看着很多。
可平常到这个时间本来就成交这么多，ZVR 只有 106%，一整天最高也只到 110%，收盘又缩回了线下。  

用的时候要加在 5 分钟或 15 分钟这样的日内图上。
日线上一天只有一根柱子，盘中拿还没走完的量去比完整的交易日，不到收盘几乎都偏低。  

红色也不保证突破成功。
Robinhood 9 月 3 日突破时 ZVR 是 391%，之后两周最多跌了 18.5%，止损照样要提前设好。  

设置里只有一个 回溯周期，默认 20，添加时认准作者 fyntrade就行。
author: OtherSideBJ
quoted_text:
18个月，1万美元做到1800万美元。

Dan Zanger的这段战绩曾被评为史上最伟大的40笔交易之一，和索罗斯，都铎·琼斯排在同一张榜上。

Dan 做交易非常简单粗暴，不靠消息也不靠指标，他只找一种机会：带量突破的图形。
买点有几条硬规则：底部没走完不买，突破不放量不买，离突破点超过5%不追。

规矩少，而且明确，非常适合小资金去尝试。
接下来我就结合实例，把他的交易策略梳理清楚。

Dan的工作本来是给有钱人修泳池，业余炒股。
赚到的钱前后吐回去三四次，又花了六年复盘，才在1998年转成全职交易。
最赚钱的那两年，他手里只拿一两只当周涨得最快的股票，刚冲出底部就买，涨不动就换，错了马上走。

带量突破的规则就是为这个定的：
底部走完，上方的卖压就轻了，突破那天放出大量，说明有大资金在买，买点又紧贴着突破位，股价一跌回去就知道买错了。

我的判断路径

1、卖工具也好，卖咨询也好，生产力场景的核心是让别人赚到钱，然后别人分你钱

当然，这个钱可能是预付，比如我知道 MacBook 能帮我赚钱，所以我不管最终赚不赚到，我先买 MacBook

2、dbskill 跑了几个月，我意识到，我的 skill 可以帮很多人赚钱，但是真正用上的人只有 1%

3、所以赚钱的机会就是：如何让 99% 的人用上 dbskill

4、用上 dbskill 两大门槛：1️⃣ 不会使用通用 Agent 2️⃣ 不会写提示词，不知道用哪个 skill 干啥事

5、问题 1️⃣ 通过微信解决，直接在微信里面扫码开箱即用，直接不用学了，bot 智能决策应该调用什么 skill

6、问题 2️⃣，即便在微信里面，我不会写提示词，AI 不说话、人也不说话，skill 依然不会被调用，那就 proactive，让 AI 主动说话，让 AI 主动告诉你，你还有什么事情没干完，而它接下来准备用什么技能帮你干好这个事情，你只需要说：“1” 就可以了

7、可是 AI 怎么才能完成这个事情呢？上下文从哪来呢？解决方案有三：

A、开场的时候主动对话，主动收集信息
B、对于不能搭建知识库的用户，售卖一个搭建知识库的服务，这个知识库既可以服务 codex，也可以服务 dondon bot
C、对于已有知识库的用户，用户直接在微信把一个压缩包发给 dondon bot 就行了，一键拥有上下文

Introducing FrontierCode 2.0: our new coding benchmark that measures a model’s ability to go beyond the spec.

Most coding evals measure a model’s ability to write code that meets a spec. With FrontierCode 1.0, we asked a new question: would you actually merge the PR?

FrontierCode 2.0 is comprised of more diverse tasks, featuring larger scopes and higher mergeability standards. We are now asking: not only would you merge this PR, but should you?

One key feature of FrontierCode 2.0 is underspecified prompts. Rather than including every engineering decision, prompts are deliberately ambiguous, giving the models room to demonstrate their judgment.

The result is a benchmark that is far from saturated, with the top model scoring just 45%.

I so desperately want to end the psyop that buybacks don't work:

1. Mechanically speaking, buybacks make the price go up

2. Crypto is not TradFi, there is a different social contract

> The Mechanical Value of Buybacks

First there's a large number of studies that confirm basic intuitions:
* Market Underreaction to Open Market Share Repurchases NBER (1995) - Buybacks create long term value, especially for underpriced stocks
* The Nature and Persistence of Buyback Anomalies (2009) - Reaffirms buybacks create persistent abnormal positive returns. They have an especially positive effect smoothing over price dips when the market overreacts to bad new
* Actual Share Repurchases, Price Efficiency, and the Information Content of Stock Prices (2017) - Reaffirms the findings of the 2009 paper. Buybacks improve pricing efficiency, liquidity, and are especially positive during market declines
* Pavilion Global Markets Buybacks Drive S&P 500 Returns (2023) - Buybacks can drive up to 43% of the returns in a single stock

tldr: buybacks make the number go up. obviously they work better when your stock is at a lower p/e because of under appreciation or market downturns unrelated to the core business, but nonetheless they are positive on the stock

THIS SHOULD BE REALLY OBVIOUS, you don't even need to read any of the papers above to understand the basic intuitions of why they work:
* Price is a function of supply and demand. When buybacks take supply off the market, price goes up all else held equal
* When shares get taken off the market, the shares you hold represent a larger share of the business meaning you benefit from EPS growth even if revenue isn't growing (let alone if it is)
* Businesses providing constant single sided buys on their own shares has a smoothing effect on liquidity making deeps shallower and setting higher price floors in the long run (more shares are repurchased on a fixed buying program when price is lower)

Some specific examples:
* about 51% of Apple's EPS growth is credited to their legendary buyback program retiring so many outstanding shares
* Autozone has bought back like 90% of their shares - the stock has had double the annualized returns of the SP for the last 2 decades
* Home Depot is similar to Autozone

What crypto people get uncomfortable is that buybacks take a long time to compound. This is totally fine in the stock market where there's many businesses you can forecast out in to the future for a decade+. In crypto I understand this rightfully makes people nervous

One prime example of this would be PONS. It kinda doesn't matter how much %of supply was bought back by PONS if their business never recovers. The entire trade/business may end up being too much a flash-in-the-pan for the long term effect of buybacks to have compounded

But we're now seeing a few crypto businesses start to cross the chasm into multi-cycle success stories. We can & should expect the businesses to implement long durable buyback programs that will compound excess positive returns for the years to come

> The importance of buybacks in crypto

I don't know if any of you noticed this, but you have no legal protections as token holders. It's also not even on any government roadmap to fix this

Regulators are just now getting around to setting some guidelines for crypto projects to not get sued - but even then, none of those guidelines relate to you. You do not have voting rights. You do not have legal recourse. In fact most times you don't even own equity in the underlying businesses which actually collect the revenues

IF token holders had legal rights. IF I could sue Compound or Aave for what they've done to token holders, I'd be far more sympathetic to the argument that teams should wait for buybacks. At the end of the day, I know I'd be able to pursue legal recourse & pressure with like minded token holders to force them to return capital when the time is right

Unfortunately, you have none of these abilities. You have nothing but the promises of the team. IN FACT, a team that likely ran a points program or other to WIN YOUR BUSINESS by trading some of their equity. I'd argue they have a moral responsibility to you to show they're aligned in the long term with you even in the lack of regulatory requirements

But nothing made this disconnect more obvious to me than when we cut the price of Sol by 50% with GPT-6 and I saw people literally saying “no one cares about API pricing” and calling the release a flop. 

Meanwhile the reaction from my enterprise accounts (some of the biggest and most technically sophisticated companies in the world) was a complete 180. To them it was a huge lever that unlocked the ability to scale AI across more workflows without having to make really tough tradeoffs around cost.

I’m glad we fast followed it with GPT-6.1 Sol, and there were absolutely lessons to learn from that launch, but the echo chamber of twitter felt so vast that week.

Announcing 3 Critical vulns for hundreds of millions of IoT, Firewalls, OT, and Military devices including: Palo Alto Networks, Comcast, D-Link, HP, Canon, Honeywell, GE, Oracle, Siemens, Rockwell, Digi, Lockheed Martin, Boeing... 

The vulns are with GoAhead Web Server which is a backend library used by these devices. There's a patch available from GoAhead but that doesn't mean there's a patch available for the devices yet -- that's up to the manufacturer.

- TLS traffic over DHE ciphers have a 1-byte secret, "04", meaning anyone can decrypt connections to these devices and steal login credentials and session tokens if the client negotiated with DHE ciphers like the latest TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, which is extremely likely.

- LibreSSL mTLS has been completely bypassed, meaning anyone can connect over mTLS. If you have one of these devices listening on the internet and are expecting mTLS to protect it from attackers, take it offline or patch asap.

- OpenSSL Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) are not enforced, meaning if a user device is stolen or compromised, and you revoke that mTLS cert, nothing actually happens. There are a lot of other attacks this can be used for.

These are critical because these types of devices run our world. Water systems, electricity, military, firewalls, critical infrastructure.

author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
Onchain lending vaults went from $1.5B to $10B in two years.

Meanwhile, actively managed onchain trading vaults are at roughly zero.

Not for lack of demand. You just couldn't run a real hedge fund book on one onchain venue. Hyperliquid fixed that this year, and @Infinit_Labs is the first team I've seen build the actual fund wrapper around it.

So I pulled the full trading wallet of their first vault and rebuilt it day by day, across 340 fills, incl. every funding payment and the daily marks.

Here's what I found:

Why HL, why now?

CTA momentum is the oldest strategy in managed futures. Rank markets by relative strength, long the top, short the bottom, across stocks, commodities and crypto. Dollar neutral, so the return comes from selection, not direction.

It only works if all three asset classes sit on one margin account tho. Until HIP-3 came to Hyperliquid, that didn't exist onchain.

Today 23 HL markets clear INFINIT's $100M open interest floor. 10 are crypto. 13 are stocks, indices and commodities (S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, Gold, Silver, Brent, WTI, SK Hynix, MU, SPCX, GOOGL, META and a few more).

That means: One venue, 24/7, one margin system, and this universe is why a cross-asset vault can exist now and couldn't 12 months ago.

Simultaneously, the rapid advances in AI play a similarly crucial role.

Not for the signals tho. Relative-strength ranking with systematic entries and exits is quant, not some sort of agentic magic, and Apex says so themselves.

Yet, AI is the ops layer, and that's another crucial part worth paying attention to:

- Trading credentials can open and close positions but can't withdraw. Deposits sit behind a 3-of-4 multisig and the manager holds none of the signing keys, so a manager's key can never block withdrawals.

- A trade gateway sits in front of the exchange. Any order outside the eligible list or the declared limits gets blocked before it lands.

- Monitoring agents check live trading against the manager's published mandate. Breaches go to a human risk team, unresolved ones pause trading access.

- Share accounting and investor reporting run on the same stack.

That's pretty much the middle office of a fund, running almost fully autonomously, and it's the reason a $500K vault can be run with institutional process at all, and the reason MS2 can take more capital without hiring ten people.

So, what does the wallet (and onchain data) say?

APEX MS1, operated by Apex Quant Capital had $506K deposited on the 3rd of August and its first fill on the 10th of August.

The overall return is about 40% annualized as of today, +8.4% actual over 78 days, before vault fees. The peak was +8.5% on the 23rd of October, and Apex reports roughly 40% annualized after fees through September, which lines up.

A few more stats:

- The worst drawdown was (only) 3.7%, all of it in the first week.

- Dollar neutral in practice, not just on paper. Net exposure averaged 1% of gross across 70 active days, with 7.5% on the worst day. Right now it's $143K long vs $131K short.

- 1x isolated on every position, every day. Gross exposure peaked at 1.04x capital.

- Ten equal position slots of about $45K at launch, roughly 9% of capital per market.

- The book went fully to cash twice when the signal had nothing. "Holds cash when conditions aren't right" is actually part of the strategy, not just marketing.

- 20 markets traded with $12M volume, $2.2K fees paid, and $3.1K funding received.

Current book, in case you're curious (on the 26th of October): long S&P 500 against short ETH, SOL, XRP, HYPE and ZEC.

So what does that mean?

Eleven weeks in, neutrality, leverage, market eligibility and cash discipline all check out onchain, and the two numbers Apex publishes match the wallet.

The PnL split is what you’d expect from a momentum book in this tape. Crypto had the trends and made the money, SOL, ZEC and HYPE about $57K net. Single stocks chopped and the stops gave back about $25K. Indices flat, commodities about +$13K in October on Brent, Gold and WTI.

Losers cut, winners left to run. And the trend is now moving into commodities, with the book flipped long the S&P. That’s the whole point of a cross-asset book. MS1 got a first taste in October, MS2 is where it gets tested properly.

Wen MS2?

Deposits open on the 28th of October until the 11th of November, and I'm looking to deposit too.

Why?

Bc a fund-structured vault with public fills, trade-only keys and a manager putting up first-loss capital for APEX 1 and 2 is the first version of this I'd actually put money in.

This is likely the model the next wave of onchain asset management gets built on, and it's live on HL right now.

What I'll be watching?

- Fee terms and the size of Apex's first-loss commitment
- Whether the stock and commodity legs keep contributing
- How the strategy behaves at size ($500K is a pilot and the real capacity test is more capital in the same 23 markets)

NFA tho ofc.
