quoted_text:
Surprise 1: Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech
.
.
.
Surprise 2: that person is me
Surprise 3: I’m here to tell you all about it

Yes, this is what you think it is; after 6 yrs of increasingly loose anonymity: the Professor Oak reveal post

…and yes, it has gotten so boring around here that I’m literally doxxing myself to spice up the timeline

-------
Ok, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Cody Tranbarger. I mostly tweet, but occasionally find time to dabble in drug dev & starting/building biotechs. My past lives span the VC, crossover, startup continuum; Prof Oak has been my way of keeping a digital foot in those worlds, despite having my physical feet planted elsewhere.

The past 18 mo, ‘elsewhere’ was Mithril Medicine, a co. I founded to develop bsAbs for LAMA2-CMD & other ECM-related genetic diseases.

Mithril was born out of hands-on building with @MikeNGladstone, @JasonPaulRhodes, @LifeSciVC, & team @atlasventure. Somehow, I made enough half-decent calls along the way (even a broken clock is right twice a day, eh?) to convince them Mithril/I warranted a small seed. While I can hardly rationalize such an outrageously cavalier bet, I’m grateful for it, & I'd partner with Atlas again in a heartbeat.

In typical AV fashion, Mithril’s primordial form was virtual, decentralized, & ultra-lean. This stage tends to be short-lived, but for Mithril, it worked surprisingly well, for surprisingly long, thanks in part to the rapid maturation of the AI tools I used liberally.

Eventually, Mithril became a bit of an experiment itself - to find the upper bound of how far it could scale as a single operator + a bunch of Claude (+ a stellar bench of part-time consultants).

In parallel, I started spending time with @nc_frey, @an1lam, & @CoefficientBio team; and promptly experienced, for the 1st time, AI at the frontier. Soon thereafter, Mithril stopped looking like an experiment, & started looking like a preview of an entirely new operating model.

From that spark came “Pipeline-in-a-Person.” The idea immediately resonated when we shared it here back in April; and it was central to the shared vision that led to Anthropic’s acquisition of Mithril, & my joining the team.

Why join Anthropic? Three reasons.
(1) For Mithril, the programs continue, with more resources & infrastructure behind them, and as much Claude as I can put to work.

(2) For me, the chance to start several more programs, & find out how many one person can actually run in parallel - an almost unprecedented luxury for a curious drug hunter.

(3) For our mission, a path to institutionalize & scale this new way of working, then put it in the hands of all of biopharma, all over the world - which, candidly, I find the most energizing.

Will AI x Bio cure diseases? Unequivocally yes, imo… but not by the route that gets the most airtime. Rather than timeline acceleration & compression, I see orchestration & parallelization as today's low-hanging fruit.

Most drug hunters see a handful of go/no-go calls in a career, & spend entirely too much of the rest trading emails (my inbox can attest).

Give them the bandwidth to run several programs at once, and the time to focus on scientific judgment, and I’m willing to bet they’ll make better calls. And at scale, better calls translate to more drugs, higher hit rates, broader patient impact, & likely, a disease or 10 or 100 cured. I couldn't be more excited to build toward that future @AnthropicAI.

Finally, a heartfelt thank you to BioTwitter/X. The end of anonymity is bittersweet, but if anyone’s earned a proper introduction, you all have.

It’s difficult to overstate how much this app has done for me: a decade of education, plenty of friends, many job opportunities, several mentors, a few investors, even a co-founder (fmr). It was the generosity of this community that inspired me to start posting 6 years ago, after just as many years lurking. I hope I’ve been able to pay it forward, in my own small way.

But, to be clear, Prof Oak isn’t going anywhere. Same beat, same themes, and now, a front-row seat to drug development at the frontier. Stay tuned for dispatches from the trenches; and remember...

Gotta Cure 'Em All

text:
AI 横行，大家更焦虑了。

打工怕被裁，创业怕被 AI 新功能直接卷掉，大家都在拼命刷新自己的能力模型，试图跟上版本节奏。

那现在什么样的人更受青睐呢？ 

a16z 合伙人 Andrew Chen 的这篇长文值得一读，他认为以前默认要“技术 + 商业”双创始人，现在 AI 给了单人百倍杠杆，一批以前很难被 VC 认真看的人，突然能站上牌桌。

他列出了几种正在出现的新画像，看看你属于哪一类：

1. 独立创始人（Solo Founders）

AI 让一个人就能做到以前团队才能做的事，一个人先把 v1 做出来已经不是幻想。大家喜欢这种画像，是因为它看起来极致杠杆、极致自由，一个人就能把产品推到能验证的阶段。
但客户会议、销售、推进业务这些事，一个人再强也容易搞不定。有的时候一个三人小团队的战斗力，可能比一个单人 10 倍杠杆更强。

2. 非技术背景创始人

金融、咨询出来的精英，或者本身就在创意行业整天做创作的人，现在不用再找技术合伙人，自己就能把产品做出来。这类人以前被挡在门外，现在突然能进场，所以很多人觉得兴奋。

但问题也在这里。从 demo 到能规模化、稳定服务大量用户的产品，中间还有巨大鸿沟。
当谁都能快速做出第一版时，真正稀缺的反而变成了技术判断力，比如什么该做、什么做不了、怎么持续领先。

3. 垂直领域专家

医生、房产经纪人、老师、甚至军人……他们每天都在自己的行业里撞痛点。大家喜欢这类人，因为“懂行”本身就是护城河。
但历史经验也在提醒，传统酒店人没做出 Airbnb，传统金融人也没做出 Kalshi。
有时候你需要的是局外人视角，才能把整个行业重做一遍，而不是在原有框架里做渐进改良。

4. 青少年 / 学生

他们早就在做 Minecraft 模组、Roblox 游戏、Discord 机器人，本来就在练“做东西给别人用”的能力。

AI 把这个过程进一步放大，年纪更小就能做出以前做不出来的东西。这类画像自带敏捷和新鲜感，也更懂同龄人在用什么。

但做朋友喜欢的小东西，和真正运营一家公司是两回事。招人、融资、管理、变现这些事不会因为你会用 AI 就消失。而且一旦进入企业软件、医疗这些更依赖行业经验和人脉的领域，年龄优势会迅速消失。

5. 内容创作者 / 网红

他们本来就在持续创作，而且自带分发渠道，知道粉丝在乎什么、怎么抓住注意力、怎么零广告触达用户。

但粉丝流量更多是爆发式的，真正值钱的软件产品通常是需要长期迭代、持续打磨的马拉松。创作者的 DNA 能不能适应这种长跑，还是未知数。

所以，看起来机会变多了，但是每一种画像的人都面临着自己的问题。AI 是技能的放大器，但过度依赖 AI，也是弱点的放大器。

New essay:
https://t.co/Tm7eYpIXxs

NEW FOUNDER ARCHETYPES IN THE AI AGE

Solo founders
- Why: Solo founders can do 100x with AI, so they can ship a v1 when previously they couldn’t have before
- Why not: Maybe a team of cofounders still makes more progress. Maybe you can agentically code but someone still needs to do a million meetings with customers. Maybe coding was never the main bottleneck for startups in the first place?

Non-technical founders
- Why: There’s elite talent that comes from areas like finance, consulting, who can’t code but are passionate about business. There’s also folks in creative industries who create all day but just not in code. Now they can build
- Why not: Why not: Maybe AI makes it easier to build a prototype, but there’s still a big gap between a demo and a reliable product that can scale. If everyone can build the first version, maybe technical judgment becomes more important in deciding what to build, what’s actually possible, and how to stay ahead as the product gets more complex. (especially true for product categories like dev tools/etc)

Domain experts
- Why: A doctor who works at a hospital understands all the problems they face each day. A real estate broker really gets the subtleties of their markets, their clients. Same with a soldier, teacher, etc. What if they could use software to solve their own problems and build business along the way?
- Why not: Hoteliers didn’t create Airbnb and the finance industry didn’t create Kalshi. Sometimes you just need an outsider’s view in order to reinvent an industry, versus building incremental improvements

Kids, high schoolers, college students
- Why: Young people have already been building products early on. Start with a Minecraft mod, a Roblox game, a Discord bot, and suddenly you’ve learned how to make something that thousands of other people use. Now add AI, and a kid with an idea can build way more, way earlier
- Why not: Building something your friends love is very different from building a company. You still have to hire, raise money, manage people, and figure out how to make money. And maybe young founders have an advantage in consumer products because they understand their peers, but much less of one when it comes to enterprise software, healthcare, or other industries where experience and relationships really matter. Sometimes you just need domain expertise

Content creators
- Why: They’re already creating. So instead of creating videos, maybe the same skills can go into creating software. Plus, they have distribution. They know what their followers care about, how to get their attention, and how to reach them without paying for ads. In the past, turning that audience into a software product meant finding a technical cofounder or hiring a team. Now a creator could build and launch something themselves, and immediately put it in front of millions of potential users.
- Why not: Having followers helps with a spike of distribution, but building a sustainable growth engine is something else. The most valuable products aren’t memes - they are long-running, long-growing products that need to be endlessly tweaked and iterated on. Does the DNA work?

What makes a blockchain important in global finance?

It isn't just the number of transactions it processes or the value of its native token. It's also how effectively people use it to move, hold, and transfer value.

That's why TRON's reported 50.7% share of the total USDT supply deserves attention.

This figure points to something bigger than a market statistic: the growing importance of blockchain infrastructure in the movement of digital dollars.

🔴 1. Stablecoin Supply Is Only The Beginning

USDT is designed to maintain a value close to the US dollar, making it useful for trading, payments, transfers, and storing dollar-denominated value.

When a substantial share of its circulating supply exists on one blockchain, that network becomes an important part of the infrastructure supporting those activities.

TRON's reported 50.7% share highlights its significant position in the USDT ecosystem.

🔴 2. Supply And Transaction Volume Tell Different Stories

Here's an important distinction.

Supply measures where tokens exist. Volume measures how much value moves.

A network can hold a large share of USDT without necessarily processing the same share of all USDT transfers.

To understand TRON's actual role in global stablecoin activity, both metrics matter, alongside transaction frequency, fees, liquidity, and real-world use cases.

This is where deeper analysis becomes more valuable than a headline percentage alone.

🔴 3. Why This Matters For Global Payments

Stablecoins are increasingly relevant to how people and businesses think about digital dollar transfers.

For users who need to move value across borders, the practical questions are straightforward:

• How much does a transfer cost?
• How quickly does it settle?
• Is liquidity readily available?
• Can recipients access and use the funds easily?

A blockchain's long-term relevance depends on how effectively its infrastructure addresses these needs.

🔴 4. The Bigger Picture For TRON

TRON's position in USDT supply suggests that it plays a major role in the stablecoin landscape.

But maintaining that position over time requires more than supply concentration. Reliability, security, liquidity, accessibility, and sustained user demand will continue to matter.

The real competition in blockchain finance isn't simply about which network holds the most tokens. It's about which networks people consistently rely on to move value.

If 50.7% of USDT supply is on TRON, what do you think matters most for its next stage of growth: deeper liquidity, cheaper transfers, greater merchant adoption, or stronger institutional use?

I'd like to hear the community's perspective.

我过去应该算比特币最大的多头，但是现在没那么狂热了。

比特币最初的愿景，是建立一套不依赖传统金融机构的点对点电子现金系统。

而事实证明，它确实成功了。

尤其是当年的小区块路线之争，虽然限制了比特币的扩展能力，却也让它得以坚持去中心化，逐渐形成了今天数字黄金的共识。

但问题也恰恰出在这里。

比特币能摆脱旧体系，但不代表它有能力建立新体系。

比特币解决了一个非常重要的问题：如何让人们在不依赖银行和政府信用的情况下，自由地持有和转移自己的财富。

但它没有在基础层上解决另一个更重要的问题：如何在去中心化的基础上，重新建立一整套经济秩序？

尤其是在AI时代，这种局限性正在变得越来越明显。

未来的Agent，可能不再只是帮助人类转账，而是能够自主完成交易、借贷、抵押、投资和清算。股票、债券乃至各种现实资产，都可能成为链上可编程的金融工具。

那时，人们真正需要的，或许不再只是一种不受中心化机构控制的货币，而是一套不依赖中心化机构也能自由运转的金融体系。

过去，去中心化解决的是谁能控制我的钱；未来，去中心化要解决的，是谁有权制定和执行经济活动的规则。

这才是我认为AI与区块链结合后，真正可能爆发的革命。

当然，比特币依然可以成为数字黄金，就像黄金无法承载现代金融系统，却依然拥有自己的价值一样。

但问题在于，数字黄金的成功，是否就等于去中心化革命的成功？我对此非常怀疑。

或许比特币最大的历史贡献，就是证明了人类可以在没有中心化信用机构的情况下建立价值共识。

但证明一条道路可以走通，与真正沿着这条道路建立一个新世界，是两回事。

电子现金可以是去中心化革命的起点，却未必能成为去中心化经济的终点。

text:
YC最新的一期Request for Startups 创业公司招募方向今天发布了，有11个方向是他们接下来最关注的：

1. 太空应用：火箭发射很快会便宜很多。今天还亏钱的太空生意，到时候可能就能成立，所以现在值得提前做。

2. AI 赋能普通人：找聪明、但不一定有专业执照的人，配上 AI，去做并购咨询、医保报销、移民材料这类过去只能靠专家干的活。

3. 美国本土机器人产业链：机器人软件进步很快，但是硬件很拉。美国现在大量依赖进口，稀土磁体还被卡脖子，所以要在美国本地做机器人和关键零部件。

4. 文风更好的大模型：大厂为了把模型练得会写代码、会当 agent，把文字风格练得很死板。专门做「写得像人、聊起来舒服」的模型，反而有机会。

5. 政府福利核验基础设施：申福利要反复交收入、住址证明，每个部门各审一遍，又慢又容易造假。做成类似 Plaid 的一层：用户授权后，从源头拉真实数据，一次核验、多个项目通用。

6. 实体 AI 基建的融资系统：建机器人、GPU 集群、数据中心要先砸大钱，银行却还按传统设备贷款来审。需要专门做租赁、贷款、证券化、风险对冲的金融公司。

6. 行业专用基础模型：做一个只服务制造、能源或生物等垂直领域的模型。目标是：算力成本远低于通用大模型，专业任务上却不输甚至更好。

7. 地方政府审批 AI：盖房、开公司都要过市政府审批，很多活还是人肉对照图纸和法规。用 AI 处理许可、zoning、投诉、检查，审批更快，项目更容易落地。

8. 数据中心供应链：AI 数据中心在大规模建设，缺的不只是芯片和电，还有变压器、开关柜、液冷设备、特种钢材。谁能补上这些缺口，谁就能赚钱。

9. 内网 / 断网可用的 AI：国防、银行、医院的核心数据不能上公有云。要卖能在客户机房、甚至断网环境里跑的模型、部署工具和安全认证。

10. 企业自有模型能力：开源模型已经够强，很多公司不想永远向 OpenAI 这类公司租接口。帮企业用自己的数据和业务流程，把模型训成自己的、并能持续改进。

⚠️注意：冒充fomo最高盈利10M+聪明钱的假号要开始收割了

@DumbCrayonEater  这个号已经被我实锤是冒充的假号，目前他在推荐这个项目 Alpha AI @AlphaAiLabs ，然后我逆向了 Alpha AI 及其内置交易终端 Striker 的源码，发现几个严重问题：

一、宣传“全网实时交易数据”，实际是主站首页靠定时器伪造

官方在首页显著展示“Live 实时构建 1,132 个智能层、实时成交 532 万美元、实时撮合 12,834 笔”

 我逆向主站前端源码后发现，这组数据底层完全是写死在 HTML 里的静态数字，通过 JavaScript 定时器每隔 3 到 7 秒自动随机累加，根本没有连接链上真实的实时数据，纯粹是用前端动画伪造全网高频交易的假象

二、宣传 68.4% 超高胜率，实际排除了所有浮亏持仓

官方宣传其用户月度盈利胜率高达 68.4%（行业均值仅 25.3%）

但主站底部的隐藏条款明确写着：Unsold bags are not counted。这意味着用户买入后亏损甚至归零的代币，只要不平仓卖出，系统就一律不计入亏损，只计算卖出且盈利的订单

三、产品宣称“AES-256 私钥非托管”，实际由服务器代管且出事完全免责

官方宣传私钥加密且资产非托管。但由于其采用 Telegram 机器人交易，私钥生成、解密与签名广播全部在项目方的云端服务器完成

其服务条款明文写着：If your credentials or keys are lost or compromised, we may be unable to help you recover assets，且仲裁管辖地还是未填写的模板占位符 [arbitration seat]，一旦资产丢失用户无处追责

项目完全匿名，私钥由项目方云端掌控，存入大额资金存在极高的安全与跑路风险

最搞笑的是，你这个小小诈骗犯@DumbCrayonEater  把 solana:3wtGGWZ8wLWW6BqtC5rxmkHdqvM62atUcGTH4cw3pump从7M喊到4M，还天天洗脑让人买，你怎么不梭哈进去，傻逼

text:
才发现Anthropic收购的AI医疗公司Mithril Medicine是一家非常典型的“一人公司”，创始人Cody Tranbarger也只有他这一个全职员工。Mithril Medicine没有实验室、没有研发团队，甚至没有传统意义上的办公室，核心就是创始人自己加上一群外部顾问和十多家合同实验室，把药物开发这件事硬生生推进到了小鼠实验阶段。

查了下创始人Cody的背景也并不算传统科学家路线，他本科在Amherst 读生物和经济学，后来在哈佛读了生物技术方向的 MS/MBA。职业生涯从高盛医疗投行开始，之后到 Casdin Capital 做基因药物投资，再转到 Prime Medicine 负责商务拓展，后来又在 Atlas Venture 做 Entrepreneur-in-Residence，同时自己创办了另一家基因写入公司 Revision Bio。他还长期在 Cure Rare Disease 当董事，对罕见病和个性化治疗一直有兴趣。

这些经历让他既懂怎么判断一个项目值不值得做，也懂怎么跟实验室、CRO 和投资人打交道。

Mithril 的做法很直白：自己不养湿实验室，把抗体生产、细胞实验、小鼠研究全部外包给外部机构。Cody 一个人负责定方向、做决策、盯进度、改方案。日常大量的合同沟通、数据整理、实验计划调整、邮件来回，都靠 Claude 帮忙处理。

公司自己把这种模式叫做“Pipeline-in-a-Person”——一个人扛着整条管道往前走，判断留在人手里，执行层面尽量交给工具和外部合作方。

项目本身瞄准的是两种罕见的儿童肌营养不良症，主要用双特异性抗体的思路，试图把肌肉里残留的蛋白和肌纤维重新“桥接”起来。从立项到拿到小鼠上比较积极的结果，大概用了不到 18 个月。小鼠实验规模不大，方法上也有局限（没有完全随机、测试时间不统一等），技术报告也还没经过同行评审，但至少证明了这种极简团队加外部协作的模式，在早期探索阶段是能跑起来的。

今年7 月，Anthropic收购了Mithril Medicine。对 Anthropic 来说，它既拿到了具体的药物项目，也拿到了一个真实的案例：一个人怎么用 AI 把多实验室的协调和日常运营压到可管理的程度。

本质上，Mithril 不是靠技术平台或庞大团队起家的，而是靠创始人自身的判断力、行业经验和愿意把大量执行工作外包、交给工具的方式，把一家药物公司从零跑到了有小鼠数据的阶段。这种模式在生物医药领域并不常见，但也正因为它足够极端，才成为后来被收购的原因之一。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
大模型Labs垂直化趋势，上周OpenAI刚刚宣布收购了Orchestra Bio（这是一家帮助生物制药团队协调药物开发复杂流程的AI平台），收购后将与OpenAI的Rosalind生命科学AI工具结合，目标是简化操作，让新治疗方法更快到达患者手中。

今天Anthropic 宣布与六家机构（BigHat Biosciences、Bristol Myers Squibb、Divergence Labs、Enveda、Generate Biomedicines、The Column Group）深度合作，利用Claude在抗体设计、CAR-T疗法优化、制造文件审核和临床试验规划等环节加速药物开发，取得显著的早期成果例如抗体结合力提升10倍以上、文件审核时间减少89%、生成3.5万种抗体设计等。

并且Anthropic还宣布收购Mithril Medicine并启动自身药物发现项目，针对罕见儿童肌营养不良症，从概念到小鼠实验阳性结果仅用不到18个月，Claude承担大量科学与运营工作，展示AI在完整药物研发流程中的潜力。

从产业的角度上看，OpenAI、Anthropic、Isomorphic/DeepMind、ByteDance系大模型等都在深化生命科学布局、在医疗医药生命科学领域的垂直化趋势愈发明显。大模型都开是自己在做这方面的工作，从模型开始介入到具体工作流了。

投资上看AIDD、Ai-Bio应该还有很大的机会、巨头们纷纷扎堆不是来凑热闹，更多的还是看到了巨大突破的可能性。

内塔尼亚胡大选暂时领先，但是依旧难以达到61的组阁数据，阿拉伯政党可能会成为最为关键的群体！

凌晨4点以色列大选截止，出口民调显示艾森科特支持率高于内塔尼亚胡，但是28日今天的实际票数统计中，结果截然相反

截止目前，大选统计票数已经完成89%，而根据目前的投票结果来看，内塔尼亚胡的利库德党依旧是议会第一大党，但是这并不意味着内塔尼亚胡可以顺利坐稳总理职位

本次大选内塔尼亚胡阵营（利库德党）约54席，艾森科特阵营约48席位，阿拉伯政党18席位，也就是说，但看内塔尼亚胡与艾森科特各自支持政党席位来看，谁都无法完成61席位的组阁，所以关键就看阿拉伯政党的18个席位支持谁。

根据目前票选席位来看，新的组阁是绕不来阿拉伯政党，但是内塔尼亚胡此前表示希望建立一个强大的民族右翼政府，基本排除了与阿拉伯政党合作的组阁的可能性

艾森科特倒是可以与阿拉伯政党组阁，但是必然也要付出极大的政治代价，其政治成本极高

以色列总理的选举机制不是看谁第一，而是看谁能联合各方政党完成61席位的组阁，谁有希望，总统才会下命令组阁，组阁成功的人才是下一任以色列总理

接下来，一方面要看最终票选完成，依旧后续的“双信封”选票是否可以推动内塔尼亚胡支持阵营获得61个席位，然后还要关注内塔尼亚胡是否开始积极的联合阿拉伯政党组阁，这都是奠定胜选基础核心条件

其实目前来看，我认为最优选的就是内塔尼亚胡与阿拉伯政党联合组阁，这样避免了一个右翼的以色列议会，同时阿拉伯政党可以变相的制约内塔尼亚胡，这样对中东地区稳定，美伊战争都是一件好事，毕竟阿拉伯政党代表的是以色列阿拉伯人民的意志，可以有效约束内塔尼亚胡疯狂扩张的军事野心！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
北京时间10月28日凌晨4点是以色列大选投票截止时间，本次投票已经刷新了以色列50年以来的最高速度，显然选举过程在被“刻意”加速

投票时间以北京时间计算：

10月28日凌晨4点投票截止，媒体公布出口民调，人工计票
10月28日上午-下午，实际票数陆续上传，开始出现真实得票率和席位推算
10月29日-30日，普通票+双信封票等特殊票基本完成，席位机构高度确定
最迟11月4日，中央选举委员会公布正式结果

按照这个大选时间来看，最晚基本上在北京时间10月30日就可以推算出内塔尼亚胡胜选概率，甚至时间上可能会更早

接下来关注重点是从明天10月28日白天开始，通过三个阶段可以分析出内塔尼亚胡的胜选概率

1,28日凌晨4点的出口民调，内塔尼亚胡是否可以达到61席位，以色列议会总共120票席61票意味着多数票

2，28日上午到下午，真实票数被统计，该统计数据将会逐步代替出口民调数据，要看内塔尼亚胡阵营可以拿到什么票数区间，

如果稳定大于61票，基本奠定胜利，
60-61则是轻度危险，
57-59难以组阁，但是不能宣布彻底失败，有斡旋空间，
≤56票组阁大概率失败

这里简单说一下以色列议会机制，总理有组阁权，但是一旦阵营组阁失败就要给到下一位议员来组阁，如果两人都失败议会会制定给某个议员，如果三次都失败则意味着选举失败，重新根据选举法调整。所以初步的组阁失败不能绝对判定内塔尼亚胡败选

3,10月29日-30日，这是包含军人、囚犯、住院人员以及其他不在登记投票站投票的所谓的“爽信封票”需要统计，而这批票可能直接影响选举的边缘席位，很有可能成为关键票。

所以按照目前以色列的选举逻辑，参考美伊局势的可能缓和时间节点，那么最大的转折点可能要放在10月28日甚至29日阶段，这个阶段一旦内塔尼亚胡拿到决定性的胜选结果，我认为可能会是特朗普迅速调整策略促成美伊缓和的关键节点。

text:
假如把我的 AI Coding 经验沉淀成一些最佳实践规则，可以给到大伙复用，会是怎么样的，于是乎，今天一下午我就在琢磨这个事情，手写反复调整后给到大伙，可以让你和你的 Agent 一起去学习。

需求
1.  从技术实现细节编程转变成许愿式编程，现在模型能力已经住足够强大，你只需要大胆把自己想法说出来，给它提足够高的要求和任务，不要担心 AI 实现不了。
2. 多给你的 Agent  讲做这件事情的背景和目标，少替他考虑技术细节，告诉它为什么要做，是给谁用的，做成什么样子你认为是最好的，具体的技术细节让它自己去判断，学会放手。
3. 优先用业界最好的模型，用差模型浪费的时候，一来回让你很不高兴的干活，二来也浪费了很多时间。
4. 要不要做一个新功能以及加一个新配置、开关的时候，让 Agent 来先问你找你确定，没有人用的功能、开关、文案都不要让他去加，慢慢把这一套你的产品规范让他沉淀起来。
5. 你的想法可以很大，但是让 Agent 干活的时候，尽量让他每次拆分成最小的可用功能版本，不要一次写非常多的代码，即使提交，这样出问题了你可以随时撤回。

规则                                                                                                                                                            
6. 让你的 Agent 了解你的说话风格，比如说看看、分析一下这个问题的时候，它只需要去读代码分析问题不要去改代码，你说修复、修改的时候才去动手，每次提交、发布和删除的时候都找你确定。                                                                        
7. Agent md、CLAUDE md 里面除去重点的项目型要求外，只写代码里面看不出来的那种规则，以及之前被否决过的方案也可以分流进去。对你而言密钥和 token 不要贴给 Agent，贴了就当已经泄露了，立马去更换一个。
8. 对于Agent必须遵守的规则不要完全信 prompt，可能会拦不住，一定要用规则脚本去限制，让它真实跑一遍通过后才算完成了。

编码
9. 开始写代码之前，先让 Agent 讲清楚要改什么地方，会影响到什么功能和效果，这样是为了补充你的上下文，方便后面更好判断决策做什么。
10. 一定要让 Agent 基于项目补充一个能够让自己验证各种结果的脚本，每次特定的时候需要去跑一下验证效果，完成功能后需要检查，让他输出结果给你看，并基于此逐步沉淀你的项目 Agent 测试功能集。
11. 假如有多个 Agent 同时干活的时候，让他们各自用一份独立的 worktree 代码目录，同时提交的时候只提交自己改的代码，不要碰他人的代码，等到各自改完合到一起，再完整跑一遍测试。
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
排查
12. 修 Bug 的时候先找到原因再去动手，假如两次都没有修好，就去加一些日志看真实的数据以及运行效果，不要盲目去猜问题在哪儿。
13. 假如尝试修复了3次还不对，直接清空上下文重新写清楚你的问题、诉求，以及尝试过的解法让 Agent 重新开始。                                                        

审查                                                                                                                                                     
14. 让写代码的 Agent 和 Review 审查代码的 Agent 分开，保持解耦，这样一方不会被另一方带偏。
15. Review 代码的时候最多让 Agent 跑 3轮，防止跑着停不下来，第二轮开始只看新改动的地方，不要再把之前 Review 的再看一遍。                                                                                                                   
16. 对于你和 Agent 判断危险的改动，越危险让他查得越深，特别对于删除、付费、发布这种单向门改动你都需要自己去看一遍，点一下，看实际效果。                                                                                                                                                                           

发布
17. 每次提交的时候，让Agent 写清楚做了什么，怎么去验证这个改动，除了问题怎么来回滚，用于给到后面开发过程中 git 记录本身就是 Agent 的一个非常好的上下文。
18. 需要对外的功能，可以先给自己用，或者给一批愿意尝鲜的用户使用，不要一上来就全量，可以在你的软件里面假如 beta 更新的开关，防止全量有问题，也是对用户负责。
18. 先给自己和愿意尝鲜的人用，没问题再发给所有人。                                                                                                              

复盘
19.  Agent 需要对每一个线上 Bug 和用户反馈的问题都留一个测试案例，每次上线前都来跑一遍，防止继续踩坑，包括你换模型的时候也可以把这些旧问题全部都跑一遍，看看模型是否还行。
20. 修复问题的时候，让 Agent 学会举一反三，把同类的问题一起修复掉。优化功能的功能，完善视觉的时候也是一样，防止只改一个地方，忘记了其他的地方。

text:
A few hours ago, a USDC tranche vault on Avalanche lost ~$1M due to inconsistent principal accounting in the fund-user claim path.

The vault has two roles: the fund provider, who deposits and withdraws principal, and the fund user, who borrows funds from the tranche and is responsible for repaying them. The attacker controlled both roles within the same tranche, allowing them to deposit funds as the provider and immediately borrow them as the user.

The claim function deducted borrowed but unmatured principal from total deposits, but ignored matured yet unrepaid principal. When the attacker claimed again after maturity, the function first processed maturity records using the current timestamp, moving the previously borrowed principal into the matured balance, then checked the available amount. Because the calculation omitted the matured balance, it incorrectly restored the full borrowing allowance, even though nothing had been repaid.

Flawed formula:
Available = Total deposited − Borrowed, not yet matured

Correct formula:
Available = Total deposited − Borrowed, not yet matured − Matured, not yet repaid

The fund-provider withdrawal function correctly deducts both balances, while the fund-user claim function omits matured but unrepaid principal.

Key attack steps:
1. The attacker created a tranche with the same address as both fund provider and fund user, setting its maturity shortly afterward.
2. Using an Aave flash loan, the attacker deposited 1,013,353.61 USDC as the fund provider, then borrowed the entire principal as the fund user in the same transaction. They used those funds to repay the flash loan, paying a 506.68 USDC fee.
3. After 163 blocks, once maturity had passed, the attacker called claim again. The incorrectly restored allowance let them borrow another 1,013,353.61 USDC without repaying the first tranche loan or making a new deposit.

The second borrowing was funded by other users’ principal deposits in the vault.

Attack TX: https://t.co/02SYQyyGqC

text:
Your coding agents forget what the last one did. A new CLI called agentlog is built to fix that.

It lets one agent search another's past session logs from Claude Code, Codex or GitHub Copilot CLI, by directory, session ID, time or task words, and returns a bounded preview with follow-up commands for edits, subagents or grep.

Per the README: it never writes to or deletes logs, makes no network connections, and has no dependencies. Those are the author's claims; I haven't audited the code.

Caveats: it was built mainly on macOS, Linux is untested on real logs, broad reads can cost tens of thousands of tokens, and logs can contain secrets, so output should be treated as data. Install is a curl-to-shell script (or go install); read it first.

Apache-2.0, created Oct 27.

投资这么多年，有两类东西，我越来越觉得像骗局，人类思维的陷阱。

一个是长期拿着杠杆ETF，比如TQQQ。类似7709这种产品，我也是最早喷、并且一路喷到底的。

另一个是买入主动管理型基金。

我现在越来越觉得，技术分析、宏观判断、行业轮动，一切的一切主观认知，到最后都像随机数。讲得头头是道，真下场也未必比扔硬币强多少，管理费倒是年年收。

马上又到了Robinhood公布财报的日子了。期权市场隐含财报后波动约 10.2%（历史模型口径约 8.1%）——说明市场本身就在定价“大动”。

上季度（Q2 2026） 是 Robinhood 上市以来最强季度之一：
营收 $1.308B（同比 +32%），超预期的 $1.287B；稀释 EPS $0.62，大幅超出 $0.43 的一致预期。
交易收入 $776M（+44%）：事件合约 $156M（增逾 10 倍，合约数达创纪录的 136 亿张）、期权 $342M（+29%）、股票 $129M（+95%）、加密 $100M（-38%）。

但是财报公布后仍然下跌。事实上，近三季财报次日股价分别下跌 -3.6%、-13.2%、-8.9%——“beat 但 sell off”已成惯性。
那这次的财报会怎么样？如果beat都是sell off，那不及预期不是完辣？

市场对于财报预期的一些核心数字：
营收 $1.44B；同比 +$12.9%，若达标将创单季新高
分项预期：期权收入约 $4.0 亿（同比 +31.5%）、股票收入约 $1.33 亿（+54.7%）、加密货币收入约 $1.19 亿（同比降约 56%）、净利息收入约 $4.31 亿。

本季财报我的关注点：
1️⃣预测市场/事件合约的持续性：
Q2有世界杯，因此给预测市场带来了巨大的增量。事件合约收入 $1.56 亿、同比增逾 10 倍。那世界杯结束之后呢？这种规模能够持续么？11 月 3 日就是美国中期选举。这部分的增量是否可以保持预测市场的增长。

2️⃣加密业务与股票的对冲效应：
很不幸的是，Q3以来的加密或者是股市其实都走的不理想。那这样的行情下，贡献主要收入的交易费用会如何表现？个人觉得不太乐观。

Timestral is a new family of open-source time series foundation models that just set a new state of the art in probabilistic forecasting.

Four sizes (5M–209M params), all on the accuracy/size Pareto front across GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench. The 209M and 123M models take the top two spots on every metric—beating models up to 90x larger.

Key ingredients:
— Decoupled Horizon Forecasting: leverages all observed values for multi-horizon forecasts without masking tricks
— Role-aware covariate handling: natively supports known-future variables (like weather)
— Massive synthetic pretraining, short real+synthetic post-training, 4x longer context

Single-pass inference up to 1,024 steps, 17–113 ms latency on CPU, 3.5–106 series/sec per core, up to 18,770/sec on H100. All weights and code open-sourced.

Forecast anything—energy, retail, finance—no task-specific fine-tuning required.

text:
It's pretty interesting thatAI usage can keep growing while some AI businesses become less profitable.

The key is who captures the money, and who carries the risk.

@PanteraCapital’s analysis follows this chain:

Power → Data centers → GPU operators → AI services → Customers

Its illustrative model estimates annual revenue supported by one megawatt of capacity:

- Data centers: ~$2.2 million.
They lease buildings, cooling and power access. Electricity scarcity could support higher rents, but existing 15–20-year leases limit repricing.

- GPU operators: ~$25 million.
They install expensive chips and sell computing capacity. Higher revenue comes with hardware costs, debt and the risk that newer chips reduce older equipment’s earning power.

- AI providers: ~$44 million.
They turn rented computing power into services customers buy, often priced per token, or chunk of text. Their earnings depend on usage, efficiency and competitive pricing.

How to read these numbers: Revenue scales as you stack more service layers on top.

The risk runs upstream:

AI pricing drops → provider margins get pinched → GPU lease obligations come under strain → financing tightens higher up the chain.

Midnight acts purely as infra replacing a tri-party arrangement where a custodian acts as collateral agent

Here the smart contracts are the collateral agent

I expect an increasing number of markets to be created for specific loans with no vault participation, keen to see if someone has data on that 

This opens up a tri-party equivalent setup for lower ticket sizes

Limitation of course is smart contract risk

That is something @aave is working on with a very interesting proposal for Aave V4 Lending Market for Anchorage-Custodied Bitcoin

For large borrowers the @aave setup will have more size sooner I would argue. Borrowers will be more comfortable, same custodian as they are used to.

Remember in overcollateralized loans the borrower weirdly has more counterparty risk than the lender

Needless to say CeFi lending with rehypo and counterparty risk on the lender is here to stay. Tends to be cheaper!

***The 2026 Budget - what to expect***

FISCAL HEADROOM

* John Healey is expected to lower the fiscal headroom from £23bn to around £15bn after economic hit caused by Iran war

* Ministers fear fresh military strikes by the US against Iran in wake of mid-terms will render OBR forecasts obsolete within days - worse is to come

ENERGY BILLS

*Healey will extend the warm homes discount for families on benefits, giving them another £100 off their energy bills

* But households not on benefits will bear the full brunt of the rise in January, when bills are due to go up by 27% to an average of £2,192

* Gas standing charges will be scrapped next year, saving £27 on a typical bill although those with larger homes who use more energy will pay more

* Healey will announce long-term plans to move more green levies off energy bills in a bid to reduce them 'for good

* He's also expected to announce long-term plans to remove the link between gas prices and electricity prices

FUEL DUTY

* The fuel duty freeze - which was due to end in January - will be extended to help with soaring prices at the pumps

BANKING TAX

* The biggest 'revenue raiser' in the Budget. Healey has been lobbied to restore the 8% surcharge on corporation tax, which would raise £2bn

ONLINE RETAILER TAX

* Online retail giants like Amazon, eBay and Temu will be made responsible for collecting tax from retailers selling on their platforms

FAMILY BUSINESSES

* Thousands of high-street shops, cafes, pubs and hairdressers will no longer have to pay business rates. Move funded with online retailer tax

MINIMUM WAGE

* The living wage, paid by older workers, and the national minimum wage, paid by those aged 18 to 21, will increase by 3.9%. Healey has chosen to stop the huge rises in the minimum wage amid concerns it was pricing young people out of work

PENSIONERS

* Healey will announce plans to shield 1million pensioners from paying income tax

* The state pension is due to rise by 3.9%, taking 1million people with low incomes above the income tax threshold

* Healey will introduce a new tax allowance for low-income pensioners

* He has also decided not to reduce the tax-free pensino lump sum

DEFENCE SPENDING

* Healey's immediate priority is filling £4.7bn hole in the defence investment plan. Cuts expected to departmental budgets elsewhere

* He is also expected to announce additional borrowing to fund government investment vehicles, which will then be used to fund defence

* But he WILL NOT set out a timeline for hitting the 3% defence spending target. That will come in the spending review next year

HELP TO BUY

* A revived Help to Buy scheme called Your First Home

* It will offer first time buyers a 20% equity loan to help them buy a new-build home, with a minimum deposit of just 2.5%

* The earnings cap will be set at £140,000 in London and £110,000 outside London

RECORD TAX LEVELS

* The OBR is expected to once again say that the tax burden will  rise to another post-war record

* It's being driven by fiscal drag. Half a million people will be dragged into paying the higher rate

* The freeze - which is pencilled in for more than a decade - is effectively the single biggest tax rise in history

OBR forecasts

* They will highlight the huge uncertainty caused by the war in Iran. Ministers think it could make the OBR forecasts obsolete within weeks

* The tax revenues underpinning the Budget assume that Rosebank will be given the go-ahead, despite Cabinet splits on the issue

WHAT ISN'T IN IT

* Healey has rejected calls from colleagues to increase Capital Gains Tax amid concerns that doing so would damage growth and end up reducing tax revenues

* Major welfare reform will wait until after the Milburn review, which is coming after the Budget. It will require significant upfront investment in employment support

* Defence spending - the big decision has been deferred until the spending review, expected in Autumn 2027

Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, featuring 2 new benchmarks and 3 upgrades. For the first time, the majority of the Index is built on private datasets

The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is our composite measure of model capabilities across tasks reflecting real-world usage today. v5 is our biggest upgrade since v4 launched in January. With v5, 60% of the Index is now based on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers.

Alongside Intelligence Index v5, we’re launching the Artificial Analysis Progress Index v1, which tracks model capability over time on one continuous scale.

New to the Intelligence Index:

➤ FrontierCode 2.0: Cognition's newly-launched private benchmark of real-world coding tasks, graded on whether a repository maintainer would merge the agent's change

➤ Terminal-Bench-Science: 70 agentic scientific research tasks, run in a terminal environment

Upgraded:

➤ HLE-Diamond (replacing Humanity's Last Exam): a refined 1,000-question version of Humanity's Last Exam, split evenly between reasoning and knowledge questions

➤ AA-Omniscience v1.1: An updated dataset with saturated and public set questions removed, new questions added, and ambiguous or erroneous questions revised

➤ CritPt v2: a private, 40-question hard subset of CritPt v2, revised by the CritPt authors and run with a code-execution tool

Staying in the Index: AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf and Terminal-Bench 4.0

Removed from the Index: GDPval-AA v2.1, SciCode, and AA-LCR v1.1

Key results:

➤ Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 58, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (max, 57) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 55): Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five models. Gemini 4 Argon (high) is next at 50

➤ The open weights gap widens from 3 points to 12: Kimi K3.1 Pro (weights not yet released) is the top open weights model at 46. Among released weights, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) and GLM-5.3 (max) lead at 32 - 26 points behind the leader and below Claude Haiku 5.5 (max, 36)

➤ Cost per task varies by more than 13x among the leading models: of the 10 highest-scoring models shown, GPT-6.1 Terra (max) is the cheapest at $0.96 per Intelligence Index task and Claude Fable 5.1 (max) the most expensive at $13.04

text:
这周OKX星球「玩赚美股财报季」预测活动，我直接交答案：

闪迪：Yes，最看好。
微软：Yes，偏向小幅超预期。
谷歌：Yes，但要防高预期。
亚马逊：偏Yes，四家里把握相对最低。

先说清楚：这是对业绩的判断，反正都是用积分玩，重在体验和开心！

闪迪我看好的是NAND涨价向利润端传导，涨价叠加企业级SSD需求，利润弹性可能大于收入弹性。

但海力士的HBM强，不等于闪迪自动躺赢，最终还得看闪迪自己的毛利率和下一季指引。

微软看Azure增长和AI商业化，云业务之外，企业软件收入提供支撑，我偏向业绩小幅超预期；股价能否涨，关键是新增收入能不能跟上资本开支和折旧。

谷歌看搜索广告韧性、Cloud增长及利润率，业务有超预期空间，但市场已经对云增长抱有较高期待，报得好，还得比大家想的更好。

亚马逊偏Yes，但AWS增长、零售利润率和投入强度要一起看，营收超预期，未必能抵消现金流承压带来的担忧。

至于海力士，今天财报已经公布、股价也已上涨，挺好！

我的排序：业绩超预期信心，闪迪＞微软＞谷歌＞亚马逊；股价表现则重点看指引，以及利好出来后能不能守住涨幅。

把答案写下来，免得财报出来以后，又变成“我早就知道”😂

大家也来交卷，尤其闪迪，你选Yes还是No？

text:
又多了一个看好 $MASK 的理由。
NullMask 创始人 @tomas_ownit 的履历确实相当亮眼。

1/ 教育背景
Tomas 本科和硕士均就读于布拉格查理大学，专业是数学与计算机科学。
查理大学是捷克规模最大、排名最高的大学之一。

Tomas 的高光出现在硕士就读期间。
他以开发者身份参与 SatoshiLabs（Trezor 母公司）相关项目，并在 Zcash 资助计划支持下，为硬件钱包 Trezor 开发 Orchard 隐私交易功能。
该项目最初申请的预算为 13 万美元，但最终只完成并支付了前三个里程碑，合计 5.98 万美元；后两个里程碑未支付，项目状态显示为已取消。
除此之外，Tomas 还曾推动 Zcash 修改 ZIP-244 签名规范。

2/ 工作履历
▌MAYA-ZK 数学家
2023 年 9 月—2024 年 3 月。
公司主要研究硬件加速零知识证明。

▌Quantum Fusion 研究员
2025 年 8 月，任职约 1 个月。
该团队早期专注于大规模并行计算，后来更名为 QF Network，转向 L1 公链方向。

▌NullMask 创始人
2025 年 9 月至今，LinkedIn 标注为兼职。
NullMask 的 ZK 隐私池已部署至 Ethereum、Base、BNB Chain、Robinhood Chain 和 Solana。
$MASK 第一季积分活动于 10 月 19 日开启，持续 90 天，奖励是 10% $MASK 代币。

▌OWNIT 区块链研究员
2026 年 7 月至今。
OWNIT 是一个链上自营交易平台，计划覆盖加密货币、黄金、美股、指数及外汇市场。
项目已入选 Solana Incubator 第 5 期，但产品尚未正式上线，官方明确表示不会发行代币。
值得注意的是，OWNIT 的 CEO Tibor Tribus 同样是 Tomas 前东家 MAYA-ZK 的 CEO。由此来看，OWNIT 很可能是 MAYA-ZK 原班团队的再次创业。

3/ 怎么看？
Tomas 的技术背景和履历确实不错，但仍有两个问题值得留意。

第一，宣传口径存在夸大。
NullMask 将 Tomas 描述为“ZEC 核心贡献者”，但从公开经历来看，他主要是在 2021—2022 年获得 Zcash 资助，为硬件钱包 Trezor 开发隐私交易支持，并参与推动 ZIP-244 签名规范的修改。
这算得上重要贡献，但与通常理解中的“核心贡献者”仍有一定差距。

第二，同时参与两个项目。
Tomas 目前似乎同时任职于 NullMask 和 OWNIT，而 LinkedIn 上的 NullMask 职位还被标注为兼职。

当然， $MASK 积分计划目前仍值得参与：
https://t.co/moUMV3LJIW

text:
Gm Folks
We are back!

This is another edition of the Predict Alpha Report, our bi-monthly collaboration with @CoinsiliumGroup tracking the rise of prediction markets, event-driven finance, and the growing role of AI agents within it. Each edition focuses on the signals that matter, from capital flows and fundraising activity to regulatory shifts and product innovation. As information is increasingly priced in real time by both humans and machines, the Predict Alpha Report will track where these signals lead.
But first, let’s get this part out of the way:

Always DYOR:
This bulletin is for informational purposes only and contains summaries of news articles originally published by third-party media outlets. Please refer to the full disclaimer at the end of the post.

Now, let’s get started.
Here are the highlights:

💸 Capital Signals
👉$1.4 Billion Linked To Election Day
👉Inflation Futures
👉Predictive Labs’ Nijinn Brings Cross-Market Intelligence to the US Midterms

📈 Industry Pulse
👉Swaps Include Prediction Markets
👉The First To..
👉Prediction Markets 🤝 Stablecoins
👉Kalshi on Phantom
👉Bitcoin-Backed Trades

💸 Capital Signals

💰$1.4 Billion Linked To Election Day

According to CNN, trading on prediction markets linked to the 2026 US midterm elections has surpassed $1.4 billion. @Kalshi leads with nearly $1.1 billion in trading volume, while @Polymarket has recorded more than $340 million across its US and international platforms. People are betting on everything from election winners and voter turnout to candidate endorsements, debates, and campaign speeches.

The growth comes as US regulations become more favourable toward election betting, encouraging existing platforms to expand and new players to enter the market. PredictIt and ForecastEx are seeing increased activity, while UK-based @Smarkets is seeking approval to launch in the US. Beyond betting, these markets are increasingly observed as indicators of public expectations and how traders assess the likelihood of different outcomes. Trading is expected to pick up even more, as Election Day approaches.

💰 Inflation Futures

Kalshi plans to launch futures contracts tied to US inflation in December. The new products will track the Consumer Price Index (CPI), a key measure of inflation, and core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices. Kalshi has brought in former Barclays trader Michael Ashton to help design the contracts and attract major banks, hedge funds and asset managers. The opportunity is significant, with the US inflation market including $2.2 trillion in Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) and more than $5.4 trillion in inflation swaps. Unlike Kalshi’s existing contracts that pay out based on whether an event happens, these futures would allow investors to trade changes in inflation expectations more directly and manage their exposure over time.

Kalshi hopes that offering standardised inflation contracts with fixed expiration dates and nearly round-the-clock trading will make the market more accessible, particularly for investors who currently rely on complex private agreements to trade inflation. While Kalshi has already built a large business around sports and event-based trading, attracting institutional investors would open up a very different source of growth.

And rounding up this section:

💰Predictive Labs’ Nijinn Brings Cross-Market Intelligence to the US Midterms

With the US midterm elections approaching, @nijinn_official's dedicated midterms platform brings prediction-market data into focus across Senate, House, and governor races. Developed by @Predictive_Labs, it combines Polymarket and Kalshi order-book data through Nijinn’s TruthIndex™ to produce a single liquidity-weighted probability for each outcome, while highlighting where the two venues’ probabilities diverge.

The platform offers an early preview of Nijinn Pro’s cross-venue analytics, with shareable graphics and live embeds helping journalists bring the data to their readers. Predictive Labs reports that it has shared the site with close to 1,000 US journalists and plans to extend the format to other major elections and sporting events, broadening Nijinn’s reach through timely, relevant applications.
Predictive Labs will exhibit at Web Summit Lisbon on 9–12 November 2026, with founder @johann_evrard showcasing Nijinn alongside leading figures in AI and blockchain.

📌 FYI: Predictive Labs is backed by Gibraltar-based venture builder, Coinsilium Group. Coinsilium’s shares are traded on the Aquis Stock Exchange Growth Market in London, under the ticker symbol "COIN", and on the OTCQB Venture Market in the United States under the ticker symbol "CINGF".

But it’s not just capital flowing into the space.
Keep reading for the latest signals in regulation, adoption, and structure.

📈 Industry Pulse

⚡️Swaps Include Prediction Markets

The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has proposed new rules that would formally classify prediction market contracts tied to sports, politics, culture, and weather as swaps, a type of financial contract whose value depends on an underlying asset or event. The proposal aims to clarify that prediction markets operating on federally registered exchanges fall under the CFTC’s authority rather than individual state gambling regulators.

The distinction matters for platforms like Kalshi, which have faced legal challenges as they expand across the US. If adopted, the proposal could give federally regulated prediction markets greater legal certainty and make it harder for states to restrict their operations.

⚡️ The First To...

The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has approved Cboe Global Markets’ proposal to introduce contracts that let investors trade on specific company performance metrics rather than just share prices. @RobinhoodApp is expected to become the first retail brokerage to offer these products, covering more than 100 metrics across 23 companies. These include NVIDIA’s data-center revenue, Apple’s iPhone sales revenue, and Robinhood’s number of funded customers.

The contracts work as binary options, allowing traders to take positions on whether a company will meet a particular performance target. For Robinhood, this adds another product to its growing range of options, futures, and prediction markets, potentially creating a new source of trading revenue.

⚡️Prediction Markets 🤝 Stablecoins

@Underdog has partnered with crypto infrastructure provider @zerohashx to let users fund their prediction market and fantasy sports accounts using stablecoins and other digital assets. Announced at the NEXTPredict NYC Summit, the new feature is expected to launch later in 2026 for eligible users and will sit alongside existing payment options within the Underdog app.

The main benefit is speed. Unlike traditional bank transfers, which can face delays during evenings and weekends, stablecoin payments can be processed around the clock, allowing users to add funds to their accounts in near real time. Zerohash will handle the underlying crypto infrastructure, so users won’t need to manage complicated wallet addresses or blockchain networks themselves.

⚡️Kalshi on Phantom

Crypto wallet provider @Phantom is bringing Kalshi’s prediction markets directly into its app, allowing millions of US crypto users to trade on real-world events without leaving their wallets. The rollout began on October 23, and access will expand over the coming weeks. Users will need to complete identity verification through Kalshi and can fund trades using Phantom’s dollar-pegged CASH stablecoin.

Funds are converted into traditional currency for settlement, while winnings and withdrawals return to users’ Phantom Cash accounts. Trading fees are set at $0.02 per contract, plus a small network fee. The integration gives Kalshi access to Phantom’s existing crypto user base while making regulated prediction markets more accessible to people already familiar with digital assets.

At the same time,

⚡️Bitcoin-Backed Trades

@Kalshi is expanding its crypto offerings through a new partnership with digital asset custodian @BitGo, allowing eligible institutional clients to borrow against their cryptocurrency holdings to fund leveraged futures trades. Through Kalshi Prime, customers will be able to use Bitcoin, Ethereum, and selected stablecoins held at BitGo as collateral for loans, rather than selling their crypto to raise cash.

The borrowed funds can then be used to support margin positions on Kalshi’s trading platform, allowing investors to take larger positions with less upfront cash, although this also increases their exposure to potential losses. Kalshi plans to add more crypto custodians to the network in the coming months, giving clients greater flexibility in how they fund their trades. The partnership marks another step in Kalshi’s efforts to move beyond event-based prediction markets and compete in the broader derivatives trading industry.

And that’s it!
Long read, but if you enjoyed this, set a reminder in your calendar for the next edition of the Predict Alpha Report.

Thanks to Coinsilium, we’ll be dropping these updates every other Monday, i.e., twice a month.

- 基金会还通过 OTC，买回部分此前曾卖出 ENA 的早期主要投资者所持有的未解锁代币，减少这部分持仓未来可能带来的抛售压力

- 但要注意：原始投资者解锁结束，不代表所有解锁结束，也不等于抛压清零

2/ 收入回购

- ENA Fee Switch 提案已经通过

- 当 USDe 供应量达到首档 75 亿美元门槛后，支付给基金会的相关业务净收入中，95% 可用于回购 ENA

- 按资料中的约 46 亿美元测算，USDe 规模还需增长约 63% 才能达到首档门槛 这里仅统计 USDe，不包含 USDtb；机制通过，也不等于回购已经启动

我继续持有 ENA 的一个原因，就是仍然看好 USDe 的增长空间

就拿最近的新进展来说 ⬇️

USDe 通过 X Layer 上的 Aave v3 增加了使用场景，也为 OKX Wallet 用户提供了新的链上入口

渠道扩大后，关键是能否转化为持续的新增需求 如果 USDe 的规模和相关收入继续增长，就有机会接近回购门槛，让业务增长逐步转化为 ENA 的实际买盘

这些是我接下主要关注的：

USDe 能不能继续增长，收入能不能支撑回购，以及回购最终能否落地

text:
I think most people approach market selection backwards. They start with what they want to trade (a coin, index, stock, whatever) and then try to force a signal out of it. The market comes first and the edge is something they hope to find afterward.

The better approach is to start with the effect you’re trying to capture. Ask what behavior you’re exploiting, whether that’s momentum, mean reversion, some structural flow, etc. and then ask where you would expect that effect to actually show up.

Universe selection matters as much as the signal and sometimes more. A mediocre signal applied to the right set of markets can beat a brilliant signal applied to the wrong ones. Where you trade can matter more than how you trade.

text:
Almost 100,000 people starred a free project that uses wifi to sense you through walls. No camera.

It's called RuView. Wifi signals bounce off your body as you move, and by reading tiny changes in them it can:

1. Tell someone is in a room, even behind a wall, up to about 5 metres away

2. Count people and spot them coming and going

3. Pick up breathing and heart rate

4. Notice when someone falls

5. Do all of it in complete darkness, with no cameras or wearables

It works with Home Assistant, Apple Home, Google Home and Alexa, and it was built with Claude, so it ships with a Claude Code plugin to set it up.

The catch: you need cheap ESP32-S3 boards ($9 each), and the full body tracking is still rough. Presence and breathing work best right now.

https://t.co/x3h0LiM0iT

text:
Meta 的 AI Agent 正在挖掘 Instagram 最有价值、也最容易被忽略的一块数据，你的收藏夹。

一位用户让 Muse 根据自己在 Instagram 收藏过的滑雪视频，为 12 月初的滑雪旅行制定训练计划。

Muse 直接读取了她此前收藏的内容，找出相关的滑雪教学视频，制定了一份五周训练计划，甚至顺手把她杂乱的收藏夹重新整理成滑雪训练、技术技巧、健身、旅行、食谱等不同合集。

Meta 的 AI 负责人 Alexandr Wang 转发了这个案例，表示 Muse 与 Instagram 的整合还会继续升级。

我觉得这才是 Meta 做 Personal Agent 真正可怕的地方。

很多人收藏过几百上千条帖子，但可能再也不会打开第二次。这些内容其实记录了大量真实的个人意图，想学什么、想去哪里、准备买什么、对什么感兴趣。

过去 Meta 主要拿这些数据来优化推荐算法，现在它开始让 AI 直接把用户的兴趣变成具体行动。

而且 Meta 根本不需要教育用户去维护一套新的知识管理系统。Instagram、WhatsApp、Facebook 已经积累了大量日常行为和个人上下文。

text:
中国 AI 芯片已经缺 HBM 缺到良率只有 20%–30%，也要硬着头皮开始量产了。

路透社独家报道称，长鑫存储（CXMT）计划在未来两个月内启动 HBM3E 的小规模生产，目前已经向多家国内 AI 芯片设计公司送样。

问题是，目前长鑫的 HBM3E 良率只有 20%–30%，而韩国 SK 海力士的良率约为 70%。更尴尬的是，长鑫的 HBM3E 在测试中的实际性能更接近海力士上一代 HBM3，成本还可能高于海外同类产品。

但长鑫依然决定推进生产。

原因很简单，国内 AI 芯片厂商已经严重缺乏 HBM。美国出口管制限制了先进 HBM 的供应，部分厂商只能通过非正规渠道以数倍价格采购。此前华为、寒武纪等国产 AI 芯片厂商已经因存储成本压力，将部分产品价格提高了 20%–50%。

这件事挺值得关注的。我们经常讨论国产 GPU 能不能追上英伟达，但一颗 AI 芯片能否大规模交付，还取决于能不能拿到足够的高带宽内存。

现在的情况是，即便国产 HBM 的性能落后一代、成本更贵、生产良率只有对手的三分之一左右，国内市场依然有动力推动它尽快投产。

对国产 AI 算力产业来说，眼下最紧迫的问题之一，已经是能不能稳定拿到足够多的芯片，而不仅仅是单颗芯片的性能有多强。

text:
Today, in collaboration with Anthropic, we’re excited to share rapid initial progress towards an antibody treatment for food allergy, which affects over 200 million people worldwide, discovered with the help of Claude.

At Divergence Labs, we believe that AI can unlock the next generation of antibody therapeutics with more effective mechanisms than before. Such mechanisms are urgently needed in food allergy, which involve overcoming one of the tightest affinity protein pairs in immunology, IgE and its receptor FcεRI, on mast cells.

Treatment with Xolair—the only approved antibody for food allergy—sequesters circulating IgE, but mast cells remain sensitized for weeks to months due to the extraordinarily slow dissociation of IgE from FcεRI.

We envision a treatment that actively pulls IgE off of FcεRI, without waiting for natural dissociation. Like picking a lock, this requires the right combination of geometry and force.

Our research team, working with Claude, ideated on mechanisms to accomplish this disruption, and converged on an antibody format with two arms with different functions and epitopes. Within one month, we designed, synthesized, and experimentally confirmed the biophysical function of the two arms, which we are now assembling into full therapeutic formats.

author: Lyskey
quoted_text:
Last week, core devs had to delay forking the Hoodi testnet to Glamsterdam to study a report by @chain_security which revealed some problems with how EIP-8037 interacts with a few contracts.
Over the weekend, ppl tried to get a better picture of the impact and by now it's quite well understood. So here's what you need to know:

What's been known is that contracts which hardcode forwarded gas are affected by repricings, e.g. making state writes (SSTORE) more expensive.

What's new is that some coding patterns rely on specific invariant which were broken with EIP-8037. 

Gas already spent can come back mid-tx, so gasleft() can go up. This causes two problems:
(1) a before / after gas counter underflows and reverts
(2) a failed sub-call hands gas back, so a path that should've been unreachable runs, and the tx looks like it succeeded

Related but different: (3) measuring the gas usage of a call using GAS - before and after the call - might undercount because the state gas reservoir is not visible during execution (e.g. gas_left).

It's now about deciding how to proceed. Delaying hoodi bought time but won't resolve the issue. This week, we have to dig deep into contracts and make sure nothing is missed. Eventually, this might just need some coordination among the involved parties (dapps, core devs, auditors, people running nodes, etc.), or worst-case, spec changes.

If you're an app dev or auditor, check your contracts for issues with EIP-8037/EIP-8038, and report them.
Also, share this with your favorite app dev to spread awareness.

突发重磅：OpenAI 计划直接采购 Google $GOOGL 的 AI 芯片TPU！

把这条突发和Oracle AI 大会连起来看，真相就浮出水面了：

1. 为什么 $ORCL 昨天刚宣布成为全球首家外部部署 Google TPU 8t/8i 的云厂商？
答案很简单：Oracle 最大的算力金主就是 OpenAI（占其 6640 亿 RPO 订单的近一半）。Oracle 突然引入 Google TPU，极大概率正是为了承接 OpenAI 的 TPU 算力与自带硬件托管需求。

2. OpenAI 为什么要买死对头 Google 的芯片？原因有三：
极限压降推理成本：OpenAI 刚发布半价的 GPT-6.1 Terra 并面临 Anthropic IPO 前的猛烈价格战，日常高并发推理急需比纯 GPU 更具性价比的 ASIC 方案。
• 软件壁垒已被打破：上周 Google 与 Meta 刚联合开源了 TorchTPU（让 PyTorch 原生无缝跑在 TPU 上），彻底扫清了 OpenAI 将核心代码从英伟达 CUDA 迁移到 TPU 的工程障碍。
• 算力议价权博弈：2025 年 OpenAI 试水租用 Google Cloud TPU 时，曾逼得黄仁勋亲自致电 Sam Altman 签下千亿大单；此次从租用升级为直接购买，是向英伟达争取配额与定价权的核武器。

3. 产业链赢家与影响：
• $GOOGL & $AVGO / 联发科：Google TPU 彻底从内部自用走向外部商业化变现，拿到全球头号大模型买家的背书。
• $ORCL：坐实中立机房底座逻辑，若 OpenAI 直接出资买芯片放到 OCI 机房托管，将大幅缓解市场对 Oracle 资本开支与现金流的担忧。
• $NVDA：绝对采购量仍处高位，但头部大厂在推理端用 TPU/ASIC 分流高昂 GPU 成本已成明牌。

text:
I think most people approach market selection backwards. They start with what they want to trade (a coin, index, stock, whatever) and then try to force a signal out of it. The market comes first and the edge is something they hope to find afterward.

The better approach is to start with the effect you’re trying to capture. Ask what behavior you’re exploiting, whether that’s momentum, mean reversion, some structural flow, etc. and then ask where you would expect that effect to actually show up.

Universe selection matters as much as the signal and sometimes more. A mediocre signal applied to the right set of markets can beat a brilliant signal applied to the wrong ones. Where you trade can matter more than how you trade.

text:
又多了一个看好 $MASK 的理由。
NullMask 创始人 @tomas_ownit 的履历确实相当亮眼。

1/ 教育背景
Tomas 本科和硕士均就读于布拉格查理大学，专业是数学与计算机科学。
查理大学是捷克规模最大、排名最高的大学之一。

Tomas 的高光出现在硕士就读期间。
他以开发者身份参与 SatoshiLabs（Trezor 母公司）相关项目，并在 Zcash 资助计划支持下，为硬件钱包 Trezor 开发 Orchard 隐私交易功能。
该项目最初申请的预算为 13 万美元，但最终只完成并支付了前三个里程碑，合计 5.98 万美元；后两个里程碑未支付，项目状态显示为已取消。
除此之外，Tomas 还曾推动 Zcash 修改 ZIP-244 签名规范。

2/ 工作履历
▌MAYA-ZK 数学家
2023 年 9 月—2024 年 3 月。
公司主要研究硬件加速零知识证明。

▌Quantum Fusion 研究员
2025 年 8 月，任职约 1 个月。
该团队早期专注于大规模并行计算，后来更名为 QF Network，转向 L1 公链方向。

▌NullMask 创始人
2025 年 9 月至今，LinkedIn 标注为兼职。
NullMask 的 ZK 隐私池已部署至 Ethereum、Base、BNB Chain、Robinhood Chain 和 Solana。
$MASK 第一季积分活动于 10 月 19 日开启，持续 90 天，奖励是 10% $MASK 代币。

▌OWNIT 区块链研究员
2026 年 7 月至今。
OWNIT 是一个链上自营交易平台，计划覆盖加密货币、黄金、美股、指数及外汇市场。
项目已入选 Solana Incubator 第 5 期，但产品尚未正式上线，官方明确表示不会发行代币。
值得注意的是，OWNIT 的 CEO Tibor Tribus 同样是 Tomas 前东家 MAYA-ZK 的 CEO。由此来看，OWNIT 很可能是 MAYA-ZK 原班团队的再次创业。

3/ 怎么看？
Tomas 的技术背景和履历确实不错，但仍有两个问题值得留意。

第一，宣传口径存在夸大。
NullMask 将 Tomas 描述为“ZEC 核心贡献者”，但从公开经历来看，他主要是在 2021—2022 年获得 Zcash 资助，为硬件钱包 Trezor 开发隐私交易支持，并参与推动 ZIP-244 签名规范的修改。
这算得上重要贡献，但与通常理解中的“核心贡献者”仍有一定差距。

第二，同时参与两个项目。
Tomas 目前似乎同时任职于 NullMask 和 OWNIT，而 LinkedIn 上的 NullMask 职位还被标注为兼职。

当然， $MASK 积分计划目前仍值得参与：

text:
$GANG is no longer just providing a launch mechanism.

0x0c6302401aa5325c2e36f170f52c00b1d220b405 

It is also beginning to produce assets that can attract traders. With the launch of V3, this expectation has expanded further.

I believe the most direct catalyst behind this rally is the much larger scope of what GANG could become.

GANG’s original differentiation was the integration of Binance Agentic Wallet Agent IDs into its launch process, with each wallet’s purchase limit during the bonding curve phase capped at 1% of the total token supply. This cannot completely prevent multi-wallet operations, but it distinguishes GANG from ordinary launchpads. V3 is not simply about adding more launch features. It further improves the launch process and clarifies the rules, creating better conditions for more projects to enter the platform.

Founder 0xLazy’s background at CoinAnk provides some reference for the team’s product execution capabilities, but actual delivery and usage data will ultimately matter more. As for potential support from ecosystems such as Binance Alpha, this should currently be treated as a possible future catalyst rather than a confirmed positive development.

What has begun to validate this model is the performance of several graduated projects. According to the latest website data, Gangstar has a market cap of approximately $257,000 and 24-hour trading volume of about $685,000; TICK has a market cap of approximately $127,000 and trading volume of about $576,000; AGORA has a market cap of approximately $51,000 and trading volume of about $375,000. These figures show that some projects on the platform are attracting traders, although high trading volume does not mean an equivalent amount of net capital inflow, nor does it prove that these projects have long-term staying power. Their real significance is that they provide a visible reference point for future developers: launching on GANG can create an opportunity to attract market attention.

This could create a positive feedback loop. Successful projects encourage more developers to launch on the platform; new projects provide more trading opportunities and bring traders back; sustained trading activity then generates greater exposure and fee revenue for the platform. Yesterday’s website data showed approximately 1,950 Agent ID wallets that had bought at least once during the bonding curve phase, a GANG market cap of around $6.8 million, and a cumulative burn ratio of approximately 0.189%. The latest figures show that the number of relevant wallets has risen to 2,808, while the cumulative burn ratio has reached 0.511%. This represents an increase of approximately 44% in wallet count, with the burn ratio reaching around 2.7 times its previous level. Another V3 update reported more than 2,000 Agent buyers and over 3,000 trades. These figures come from different time windows and should not be combined into a single continuous growth curve, but they are sufficient to show that platform activity is expanding.

However, wallet growth is only an initial indicator of participation. It does not tell us whether these wallets belong to distinct users, nor does it prove that they will continue trading. The more important question is retention after graduation. If tokens continue to trade actively after completing the launch process, GANG may gradually reduce its dependence on short-term enthusiasm for new coins. Conversely, if most projects rapidly lose liquidity after graduation, increasing the number of launches will not necessarily create greater ecosystem value.

Another reason I remain bullish on GANG over the longer term is that it does not necessarily have to remain a launchpad. GANG Pair already supports pairings with other tokens that have liquidity pools on BNB Chain, and the website also displays trading scenarios involving tokenized stocks such as NVDAB, TSLAB, and AAPLB. Meanwhile, Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow are designed to connect trading opinions, transaction records, and follow-on trading behavior. Agents can record their views before a trade, users can share relevant assets and trading progress, and they can decide whether to follow other Agents based on their activity. These features are not enough to prove that a mature Agent economy has formed, but they point toward a broader direction: Agents may become ongoing participants in trading, information exchange, and application development rather than simply serving as an eligibility requirement for token launches. If developers begin building tools and services around these participants, GANG’s growth potential could extend beyond token issuance itself.

Whether the tokenomics can support these expectations is equally important. The website’s buyback-and-burn page shows that approximately 5.11 million GANG tokens have been burned, representing 0.511% of the total supply. The cumulative buyback amount is approximately $31,500, with around 295 buybacks executed, while another approximately $7,878 has been allocated to the treasury. According to the officially published mechanism, 80% of the relevant trading fees during certain launch phases is used for buybacks and burns, while the remaining 20% goes to the treasury. Fee rules differ by token type and after graduation, so it would be incorrect to multiply all platform trading volume by 80% to estimate actual buyback demand. The existing records show that the mechanism is already operating, but the buyback amount remains limited relative to the current market cap of several million dollars. What would be more convincing is sustained growth in actual fees and buybacks as platform activity expands.

There is also an important limitation that is easy to overlook: untaxed tokens no longer contribute the original bonding-curve platform fees after graduation. GANG therefore needs a continuous supply of new projects or trading scenarios capable of generating recurring revenue to maintain its fee sources. If V3 increases the number of launches without improving activity after graduation, it may not solve this problem. This is why I pay more attention to whether projects can retain traders than to how many tokens are launched each day.

From a valuation perspective, the market has already priced in a considerable portion of the growth expectations. If graduated projects remain active, V3 attracts more viable launches, and platform revenue and buybacks continue to expand, the market may raise its expectations further. But if trading volume is primarily driven by short-term turnover, or new projects fail to maintain attention, the current valuation may already be pricing in too much future ecosystem growth.

Therefore, I believe GANG’s fundamentals have strengthened compared with the early stage. V3 is live, the launchpad has produced graduated projects with notable trading activity, and both the number of participating wallets and cumulative burn records are increasing. However, GANG remains in an early validation phase, and the relationship between product usage, platform revenue, and token demand is not yet mature. The developments worth watching next are whether projects such as Dafeiyu and Gangstar can sustain their trading activity, whether new projects can reproduce their performance, and whether GANG Pair and Agent-related tools can generate demand beyond token launches.

To sum up, what makes me bullish on GANG is not how many new tokens it can launch, but its potential to turn Agents from an eligibility requirement in the launch process into active participants in a continuously operating ecosystem. The market has now seen the possibility of successful trading projects emerging from the launchpad. The next step is to determine whether those winners can attract new developers, liquidity, and users. If this cycle genuinely takes shape, GANG could evolve from a launchpad with differentiated mechanics into a trading gateway for the Agent economy. Otherwise, more features and buyback announcements alone will not be enough to support a long-term valuation.

Compared with product updates such as Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow, the more immediate catalyst today is that $GANG launchpad has started producing tokens with meaningful market caps and high trading volumes.

0x0c6302401aa5325c2e36f170f52c00b1d220b405 

Projects such as Big Fat Fish and Gangstar have graduated and established independent trading markets on PancakeSwap. The market is beginning to see the potential for GANG's ecosystem to grow organically: people are launching tokens through the platform, and those tokens are starting to attract traders.

With GANG's market cap rising from around 4m to nearly 8m, I believe the market is betting on whether it can evolve from an Agent-exclusive launchpad into an ecosystem on BNB Chain built around Agent issuance, trading, and collaboration.

The performance of Big Fat Fish and Gangstar is an important signal to watch in this rally. Previously, GANG's differentiation mainly came from its Agent ID access requirement, per-wallet purchase limit, and internal-market fee distribution mechanism. These designs distinguish it from ordinary launchpads, but they cannot independently prove that the platform has the ability to grow sustainably. The real test is whether projects can continue attracting traders after launch. If tokens lose their liquidity as soon as they graduate, no matter how many tokens are issued, it will be difficult to maintain the participation of creators and users. Conversely, when some projects continue to generate trading volume after graduation, the market has a more concrete reason to believe that this platform can consistently create new trading opportunities.

The changes in the website data are also worth watching. Yesterday, there were approximately 1,266 unique Agent ID wallets that had bought at least once during the internal bonding-curve phase. GANG had a market cap of around $3.94m, 24h trading volume of approximately $1.98m, and a cumulative burn percentage of about 0.081%. In the latest website screenshot, the number of qualifying wallets had risen to 1,950, an increase of around 54%. GANG's market cap reached approximately $6.8m, up around 73%; 24h trading volume increased to $2.88m, up around 45%; and the cumulative burn percentage rose to 0.189%, approximately 2.33 times the previous figure. The subsequent token chart showed the market cap rising further to around $7.15m, with 24h trading volume reaching approximately $3.4m.

These figures come from different points in time, but together they reflect a change: as the price rose, the number of wallets that had participated in internal trading, platform trading activity, and cumulative burn records also increased. Of course, wallet counts do not equal unique users, and trading volume does not equal net capital inflows. These figures are not enough to conclude that a sustainable growth flywheel has already formed. However, compared with looking only at GANG's own price, they provide a more concrete perspective: trading activity within the launchpad has indeed become more active during this rally.

More importantly, this development could attract new creators and Agents in turn. When a project succeeds, other developers see an opportunity to launch assets on GANG. More projects then give traders additional choices. If some of these tokens can sustain market attention, the launchpad may have an opportunity to develop a positive feedback loop instead of relying entirely on GANG's own price action to attract users. This is why I believe the significance of Big Fat Fish and Gangstar goes beyond their individual performance. What matters is whether they can serve as examples that encourage the next wave of projects to enter the ecosystem.

Another reason I have been bullish on GANG is that Agents themselves could become the core of the ecosystem, rather than simply serving as an eligibility requirement for the launchpad.

When many people discuss GANG, they focus on the 1% per-wallet purchase limit and whether Agent IDs can effectively prevent sniping and excessive token concentration. But I believe the 1% limit is just a rule. Agents are where the future growth potential lies. If the project ultimately relies only on this restriction to attract market attention, it will remain just another launchpad. The more interesting scenario is that Agents begin by participating in token launches and trading, then gradually attract developers to build tools, applications, and trading services around them, allowing different Agents to operate continuously within the same ecosystem.

GANG is already trying to expand in this direction. GANG Pair supports pairing with other tokens that have liquidity pools on BNB Chain, and the website also showcases trading scenarios involving tokenized stocks such as NVDAB, TSLAB, and AAPLB. Meanwhile, Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow are beginning to connect trading ideas, transaction records, and copy-trading behavior. Agents can write down their views before executing trades and link that content to transaction records through hashes. Users can share tokens, Agents, and trading progress, and can also follow other Agents' buy or launch records.

These features do not yet prove that a mature Agent economy has emerged, but they show that the team is attempting to bring issuance, trading, and information sharing into the same system. If users begin to follow the trading behavior of different Agents on a regular basis, and developers become willing to build tools and applications around these participants, GANG's use cases may eventually extend beyond simply launching tokens. This kind of ecosystem expansion will not happen automatically just because a feature goes live. It depends on whether enough participants continue using it.

In terms of tokenomics, the growth in platform activity also provides a more practical basis for evaluating the buyback-and-burn mechanism. According to the published mechanism, 80% of the fees generated by internal-market buys and sells are used to buy back and burn GANG, while the remaining 20% goes to the operating treasury. GANG Pair uses a different fee-distribution arrangement, with a portion of the relevant trading fees distributed to eligible holders and the remainder used for buybacks and related distributions. These mechanisms apply to different trading scenarios, so not all trading volume should be assessed using the same buyback ratio.

The cumulative burn percentage has increased from 0.081% to 0.189%, indicating that the mechanism continues to operate. However, what matters more than the burn figure itself is whether actual buybacks can continue growing as trading activity across the ecosystem expands. If new projects lack genuine demand, short-term high trading volume is unlikely to provide a stable source of fees. Conversely, if more projects maintain trading activity after graduation, the fee mechanism could gradually become part of GANG's long-term value-capture model.

From a chart perspective, GANG's short-term trend is clearly strong, but the rapid rise has also increased the risk of chasing the price. The latest market cap is around $7.15m, the intraday high is approximately $8.44m, 24h trading volume is around $3.4m, and liquidity is approximately $344,900. The price is well above the MA10 at around $4.71m and the MA20 at approximately $4.33m. RSI has reached 82.09, placing the token in significantly overbought territory in the short term. This indicates strong market momentum, but it does not mean the price can continue rising without a period of consolidation.

Going forward, the intraday high of $8.44m is an important level to watch. If the price breaks above it convincingly with sustained trading volume, the market may enter a further price-discovery phase. If a pullback occurs, the areas around $6.66m, $5.25m, and $4.27m are worth monitoring. If buyers continue supporting the price during a retracement and it subsequently challenges the previous high again, the trend would become more convincing. Conversely, if trading volume declines rapidly and the price falls back into the previous consolidation range, the rally may have been driven more by short-term capital than by a sustained price-discovery process.

I believe GANG's fundamentals have strengthened compared with yesterday, although this improvement remains at an early stage. The most important changes are that the launchpad is beginning to produce graduated projects with strong trading activity, the number of wallets that have participated in internal trading has increased, platform activity has expanded, and the cumulative burn percentage has risen. Updates such as Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow also provide additional avenues for future ecosystem expansion. What still needs to be proven is the long-term connection between product features, user participation, and demand for the token.

The most important things to watch next are whether projects such as Big Fat Fish and Gangstar can maintain trading activity after the initial excitement fades, and whether they can attract more creators and Agents to GANG. If these projects only experience brief bursts of activity, the platform's growth thesis will remain fragile. If they remain active and drive subsequent launches, paired trading, and tool usage, GANG may gradually establish a growth path that does not depend entirely on a single market rally.

To me, the most compelling aspect of GANG is the possibility that it can turn Agents from an eligibility requirement in the token-launch process into active participants in a continuously operating ecosystem. The market has now seen the possibility of successful projects emerging from the launchpad. The next thing to verify is whether these projects can encourage more participants to stay and drive the continued creation of new assets, tools, and applications. What ultimately determines how far GANG can go is not how many more tokens it can launch, but whether the first successful projects can give the next wave of projects a compelling reason to enter the ecosystem.
