$GANG has risen from a market cap of approximately $995K when I first shared the project to $4.11M, a gain of more than 3x.

0x0c6302401aa5325c2e36f170f52c00b1d220b405 

But rather than focusing on the price itself, I am more interested in how the project has been changing its positioning during this period. Initially, GANG was trying to build a launchpad that only wallets holding an Agent ID could participate in. Now, it is beginning to build a more complete on-chain ecosystem around Agent issuance, trading, trade records, and copy trading.

I believe this is the more interesting development behind the current rally. The market may be betting not just on the popularity of the AI Agent sector, but on whether Agents will become real participants in the on-chain economy, and whether GANG can secure an important entry point into that ecosystem.

GANG's original design had one defining characteristic: rather than simply adding an AI narrative to a traditional launchpad, it incorporated the Agent ID from Binance Agentic Wallet into the issuance process. Only eligible wallets can participate in the internal market, and each wallet's purchase limit during the bonding curve phase is capped at 1% of the total token supply. Once a token reaches its graduation requirements, it migrates to PancakeSwap V2, its liquidity pool is burned, and the trading restrictions are lifted. Under the mechanism announced by the project, 80% of the 1% fee generated by buying and selling untaxed tokens in the internal market is used to buy back and burn GANG, while the remaining 20% goes into the operating treasury. This design attempts to address issuance permissions, early token concentration, and the use of platform fees at the same time. It cannot completely eliminate multi-wallet activity or sniping, but it does give GANG a distinct identity in the way tokens are launched.

What really made me reassess GANG was its expansion beyond being a simple launchpad. GANG Pair now supports pairing with other tokens that have liquidity pools on BNB Chain, and the project has also showcased trading scenarios involving tokenized stock assets such as NVDAB, TSLAB, and AAPLB. Previously, GANG's activity depended primarily on new token launches and internal-market trading. Now, if other assets are willing to use GANG as a trading pair, it has an opportunity to participate in their subsequent trading activity instead of relying on new projects to generate demand every time. There is an important distinction here: a launchpad needs to continuously attract creators who are willing to issue new tokens, while trading infrastructure has the potential to find more use cases among assets that already exist. Whether GANG Pair can generate genuine trading volume will determine whether this expansion merely adds another feature or fundamentally changes the project's long-term growth trajectory.

The recent launch of Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow adds another layer worth examining. Agents can write down their thoughts before a trade takes place, with the CLI generating a hash and recording it in the trade data. After the transaction is confirmed, the platform recalculates and verifies the hash, and only content that matches the recorded hash is displayed. Notes can also be set to become public after a delay, while unrevealed notes remain sealed. Meanwhile, Share is live, allowing users to share tokens, Agents, trade records, and bonding-curve progress. Follow allows users to follow trades based on another Agent's buying or launch notes.

I believe the idea behind these features is more valuable than simply adding a few social buttons. GANG is trying to make Agent trading behavior discoverable and traceable. In the future, traders may look beyond a token's price chart and examine what a particular Agent has done, how it explains its trades, and whether its past behavior is worth paying attention to. If this habit gradually takes hold, GANG could connect launchers, traders, and Agents, allowing trading activity to develop around a group of participants who can be observed over time. However, verifiable trade records do not mean the trading ideas themselves are correct, and the Follow feature does not guarantee that users will achieve the same returns as the Agents they follow. Whether it can create a genuine network effect ultimately depends on how many users continue to use these features and whether the records provide meaningful information.

The founder's background is also relevant to the assessment. GANG's founder, 0xLazy, is also a core builder behind CoinAnk, which has long specialized in crypto derivatives data, order flow, liquidations, open interest, and funding rates, while continuing to explore MCP interfaces and Agent trading tools. This experience has some relevance to GANG's product direction. Someone who has worked with trading data and trading tools for a long time may have a clearer understanding of what traders need and how that information can be incorporated into a product. However, the founder's experience can only serve as a reference point for execution capability. It cannot replace GANG's own user growth, product adoption, and business data. What matters is whether the team can turn that experience into products that people consistently use.

The latest data suggests that GANG is no longer entirely at the conceptual stage. The latest website figures show that 1,266 distinct Agent ID wallets have met the eligibility criteria and purchased tokens at least once during the internal bonding-curve phase, up approximately 41% from the roughly 896 shown in an earlier snapshot. This indicates that participation has expanded, but it does not mean that the number of active traders has increased by the same proportion, nor does it prove that every wallet is controlled by a different person. The website also displays a market of GANG and other Agent-related tokens, showing that the platform has established an initial supply of assets and some trading activity. Going forward, what matters more than the number of new tokens is how many projects successfully graduate, whether they maintain trading activity afterward, and whether these new features can keep users engaged on the platform.

GANG's tokenomics are also beginning to produce more verifiable execution records. The project announced that its first-day buyback had been completed, then published a record showing approximately 141,608.69 GANG burned on the second day, with a BscScan transaction link. A more recent update also indicated that the team plans to consolidate historical burn records into a dashboard on the website, making it easier for users to track buybacks and burns. In my view, this is more meaningful than simply promising a deflationary model in a white paper, because it gives the market a way to verify what has actually happened.

The two transaction-fee mechanisms announced by the project also need to be understood separately. Fees from internal-market trading are primarily allocated to buybacks and burns, as well as the operating treasury. Transactions involving GANG Pair use a different fee-distribution arrangement, under which part of the fees goes to eligible holders, while the remainder is used for buybacks and related allocations. These mechanisms apply to different trading scenarios, so it would be incorrect to apply a single buyback ratio to all trading volume.

The current chart provides another perspective on the rally. According to the latest figures, GANG has a market cap of approximately $4.11M, less than 10% below its all-time high of around $4.53M. Its 24-hour trading volume is approximately $2.2M, with liquidity of around $253.2K. The price remains above the MA10 and MA20 levels, both around $3.59M, while the RSI stands at 61.84. This suggests that the short-term trend remains strong, although the price is approaching its previous high. If GANG can break above $4.53M on sustained trading volume and maintain strength after the breakout, the market could enter a new price-discovery phase. If buying pressure weakens, a pullback toward the short-term moving averages would also be normal.

One figure I am particularly watching is that current trading volume is approximately 8.7 times liquidity. This reflects strong market attention, but it also indicates frequent turnover between traders. High trading volume is not the same as net buying, and the available liquidity may not be sufficient to absorb a sudden wave of large sell orders. The chart's indicators for the top 10 holders' average buy and sell market caps are approximately $1.47M and $1.80M, respectively, both well below the current market cap. These figures cannot fully reveal the actual cost basis of every large holder, but they remind me that early participants may have accumulated substantial unrealized profits, making short-term profit-taking an important factor to consider.

I believe the market is currently betting on three things. First, Agents may evolve from merely executing tasks into on-chain economic participants capable of issuing assets, trading, and managing funds autonomously. Second, GANG has the potential to develop from an Agent-exclusive launchpad into a trading network built around transaction records, social discovery, and copy trading. Third, GANG Pair may create demand beyond the internal market and connect part of the ecosystem's activity to the native token through its fee mechanism. Of these three, I am most interested in whether the third can reinforce the first two. If more Agents begin participating in real trading and more assets adopt GANG as a trading pair, the platform may no longer need to depend entirely on new token launches to remain active.

The catalysts worth watching next are not simply additional features announced by the team, but whether those features produce measurable usage. Whether Agent Thoughts and Follow generate recurring visits and continued copy-trading activity, whether GANG Pair attracts new assets and liquidity, whether the launchpad continues producing projects that graduate, and whether actual buyback and burn amounts increase alongside platform activity will all be more convincing than a single price rally. Conversely, if the new features fail to generate sustained usage, paired pools lack meaningful trading volume, and buybacks remain small, GANG's product advantages may not translate into long-term token demand.

The risks also need to be considered. The Agent ID requirement creates differentiation but limits participation by ordinary users. Multi-wallet activity may still undermine the effectiveness of identity restrictions, while cross-asset pairing and on-chain trading introduce additional liquidity, execution, and security complexities. Making the code public does not mean the contracts have passed an independent audit, and the relevant deployments still require further verification. Furthermore, GANG has already risen from a market cap of approximately $995K to $4.11M. Some expectations have been priced in, and improving fundamentals alone do not guarantee that its valuation will continue expanding at the same rate.

Overall, I believe GANG's fundamentals have strengthened meaningfully compared with its early stage. The product has expanded from an Agent-only launchpad into trading pairs, transaction-thought and sharing mechanisms have begun to go live, the number of participating wallets has increased, and buybacks and burns now have initial execution records. However, the project remains at an early stage, and the relationship between product usage and token value capture has not yet been fully validated.

What makes GANG worth watching, in my view, is not whether it can continue earning a short-term premium from the AI Agent narrative, but whether Agent trading behavior can gradually form a market where activity is discoverable, traceable, and sustained. If more Agents and developers begin relying on this system to issue, pair, and trade assets, GANG could evolve from a launchpad with differentiated features into trading infrastructure for the Agent economy. Ultimately, its ceiling will not be determined by how many Agents or tokens appear on the platform, but by whether these participants continue to generate trading activity on GANG and bring verifiable economic activity into the ecosystem.

author: 0xJaehaerys
quoted_text:
TxFlow is Hyperliquid from Temu

They forked Hyperliquid's Arbitrum bridge and changed the name. They copied HyperUnit too and forgot to change the name: txrelay[.]com literally says "Unit is the asset tokenization layer on TxRelay". The frontend, the API and the fees are Hyperliquid's. Even the slogan. The L1 is closed source, with Hyperliquid's naming on everything: TxCore, Tx-BFT, TIPs

Hyperliquid is closed source too, but it has 27 validators that each post prices, and anyone can run a node to check them. TxFlow has 5 validators, all its own, nothing you can run, and one key that acts as the entire oracle. The same key sits on the bridge multisig

So it's a centralized exchange secured by a 3/4 multisig. Their own audit says those keys "can propose arbitrary withdrawals"

And the growth plan is KOLs shilling ref codes

text:
One of my stronger convictions in RWA-Fi is that @pendle_fi is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of onchain capital markets.

We're talking about trillions $$$ in potential tokenised asset supply over the coming years, but bringing assets onchain is only half the equation.

The real opportunity lies in unlocking their productivity once they're there.

Its obvious that Pendle is increasingly becoming a fundamental layer for that.

A few developments worth highlighting:

1. From yield tokenisation to broader asset productivity

PTs have already established themselves as a core DeFi primitive for fixed-yield exposure + capital-efficient looping strategies.

With PendleLoop, that utility is expanding beyond traditional yield-bearing assets into leveraged exposure across BTC, ETH + tokenised equities.

Tokenised stock long strategies on @base now integrate borrowing through @aave, (up to ~4.2x leverage) enabling users to trade yield expectations towards helping them deploy capital more efficiently across different asset classes.

2. Becoming a value discovery layer for RWAs

From tokenised treasuries + private credit to AI infrastructure, reinsurance + equities, Pendle has reportedly listed 100+ RWA markets YTD.

*FYI: RWAs now account for >80% of its TVL.

What stands out is the breadth of exposure being brought into DeFi.

As more institutional assets come onchain, Pendle provides a venue where their yields can be priced, traded + incorporated into broader DeFi strategies.

Tokenisation creates asset availability, yield markets help turn that availability into financial utility.

3. Institutional credibility as a compounding advantage

The growing roster of asset managers is particularly notable:

🔸 Janus Henderson (deJAAA)
🔸 Franklin Templeton (FLHYon)
🔸 Partners Group (NGI+)
🔸 Bitwise (PPLUS)

Alongside its RWA Insights series featuring institutions such as Grayscale, Pendle is building relationships with some of the most established names entering tokenised finance.

This matters wayy beyond the immediate TVL contribution.

Institutional relationships bring credibility + differentiated asset supply, which can attract more liquidity, improve market depth + strengthen Pendle's position as a destination for future RWA listings.

And that's where the reinforcing flywheel gets interesting.

More institutional assets → broader yield markets → deeper liquidity + capital utility → greater incentive for new issuers to participate.

Ofc, the flywheel depends on actual market demand + sustainable liquidity, not simply the number of listings.

But the direction is pretty clear.

As tokenised assets proliferate, the opportunity increasingly shifts from who can bring assets onchain to who can make those assets productive.

Pendle is building a pretty compelling position at that intersection.

A 24/7 yield discovery layer for an increasingly onchain financial system.

Best part of this? We're still vv early in this transition.

Pendle 🫡

text:
buybacks are simply just a capital allocation decision

even if hyperliquid allocates 99% of its revenue to buybacks, you shouldnt expect projects to blindly copy that

every dollar of revenue has two obvious destinations: return it to holders or reinvest it into making the business more valuable

imo the right split should constantly change depending on valuation + available reinvestment opportunities

if your token trades at 10x earnings but you can consistently reinvest capital into the product at 30%+ returns, spending everything on buybacks destroys long term value

on the other hand, if the business is already generating huge amounts of cash, the token is cheap and there arent many high return investments left internally, then buying it back aggressively makes perfect sense

"highest buyback percentage wins" is pretty dumb thinking and endgoal should be allocating every dollar wherever it compounds holder value the most

text:
It's pretty interesting thatAI usage can keep growing while some AI businesses become less profitable.

The key is who captures the money, and who carries the risk.

@PanteraCapital’s analysis follows this chain:

Power → Data centers → GPU operators → AI services → Customers

Its illustrative model estimates annual revenue supported by one megawatt of capacity:

- Data centers: ~$2.2 million.
They lease buildings, cooling and power access. Electricity scarcity could support higher rents, but existing 15–20-year leases limit repricing.

- GPU operators: ~$25 million.
They install expensive chips and sell computing capacity. Higher revenue comes with hardware costs, debt and the risk that newer chips reduce older equipment’s earning power.

- AI providers: ~$44 million.
They turn rented computing power into services customers buy, often priced per token, or chunk of text. Their earnings depend on usage, efficiency and competitive pricing.

How to read these numbers: Revenue scales as you stack more service layers on top.

The risk runs upstream:

AI pricing drops → provider margins get pinched → GPU lease obligations come under strain → financing tightens higher up the chain.

text:
昨晚Robinhood公布财报，股价盘后直接跌了7%。

公司第三季度营收创下历史新高，股票、期权、预测市场的交易量也都在刷新纪录。

按理说，这业绩还挺亮眼的。

但翻了翻财报后，发现还真不完全是。

Robinhood现在遇到的最大问题是，来平台交易的人越来越多，交易也越来越频繁，但每笔交易能够赚到的钱，反而在变少。

举几个数字，大家感受一下。

第三季度，Robinhood的股票交易额同比增长53%，但股票交易收入只增长41%。

期权交易量增长48%，收入只增长31%。

最夸张的是预测市场，第三季度一共交易了164亿张事件合约，交易量环比增长超过20%，但收入只增长了约11%。

尤其是预测市场，第二季度平均每张合约大约能带来1.15美分收入，第三季度已经降到1.05美分左右。

别小看这零点1美分的变化，这可是10%的收入下降。

对于一家一个季度处理上百亿张合约的交易平台来说，单位收入哪怕只下降一点点，最终都会变成非常可观的利润差距。

而且，这个交易价差还在进一步收窄。

以前大家买Robinhood，看中的就是它能够把越来越多的散户吸引进来，然后让这些人在平台上不断交易。

但现在却发现，交易量增长和收入增长，在逐渐脱钩。

也就是说，Robinhood想要维持过去那种爆发式增长，就必须不断寻找新的收入来源。

实际上，已经在这么干了。

大家可能不知道，Robinhood现在通过预测市场赚到的钱，已经超过了加密货币交易。

去年第三季度，Robinhood的加密货币收入还有2.68亿美元。

今年呢？只剩1.2亿美元，直接腰斩了55%。

但是另一边，预测市场收入却暴涨超过6倍，达到1.73亿美元。

以前Robinhood靠散户炒比特币赚钱，现在比特币交易有点凉，它又开始靠大家交易体育赛事、经济数据以及各种事件合约赚钱。

甚至从收入增量来看，预测市场这一年新增的钱，几乎刚好填上了加密货币留下的窟窿。

不得不说，Robinhood挖掘新生意的能力确实很强。

但问题也随之而来。

一家金融平台，如果必须不断找到下一个热门交易品种，才能维持增长，那么它到底是一家长期成长的金融科技公司，还是一家高度依赖市场情绪的交易平台？

更何况，预测市场本身也没有看上去那么靠谱。

现在Robinhood的事件合约交易活动，体育相关占据大约七成。

美国部分州的博彩监管机构已经开始盯上这类体育事件合约的合法性。

也就是说，Robinhood如今增长最快的业务之一，恰恰也是监管不确定性相当高的业务。

还有一个更加冷门的数据。

Robinhood有一项业务叫证券借贷。

简单理解，就是客户把自己持有的股票借出去，平台通过证券借贷赚取收入。

去年第三季度，这项业务的净收入还有8700万美元。
今年第三季度，居然变成了负1900万美元。
一年恶化了1.06亿美元。

可奇怪的地方是，同期参与证券出借计划的客户数量增长了30%，相关股票资产规模增长了62%。

这就相当于，你经营一家租车公司，愿意把车交给你出租的车主越来越多，车队规模越来越大。

结果愿意付高价租车的人却变少了，最后不但没多赚钱，反而还亏了。

还有一件很有意思的小事。

管理层在财报会上特别强调，10月份客户净存入资金已经超过130亿美元。
听起来是不是非常厉害？
但仔细一看，其中有60亿美元来自戴尔家族向Trump Accounts儿童账户计划提供的资金。

Robinhood 的盈利能力仍然很强，也确实在不断开拓新业务。

可问题恰恰在于，市场已经给了Robinhood一家高成长金融科技公司的估值，而不是一家普通券商的估值。

当市场用这么高的标准要求你，光是营收创纪录，显然已经不够了。

投资者还希望看到，你的用户越来越多，交易越来越活跃，每个用户创造的利润也越来越高。

现在Robinhood交出来的业绩却是另一回事。

股票交易量大增，单位变现能力下降。
期权交易量大增，单位变现能力下降。
预测市场爆发，单位变现能力同样下降。
加密货币业务缩水，证券借贷净收入转负，信用业务的风险准备还在增加。

Robinhood越来越像一家金融超级平台，但也越来越难仅仅依靠某一项业务，维持过去那种令人惊艳的增长速度。

毕竟，靠市场热闹赚钱是一门好生意，但能够穿越市场冷暖赚钱，才是一家金融巨头真正的护城河。

text:
NEAR Intents generates 6x less in buybacks than needed just to offset NEAR’s L1 inflation.
But that’s not even the biggest problem.

Here’s what I think about the long-term economics of NEAR Intents.

1 Cross-chain is becoming a commodity.
Ten years ago, fast blockchains were exciting. Today, fast and cheap blockspace is simply expected.
Cross-chain is heading in the same direction.
USDT and USDC have their own interoperability solutions. Even Pumpfun recently built its own cross-chain infrastructure.
Stablecoins, apps, and entire ecosystems are building native solutions, fragmenting what once looked like a massive market.

2. Solvers won’t own this market forever.
Today, cross-chain execution relies on solvers, market makers, and liquidity.
But canonical interoperability solutions are evolving. More transfers could eventually rely on cryptography and native infrastructure instead of intermediaries.
For some transactions, costs could approach basic network fees.
Good luck protecting margins in that environment.

3. The addressable market is shrinking.
As more ecosystems build native interoperability, there’s less room for independent cross-chain providers.
Some of the remaining opportunities may eventually be chains without native smart contracts, like Zcash.
But why would Zcash holders keep paying external solvers forever?
Even these ecosystems could develop native solutions, keeping the economic value within their own networks instead of handing margins to third parties.

4. The real prize is becoming essential infrastructure.
NEAR Intents already offers infrastructure that other products can integrate.
But the biggest opportunity is becoming the default interoperability layer embedded directly into protocols, stablecoins, and entire blockchain ecosystems.
The challenge? Many of these ecosystems are building their own canonical solutions instead of relying on external providers.
Being useful is one thing. Becoming indispensable infrastructure is another.

5. And then there’s the NEAR token.
NEAR Intents generates revenue from providing a service, not from NEAR’s token price.
If NEAR doubles in price, the same dollar-denominated buyback budget purchases half as many tokens, making it harder to offset inflation measured in NEAR.
You can’t simply double service fees to compensate. Users would go elsewhere.

The bottom line: NEAR Intents faces three simultaneous pressures.

Shrinking addressable market: Native interoperability reduces opportunities for independent providers.
Shrinking margins: Cross-chain execution becomes cheaper and more commoditized.
Token appreciation: Higher NEAR prices make fixed dollar-denominated buybacks less effective against token inflation.

NEAR Intents may succeed as a product while failing to solve NEAR’s tokenomics.

That’s the real risk. What am I missing?

text:
明天凌晨联储利率决议，不加息大概率关键是沃什怎么表态？10月份多位联储官员的密集表态都在传递一个信号：以"每隔一次会议加息"的节奏推进紧缩——即9月已加息，10月跳过，12月再次加息。

之前纽约联储主席约翰·威廉姆斯明确表示"10月无紧迫行动的必要"，并暗示今年仅剩一次加息；美联储副主席菲利普·杰斐逊称政策制定者可能需要更多时间评估数据；理事沃勒则将这一立场概括为：加息"无需在连续会议上进行，但应在合理时间内到位"。9月FOMC会议纪要同样印证了这一框架：全部19位官员支持9月加息，且"大多数"官员认为年内再加息一次是适当的。

所以这一次FOMC不加息是大概率，但沃什怎么看12月的行动可能是个关键：1）沃什需要向市场解释如何看待通胀走势？
2）他会更多强调通胀将强化曲线平坦化，并推动前端利率继续走高；还是更多强调金融条件收紧则可能令曲线重新陡峭化；
3）看看会不会说类似"任何进一步的利率调整，将取决于数据趋势、前景演变及风险平衡"的表述。还是对政策路径完全保持沉默。

如果联储确实这一次不加息、同时对12月路径比较模糊、对于市场来说就开始关注当下。明天凌晨还是微软和谷歌的财报、如果财报能给到更多AI商业化比市场预期更快的加速趋势。

那么确实可以期待在Anthropic路演之前有一波行情。

$microduck is beginning to gain a kind of exposure that sets it apart from ordinary AI projects.

0xd5f1afea47b1a9eab414d2ee740cf1d6d039e725 

Jensen Huang first interacted with the robots in person at GTC, then mentioned the ducks on X, and Elon Musk also joined the conversation.

Individually, none of these posts seems sufficient to change the project's long-term value.

But when a real product repeatedly enters the public spotlight through high-profile figures, the market has reason to reassess its potential reach.

Of course, I would not treat Jensen Huang mentioning Microduck once, twice, or three times as a linear increase in bullishness. His latest post still revolves around the previous GTC demonstration. It was not a new product launch, and it does not mean that either Jensen or Elon endorses the on-chain token. However, it has given a moment from the original demonstration another opportunity to circulate rather than fade away over time. A single interaction can be a coincidence; repeated mentions can make the market pay attention to the character itself. What ultimately determines the narrative's ceiling is whether it can continue generating content without the help of high-profile figures.

My bullish view on Microduck was never based on the possibility that another prominent person might mention it. It was based on the fact that there is a real physical AI product behind it. Priced at $399, the robot is compact and comes with an open SDK and training framework. Users can teach it to walk, dance, roller-skate, or even perform entirely different movements. It is not limited to following a fixed script in a promotional video. Different users have the opportunity to produce different behaviors with the same robot.

This is what distinguishes Microduck from many projects that attract attention purely through the AI narrative. Ordinary AI Memes often need to keep producing new images, videos, or trending topics to maintain interest. Microduck, by contrast, has a physical product that can continuously generate new material. The movements the robot performs, unexpected outcomes during training, and new ideas developed by users can all become independent pieces of content. The GTC demonstration showcased precisely this potential: the ducks did not execute every instruction perfectly, and their unpredictable reactions made the demonstration more entertaining.

From this perspective, Jensen Huang's exposure changes Microduck's distribution opportunities rather than its underlying product proposition. Previously, it relied mainly on product launches, developer communities, and technology media for attention. Now, the character has an opportunity to reach a much broader social media audience. Elon's interaction added another layer of momentum to the circulation of that content, potentially introducing Microduck to people who otherwise might never have paid attention to Physical AI.

However, the first wave of traffic generated by celebrity attention and the long-term distribution potential of a product are two different things. If the discussion ultimately remains focused on Jensen and Elon interacting with the ducks, the market is still trading a short-term event. If this exposure introduces Microduck to new audiences who then continue following the product and user-generated content, the event could become the starting point of a much longer narrative.

The physical product's sales data also provides some support for this thesis. Earlier reports indicated that Microduck had surpassed 15,000 pre-orders in September, generating more than $6 million in sales. On October 23, TechCrunch reported that pre-orders had subsequently exceeded 20,000 units. It is important to distinguish pre-orders from robots already delivered, and from actual active users. Nevertheless, these figures confirm that Microduck already had a real product and existing pre-order demand before receiving this additional exposure. It is not an empty concept waiting for a celebrity to give it a story.

What matters next is what happens after the first batch of robots reaches customers. If the previously announced delivery schedule proceeds as planned, users could start posting unboxing videos, interactions at home, newly trained movements, and all kinds of unexpected use cases. Some people will teach their ducks to dance; others might put them through gaming challenges, while others will share their training failures. These pieces of content will be created independently, yet they will all revolve around the same recognizable character. Compared with waiting for Jensen to post again, this form of distribution has a better chance of producing a sustained stream of content.

I believe this is the most compelling long-term direction for MICRODUCK: evolving from a physical AI product that has attracted attention into an AI pet that users want to train, showcase, and share. If it really makes its way into more people's lives, Microduck could evolve from a product passively waiting for exposure into a character that actively generates new content. At that point, its distribution would no longer depend entirely on official releases or require an external celebrity to provide every new catalyst.

From the token's perspective, the market has clearly started trading this narrative. The previous rally shows that investors are willing to assign a premium to the combination of a physical AI product, celebrity exposure, and the potential for user-generated content to spread. However, I would not conclude that the fundamental value of MICRODUCK has changed dramatically simply because Jensen mentioned it again and Elon subsequently interacted with the post. There is currently no evidence that the on-chain token entitles holders to a share of the physical product's revenue, commercial rights, or official endorsement. Strong product sales do not automatically mean that customers will buy the token. The connection between the two remains primarily driven by market attention and narrative.

Therefore, I am watching two main catalysts going forward. The first is whether Microduck can generate substantial amounts of authentic user-created content after the first deliveries, allowing the ducks to appear in more than just demonstrations involving a handful of prominent figures. The second is whether Jensen Huang or other high-profile figures mention Microduck again in new contexts, expanding its reach further. The first determines whether the narrative can sustain itself; the second could create another window of exposure. If these two forces begin reinforcing each other, the market will have a stronger reason to reassess the project's potential reach.

Overall, I believe MICRODUCK's narrative fundamentals have strengthened compared with before. Jensen's renewed public mention, Elon's interaction, and growing attention toward the physical product have all increased the likelihood that Microduck will be discovered by a broader audience. However, it still needs to prove that external exposure can translate into sustained user participation, and that these developments can ultimately generate real, lasting demand for the on-chain token.

I am not simply betting on whether Jensen Huang will publish a third post. What I really want to observe is whether people continue making content about Microduck after the current excitement fades. If the answer is yes, it has a chance to evolve from a robotic duck that attracted attention at a technology conference into a recognizable character capable of sustained distribution in the Physical AI space. If all the discussion ultimately returns to the same demonstration video, then even with both Jensen Huang and Elon involved in spreading the content, this rally could still turn out to be a short-term event trade with unusually high visibility.

text: Stay SAFU! 🙏
author: ohyishi
quoted_text:
4 data leaks reported today:

1. Coinbase's vendor Amplitude exposed some users’ contact data (funds unaffected).
2. Bithumb (Korea) had user data leaks.

In TradFi, two securities firms in Korea leaked data: 
3. Mirae Asset
4. Daishin Securities

You can't prevent a leak, but you can protect yourself.

Leaked exchange data (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ID documents, transaction history) is mostly used for phishing, SIM swapping, and social engineering.

Reduce info you share
- Use a unique email alias for each exchange (SimpleLogin, Apple Hide My Email, etc). A leak then can't be linked to your other accounts, and you can spot which service leaked.
- Share only what's required. Don't add optional profile details.
- Use a dedicated phone number (a VoIP or secondary SIM) for exchange accounts if you can, since leaked numbers are the main route to SIM swaps.

Lock down the account
- Use a unique, long password from a password manager.
- Turn on hardware security keys (YubiKey) or passkeys, or at least an authenticator app.
- Avoid SMS 2FA.
- Enable withdrawal address whitelisting and a withdrawal time lock if the exchange offers them.
- Set up an anti-phishing code, which puts a code you choose in every legitimate email from the exchange.
- Review active sessions and API keys regularly. Delete any API keys you don't use.
- Restrict API keys to withdraw-disabled and IP-whitelisted.

Defend against
- SIM swapping: Ask your carrier to add a port-out PIN or number lock.
- Phishing and impersonation: Assume anyone who contacts you about your account, "security issues," or "refund recovery" is a scammer, even if they know your name, balance, or recent trades.
- Exchange support staff don't ask for your password, 2FA codes, or seed phrase.
- Never click links in emails or texts. Go to the site yourself.

- "Wrench attacks": Leaked addresses plus holdings data have led to real-world extortion and robberies. Don't publicize your holdings, and keep large balances out of anything tied to your home address if you can.

If a breach is announced
1. Change the exchange password and any other account that reused it.
2. Check https://t.co/qtIGFkbaPO for your email address.
3. Revoke API keys and active sessions.
4. Review recent withdrawals and security settings.
5. Watch for phishing emails and texts that reference the breach, because scammers move fast after one.

Stay SAFU! 🙏

text:
As part of our contribution to @progmat_en's Tokenized JGB working group - alongside MUFG, Mizuho, BlackRock Japan, and State Street - Zenith validated an end-to-end JGB collateral lifecycle spanning @CantonNetwork and Zenith EVM.

Japan’s JGB repo market processes approximately $1.6 trillion annually. It is one of the largest fixed income markets in the world, and much of its inefficiency comes from the same place: collateral that moves slowly, settlement that takes days, and liquidity that sits idle because the infrastructure to mobilize it in real time doesn’t exist yet.

What we validated is a workflow that addresses exactly that. A tokenized JGB is issued on Canton, purchased against stablecoins in an atomic DvP settlement, deposited as collateral in a Solidity lending protocol on Zenith EVM, monitored in real time from Canton, and ultimately released or liquidated, all within a single coordinated system where Canton remains the compliance and settlement layer throughout.

This is what programmable collateral looks like in practice, institutional assets that can participate in lending markets and liquidity workflows without leaving the environment that governs them.

로이터 설문에서 이코노미스트 100명 중 94명이 오늘 밤 연준이 3.75~4.00%로 금리를 동결할 것으로 봤다. 

시장이 반영한 인상 확률은 10% 안팎이다. 

반면 12월 인상은 100명 전원이 예상했고, 시장은 2027년 9월까지 추가로 75bp 인상을 가격에 넣고 있다.

한 달 전만 해도 GS 트레이딩 데스크는 워시가 9월에 동결하면 역대급 정책 실수가 될 거라고 했는데, 이번엔 인상이 상상조차 안 된다고 말을 바꿨다.

9월 근원 CPI는 전월 대비 0.3%, 전년 대비 2.6%로 뜨거웠지만, 네오클라우드 크레딧이 깨지면서 인상 확률이 무너졌다. 

윌리엄스와 제퍼슨이 연속 인상에 서두를 필요 없다고 했고, 워시도 이를 반박하지 않았다.

JPM 페롤리는 9월에 0.2% 근원 PCE를 보고 올렸던 연준이 0.3%가 예상되는 지금 동결하는 이유를 워시가 설명해야 한다고 했다. 

중간선거 6일 전 동결을 설명 없이 넘기면 정치적 고려라는 의심만 키운다는 경고..

해맥, 로건, 카시카리 세 명의 인상 소수의견도 다시 나올 수 있다.

GS는 12월 한 번 더 올리고 끝이라는 가장 비둘기적인 전망을 유지한다. 

관세, 이란 에너지 쇼크, AI 물가 왜곡이 근원 PCE 초과분 1.1%p를 전부 설명하고, 이것이 설명에서 빠지면 2027년 말 2.2%로 내려온다는 논리다. 

반대로 샌프란시스코 연은 데이터는 현재 인플레이션의 절반이 수요 요인이라고 본다. 

수요 쪽은 기다려서 해결되지 않는다. 

그렇다면 시장이 반영한 세 번의 추가 인상이 틀린 게 아닐 수도 있다.

GS 트레이더들은 하이프리미엄이 거의 빠진 만큼 매파적 동결에도 금리는 추가 랠리 쪽이 조금 더 가능하다고 봤다. 

S&P 500은 올해 FOMC 당일 매번 하락 마감했고, 옵션시장은 이번 회의에 0.62% 움직임만 반영해 4월 이후 가장 낮다. 

FOMC와 빅테크 실적을 넘기면 위험자산에 잠깐 우호적인 구간이 올 수 있지만, 유가와 중간선거, AI 심리가 남아 있어 보호를 깔고 가라는 게 GS의 조언이다.

text:
今天参加了One Earth Summit，以及“人工智能促进共同繁荣”闭门午宴。
这场会的核心，不只是讨论“AI能做什么”，而是讨论如何以人类智慧和公共价值引导AI，通过资本、技术和跨界合作，让AI真正改善人类福祉，并在地球生态边界内实现规模化落地。
今天部分嘉宾的观点与议题让我颇有感触：@WaterDrop_Inc 股东、One Earth Initiatives创始人罗宝文（Poman Lo）说：“可持续不是AI的附加题，而是它的边界条件。” 联合国教科文组织前总干事Irina Bokova的议题提醒大家，AI时代更不能只谈技术，教育、文化与国际合作，是培养下一代负责任领导力、增强社会韧性的长期基础；清华大学校务委员会副主任、清华大学可持续社会价值研究院院长杨斌教授聚焦大学如何革新教育，把科研、人才与产业连接起来，共同回应真实世界的问题；清华大学张亚勤教授关注如何推动AI向善走出实验室，通过科研合作与商业协作实现规模化，让成果更广泛地共享；淡马锡基金会首席执行官黄文雄则让我们看到，公益资本的价值不只是“给钱”，更在于承担经过计算的早期风险，支持创新试点，再通过合作把有效方案规模化。
今天的另一份收获，是与师友相聚：腾讯集团副总裁、水滴公司投资人李朝晖Jeffrey，我在清华上学时的老师杨斌教授，我的好朋友罗宝文，以及水滴公司的合作伙伴、亚洲保险行政总裁兼执行董事Winnie。技术议题让人思考未来，师友相见则让人感到温暖与踏实。真正让未来发生的，从来不只是技术本身，还有价值观、信任与长期合作。
AI时代的“进步”，应该先看模型多强、估值多高，还是看有多少人真正受益？当市场还在观望时，公益资本又是否应该更勇敢地迈出第一步？

text:
Google财报+FOMC 前瞻

因为组里比较忙 因此文章发的晚了一些，不过还算来得及。

正文开始，

明天10月28日，我认为会是这周科技股非常重要的一个交易日，因为FOMC利率决议和GOOGL的Q3财报都在同一天，而且只隔了几个小时

先给大家整理一下时间，全部是美东时间 ET
2:00 PM — FOMC利率决议
2:30 PM — Fed主席Kevin Warsh新闻发布会
4:00 PM以后 — GOOGL公布Q3财报，官方没有指定准确发布时间
4:30 PM — GOOGL Earnings Call

然后根据这个日程表我们不难看出 GOOGL周四的开盘价会同时消化两件事情，一个是Fed对于未来利率的态度，另一个就是Google这次财报到底有没有达到市场预期以及对AI demand本身的暗示

明天先focus on Warsh明天的讲话，这比利率决议本身更重要很多

目前Fed Funds Rate在3.75%-4.00%，9月份刚刚全票加息了25bps，而市场对于明天维持利率不变的定价已经接近九成，所以明天利率大概率是维持不变，这并不会给市场带来任何波动毕竟这个结果大家本来就已经pricing in了

我希望你们去更加关注的是Warsh会不会继续给12月份加息铺路，高利率路径对于高beta板块一直都是十分不友好的；

尤其是目前9月份CPI同比仍然有3.7%，最新非农只增加了2.9万人，通胀压力和就业放缓同时存在；而10Y Treasury yield现在也已经在5%附近一下不到4%的level

所以，我个人对明天FOMC的base case是维持利率不变，但是Warsh不会急着转鸽。

这里如果他继续强调通胀风险，甚至明确暗示12月份还需要加息，那我会重点关注10Y能不能重新站稳5%并继续上涨，我们回到了我们之前一直关注的十分重要的宏观indicator。

我们主要来讲对于google的影响；那么为什么我会着重强调高利率路径的另一个原因就是因为对于GOOGL来说，现在市场最担心的事情之一就是公司未来几年需要投入非常大的AI CAPEX，如果长期利率继续上涨，那么市场给它未来cash flow的valuation也可能继续受到pressure

反过来，如果Warsh开始淡化12月份加息的必要性，或者更多强调就业放缓，我认为科技股会有机会出现一轮valuation recovery，尤其是这几周已经下跌不少的GOOGL

2. 此次GOOGL财报得重点我们怎么看，我更看好Cloud，

但是担心CAPEX

先来看市场预期：

Revenue： 约1279亿美元，YoY +25%
Adjusted EPS： 市场不同数据源约2.94-3.03美元
Google Cloud： 约291亿美元，同比增长接近90%-95%
广告收入： 约835亿美元
2026 CAPEX guidance： 1950-2050亿美元

我个人预判，GOOGL这次revenue和Cloud有机会小幅beat，EPS大概率在市场预期附近；但是CAPEX我反而更加担心继续上修

为什么？我的推断依据是什么？

因为Google Cloud上一季度已经增长82%，backlog也达到了5140亿美元，说明AI相关需求确实还在增长

但是呢，市场现在对于Cloud的预期已经接近90%-95%的YoY growth了，所以明天即使Google公布一个非常漂亮的增长数字，也不代表股价一定上涨

就比如如果Cloud做到300亿美元，确实比市场预期高了一些，但是管理层同时宣布2027年CAPEX还要继续大幅提高，而FCF短期又没有明显改善，我认为市场可能根本不会给予这部分revenue beat太多奖励

尤其是根据目前的预测，2027年Google的CAPEX可能达到3000亿美元左右，这已经是非常惊人的capital investment了

而且我还会特别关注Cloud的operating margin，市场目前预期大概在33.5%附近

我希望看到的是Cloud增长的同时margin也能守住，因为收入增长90%，但是需要通过大量新增投入才能维持这种增长，和Cloud revenue增长的同时operating leverage开始改善，最后反映到EPS上的结果会差很多
所以对于这份财报，我看好Google Cloud继续增长的confidence，要明显高于我对GOOGL财报后直接上涨的confidence

3. 接下来我对GOOGL财报后的三个走势预判

GOOGL今天10月27日收在320.58美元，期权市场目前给这次财报定价的波动大概是±6%，也就是约301-340美元。

下面是我自己对三种情况的主观预判。

乐观情况：30%，340-353美元

如果Google Cloud直接做到310亿美元以上，backlog相比之前5140亿美元继续明显增长，同时Cloud margin没有恶化，管理层又能够给出比较清楚的cash flow改善路径，那我认为GOOGL有机会重新回到340美元以上。

这里我会先看345，突破以后关注350-353，这个区域也是我的工具箱目前给出的强压力区

不过要达到350以上，需要大约9%的上涨，已经超过目前options pricing的±6%，所以我认为需要非常明显的earnings surprise，或者Fed同时带来比较大的利率利好

中性情况：40%，310-332美元

这个其实是我现在更加倾向的结果。

Google的revenue和Cloud小幅超预期，但是CAPEX继续维持在高位，管理层对于2027年的投入也没有给出明显更乐观的现金回报预期

这种情况下，我认为市场可能会认可Google业务增长，但是不愿意马上提高它的valuation

股价先看310-332的震荡区间，其中308-314也是工具箱给出的第一层support

悲观情况：30%，289-302美元

这里我最担心的是Cloud revenue低于预期，或者operating margin不及预期，同时管理层又大幅提高2027年的CAPEX forecast

如果再叠加Warsh明天继续hawkish，10Y重新明显上涨，那我会提高这个悲观scenario的权重

因为这时候Google面对的就不只是财报miss，市场还会同时降低对于未来earnings愿意支付的P/E

技术面上我会先看308能不能守住，跌穿以后就直接看300附近，296也是一个需要关注的位置。

不过289-302这个区域已经超过了期权市场目前定价的正常财报波动下沿，我认为需要Cloud和CAPEX同时出现明显不利的信息，才更有理由去看这么深

如果悲观情景发生并且市场在300的位置出现承接，我会毫不犹豫地额外补仓，Google目前是我认为在未来能够超越nvda成为第一市值的公司；我会专门在后面写详细的长文分析和思路

4. 明天我自己的重点判断

我目前对GOOGL的基本面依然偏乐观，尤其是Google Cloud和Search的赚钱能力，但是对于这份财报，我没有非常强的看涨股价预期。

主要因为市场现在对Cloud增长的预期已经很高，而且Google的AI CAPEX也确实到了需要开始认真计算它的capital return的阶段

如果明天Fed维持利率不变，Warsh没有进一步hawkish，Google Cloud又能够明显beat，同时margin守住，我会把340-353作为主要上涨观察区。
如果FOMC偏鹰，Google财报又只是小幅beat，CAPEX继续增加，我反而更倾向股价先测试310附近，甚至300。

这里我比较看重的是什么呢？不是google明天能不能多赚一点revenue，却是google的管理层到底有没有办法让未来每年接近2000亿，甚至3000亿美元的AI投入，逐渐转化成更强的earnings和free cash flow

因为这份财报如果只是告诉市场Cloud继续增长，但是未来还需要花更多的钱，GOOGL就很可能继续面临和上个季度类似的valuation pressure

overall，所以我个人对明天的预判与思路是，FOMC大概率不会给科技股太大的正面surprise，GOOGL财报的Cloud可能不错，但是CAPEX仍然是决定它能不能真正反弹的最大变量。320.58这个价格 目前的期权已经偏贵并且外加今天的整体科技盘涨幅，我并不会提前埋伏财报。

KEYSTONE TO DESTROY 18,835 HARDWARE WALLETS AFTER HACKERS STEAL DEVICE AUTHENTICATION KEY

Keystone has confirmed it will destroy 18,835 hardware wallets in existing inventory after attackers stole the cryptographic key used to verify the authenticity of its devices.

The breach is particularly concerning because the stolen key could allow attackers to manufacture counterfeit Keystone wallets that successfully pass the company's official authenticity checks, potentially putting users' Bitcoin at risk.

The key is permanently embedded in existing devices and cannot be erased or replaced, forcing Keystone to destroy its remaining inventory, suspend shipments and manufacture new devices with a replacement key.

The company says attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party monitoring tool on its official website on October 20, gaining access to:

- 25,964 customer records containing names, contact details, shipping addresses and purchase information.

- 12,873 abandoned checkout records containing potentially sensitive customer information.

Keystone also acknowledged that its automated data deletion system had failed, leaving customer information stored beyond its stated retention period.

The company says recovery phrases, private keys and transaction signing were not compromised.

Devices delivered before October 20 remain unaffected, but customers receiving devices with the old authentication key after that date are advised to seek additional verification.

Keystone has suspended shipments, begun notifying affected customers and is moving production to a new authentication key.

text:
I think people don't understand the structure of the gap. There are multiple components, and "benchmaxing" in the naive sense, direct training on test or its narrow paraphrases or reconstructions in case of private evals, is trivial. The interesting gap on most of these metrics now comes from the coverage of problems by RL, both in terms of effective compute (so, for example, DeepSeek with V4.1 can afford like 16-50x more trajectories per GPU-hour compared to Kimi with K3.1) and, even more importantly, in the sense of quality of environments (tasks, grading, guards against reward hacking). Data is upstream of the function gain here.
A lab with a high-quality internal research program and sufficient resources may still get set back by the eval refresh, because the base models are weak, because the tasks get intrinsically harder, because they haven't yet collected enough data for tasks in this regime, because they just haven't dedicated enough RL to this new distribution of tasks. But such a lab doesn't need a lot of effort to upgrade, they're already doing it, they will catch up quickly, and their current model will likely decline relatively less. A lab whose internal program is less advanced and more reactive will fall off harder, and will struggle more to catch up.

This allows us to make some interesting comparisons.
As we see here, V4.1F-0910 and 1017 score identically on FrontierCode 1.1 (≈44%), and diverge heavily on FrontierCode 2.0 (19.3% vs 28.5%).
This is a gain over 37 days.
K3 did 43.6% on 1.1 and 17.1% on 2.0. 
Kimi K3.1 scores 47.1% on FrontierCode 1.1, and 25.5% on 2.0.
This is a gain over ≈97 days. 
(though adjust for noise, Cognition != AA)

Nominally, 44 is not far from 47, and 25 is not far from 28. But I think the direction of delta, as well as the timeline, matter. We can assume both labs target this broad capability basin to a similar extent. FrontierCode 1.1 was released on July 7, ≈10 days before Kimi K3's debut and months before V4.1. By October, we can expect that both labs have hill-climbed it about as much as their resources and model allowed. But Kimi's climb has been narrower, so they got *higher* on 1.1 and fell off *harder* on 2.0. 1017 doesn't gain on 0910 whatsoever on 1.1 – which suggests that DeepSeek weren't even going after it with this release, they dedicated extra resources to new aspects of quality (here, product-grade mergeability), were expanding their RL pipeline, and perhaps have better understanding of the direction in which the frontier propagates.

The MiMo story and GLM story would benefit from more comparison points, but the logic is similar to Kimi's.

I recommend reading the post below to understand my perspective better.

https://t.co/IdPvwRg8eg

My specific reason to think that Lisan's projection for the Chinese trend is wrong (irrespective of the gap convergence/divergence that's dependent on American acceleration):
Kimi K3's ECI is pulled down almost entirely by Frontier Math, just like scores of Chinese models have historically been pulled down by underperformance on the latest frontier Americans are expanding (simple math, coding, agentic work); they always catch up on that frontier on the next iteration. On the other hand, K3 greatly outperforms its score on PostTrainBench (we have good reasons to suspect that US labs are sandbagging it though) because Kimi is AGI-pilled and are making the machine that makes the machine, which is the most frontier thing of all.

OpenAI is great at FM because of 1) compute and 2) Ph.D level data annotation for mafs (likewise for Anthropic and GDM – Gemini 3.1 Pro, which Lisan rightfully despises, is still top tier on ECI largely because of mafs). Chinese labs are becoming OOMs richer and also scaling RL compute. Soon enough there'll be a data provider who monetizes all these underpaid Chinese Ph.Ds and sells their data in bulk to Kimi/DS/etc (this likely already happens to an extent). Just like Kimi went 8%-10%-24% on CritPT (and GLM went 4%-5%-21%), we may see a discontinuous jump on those crippled subsets.
K3 scores 39% on Frontier Math Tier 4, up from 26% in K2.6 (K2.7 Code inexplicably collapsed to 12%). Lisan fits to get a 155.53 estimate. So let's say K3.1 only improves on FMt4, to the level of Opus 4.8 (56%). This alone would get us ECI = 156.734, ie between GPT 5.4 and 5.4 Pro. If they get to parity with 5.4 Pro (xhigh) on FMt4, that's ECI≈158, ie between Opus 4.8 and 5.6 Terra.

Sol has 161.82. It's a long way to Sol. But looking at Luna, I think they'll get there faster than it seems possible now.

quoted_text:
4 data leaks reported today:

1. Coinbase's vendor Amplitude exposed some users’ contact data (funds unaffected).
2. Bithumb (Korea) had user data leaks.

In TradFi, two securities firms in Korea leaked data: 
3. Mirae Asset
4. Daishin Securities

You can't prevent a leak, but you can protect yourself.

Leaked exchange data (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ID documents, transaction history) is mostly used for phishing, SIM swapping, and social engineering.

Reduce info you share
- Use a unique email alias for each exchange (SimpleLogin, Apple Hide My Email, etc). A leak then can't be linked to your other accounts, and you can spot which service leaked.
- Share only what's required. Don't add optional profile details.
- Use a dedicated phone number (a VoIP or secondary SIM) for exchange accounts if you can, since leaked numbers are the main route to SIM swaps.

Lock down the account
- Use a unique, long password from a password manager.
- Turn on hardware security keys (YubiKey) or passkeys, or at least an authenticator app.
- Avoid SMS 2FA.
- Enable withdrawal address whitelisting and a withdrawal time lock if the exchange offers them.
- Set up an anti-phishing code, which puts a code you choose in every legitimate email from the exchange.
- Review active sessions and API keys regularly. Delete any API keys you don't use.
- Restrict API keys to withdraw-disabled and IP-whitelisted.

Defend against
- SIM swapping: Ask your carrier to add a port-out PIN or number lock.
- Phishing and impersonation: Assume anyone who contacts you about your account, "security issues," or "refund recovery" is a scammer, even if they know your name, balance, or recent trades.
- Exchange support staff don't ask for your password, 2FA codes, or seed phrase.
- Never click links in emails or texts. Go to the site yourself.

- "Wrench attacks": Leaked addresses plus holdings data have led to real-world extortion and robberies. Don't publicize your holdings, and keep large balances out of anything tied to your home address if you can.

If a breach is announced
1. Change the exchange password and any other account that reused it.

ohm does demonstrate that the reserve cant establish or sustain a monetary premium. on this we agree

ore still has to establish lasting monetary demand. but i think the reserve can support this

CONFIRMED. Gas Standing Charges to be scrapped. I've just come out of a meeting with the Chancellor. The gas standing charge will be scrapped in 2027 (my guess, either for 1 Oct price cap or the 1 Jan 28 price cap). Having campaigned against the moral hazard of standing charges for years, I'm pleased.

It's currently £108 a year. That cost will be shifted onto unit rates. We don't know how much yet, but I suspect just under 1p per kwH.

The Chancellor also said he will be talking to Ofgem about how they get rid of the charge on electricity as well, but that is 'trickier' apparently and will take longer.

This is primarily about the price cap standing charges. There will still be an open market, so other firms can offer other forms of prices with or without the standing charge. My suspicion is that once it goes on the price cap, it will tend to be reduced on other tariffs as well.

As for those on fixes: if you get a fix now, the rate of your fix is fixed, so this should not affect it. You will pay what you pay and if it has standing charges they will continue (some asking if they should delay fixing because of this, no if a fix is right for you and will save you money, don't let this change that - this is about the structure of bills, as opposed to the actual costs on bills).

About 60% of people will pay less due to this, 40% more. My guesstimate is the dividing line will be somewhere around 12,500 kilowatt hours of gas (can't know until there is actual pricing). According to a study by Nesta, this switch would leave the majority of people in all income groups under £100,000 better off.

Of course, when this does come in, if we're still in the nightmare that we are right now, there will need to be support put in for vulnerable higher users, who will have to pay more. Though hopefully by then the mid-east will have calmed and energy prices lower. 
---------------

That's all long term. The biggest issue in energy right now is that we're expecting a 27% rise in the price cap in January. I asked the Chancellor whether he will be intervening on that. He told me I'd have to wait for the budget, but reading between the lines, yes, there will be an announcement today. 

Whether it's an increase in the Warm Home Discount, or whether it's council tax banned, or whether it's done via a payout for people in say council tax bands A-D as a proxy for household income as Rishi Sunak did who knows.

text:
I think people don't understand the structure of the gap. There are multiple components, and "benchmaxing" in the naive sense, direct training on test or its narrow paraphrases or reconstructions in case of private evals, is trivial. The interesting gap on most of these metrics now comes from the coverage of problems by RL, both in terms of effective compute (so, for example, DeepSeek with V4.1 can afford like 16-50x more trajectories per GPU-hour compared to Kimi with K3.1) and, even more importantly, in the sense of quality of environments (tasks, grading, guards against reward hacking). Data is upstream of the function gain here.
A lab with a high-quality internal research program and sufficient resources may still get set back by the eval refresh, because the base models are weak, because the tasks get intrinsically harder, because they haven't yet collected enough data for tasks in this regime, because they just haven't dedicated enough RL to this new distribution of tasks. But such a lab doesn't need a lot of effort to upgrade, they're already doing it, they will catch up quickly, and their current model will likely decline relatively less. A lab whose internal program is less advanced and more reactive will fall off harder, and will struggle more to catch up.

This allows us to make some interesting comparisons.
As we see here, V4.1F-0910 and 1017 score identically on FrontierCode 1.1 (≈44%), and diverge heavily on FrontierCode 2.0 (19.3% vs 28.5%).
This is a gain over 37 days.
K3 did 43.6% on 1.1 and 17.1% on 2.0. 
Kimi K3.1 scores 47.1% on FrontierCode 1.1, and 25.5% on 2.0.
This is a gain over ≈97 days. 
(though adjust for noise, Cognition != AA)

Nominally, 44 is not far from 47, and 25 is not far from 28. But I think the direction of delta, as well as the timeline, matter. We can assume both labs target this broad capability basin to a similar extent. FrontierCode 1.1 was released on July 7, ≈10 days before Kimi K3's debut and months before V4.1. By October, we can expect that both labs have hill-climbed it about as much as their resources and model allowed. But Kimi's climb has been narrower, so they got *higher* on 1.1 and fell off *harder* on 2.0. 1017 doesn't gain on 0910 whatsoever on 1.1 – which suggests that DeepSeek weren't even going after it with this release, they dedicated extra resources to new aspects of quality (here, product-grade mergeability), were expanding their RL pipeline, and perhaps have better understanding of the direction in which the frontier propagates.

The MiMo story and GLM story would benefit from more comparison points, but the logic is similar to Kimi's.

I recommend reading the post below to understand my perspective better.

https://t.co/IdPvwRg8eg

quoted_text:
My specific reason to think that Lisan's projection for the Chinese trend is wrong (irrespective of the gap convergence/divergence that's dependent on American acceleration):
Kimi K3's ECI is pulled down almost entirely by Frontier Math, just like scores of Chinese models have historically been pulled down by underperformance on the latest frontier Americans are expanding (simple math, coding, agentic work); they always catch up on that frontier on the next iteration. On the other hand, K3 greatly outperforms its score on PostTrainBench (we have good reasons to suspect that US labs are sandbagging it though) because Kimi is AGI-pilled and are making the machine that makes the machine, which is the most frontier thing of all.

OpenAI is great at FM because of 1) compute and 2) Ph.D level data annotation for mafs (likewise for Anthropic and GDM – Gemini 3.1 Pro, which Lisan rightfully despises, is still top tier on ECI largely because of mafs). Chinese labs are becoming OOMs richer and also scaling RL compute. Soon enough there'll be a data provider who monetizes all these underpaid Chinese Ph.Ds and sells their data in bulk to Kimi/DS/etc (this likely already happens to an extent). Just like Kimi went 8%-10%-24% on CritPT (and GLM went 4%-5%-21%), we may see a discontinuous jump on those crippled subsets.
K3 scores 39% on Frontier Math Tier 4, up from 26% in K2.6 (K2.7 Code inexplicably collapsed to 12%). Lisan fits to get a 155.53 estimate. So let's say K3.1 only improves on FMt4, to the level of Opus 4.8 (56%). This alone would get us ECI = 156.734, ie between GPT 5.4 and 5.4 Pro. If they get to parity with 5.4 Pro (xhigh) on FMt4, that's ECI≈158, ie between Opus 4.8 and 5.6 Terra.

Sol has 161.82. It's a long way to Sol. But looking at Luna, I think they'll get there faster than it seems possible now.

The Restore Britain Budget.

Britain has spent decades being governed by politicians who believe the answer to every problem is yet more government - that policy has destroyed our country.

More spending. More borrowing. More regulation. More taxes. More state.

Parasitic overreach into our lives - delivered by politicians and civil servants who have no understanding or appreciation of how real wealth and opportunity is generated in the private sector.

And what have the British people received in return?

A country where working families struggle. Where businesses face punishing costs. Where young people cannot afford homes. Where failing public services demand ever more money, whilst prioritising endless third world migrants. Where inflation runs rampant.

For British men and women, it is a government-backed scam. Corrupt incompetence.

It is impossible for Britain to tax itself into prosperity. I repeat, IMPOSSIBLE.

Wealth is created by people - the public sector should exist to support the private sector, not the reverse and that is the principle which underpins our philosophy.

Restore Britain backs the farmer producing food, the white van man driving the economy, the engineer designing machinery, the shopkeeper serving customers and the entrepreneur risking everything to start a business.

It comes down to this - Restore Britain will protect their freedom to succeed.

If you work hard and contribute, we are on your side.

Our Budget would begin the work of returning power, responsibility and money to the British people.

First, the spending cuts - to come before ANY reductions in tax.

Our 20 point plan to restore prosperity…

1. Freeze working-age benefit rates.

We will freeze working-age benefit rates for the duration of the first Parliament. Britain cannot indefinitely increase expenditure without considering the burden on the people funding it. That would be morally wrong. The healthy indolent will not be rewarded.

2. Restrict welfare eligibility.

No more benefits for foreigners, saving billions. No need to expand.

3. Reform sickness and disability benefits

We will overhaul eligibility, assessment procedures and return-to-work support.

People with serious disabilities and health conditions must receive appropriate protection.

But those who can work, will work. If they refuse, they will be put to work. That simple.

4. Reform pensions.

We will protect the State Pension while replacing the triple lock with annual CPI uprating. Public-sector pension arrangements will be overhauled to address differences with private-sector provision.

These measures will save tens of billions - all outlined in full in our economic paper, The Wealth Of Our Nation.

Next, take an axe to unnecessary government spending

5. The quango bonfire.

We will conduct a comprehensive review of arm's-length public bodies, the default will be abolish unless there is a serious reason to retain. Where its functions duplicate a government department, consolidate them. Deliver accountability and savings. AI will mean vast cuts are possible.

A LOT of Whitehall civil servants will lose their jobs. To be frank.

6. Freeze most departmental budgets.

We will introduce a three-year nominal spending freeze across most government departments - the main exception will be our programme of mass deportations, which in the short term will cost, however as we know, any immediate funds will be quickly recovered and then some.

7. End public spending on Net Zero.

We will end all public expenditure directed towards achieving Net Zero. Energy security will be our main priority. We will support investment in dependable domestic energy supplies, including the infrastructure needed to maintain a resilient electricity system. Energy security will be placed above any ideological dogma. If it makes Britain more resilient, we will pursue it.

8. Review government consultancy and discretionary expenditure.

We will audit consultancy contracts, procurement services, and ALL external advisory work - spending that cannot demonstrate a clear public benefit should end.

The procurement scam will end.

All bullshit ESG and social value nonsense will be stripped away - if the public sector wants to use a third party firm, make it the best one - subject to right-to-work checks to ensure no illegals are being employed.

As stated - spending cuts first, then tax cuts. Done carefully and responsibly. Here’s an overview of how a Restore Britain Government will lift the tax burden…

9. Raise the income tax personal allowance to £16,000.

Nobody should be paying income tax on their first £16,000 of earnings.

We will raise the personal allowance and extend the basic-rate income tax band to £100,000.

We will also restore the full personal allowance to higher earners, ending the withdrawal that creates exceptionally high effective marginal tax rates.

Success will be rewarded, hard work will be rewarded, ambition will be rewarded.

10. Cut corporation tax.

We will introduce a zero corporation tax rate on the first £50,000 of company profits.

Above that threshold, we will restore the headline rate to 19%, with a longer-term ambition of 15%. As soon as fiscal conditions allow.

Let’s give small businesses the genuine breathing room to get their operation off the ground, and then use the corporation tax cut to compete with our neighbours.

11. Abolish inheritance tax and stamp duty.

Families should not be punished for saving, investing and passing assets to their children.

We will abolish inheritance tax.

For farmers, for family businesses, for everyone.

The state has no claim to a family's lifetime of accumulated wealth simply because somebody has died. I detest it. It will be binned for all.

Stamp duty makes moving home more expensive, discourages mobility and creates unnecessary friction in the housing market.

We will abolish it.

12. Reduce disruptive tax.

We will cut the standard rate of VAT from 20% to 18%.

We will also raise the VAT registration threshold to £150,000, helping smaller businesses grow without immediately facing additional tax burden. The amount of businesses hovering just under the current threshold is painful. The issue is OBVIOUS, yet nobody in government has thought to act.

And we will ditch unnecessary taxes.

We will abolish:
Insurance Premium Tax.
Air Passenger Duty.
The Climate Change Levy.
The UK Emissions Trading Scheme.

We will also substantially increase the annual Capital Gains Tax exemption.

Restore Britain’s objective is a tax system that is simpler, more predictable and less hostile to investment.

Next, we will restore a state that works for our people.

13. Hold the NHS accountable.

The NHS will remain free at the point of use for British citizens.

We propose charging non-citizens at market rates - ensuring they actually pay the bills.

We will make private healthcare expenditure tax deductible. If people want to go private, let’s make it cheaper.

Alongside far-reaching structural reform, we will demand basic improvements in patient communication. Answer the telephone. Confirm referrals. Explain test results. Keep patients informed. Use AI to clear pressure on GPs.

All patient-facing staff must demonstrate the English-language communication skills necessary to perform their roles safely. If staff can’t speak English to the required standard, they will no longer have a job.

14. Restore Britain’s education system.

We will move towards greater school-level autonomy, with funding more closely linked to pupil numbers.

We will remove VAT from private education and make private education tax deductible.

We will also promote practical education, apprenticeships and stronger links between schools and employers. The aim will be to prepare children for working adulthood - full paper to come.

Apprenticeships are vital - my businesses have developed hundreds and hundreds. It works, especially with the rise of AI.

Student loan interest abolished for British nationals resident in the UK, full paper published.

An overhaul of childcare regulation and funding - led by those in the sector who know what’s necessary and what’s not.

Next.

The Restore Britain Budget will work to restore a self-sufficient Britain, backed by sovereign AI capabilities.

15. Support British farming and food security.

We will review the regulatory and tax burdens facing British farmers.

Food security must be recognised as a matter of national resilience and urgency. That will be central to everything.

We will make it FAR easier for domestic producers to compete for public-sector food contracts and examine ways to reduce unnecessary administration. Let’s use the public sector spend to back our own people, not import from foreign farmers.

Britain should not become increasingly dependent on imported food while making it harder for its own farmers to survive. And we desperately need to bring more young people into the industry…

16. Ease pressure on transport network.

We will rebuild Britain's transport network, tackling potholes, congestion and crumbling infrastructure while improving vital freight routes and rural roads - motorists will no longer be treated as cash cows. Fuel duty cut, and plenty more. (Full paper about to be published.)

Get this right, and the whole economy is lubricated.

17. Back small businesses.

We will review regulations introduced over recent decades, with a presumption in favour of removing law. Compliance simplified, licensing stripped back. Administrative burdens burned away. Scrap IR35, obviously.

Business rates abolished for small high street businesses. Review car park charges. Boost police numbers in town centres.

Restore confidence on the high street. Bring footfall back. Watch businesses thrive.

18. Develop sovereign AI capability.

AI is coming whether we like it or not. We need to ensure that we have our own protected AI capability which can promote and defend our own interests. We’re already falling behind, and it’s getting worse. We have the opportunity to be a genuine world-leader. Let’s pursue it.

19. A foreign policy that puts Britain’s interests first.

No endless foreign wars driving up the cost of living for ordinary families, no foreign aid unless explicitly to advance our interests. We will prioritise national security, trade, energy independence and protecting British citizens abroad.

Spending will be increased, but our armed forces exist to defend Britain and our vital national interests, not to act as the world's policeman.

20. Protect sound money and fiscal stability. This is the most important of all.

We will pursue a balanced Budget over the medium term and a declining debt-to-GDP ratio. Our aim is to cut the debt, not just the deficit.

The era of mass money printing will end. Inflation will be controlled. The cost-of-living reduced.

The aim - a Britain that belongs to its people

Every Budget promises change, while the state grows larger and the taxpayer becomes poorer.

Restore Britain offers a completely different direction.

A smaller government that spends less - all helped by a massive reduction in the number of migrants living in Britain.

Doing a small list of things, but doing them well.

A welfare state that protects genuine need and expects personal responsibility.

A tax system that rewards work, saving and enterprise.

Public services that answer to the people who fund them.

An economy built on productive businesses rather than a parasitic state.

We do not believe the British people need politicians to manage every aspect of their lives.

We believe they need the freedom to build better lives for themselves.

In short - we will stop buying votes with other people’s money.

Our ambition is not to make government richer.

It is to restore the prosperity of the British economy, the British nation and the British people.

text:
This is why @ZIGFinance matters. The people helping drive the world’s growth should have a fair opportunity to invest in it.

Some of the world’s largest companies have built their businesses around global participation. We should be asking why participation in their upside remains so uneven.

These companies shape how we communicate, work and build businesses. People across emerging markets buy their products, pay their subscriptions and build entire businesses around their technology. Governments spend taxpayers’ money on their infrastructure and services.

Over decades, that spending supports revenues, profits, dividends and shareholder wealth.

A business owner can pay for the software powering a global company’s growth every month and still face considerable friction trying to invest in its success.

Why should we accept that gap as permanent?

I come from banking and have benefited from the relationships and access this system rewards. That experience makes me more conscious of how differently it treats someone without those advantages.

Investors should be able to decide what exposure they want, how they want to invest and which provider they trust. Different people will choose different products and structures based on their circumstances.

Brokers, fund managers and platforms have built entire businesses around providing access to markets. Tokenization creates more ways to serve that demand. Let businesses compete on access, cost, convenience and transparency, and let investors choose.

Of course the money must be lawful, investors must meet the applicable requirements and people must understand what they are buying. Those protections should support a market where informed choices are possible.

Tokenization can bring more participants and capital into markets, create additional sources of liquidity and support price discovery across venues. It can make investment products easier to distribute and transactions easier to inspect.

Companies should scrutinise how their shares are represented and raise specific concerns. We should also scrutinise restrictions that prevent eligible investors from choosing how to participate.

This is why ZIG Finance matters to me. We are working to connect real financial opportunities with people who have been poorly served by existing channels.

text:
"You just need to treat marketing like a science"

Rite of passage for all consumer marketers
author: benaratame
quoted_text:
2 years ago, i had done zero marketing. i'd been an engineer my entire life.

when i told a founder friend we were building a consumer product, he told me, "tanay, you don't have that consumer dna. you don't know how to build a brand. you shouldn't do this."

it sounded like a fun challenge. game on. 

2 months after we pivoted Wispr from hardware to Flow, our first launch did millions of views and hit #1 on product hunt for the day and the week.

what i've learned about marketing since:

1/ take almost no inspiration from others. standing out means doing things your own way. be unique and bold in your decisions. 

2/ pick your first users by who will cause PLG. hundreds of avatars of people loved wispr flow. we focused on 2. developers, because they post about tools they love everywhere. founders, because they roll them out to their whole team.

3/ make every user feel it was built for people like them. most tools assume american english. in wispr you can pick british english, swiss german, or simplified vs traditional chinese

4/ build small moments that make people feel seen. in india, after you've spoken 1,000 words in an indian language, a banner says congratulations in that language, with the flag

5/ do pr even if you can't measure it. if i put its roi in a spreadsheet, the column would be empty. but asking what i'd pitch a journalist about every new feature gives us a lot of our ad ideas

6/ make the message something you can see, touch, feel. have fun with it. we said we'd kill the keyboard, so i sawed one in half in our office for a launch video

7/ treat word of mouth as a science, not an art. after we hit product-market fit, the first thing we optimized for was getting every user to tell their friends

turns out you don't need consumer dna or to be the most creative. you just need to treat marketing like a science.

Rumors I’ve been hearing. I’ll start with OpenAI, then Anthropic.

OpenAI: The internal model’s reasoning jump comes from more aggressive RL, including training in games and simulated environments. Strategies learned there transfer to research mathematics and other fields. Navier–Stokes and ETH show the scale of the improvement. The clue is in the Synthetic RL hiring: self-play, simulators, and synthetic feedback.

Anthropic: Same direction with its internal Claude model. It’s trained on long, difficult tasks in demanding environments, and the reasoning skills transfer to other fields. Its ETH result shows how far the improvement has gone. The earlier Universes listing and the RL hiring around mathematical reasoning align with that.

Musk’s Digital Optimus hiring explicitly calls for measuring transfer from games into general computer use. That’s why his game-playing AI push matters: games develop abilities that work far beyond the games themselves.

The interesting part is where those abilities show up. Each lab’s internal model applies reasoning developed through interactive training to mathematical problems that had resisted decades of work.

text:
which VC raises next?

a few weeks ago @murphcapital mapped who backed the 25 hottest AI companies. our hypothesis was that a stake in OpenAI/Anthropic makes the next fundraise easier, so we tested it.

in our Q3 fundraising data, managers holding at least one of the top 25 closed 26 of 152 funds (17%) but took $28.8B, or 63% of the $46.0B raised. they also come back bigger: of the 24 managers from our map we could size, 21 raised more than last time, a median of 1.3x.

that could just be scale, since the biggest VCs hold the biggest names, so we widened the set. we used @harmonic_ai and pulled 1,889 venture-backed AI startups and their investors, and kept the 429 US VCs that hold at least 3 of them and filed at least one fund with the SEC in 2023–24.

for each one we compared new funds filed in 2025–26 with 2023–24 (counted funds only, with no SPVs or feeders, and only top-25 stakes bought before 2025):

1/ no top-25 stake: 43% fewer new funds. 4+ stakes: 35% more.
2/ after controlling for portfolio size and prior activity, holding even one of the top 25 nearly doubles the odds of getting a new fund done (1.8x).
3/ stakes bought in 2025 or later, tested separately, made no measurable difference. only the early ones did.

holders also come back faster. among the 429, managers with no stake took a median of 34 months to file their next fund after a 2023–24 raise. with 2–3 stakes it was 23 months, with 4+ it was 20. part of that is size: after controls, holders are 1.3x as likely to come back in any given month, a borderline result.

to time the next raises, we pulled Form D filings back to 2009 for the 26 managers on our map that raise in cycles: 215 raises, with a typical gap of 18 months. 7 closed new funds last quarter (~$18B, 40% of Q3), and 11 more are already back in market. our calls:

> dragoneer files next, likely in January. it raises every 18 months, and Opportunities VII started in July 2025.
> @lightspeedvp follows by spring. its median gap is 27 months, and its last fund started in December 2024.
> @ThriveHoldings is back by mid-2027, and bigger. every fund since 2011 has outgrown the last, up to $10B today. the last gap was 14 months.
> @Accel now raises on rotation: Growth VII in December 2024, Leaders V in December 2025, Accel XVII and Growth VIII in August 2026. next up around August 2027.
> @a16z won’t wait for a full cycle. 7 months after its $15B, it launched a $1.1B AI hardware fund and topped up Growth V with $1.75B. next platform raise around the end of 2027.
> @foundersfund is the wildcard. Growth IV came just 11 months after Growth III. its usual cycle points to late 2028, its latest pace to 2027.
> @benchmark sits at the back of the queue. It raises every 3 years, so the next one lands in mid-2029.

who do you think we got wrong?

Binance 和  Coinbase 可谓是冰火两重天

Binance 现货以主动买入为主导，Coinbase 现货以主动卖出为主导；两边的投资者行为表现截然相反。

当BTC回调至$79,500时，Binance 的BTC余额突然减少了15,436 枚 ；而此刻，Coinbase 的余额却增加了 5,686枚 BTC。

说明在当前环境下，不同区域的资金出现了明显分歧。一部分正在积极承接筹码，另一部分仍在寻求退出。

难道这就是传说中的“东西方对立”？

按这个趋势，决定方向就看Binance的买盘能否持续？亦或是Coinbase的卖压何时衰减？

如果Coinbase的卖压逐渐耗尽，而Binance的买方依然强势，那$79,500就有可能成为新一轮供需关系转变的重要节点。

底部的形成可以始于有人愿意承接抛压；而趋势的反转却需要更多资金形成共识。

毕竟，仅靠一个市场的买盘，很难长期对抗另一个市场持续释放的压力。

text:
项目方怎么熬过漫漫熊市？

市场唯一不变的就是一直在变化，尤其是资本市场，尤其是币圈，资金流动快叙事变得也快，假设你 21 年想做项目应该怎么办呢？

- 21 年的时候都在做 DeFi，连游戏也比必须是 GameFi，所以你需要做 DeFi

- 22 年 DAO 火了，所以很多项目在 22 年转型 DAO，而且也认为 DAO 是未来，如果那个时候要搞事情的话要转型 DAO

- 结果 Luna、三箭资本、FTX 连续爆雷，整个行业进入漫长熊市。这个时候别说创新了，能活下来就算成功。

- 好不容易熬到 2024 年，L2 又成了版本答案。大家争着搞 xxChain、积分挖矿、空投

- 但是去年 L2 都不行了，都变成鬼链这时候 RWA 来了，所以项目方们都开始做 RWA，最后跑出来的是 Ondo、Tradexyz 其他人都不太好

- 26 年底 DeFi 回来了，Uniswap 开始回购了，Uni 连带着 arb 都开始回来了，如果你还没有放弃的话，你是不是应该顺应潮流做回购 DeFi 呢？

你想到了哪个项目？

我看到的这个项目是 Zig Finance，说真的我不知道他居然还活着，从 21 年开始做 DeFi，DAO、L2、RWA，现在追随 Uni 转型做回购 DeFi

$ZIG 是 2021 年就发行的老 Token，前身是 Zignaly，后来发展到 ZIG Chain，再到现在的 ZIG Finance

它经历了完整的牛熊周期。如今甚至主动关闭了原来的 Zignaly 投资平台，把资源集中到新的链上金融业务上

但真正让我对它重新产生兴趣的，并不是它活了多久，而是它现在开始做一件很有意思的事情：

把真实金融业务赚到的钱，拿出一部分在二级市场回购 $ZIG。

真实金融资产 → 业务收入 → 公开市场回购 $ZIG → 生态发展。

这让我想到了最近 Uniswap 的变化。

过去 UNI 最大的问题之一，就是协议很成功，却不意味着 Token 一定能捕获到相应的经济价值。

如今 UNI 开始通过协议费用进行 Token 回购销毁，市场也开始重新审视 DeFi 的估值逻辑。

太多朋友被 Uni 套住了，但是 2 个月 Uni 涨了一倍（虽然离解套很远），大家都在喊 DeFi Summer 2.0 回来了，这次 Zig 能成功么？

text:
I remember when ICOs had pretty much lost all credibility, and most people had written off the model altogether. MetaDAO was interesting because it brought the model back, but tried to address the very things that made ICOs such a mess in the first place.

I'm getting a similar feeling with @umia_finance on EVM.

Could be too early to draw that parallel, but there are a few things I genuinely like about what they're building.

> They did their own raise without the usual special deals or side letters. The treasury is governed through decision markets that can actually execute, and they've put thought into the legal structure too, tying the token, IP and team together rather than leaving convenient gaps between them.

> The project selection side is interesting as well. There's a curated route for teams with some traction, and another where the community gets a say in what makes it through. They've also gone beyond the usual yes/no markets into multi-outcome ones.

Think they've had a few hundred applications already, with @SlopCash being one of the names announced publicly.

I'm not saying this makes Umia the next MetaDAO. A good design is one thing, how it behaves when things go wrong is another. And the EVM crowd isn't exactly the same as Solana, so there's no guarantee it'll play out the same way.

But I do think people were a bit too quick to write off ICOs as a model, when a lot of the problem was the way they were structured and the incentives around them.

They seem to be addressing the right problems, which is what got me interested in the first place. Still early days, but I’m curious to see how this plays out.
