quoted_text:
Claude风控天机泄露😱

1. Claude 的风控是积分制：注册时会先给账号打分，之后根据行为加分或减分，低于一定分值就会直接封号（很少加分）。

2. 注册：邮箱和 IP 的权重最高。IP 不一定要家宽，但一定要干净，例如自建 IP。Gmail 已经不是最优选，他们现在使用的是一些其他高权重邮箱。注册时直接弹 KYC 的账号可以直接放弃。注册环节很重要，否则后续稍有高危行为就可能直接封号。使用手机 App 注册会加分。

3. 支付：刚注册就订阅会减分，直接订阅 Max 会大幅减分，最好间隔一两天再订阅 Pro。订阅时弹出 KYC 意味着账号处于考察期，但不一定会封；简而言之，A 社想先看 KYC 结果再决定。KYC 使用中国护照没有问题，最大的问题是不能一人多扫；闲鱼上很多账号都属于这种情况，要小心。

4. 注册后的 IP：最重要的是稳定，千万不要随便切换，尽可能一直使用同一个 IP；同样要求干净即可，不要求一定家宽，最好与注册 IP 一致。代理一定要开启全局模式并启用 TUN，这是重点。

5. 老号：老号权重非常高，也就是积分很多，容错率更高。账号积分会随着账号寿命增加，不过 2023 年的老号才是显著更高。

6. 使用：不要一上来就把周限额用完，尽量控制并平均使用；用量大的宁可开两个号轮换使用，也不要一次性用完。使用 CLI 和 Desktop 都可以，Desktop 似乎会少量加分。尽量少用网页端，最好只保留手机端和 Desktop 登录。

7. 时区和语言基本不减分，或仅极少量减分，没必要特意调整。

8. 高并发、反复提问同一个问题、频繁登录、频繁切换 IP 都会大幅减分。

9. 手机端使用会少量加分。开启记忆功能会加分，甚至可能记忆文件越多分数越高。

10. 支付方式为国外实体正规银行信用卡会加分，其次是 Google Play。Apple Pay 不了解；官方礼品卡不减分，但要注意来源是否为黑卡；虚拟卡直接绑定会减分。

11. 到达斩杀线后可能进入观察期。例如及格线是 60 分，账号 55 分就进入观察；如果继续扣分直接掉到 40 分，就会直接封号。观察期的典型特征是掉登录。有的高权重号可能经历两三个观察期才被封。

12. 多设备登录会大幅扣分，最好只在一台电脑上使用一个客户端。

13. Windows 和 macOS 没什么区别，Linux 使用会减分。

14. 跟 Claude 说自己是中国人也没事，不会因为记忆文件就封号。

15. 充值 Credits 会加分，不过成本太高，尚未进行大量实验。

16. 大量使用 Fable 会减分。

17. 升级 Max 大概率会直接进入观察期，除非是积分特别多的高权重号。观察期内有减分行为，大概率会封号。

18. 在工作时间使用不会扣分，不会出现因为使用北京时间就封号的情况。

text:
Let me get this straight.

Crypto has a name for this scheme. Insiders hype a worthless token, flood your phone with fake urgency, take your money, cash out, and leave you holding the bag. The regulators shrug, and the insiders run it again next quarter under a new name. In Washington they call it the two-party system, and they were running it long before anyone had heard of Bitcoin.

Republicans and Democrats will tell you they are mortal enemies. Watch what they do with your phone number and you would never guess. They run the same tricks on the same victims, and they protect each other with the same exemptions they wrote for themselves. Two logos on one cash machine.

Every pump starts with distribution. You average thirteen political calls and texts a week. Reply STOP, and 72% of you keep getting them anyway. The Do Not Call list does nothing, because the people who wrote that law exempted the only telemarketers you aren’t allowed to escape: themselves. Your number came from the voter file, enriched by data brokers, then rented, swapped and sold to the next committee in line.

Then comes the token, something that sounds valuable and is worth nothing. On the right, Trump’s PAC emailed supporters, in his voice, “I want to try and get to heaven,” and asked for fifteen dollars. A billionaire president, crowdfunding his way past Saint Peter. Next came a “Citizens Only Survey” asking whether you’re an illegal alien and whether “ICE need[s] to come and track you down,” which you had to pay to submit. After that, a “National Security Briefing Membership” nobody has ever explained. Finally, a request to confirm the spelling of your name for your Tariff Check. The check is still in the mail. So is heaven.

The left minted its own coins. The DSCC warned that your membership expires at midnight. The five-dollar membership does not exist. The real one costs $44,300, and you are not invited. The DCCC offered a 400% match. House Majority PAC smelled weakness and pumped it to 600%. Nobody has ever met the matching donor, because the matching donor is Helvetica Bold.

Once you buy in, they lock you in. In 2020, Trump’s campaign pre-checked a tiny box that turned one donation into a weekly withdrawal, then pre-checked a second box to double it. When the banks drowned in fraud complaints, the campaign refunded $122 million. The FEC, a body that agrees on nothing, voted six to zero to ban the trick. Congress never touched it, because the trick works for everybody. Four years later CNN caught both the Trump and Harris campaigns using pre-checked boxes. Two parties, one checkbox, zero shame.

Every pump and dump needs bagholders, and the best ones can’t read the fine print anymore. An 81-year-old man in Arizona with dementia gave more than $80,000 through WinRed, sometimes more than a hundred donations in a single day, because he believed Donald Trump was texting him personally. A woman in cognitive decline gave more than $200,000 through ActBlue. Some elderly donors opened new credit cards and took out mortgages to keep the deadlines from expiring. The FTC says it has no jurisdiction. Neither does Grandma, and that is the entire business model.

When the heat came, Washington held a pair of hearings aimed carefully away from home. Republicans hauled ActBlue before Congress, where its CEO pleaded the Fifth twenty-two times. Democrats demanded the records of WinRed, which racked up 803 FTC complaints to ActBlue’s 120. Each party investigated fundraising fraud with tremendous courage and discovered, every single time, that it lives on the other side of the aisle. Neither has ever opened its own inbox.

Then the dump. One Democratic consulting network raised $678 million from people trying to save democracy, and by one Stanford count about 1.6% reached actual candidates. The consultants dispute that, and their best defense is that the real number might reach single digits. End Citizens United, a PAC founded to get money out of politics, raised $21.18 million and spent $21.14 million. They did get the money out. Of you. On the right, scam PACs played Trump’s own voice in robocalls, told seniors to press 3 to show their support, and sent 3% of the haul to candidates. Another promised a 100X match and spent 73% of what it raised on raising more. Mankind finally built the perpetual motion machine. It runs on retirees, and both parties hold the patent.

Your five dollars was never the point anyway. More than $15 billion has been raised for this midterm, and the biggest checks come from people who will never see a midnight deadline in their lives. What your five dollars buys them is your belief that you own a piece of the thing. You don’t. You own the bag.

Here is what the product delivered. A Congress at 10% approval. A 43-day shutdown, then a 76-day shutdown, each a record when it happened. New members told by their own party to dial for dollars four hours a day and legislate for about two, and judging by the output, they’ve been rounding the second number down. On the single question of protecting you from them, the two parties have voted in perfect harmony every time. They passed no ban on pre-checked boxes, left you no Do Not Call protection, and gave no agency jurisdiction over a dementia patient drained a hundred times in one afternoon. Every loophole that hurts you is one they built, and one they both keep open.

Even the con men get conned. The DNC, $18.5 million in debt, wired $28,860.92 to a scammer pretending to be its own chairman. Somebody finally sent a fake urgent email to a political party, and the party paid. It was the only fundraising email in history that worked exactly as written.

So let me get this straight one last time. They pump you with fear, mint worthless memberships, lock your card into autopay, harvest your grandparents, cash out to their consultants, sell your number to the next crew, and deliver shutdowns. In any other market that would be securities fraud. In this one it’s called a midterm.

Democracy dies at 11:59 p.m., one minute before a deadline that was never real, matched 600% by nobody.

Reply STOP to unsubscribe. Congress already did.

text:
Surprise 1: Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech
.
.
.
Surprise 2: that person is me
Surprise 3: I’m here to tell you all about it

Yes, this is what you think it is; after 6 yrs of increasingly loose anonymity: the Professor Oak reveal post

…and yes, it has gotten so boring around here that I’m literally doxxing myself to spice up the timeline

-------
Ok, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Cody Tranbarger. I mostly tweet, but occasionally find time to dabble in drug dev & starting/building biotechs. My past lives span the VC, crossover, startup continuum; Prof Oak has been my way of keeping a digital foot in those worlds, despite having my physical feet planted elsewhere.

The past 18 mo, ‘elsewhere’ was Mithril Medicine, a co. I founded to develop bsAbs for LAMA2-CMD & other ECM-related genetic diseases.

Mithril was born out of hands-on building with @MikeNGladstone, @JasonPaulRhodes, @LifeSciVC, & team @atlasventure. Somehow, I made enough half-decent calls along the way (even a broken clock is right twice a day, eh?) to convince them Mithril/I warranted a small seed. While I can hardly rationalize such an outrageously cavalier bet, I’m grateful for it, & I'd partner with Atlas again in a heartbeat.

In typical AV fashion, Mithril’s primordial form was virtual, decentralized, & ultra-lean. This stage tends to be short-lived, but for Mithril, it worked surprisingly well, for surprisingly long, thanks in part to the rapid maturation of the AI tools I used liberally.

Eventually, Mithril became a bit of an experiment itself - to find the upper bound of how far it could scale as a single operator + a bunch of Claude (+ a stellar bench of part-time consultants).

In parallel, I started spending time with @nc_frey, @an1lam, & @CoefficientBio team; and promptly experienced, for the 1st time, AI at the frontier. Soon thereafter, Mithril stopped looking like an experiment, & started looking like a preview of an entirely new operating model.

From that spark came “Pipeline-in-a-Person.” The idea immediately resonated when we shared it here back in April; and it was central to the shared vision that led to Anthropic’s acquisition of Mithril, & my joining the team.

Why join Anthropic? Three reasons.
(1) For Mithril, the programs continue, with more resources & infrastructure behind them, and as much Claude as I can put to work.

(2) For me, the chance to start several more programs, & find out how many one person can actually run in parallel - an almost unprecedented luxury for a curious drug hunter.

(3) For our mission, a path to institutionalize & scale this new way of working, then put it in the hands of all of biopharma, all over the world - which, candidly, I find the most energizing.

Will AI x Bio cure diseases? Unequivocally yes, imo… but not by the route that gets the most airtime. Rather than timeline acceleration & compression, I see orchestration & parallelization as today's low-hanging fruit.

Most drug hunters see a handful of go/no-go calls in a career, & spend entirely too much of the rest trading emails (my inbox can attest).

Give them the bandwidth to run several programs at once, and the time to focus on scientific judgment, and I’m willing to bet they’ll make better calls. And at scale, better calls translate to more drugs, higher hit rates, broader patient impact, & likely, a disease or 10 or 100 cured. I couldn't be more excited to build toward that future @AnthropicAI.

Finally, a heartfelt thank you to BioTwitter/X. The end of anonymity is bittersweet, but if anyone’s earned a proper introduction, you all have.

It’s difficult to overstate how much this app has done for me: a decade of education, plenty of friends, many job opportunities, several mentors, a few investors, even a co-founder (fmr). It was the generosity of this community that inspired me to start posting 6 years ago, after just as many years lurking. I hope I’ve been able to pay it forward, in my own small way.

But, to be clear, Prof Oak isn’t going anywhere. Same beat, same themes, and now, a front-row seat to drug development at the frontier. Stay tuned for dispatches from the trenches; and remember...

Gotta Cure 'Em All

text:
one more note: shorter hbm stacks doesn't mean less memory demand moving forward

its actually opposite.. customers are redesigning around the memory shortage.

on sk hynix’s call, management explained that customers are lowering stack heights to build more ai accelerators from limited hbm supply.

and supplying the same bit volume with shorter stacks requires more memory packages, increasing the need for base dies and back-end processing.
-> ie fewer HBM layers increase pressure elsewhere in the production chain.

denser memory dies can also offset part of the reduction in stack height. moving from 12 layers to 8 doesn’t automatically mean one-third less memory.

sk says customer volume requests exceed twice what it can currently supply.

(from the post-call notes on @tessara_ai)

a few things i think many ppl skimmed past on the SK Hynix call:

"sold out through 2029" isn't all signed. it's LTAs plus demand still being negotiated. the LTAs cover >50% of 2027-28 capacity, and pricing still moves with the market inside an agreed range. so the revenue looks dependable. the margins.. less so

capex goes up a lot in 2027, but cleanrooms open in phases and tools go in as demand shows up. building ahead, but not blindly

text:
RedotPay 估值一年翻五倍，50 亿美元有点贵

据彭博社，这家成立仅三年的加密支付卡公司正考虑年底前秘密递交美国 IPO 申请。按报道披露的年化营收估算，50 亿美元相当于约 28 倍营收。

支撑这个价格的业务，如今走到了哪一步？

1️⃣ 同比还在涨，最近两个月却走平了

前三季度卡消费额同比增长约 64%，但 8 月和 9 月均在 4.03 亿美元左右，链上充值额也基本持平。

2️⃣ 赛道越做越大，领先优势却在缩小

在 Paymentscan 追踪的约 30 个卡项目中，RedotPay 的消费额占比从 2024 年一度超过 90%，降至今年 9 月的约 33%。

发卡门槛降低后，后来者正在更快放量，依靠较高费率支撑推广激励的模式，也面临竞争压力。

3️⃣ 上市之前，还有合规和诉讼要处理

日本现有服务将逐步终止，三位联合创始人还面临币安关联实体约 4.7 亿美元索赔。RedotPay 否认相关指控，案件尚无裁决。

从业务增速到获客成本，再到合规结构，看看它距离撑起 50 亿美元估值还有多远👇

20 Open-Source Humanoid Robots You Can Build Yourself | From $50 to $900

What if you could build your own humanoid robot without spending thousands of dollars?

In this video, I explore 20 open-source and DIY humanoid robotics projects, ranked from 1 to 20. The list covers a wide range of budgets, from around $50 to $900 for an upper-body build.

Some projects provide official 3D models, CAD files or assembled STEP models. Others do not have a complete, ready-to-use 3D model matching the robot shown in the video.

For some entries, I arranged available components or created my own visual representations. The 3D models for projects 2, 8, 10 and 6 require verification. Some visuals may be reconstructions or assemblies rather than official models of the original robots. Please check the project documentation before treating any visual as an exact representation of the hardware.

The 20 projects featured

1. RoboPrime | Around $60–100
   A low-cost robotics project with an open-source design.

2. Open-source DIY humanoid builds
   A general category covering custom humanoid builds assembled from different hardware components. The humanoid shown is a generic 3D model created by me, not an official robot model.

3. Qmini | Price unconfirmed
   A compact robot project from Unitree Robotics.

4. Zowi | Around €100
   A small educational robot associated with BQ.

5. Otto Humanoid / Otto DIY | From around $50
   A DIY robotics platform. The final cost depends on the selected components and configuration.

6. Kayra | Price unconfirmed
   The visual combines official leg designs with additional components positioned by me.

7. PLEN2 | Around $499 for the kit
   A compact humanoid robot with published CAD files and walking-related software.

8. Nova Desktop Humanoid | Around $150
   A desktop humanoid project by Daniel Hany. I positioned the available head and arm components myself in the 3D scene.

9. Bambot | Around $300
   A low-cost robotics project with open-source design resources.

10. Rapiro | Around $390
    A small humanoid robot designed by Shota Ishiwatari. The 3D reconstruction shown in the video requires verification against the original model.

11. Valera | Around $400
    An open-source humanoid robotics project.

12. Reachy Mini Lite | Around $399
    A compact robotics platform developed by Pollen Robotics in collaboration with Hugging Face.

13. Open Duck Mini | Under $400
    An open-source bipedal robot project for robotics enthusiasts and developers.

14. MicroDuck | Around $399
    A Pollen Robotics project with reinforcement-learning resources.

15. ROBOTIS MINI | Around $540
    A compact humanoid platform associated with ROBOTIS components.

16. Halley | Around $500–800
    An open-source robot project with 3D design resources.

17. Microban | Around $550–600
    A robotics project associated with the Rhoban team at the University of Bordeaux.

18. Endeavor II | Around $600
    A humanoid project with an assembled STEP model.

19. XLeRobot | Around $660
    An open-source robotics project with accessible hardware designs.

20. InMoov | Around $900 for the upper body
    Created by Gaël Langevin, InMoov is a well-known 3D-printed humanoid robotics project.

What I noticed while preparing this video

The projects vary in price and in the amount of design information available. Some provide official 3D models and detailed mechanical files, while others need additional work to create a visual representation.

The models shown for projects 2, 6, 8 and 10 need to be distinguished from verified official 3D assets. Check the original repositories and documentation for confirmation.

text:
AI just proved that the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) is false. Cryptography relies on ETH, but luckily this particular discovery doesn't threaten core algorithms yet. However, ETH was thought true for almost 30 years, and is highly relevant in the field. This illustrates how AI is the true threat to crypto and security, because it can move the ground under our feet, and it's here today. 

Currently, many chains are promoting their migration to "quantum safe" signatures and other schemes. Meanwhile, cryptographically-relevant quantum computers won't be around for some years, and even when they are, they'll be specialized machines, requiring special environments, rather than easily accessible mass market devices, and it will be relatively easy for authorities and regulatory frameworks to control their use, at least initially. Renting them for the purposes of hacking won't be allowed, for obvious reasons (not that this is something we should rely upon, but it impacts any objective threat analysis).

However, there are dangers with adopting these schemes. The less well-studied and more complex a cryptography algorithm, the greater the chance that a sudden shift in our understanding of theoretical computer science or mathematics, or sophisticated analysis by AI, will suddenly reveal a catastrophic bug. The first real-world harbinger of the dangers occurred when AI found issues with HAWK, a quantum-safe algorithm that was passing through NIST's standardization process at the time (it was withdrawn).

Chain operators' desire to ride narratives and exploit the tendency of web3 investors tendency to seize onto this or that carefully promoted story, who for the most part do not use crypto technology beyond holding and trading tokens, and who lack understanding of the theoretical issues involved, is certainly exploitative for a simple reason — whereas historical technical safety manias used for commercial purposes, such as Y2K, only collected money, this one also risks user safety.

Chains sell adoption of quantum safe signature schemes to token buyers and users that in reality reflect a kind of stupidity, and irresponsibility, rather than actions reflecting wise stewardship protecting people from an imminent quantum meltdown. Meanwhile, of course, while adding support for a new post quantum signature algorithms doesn't involve much engineering work, it allows them to post pictures of their logo next to photos of quantum computers, so they can sell the ignorant on how sci-fi and advanced they are, which makes it particularly attractive to them.

Important note: you'll hear about some serious people performing post quantum encryption of messages. That's different. They're calculating the risk that adversaries, such as state adversaries, perform mass storage of encrypted messages containing secrets, so that they can extract the secrets from them 10 years from now, say, when they finally have cryptographically-relevant quantum computers. This is a different kind of risk they are addressing. 

The perverse tragedy of the quantum mania craze that's currently gripping crypto is that on the one hand it shows how so many chains are driven by a desire to sell tokens first, rather than pursue sound engineering practices, and on the other, their willingness to lie and risk user safety in the process. This, all while the real wolf is at the door as concerns our engineering — AI that's rapidly advancing, here today, accessible to many, and difficult to control.

text:
Within less than a day of launch, $REBATE had distributed 231m bonus tokens to buyers, worth approximately $78,549 at the prices at the time. Holder distributions and REBATE buybacks and burns had also begun.

0xb7ff57631b97000d950236ef63bd463da5beba7e 

What I find particularly interesting about this project, however, is that it directly incorporates holding duration into the distribution mechanism: the longer you hold, the greater your distribution weight, reaching up to twice the base weight.

This gives Rebate Pad an opportunity to change the typical behavior of capital in new-token launchpads. Buyers no longer have to wait for the price to rise before selling; holding can also generate distributions paid in USDG. What remains to be proven is whether this mechanism can retain users and turn short-term trading activity into sustained platform revenue and genuine demand for REBATE.

The project has already attracted considerable attention during its initial launch phase. Approximately 90 minutes after launch, the team reported six community-launched tokens, around 1,300 trades, 68 million bonus tokens distributed to buyers, and three rounds of holder distributions completed. About 14 hours after launch, the reported market cap had reached a high of 1.551 million USDG, with 902 token holders, approximately 455,000 USDG in trading volume, 14 rounds of hourly distributions, 97 million bonus tokens distributed, and around 1.5 million REBATE burned. By the time of the approximately 17-hour update, buyers had received a cumulative 231 million bonus tokens, valued at around $78,549 at the prevailing prices, across 2,907 buy transactions.

A subsequent update on the official website showed that the bonus tokens distributed were worth approximately $78,877.66 at the prices at the time. Holders had received approximately $3,476.55 in cumulative distributions across 30 payout rounds, with 7,583 individual payout records. Approximately 1.91 million REBATE had been burned, representing 0.191% of the initial supply, with a stated value of approximately $3,403 at the price displayed on the website. Over the same period, the number of community launches had increased from the initial six to eight. These figures confirm that buy bonuses, holder distributions, and buybacks and burns have all begun operating in practice rather than remaining theoretical mechanisms in a whitepaper.

What really draws my attention is the treatment of holding duration. Many dividend tokens distribute earnings based on the amount held, but Rebate Pad introduces an additional holding-time multiplier: holdings from day 0 to day 3 receive a 1x multiplier, holdings from day 3 to day 7 receive 1.5x, and holdings held for seven days or longer receive 2x. Distribution weight is determined jointly by the amount held and the holding-time tier. Additional purchases do not reset the holding clock for tokens already held, while selling resets the clock only for the portion of tokens sold.

This detail matters because it changes the incentives facing holders. The usual launchpad strategy is to buy early, wait for a price increase, and look for an exit. Holding tokens itself generally provides no additional return. Rebate Pad attempts to make holding economically meaningful: as long as trading activity continues, holders have the opportunity to receive distributions in the paired asset, with longer holding periods carrying greater weight. For REBATE, that distribution asset is USDG.

This could reduce some users' incentive to trade frequently and help the platform build a relatively stable holder base. In particular, once a holding period exceeds seven days and the multiplier reaches 2x, early participants have a reason to continue monitoring the platform rather than focusing exclusively on short-term price movements. However, one point must be made clear: the time multiplier increases distribution weight; it does not guarantee that actual returns will grow at a fixed rate over time. The amount each holder ultimately receives still depends on trading volume and the actual distributions generated. The official rules also explicitly state that distributions may be very small or even zero.

Buy bonuses, meanwhile, are designed to lower the psychological barrier for new users entering the market. Some traditional launchpads impose taxes when users buy tokens, meaning buyers can incur an immediate cost upon execution. Rebate Pad takes the opposite approach by adding bonus tokens directly to the purchase transaction. For REBATE, the bonus rate on each buy is 3%, and the sell fee is also 3%. For other tokens launched on the platform, the bonus rate, sell fee, and holder distribution ratio are set at launch, with the current rules allowing different projects to choose different parameters. Bonus tokens come from the project's locked treasury rather than being created through unlimited inflation.

However, bonus tokens are not cash refunds, and receiving them does not mean a purchase will be profitable. If the token price falls, receiving an additional 3% in tokens may not offset the price decline. Sellers must also pay the corresponding fees. Therefore, the real test of this mechanism is not how large the bonus looks on paper, but whether users remain willing to trade beyond the initial incentive.

For REBATE itself, the value-capture mechanism adds another layer. Its rules follow a structure similar to those of other tokens on the platform: a 3% buy bonus, a 3% sell fee, and a 0.5% holder distribution paid in USDG. In addition, the platform collects fees from trading in other launched tokens and uses the funds to buy and burn REBATE. According to the official rules, the protocol fee on ordinary platform tokens is 0.7%, while the protocol fee on REBATE's own trades is 0.2%. Once collected, the funds are converted into USDG, with 40% used to buy and burn REBATE at market prices and the remaining 60% used to place automatic buy orders below the current price. Tokens purchased through those orders are also burned.

There are two distinct return mechanisms here, and they should not be conflated. The first is the USDG distribution received by REBATE holders, which is linked to trading activity involving REBATE itself. The second is the use of fees generated by trading across all tokens launched on the platform to buy and burn REBATE. The latter creates an opportunity for the token to benefit from the broader launchpad's business growth.

This is also why the market may assign the project a higher valuation. If the community continues launching tokens on Rebate Pad, those tokens generate trading activity, trading produces platform fees, and those fees are used to buy and burn REBATE, then the native token has the potential to establish a more direct connection to the activity of the entire ecosystem. More importantly, the platform would not need to rely on a single popular token: in theory, trading across multiple projects could contribute to its fee revenue.

However, this model is still in its early validation stage. The initial trading volume of 455,000 USDG, thousands of buy transactions, and bonus tokens valued in the tens of thousands of dollars demonstrate that users are willing to try the mechanism, but they do not prove that the activity will persist. Trading during the first day is often driven by novelty and short-term expectations. Furthermore, the market value of bonus tokens fluctuates with token prices and does not mean the platform has paid out an equivalent amount of cash. What really matters is whether trading volume and holder distributions can remain stable after the initial excitement fades, whether the community continues launching new projects, and whether buybacks and burns can expand alongside the platform's business.

In my view, the most promising catalyst for REBATE is the point at which the holding-time mechanism begins to influence user behavior. As early holdings gradually enter the 1.5x and 2x tiers, users may reassess whether to keep holding or sell. If distributions remain meaningful as trading activity continues, the platform could establish a more stable holder base. However, this requires evidence from actual holding-retention and distribution data. Demand should not be assumed to increase simply because the time multiplier rises.

The second catalyst is the launch of more community tokens and the development of sustained trading activity around them. The platform already has multiple trading markets. The next question is whether these tokens can continue attracting buyers after launch rather than generating a burst of activity before quickly losing attention. If trading activity comes from multiple projects, the platform's sources of fees could become more resilient, strengthening the sustainability of the buyback-and-burn mechanism.

Third, the scale of buybacks and burns needs to become more meaningful relative to the token's market capitalization. The existing record of approximately 1.91 million tokens burned demonstrates that the mechanism is operating. However, based on the price displayed on the website, the burn value of approximately $3,403 remains modest compared with the early market-cap high of around $1.55 million USDG. If platform revenue grows, buyback amounts rise accordingly, and the process can be continuously verified through on-chain records, the market will have a stronger basis for assessing its impact. Conversely, if the rate of burning remains low, even a well-designed mechanism may struggle to support the token's long-term valuation through deflationary expectations alone.

The main risks fall into three areas. First, the distribution mechanism depends on genuine trading activity. If volume declines, the actual distributions received by holders may also shrink; a holding-time multiplier cannot create revenue that does not exist. Second, bonuses and distributions may attract participants who are interested only in short-term returns. If trading activity falls once incentives become less attractive, those users may not stay. Finally, allowing community members to launch tokens does not guarantee project quality. New tokens may lack liquidity or even involve deceptive projects, and the platform remains exposed to smart-contract, network, and external-service risks. The official terms explicitly state that bonus tokens and holder distributions do not prevent price losses, and some tokens may be impossible to sell at a reasonable price.

Overall, what makes REBATE worth watching is not simply the strength of its initial trading activity, but the combination of buy bonuses, holding duration, and platform-level buybacks. The time-based distribution multiplier is an important feature that distinguishes it from ordinary launchpads, while the buyback-and-burn mechanism offers a potential path for connecting the native token's value capture to trading activity across the ecosystem.

What will ultimately determine how far it can go is not the cumulative number of bonus tokens distributed, but whether early users remain, community tokens continue generating trades, and those trades translate into sustainable holder distributions and verifiable REBATE buybacks. If Rebate Pad can persuade traders to participate over the long term because of ongoing distributions, rather than simply chase price movements on launch day, it could change more than the reward structure of a launchpad. It could change how users participate in the broader new-token market.

A token launch platform built on Rh Chain.

The core idea is: when buying a token, users get extra tokens on top, and while holding, they automatically receive dividends. The rules are locked in at launch and no one can change them.

It solves common problems with traditional launch platforms: users get taxed on entry, losing a bit the moment they buy; holders basically get no rewards, making it easy for things to devolve into pure speculation and quick dumping. Rebate Pad flips this: buyers get extra tokens right at entry, holders earn real paired-asset dividends from every trade, and distributions are weighted by holding amount and holding time.

Specific mechanism:
- Each new token has a fixed total supply of 1 billion. The "buy bonus ratio" and "holder dividend ratio" are set at launch, and no one can change them afterward.
- When buying, the bonus tokens are added directly within the same transaction, not compensated afterward.
- Holders automatically receive dividends in the paired token, allocated by position size and holding duration.
- Selling incurs a fee equal to the bonus ratio. These fees go into a locked treasury. The treasury must lock at least 7% of the supply, and bonus tokens can only be distributed to buyers from the treasury—they cannot be arbitrarily withdrawn.
- Optional sniper protection: high tax rate for the first 10 seconds to protect early buyers.
- Platform fees flow back to the REBATE token.

REBATE token utility: the platform's own token, also running the same rules:
- Buying gives an extra 3% bonus; selling incurs a 3% fee.
- Holders receive 0.5% of trading volume.
- The platform takes fees from all launched token trading, and after conversion: 40% is used to market-buy and burn REBATE; 60% is placed as limit buy orders below the price to buy and burn REBATE. Supply can only decrease, never increase.
- More tokens launched and traded on the platform → more fees flow back → more buy pressure and burns, forming a flywheel. Holding REBATE is equivalent to indirectly sharing in the entire platform's activity volume.

author: Ryder2087
quoted_text:
今天海力士最新财报，能回答8月份关于存储这三个思考框架么？海力士三季度营收104.62万亿韩元，营业利润83.33万亿韩元，营业利润率接近80%，确实很强。但如果担心的是2027年以后会怎样，单季利润再高，也解决不了全部疑问。大家的是这笔利润还能赚多久，之后会掉到哪里。

看完今天的财报和电话会，个人倾向于把本轮高景气持续的时间看得更长。下一轮底部抬高也有了更具体的依据。至于现在这些利润有多少能够长期保留下来，还需要持续观察。

1、关于周期顶部，今天给出的增量相当明确。 
海力士已经完成与主要客户的2027年HBM供货量和价格协商。与此同时，长期供货协议LTA覆盖了2027至2028年总产能的50%以上，签约客户增加到14家，协议通常以五年为期。

关于明年电话会上更吸引眼球的一句话，是DRAM和HBM到2029年基本售罄。这里要看清口径：它包括已签LTA，也包括正在与客户具体洽谈的需求。后者有明确采购计划支撑，但尚不能全部算成已经锁定的订单。

再往远看，公司判断供不应求可能持续到2030年。这是管理层对供需的预测。把它和已经谈妥的明年交易条件放在一起，确实能提高对景气持续性的信心

需求也在向更多产品扩散。三季度服务器DDR5出货环比增长超过40%，AI基础设施对存储的拉动已经延伸到系统内存和企业级SSD。长上下文与Agent应用需要保存和反复调用更多数据，容量与成本约束又会推动部分数据转移到SSD。海力士的产品组合因此有机会覆盖更广的需求。

从这个角度看，把2027年直接设定为盈利终点，显得过于机械。至少今天的披露支持我们把时间周期再往后延。

2、下一轮周期底部能不能抬高，我认为这次有了更值得重视的证据。
今天海力士披露，LTA会在双方约定的价格区间内反映市场变化，同时加入保证金等履约安排。合同开始承担一部分稳定采购和定价的作用，这有助于减轻需求调整对公司的冲击。

客户愿意为远期供给承担一定的约束，对原厂当然有价值。公司也更容易按照相对确定的采购安排规划生产，减少一边扩产、一边猜需求的成分。

但这里还缺一些决定底部有多高的细节。价格区间的下沿在哪里，能不能覆盖下一代产品的全部成本？保证金有多少，客户推迟采购需要承担什么代价？这些条件，比协议写了几年更重要。

供给端也有一个积极变化。海力士表示，新厂房可以先建，设备投入和量产扩张则分阶段推进，根据需求和盈利情况调整。这样能保留一部分扩产弹性，不过一家公司的资本纪律，还需要放到全行业供给里检验。

因此，下轮盈利回落得幅度小一些，是有商业依据的判断。但这个只算是定性而非定量的判断。

3、最后是正常化利润，这会直接决定海力士应该值多少钱。
今天电话会上有一个细节很有意思：公司预计明年HBM与普通DRAM的盈利差距会缩小。结合管理层对HBM交易条件和盈利改善的说明，普通DRAM当前的价格景气对利润贡献有多大，就值得单独拿出来看。

三季度DRAM出货环比增长约10%，平均售价上涨幅度达到百分之二十几的后段；NAND出货略有下降，平均售价仍上涨百分之二十几的中段。这里包含产品组合改善的影响，但也足以说明当前业绩对价格环境相当敏感。

如果未来普通存储价格不再大涨，海力士能留下多少利润，才是正常化估值的主要依据。HBM确实有机会提高盈利质量。它与客户芯片和系统的协同更深，定制化也在增加，技术领先和稳定量产能力可能带来更强的客户黏性。

对海力士，更有用的做法是分别估算HBM、服务器DRAM和其他存储业务的持续盈利能力，再把它们加起来。

对长期估值来说，接下来很关键的一步，是新产能陆续投产、普通存储涨价放缓以后，海力士还能不能保持较好的利润和现金流。如果能做到，市场就有更多理由接受一个高于过去的盈利中枢。当然最终还是要看需求增长能持续多久？这是一切估值的起点，未来两年最下游token的消耗大概率还是高速增长，但说实话再往后我也看不清。

随意简单说，根据今天披露的信息，可以得出：
1）景气持续时间比市场想象的要长；
2）下一轮下行幅度相比之前大概率大幅收窄；
3）长时间维持正常化利润这点，长协已经给出了有价值的起点，未来的交付、价格和资本回报会继续给出证据。

整体来说，今天海力士财报能给市场更大的信心，也能支持一波向上的走势。也是周一这里https://t.co/EJK02ZdFdL聊到的、Anthropic路演开始之前应该有一波行情。

text:
尼玛，Anthropic又被扒出来搞小动作，偷偷提高了SDK的额度消耗！！！

Claude Code被发现了一个有点离谱的问题：同样的模型、同样的任务、消耗几乎相同的 Token，5 小时额度的扣减居然能差一倍以上。

有开发者在 @AnthropicAI  的GitHub上提交了一个Issue #97074，并且做了多组对照实验。

其中一组测试使用Claude Opus 5.5，让模型读取相同的 10 个文件，完成相同的任务。

TUI的Claude Code：142 万折算 Token，消耗 5% 额度。
无头模式的claude -p：132 万折算 Token，消耗 8% 额度。
自定义入口名称的claude -p：143 万折算 Token，只消耗 4% 额度。

也就是说，默认的SDK入口消耗额度的速度，大约是自定义入口的 2.2 倍。

而解决办法，居然只是修改一个环境变量就行了....
在环境变量里的CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT这个地方，你可以给自己的工具设置一个自定义入口名称，例如 my-tool。
然后模型和实际执行的任务没有变化，但订阅额度的消耗明显下降。

更有意思的是，10 月 17 日还有另一位开发者进行了独立测试，发现Agent SDK的sdk-ts和sdk-cli入口，相比VS Code扩展使用的 claude-vscode，消耗 5 小时额度的速度接近 3 倍。
这意味着，差异很可能与Anthropic如何识别、分类不同客户端有关。
目前Anthropic的官方文档只说明，Claude Agent SDK和 claude -p会消耗订阅额度，并没有明确解释不同入口是否存在不同的计量权重。

这件事对大量使用Claude Code自动化、Agent SDK和第三方编程工具的人影响尤其明显。
因为开发者可能一直以为自己遇到的是额度不够用，实际上，不同调用入口可能直接影响同一份订阅额度能够完成多少工作。

目前这个Issue仍然处于Open状态。
究竟是配额统计的Bug，还是Anthropic有意设置了不同的计量策略，仍然没有得到官方回应。
如果这是一项有意设计的策略，我觉得 Anthropic 至少应该把规则公开。

毕竟大家付的是同一份订阅费，连额度怎么扣都搞不清楚，确实有点奇怪。

原 Issue：https://t.co/m0iMLk8JZS

其中 Reality 提供代币化股票资产敞口，Keyring 负责开发指数方法论并构建相关借贷市场。该指数旨在通过组合 rToken 持仓与对应股票永续合约的对冲仓位，捕捉资金费率及基差收益机会，为代币化股票在链上金融场景中的应用提供新的策略路径。

No, it definitely won't. I personally spent several years building SHA-256 as a Boolean circuit and then using all the most sophisticated techniques known to math and cryptography to try to invert that function (to execute a preimage attack). I know the math of SHA-256 more deeply than most people on this planet. It's exceptionally well-defined as a trapdoor function, and inverting it is most certainly NP complete.

I also spent over 30 years trying to prove that P = NP, and threw my entire 30 years of knowledge of this problem at frontier LLMs to try to crack it. What they ended up doing was to thoroughly and convincingly refute every single line of reasoning and "clever" trick I came up with over those decades, which has now left me believing for the first time that actually P≠NP.

text:
Is automation killing web3 gaming?

I recently had a convo with @inhuman about automation in web3 gaming, and I haven’t stopped thinking about it since.

Bots, AI agents, scripts - they’ve always been part of gaming - legally or not. In fully onchain games even more so, because everything is open and there’s basically no way to protect against them. So the question isn’t “will automation happen”, it’s “where do we draw the line”.

For me, it goes like this:

Repetitive stuff like “come back in 12h and claim your resources”? Automate it. Fishing in @onchainheroes is a great example. Nobody loses anything when a script collects rewards for you.

But the moment we get to direct interactions with other players, everything changes. Doesn't matter if directly or indirectly (via some incentivized leaderboards for example). Who sends the tx first, who misses by a second, who doesn’t even log in because a bot does everything for them.

As far as I talked to some poeple I think that was the case with @gigaverse as well at some point (don't quote me on that - that's someone else's opinions) - either you automate your play or you're not competitive anymore. That changed a lot during the recent The Awakening event -  new mechanics forced people to play by hand and overally feedback around the game was really positive.

At that point the game loses its core. It stops being a game and becomes a bot vs bot arena. The fun is gone, the human factor is gone, all that’s left is numbers from incentives.

And the irony? Something that was supposed to be the salvation of web3 gaming (you don’t have to sit at your computer all day) and a growth driver for a project, ends up pushing players out in the long run. They burn out and leave, demotivated by fighting automated farms.

And here’s the trap. Metrics can look amazing, because you have thousands of fully automated accounts. But behind them? 50 people.

That’s why I believe a game should ALWAYS reward human play more. Whether through the fun of playing itself or through extra possibilities that can’t be automated. If a game can’t reward a human, that’s not the bots fault. It’s just bad game design.

Do you think automation helps or destroys the web3 gaming projects?

text:
回顾一下海力士财报——营收增长不是重点，AI商业逻辑被验证，正好“押中”本季度财报的核心重点！

凌晨的前文中已经明确海力士财报的看点，

看HBM4增长
看2027年的HBM订单情况
看DRAM价格

再看营业利润里、电话会议2027年的指引以及股东回报等

而海力士的财报基本属于满分答卷

1，HBM4正式接棒HBM3E，Q4出货量以及营收都将会超过前代HBM3E，意味着Q4将会完成产品迭代，同时2027年将会进入HBM4主导阶段，公司未来收入有保障

2，2027-2028年订单被锁定，14家主要客户，签署长期供应协议，包括全球大型GSP，重点是目前签署的订单已经覆盖了2027-2028年总产能的50%以上，这个数据意味着AI资本扩张可见度已经从2027年扩张2028年。

3，传统DRAM 也在赚钱，服务器DDR5销售大幅增长，321层 TLC eSSD销售扩大，存储 超级周期叙事得以延续

4，公司未来指引，将存储却扩周期看到2030年，如果我们担心这个预期过于夸张，就算是保守也可以看到2028年的上半年，而目前也仅仅处于2026年的下半年，未来想象空间打开

5，2027年继续扩大资本开支，扩产，

6，疯狂回购+分红，约100万亿 韩元股东回报，敢分红意味着海力士认为当前的盈利不是短暂的，而是长期的，且看好未来盈利能力，只有预期未来赚的多，才敢当下大量分红。

7，净利润虽然受损，但是营业利润大幅增长38%，核心经营利润仍然增长，而Q2的净利润受到投资与非经营项目影响，因此Q3的大幅下降不能作为有效参考

整体来看，海力士的财报对于本周关键财报是一个不错的铺垫，昨天我说过，谷歌、微软、亚马逊作为AI产业逻辑链中的核心中枢，起到的是承上启下的作用，而海力士作为上游半导体硬件产业，财报利好反向也进一步给三家财报带来一定的积极作用。

接下里就要看三大云厂商财报能否进一步验证当前的AI产业叙事，相比海力士而言，三家云厂商财报可能需要验证AI 资本支出 → AI 收入 → AI 利润这套逻辑。

海力士财报验证了AI资本开支继续扩张，而接下来三家云厂商就需要验证如此大的投入是否可以形成完整的商业闭环与赚钱效应！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
对于AI叙事明天第一战就要迎接海力士财报，北京时间上午9点，海力士财报公布，通过今天的情况来看，海力士财报预期走强，并且今天的亚盘阶段提前发酵利好，美股阶段延续部分利好情绪

接下来对于海力士财报关注点基本是关于HBM4、2027年HBM指引、DRAM ASP 、利润率与资本支出，还有NANA与Solidigm的情况

核心点关注三大点

a，看HBM4而不是看HBM3E，显示市场预期海力是的HBM很强，但是强在哪？HBM4的能否顺利接棒HBM3E继续为海力士带来收入

b，2027年的HBM订单情况，在AI巨头继续扩大资本开支的前提下，GPU订购增加，HBM是否也增加订购，然后传导至海力士订单是否真正增加，未来产能锁定很重要

c，DRAM价格，目前市场预期HRAM ASP 价格继续上涨，能否符合预期，将关乎海力士的未来盈利能力评估

至于营业利润里、电话会议2027年的指引以及股东回报属于其他关注因素

不过海力士的财报就算是利好，依旧不够扭转整个AI产业被宏观挤压的局面，在Brent价格不回归110美元上方的前提下，核心还是要看周四的微软、谷歌与亚马逊财报

目前美股阶段市场提前发酵三大云厂商巨头的财报利好，算是对市场信心的增加以及此前估值调整后的技术性修复，如果海力士财报没问题，利好以及信心提振将会延续，但是如果Brent 回归110美元上方，或者10Y 收益率继续飙升，都会对冲掉海力士的财报利好需要注意

New Bench Tool: Compare LLMs 

Labs and devs can now compare a base model vs. its quant using Bench. The Compare tool measures how similarly two models actually behave, showing 3 main results:

- KL Divergence: do their next-token distributions match?
- Hidden layer comparison: do they process tokens the same way at every layer of the process, and not just at the output?
- Cross Model Perplexity: shows how "surprised" a model is when reading the other model's text.

Behavior similarity matters for Subnet 65 because it's harder to fake; it measures whether the quant thinks like the model it came from.

text:
I like to look at claims like this in case I can improve Ghostty. I grabbed your source and immediately spotted the issue: your read loop overwrites a 64 KiB ring. Everything older is discarded unparsed per tick. You're faster because you're not actually terminal emulating.

It means the number isn't a throughput number. In a kitten benchmark run at the rate you're claiming, roughly 6.6 MB arrives per 60 Hz tick and 64 KiB of it gets parsed. You're read(2)-ing 100% of the data and parsing about 1% of it. 

There are other minor issues (a small fixed scrollback in a preallocated ring buffer, no grapheme clustering, throwing away data like OSC 8 URIs, etc.), but the major one is simply that you're discarding ~99% of the input.

For plain text, e.g. your cat benchmark, the final screen ends up looking right, but the scrollback is missing 99% of the file and each retained chunk starts mid-line. As soon as there are escape sequences in the dropped spans, your emulator is fully out of sync and invalid: a cut inside a CSI prints the parameters as text, and any SGR, mode, title, or alt-screen change in the gap is just... gone.

FYI, this is why I don't like when people point at refterm as a terminal benchmark. refterm implements a TINY subset of what a terminal emulator must support, it's closer to a fast file reader, not a terminal emulator. 

I also don't mean any shade by this. I like to look at technology objectively to try to learn something and improve my own craft and work. So I'm sharing what I found.

I modified your code very slightly to parse on every full buffer (rather than per tick). And the results are attached. Both use main commit in each repo at the time of this post.

Note the graph is in log scale, the discrepancy between performance for things like Kitty images is measured in GB/s.

DoubleZero co-founder Austin Federa says it's a mistake to treat crypto entertainment like an asset class

"Oftentimes, we look at things that are entertainment products as financial products in crypto. NFTs were not really a financial product. I'm not sure memecoins are ever really a financial product."

"No one's particularly mad that people are spending $600 to go see a band and then they're spending $48 on a beer, because it's entertainment. We don't consider it an investment class."

"The problem was when people started conflating memecoins, which were effectively people having fun onchain and getting some dopamine from numbers moving around on the screen, with an actual financial asset class."

"Obviously, you really should not invest in memecoins. But if you think this is fun and you want to play around with it, great. I have no problem with that."

text:
Ethereum just delayed the Glamsterdam upgrade.

And it's a good thing they did.

The upgrade was supposed to go live on the Hoodi testnet on Oct 26, but devs postponed it after security researchers flagged a potential problem.

The concern is that these changes could make existing smart contracts behave differently, even without anyone changing their code.

Here's what could happen:

→ Failed operations could block future retries
→ Valid transactions could run out of gas
→ Gas safety checks could miss failures

This is a great example of why testnets and security reviews matter. Respect to Ethereum's devs for taking the warnings seriously.

That's why they're the best in the game.

text:
I wanted to write a post this morning offering some honest thoughts on the whole "Pump fun is the enemy" discourse I've been seeing across the timeline.

As someone who has been here full-time since late 2020, this isn't my first rodeo when it comes to watching CT collectively turn against the very infrastructure that defined a previous market cycle.

In fact, I'd argue this is an almost predictable phenomenon that occurs at every major paradigm shift in crypto, particularly when we transition away from a dominant speculative asset class and towards whatever comes next.

The platform that facilitated the previous meta inevitably becomes the focal point of frustration when the economics underpinning that meta begin to deteriorate.

Most of you probably haven't been around long enough to remember, but we witnessed an almost identical situation with OpenSea during the transition away from NFTs in 2022–23.

At that point, there was virtually nothing OpenSea could have done to satiate its existing user base.

The NFT boom that it had largely facilitated was over, liquidity was evaporating, and the core participants who had previously made substantial amounts of money trading NFTs were suddenly finding it increasingly difficult to generate returns.

Predictably, people started to get pissed off.

OpenSea was suddenly extractive. OpenSea wasn't innovating. OpenSea wasn't doing enough for its users. OpenSea was responsible for the deterioration of the very market it had helped popularise.

And while there were certainly legitimate criticisms to be made regarding its business model the broader reality was that NFTs were simply no longer the dominant speculative asset class.

With the benefit of hindsight, it's difficult to imagine any realistic set of decisions OpenSea could have made that would have fundamentally reversed that trajectory.

The writing was already on the wall.

Yet, to this day, you'll still encounter people who genuinely believe OpenSea somehow "killed NFTs".

Which, to me, is an absurd interpretation of how speculative markets function.

No emerging asset class gets to enjoy an indefinite period of extraordinary returns, particularly once the opportunities that initially made it attractive become widely understood, commoditised and increasingly competitive.

And I believe we're now witnessing an almost identical phenomenon with pump fun.

Call it the OpenSea-ification of the trenches.

We're experiencing the gradual exhaustion of capital-M memecoins as the de facto speculative asset class of this cycle, and the platform most closely associated with their proliferation has become the natural target for everyone's frustration.

The uncomfortable reality is that most people, outside of a relatively small subset of sophisticated participants, simply aren't making meaningful money trading memes anymore.

There are numerous reasons for this, but without getting lost in the weeds, the underlying dynamics are relatively straightforward.

Liquidity is considerably more fragmented, the number of competing tokens and narratives has expanded dramatically, and the capital required to sustain the valuations we witnessed during the height of the mania simply isn't circulating through the market in the same way.

At the same time, the average participant is competing against an increasingly sophisticated group of traders who have spent years refining their strategies, infrastructure and understanding of the trenches.

This is an important point that I don't think gets nearly enough attention.

Every speculative asset class eventually becomes a more solved game.

The inefficiencies that initially created extraordinary opportunities are gradually arbitraged away. As more participants figure out how to play the game, the edge that once existed begins to disappear, and making money becomes increasingly difficult for the average trader.

Consequently, the risk/reward profile deteriorates for the average participant.

What was once an environment where relatively unsophisticated traders could generate extraordinary returns becomes one where those same participants are effectively competing against professionals.

This isn't a unique failure of memecoins.

It's how financial markets function.

It happened with NFTs, and it's happening with memes.

Which brings me to what I consider the fundamental misconception underpinning much of the current anti-pump discourse.

There's this persistent belief that if only pump fun had implemented different incentives, distributed fees differently, worked with different KOLs, or simply never existed in the first place, we'd somehow be living in a memecoin utopia where everyone continued making money indefinitely.

I find that argument deeply unconvincing.

For one, it assumes pump fun exists in a vacuum, rather than within an intensely competitive market where alternative platforms would inevitably emerge to service the same underlying demand.

Remove pump fun from the equation, and you don't magically remove the economic incentives that gave rise to it.

You simply create an opportunity for another platform to occupy the same position.

More importantly, it assumes that the structural deterioration in memecoin profitability is primarily a consequence of platform-level decisions rather than the natural maturation and saturation of the asset class itself.

I don't believe that's the case.

And to be clear, none of this is intended as an unconditional defence of pump fun.

There are absolutely decisions worth criticising.

But IMO the distinction I think people are missing is that...

A platform can make suboptimal decisions without being responsible for the structural decline of the market it operates within.

Even if pump fun had executed perfectly, two fundamental realities would remain unchanged.

First, crypto has largely failed to attract sufficient new capital and participants to sustain the increasingly large speculative ecosystems we've built across successive cycles.

Second, memecoin trading has become an increasingly competitive activity, where the average participant is now competing against a much more sophisticated and experienced subset of the market.

Neither of these problems disappears because pump fun changes its fee structure or starts working with different influencers.

And neither would disappear if pump fun ceased to exist tomorrow.

Simply put, people are looking for a platform-level solution to what is fundamentally a market-level problem.

I think that's the real source of the disconnect.

When an asset class stops generating the returns people have become accustomed to, it's psychologically much easier to identify a villain than to accept that the opportunity itself has fundamentally changed.

OpenSea became that villain for NFTs.

Pump fun is becoming that villain for memecoins.

And I suspect that when the next dominant speculative asset class eventually emerges, we'll watch this exact same cycle play out again.

None of this means platforms should be immune from criticism or that participants shouldn't demand better incentives, transparency and alignment.

They absolutely should.

But there's a meaningful difference between holding a company accountable for its decisions and attributing the inevitable maturation of an entire speculative market to that company's existence.

Until we start distinguishing between those two things, I think we're going to keep having the wrong conversation.

And sure, call me a pump fun shill if you want, but many of you made life-changing gains during peak memecoin mania precisely because pump democratised launches.

It's worth acknowledging that, just as it's worth recognising that the decline in liquidity and profitability isn't solely the fault of the launchpad that helped facilitate the boom.

Ultimately, I think it's worth asking whether any single platform could have fundamentally changed where we find ourselves today, or whether this was always the natural trajectory of the market.

Food for thought.

author: JaydenWei
quoted_text:
我给百合网创始人转了2000后拉黑了他。

今天天气不错，
二连板，吃着天妇罗刷着抖音，
突然看到一条新闻：百合网的联合创始人慕岩，因为财产被冻结，生活遇到了困难，甚至在朋友圈发了收款二维码，向朋友们寻求帮助。
我跟慕岩认识，以前连过麦，微信里偶尔也会聊几句。上一次聊天，我们还在讨论孙宇晨。印象里，他以前在我直播间刷过几百块钱的礼物。
所以看到新闻，我就想着给他转点钱。
本来准备转一万块钱的。
但看到他当时一共才筹集了五千多块钱，我又觉得不合适。一个曾经那么成功的企业家，如今愿意发二维码求助，想必已经经过了一番心理挣扎。大家几百块地转，我突然转过去一万块钱，比他筹集的总金额还多，反而可能让他不好意思收。
于是改成了2000块钱。即便如此，按照我当时看到的记录，这依然是最大的一笔。
转完之后，我又想了想，干脆把他微信删了。
我给他留了一句话：
“为避免收款心里有压力，我就先删除了，回头有事找我随时加回来。你的放下，注定你可以再次找到人生的方向，下一个人生路口再聚。”
为什么要删呢？
因为我们算不上特别亲密的朋友。我怕他不好意思收，也怕他想着怎么感谢我、怎么还这份人情。
反正我都把他删了，他收了也就收了。我希望他能少一点心理负担。
这件事让我想了很多。
慕岩曾经是中国互联网创业浪潮里非常成功的一批人。百合网最辉煌的时候，他拥有过的财富和社会地位，恐怕是绝大多数人一辈子都无法企及的。
但人生有时候就是这么奇怪。一个人可以花二十年建立自己的事业，却未必能够决定未来二十年会发生什么。
我在人选天选论里写过两句话：
选择必有代价，不选择也是选择。
未失而能止者，人选也；既失而后止者，天选也。
这两句话放在财富上，尤其值得思考。
我们总是把赚钱看成一种能力。一个人从零赚到一千万，我们佩服他；从一千万赚到一个亿，我们更佩服他。
可一个人赚到一个亿之后，决定不再追逐下一个十亿，安安稳稳守住财富，难道就不值得佩服吗？
我甚至觉得，后者可能更难。
因为赚钱需要不断寻找机会，而守钱往往需要不断放弃机会。
一个人已经赚到足够生活一辈子的钱，却依然要面对无数诱惑。有人告诉他项目可以让资产翻倍，有人告诉他某个行业正在风口上，错过就再也没有机会。
他过去又确实成功过很多次，于是继续下注，继续扩张，继续承担风险。
可财富积累到一定程度以后，风险和收益对人生的意义，已经不再对称。
一个拥有一个亿的人，再赚一个亿，生活未必会发生多大改变。但失去这一个亿，生活却可能翻天覆地。
所以关于财富，我觉得有一个特别简单的道理：
永远不要用我们需要的钱，去挣我们不需要的钱。
什么叫需要的钱？
是能够让家人安稳生活的钱，是孩子的教育、父母的养老，是生病时不必借钱，是不想工作时还能有底气休息几年。
什么叫不需要的钱？
是已经拥有足够的财富，却还想再多赚一点；是一个亿变成两个亿，两个亿变成五个亿；是那些即使没有赚到，也不会影响生活的数字。
如果为了后者，把前者也押上去，无论最后赢了多少钱，这个选择都值得警惕。
我不反对冒险，也不反对追求财富。但至少应该知道，哪些钱可以冒险，哪些钱无论如何都应该留下来。
选择继续追逐财富，要承担失去财富的可能；选择停下来，也要承担错过机会的遗憾。
但人最容易犯的错误，就是把错过赚钱机会的遗憾，看得比失去已有财富的痛苦还重。
赚到一个亿以后，看到别人赚了十个亿，觉得自己错过了九个亿。可那九个亿原本就不属于你。
你真正拥有的，是手里的一个亿。
为了追逐那九个亿，把已经拥有的一个亿也输掉了，这才是真正的损失。
这就是“未失而能止者，人选也；既失而后止者，天选也”。
在还有选择权的时候，主动决定不再追逐什么，这叫人选。等到财富失去，现实逼着你停下来，那就由不得自己选择了。
当然，我不知道慕岩今天的处境究竟是怎样造成的，更不知道他过去做过哪些财务选择。我虽然想用一个人的困难去证明自己的观点，但不能。
但他的事情确实再次提醒了我，人在有的时候，一定要懂得守，尤其要懂得放弃。
而财富的得失，还只是事情的一面。
更难的是，一个人失去财富以后，能不能放下过去的自己。
我们这个社会特别喜欢讲东山再起。一个成功的企业家遇到困难，大家第一反应就是，他什么时候能够重新成功？
仿佛曾经拥有过一个亿，以后就必须再赚回一个亿，否则就意味着失败。
可为什么呢？
一个人曾经站在山顶，难道就没有资格走下山来？
他可以重新创业，也可以过普通人的生活。可以继续追逐财富，也可以做过去一直想做、却没有时间做的事情。
人生又不是只有一场考试，考过一次第一名，以后就必须永远考第一名。
有时候，最难放下的可能已经不是钱，而是曾经那个成功的自己。
曾经别人见到你，会主动打招呼，尊重你的意见，认真听你讲话。突然有一天，这些东西都变了。
你还能不能接受自己？还能不能坦然面对曾经认识你的人？还能不能允许自己重新成为普通人？
这些问题，可能比失去多少钱更难回答。
所以看到慕岩公开求助，我并不觉得有什么可笑的。一个人愿意承认困难，愿意向别人开口，本身就需要勇气。
我希望他能渡过难关，也希望他不必被过去的成功困住。
说回那2000块钱。
我为什么转完以后，要把他删掉？
除了不想让他收款时有压力，还有一个原因。
我不想让这2000块钱变成一笔未来的投资。
慕岩毕竟曾经是成功的企业家。也许有一天，他真的东山再起了。
到那个时候，我会不会想起自己曾经帮助过他？会不会觉得，我们之间因此多了一份特殊的关系？
我不敢保证自己一定不会。
人对自己的道德评价，往往比真实的自己要高。
《人选天选论》里还有一句话：
道德是选择完成后对自己的解释。
我今天可以说自己出于好意，过几年，也许又会给这件事找出另外一套解释。
所以我选择把这段关系暂时放下。
他曾经给我刷过礼物，我今天有能力，就给他转2000块钱。至于他将来会不会重新成功，会不会记得，都不重要。
当然，有人可能会问：既然不想要回报，为什么还要发文章讲这件事？
两个原因。
第一个，给自己的决策装装逼。
我没必要把自己包装得多么高尚，仿佛连一点虚荣心都没有。
第二个，希望这件事能被更多人看见。
慕岩求助的消息已经传了出来，我不知道他是否希望得到更多关注，也不知道外界的帮助能不能解决问题。但如果文章能让更多人了解他的处境，或许也能带来一点帮助。
虚荣心是我的，2000块钱也是我自愿给的。我可以承认自己想装逼，但不想因此要求他欠我一个人情。
其实人与人之间的缘分，有时候挺奇妙的。
我们上次还在微信里讨论孙宇晨，讨论别人的事情。没想到过了一段时间，我却在新闻里看到了他的事情。
今天我有能力给他转2000块钱，明天也许我会遇到自己的困难。谁又能保证一辈子都顺风顺水呢？
至于慕岩兄，如果将来他东山再起，我会不会替他高兴；如果他选择放下过去，重新开始另一种生活，我倒是会祝福他。
我们曾经有过一麦之缘，
他不必因此记住我，如果有一天，我们又在什么地方碰见，还能像以前一样，聊聊孙宇晨，聊聊各自的经历着就很好。
君子之交，淡如水，下个人生路口再见。

Claude wrote the Blender scripts. A human kept pointing out what looked fake.

One creator’s Claude Code + Blender workflow became increasingly specific:

• Compare every render against one fixed reference image.
• Inspect individual objects at full resolution.
• Use scanned assets and measured terrain where procedural detail falls short.
• Add scripts to flag geometry and material issues.

The creator reports that a .blend linter flagged 87 problems they had missed by eye.

My takeaway for agent builders: turn specific human feedback into repeatable checks the agent can run on the next iteration.

The bank also lifted its March 2027 target to $95 and June 2027 target to $90.

Global visible oil inventories have fallen by more than 500 million barrels since February, while tanker freight costs from the Middle East to China have surged to $30–$40 per barrel.

text:
Last week in quantum:

@Starknet backed research into becoming an independent post-quantum Layer 1.

More than 93.5% of voting power backed the research, across 2,800+ wallets, and StarkWare didn’t vote. It’s research only. Any actual move needs a second vote, and a whitepaper draft is expected in November.

Quantum risk entered the insurance conversation.

@projecteleven named Relm Insurance a development partner for Strongpoint, its custody product, to explore how post-quantum security could factor into digital asset underwriting. No premium or policy changes have been announced.

@QuantinuumQC reported a new error-correction record.

Its Helios system reached 99.9995% logical memory fidelity per cycle, about 10 times better than its own September result.

That figure measures memory reliability, not a complete computation. The team also demonstrated improving logical gate accuracy, though further work remains to scale all the components needed for universal fault-tolerant computing.

Postquant Labs launched the Quip Virtual Machine.

The QVM provides a shared programming environment for quantum annealers, gate-based quantum computers, and classical machines, with a maximum cost quoted before execution.

It is live on @quipnetwork’s Aglais testnet.

Post-quantum readiness increasingly needs evidence. Chains need tested migration plans. Custodians need controls insurers can assess. Quantum hardware needs reliable computation beyond memory benchmarks.

The useful question is what each announcement actually demonstrates.

We expect a "hawkish pause" today.

The Fed will hold interest rates unchanged but lay the groundwork for a December rate hike, bringing total rate hikes in 2026 to +50 basis points.

Why?

Because the US economy is now facing both supply-side and rising demand-side inflationary pressures, while the labor market continues to weaken beneath the surface.

This puts the Fed in an increasingly difficult position: Inflation is demanding tighter monetary policy, while underlying labor market weakness is calling for the opposite.

We expect the Fed to prioritize inflation today, keeping the door open for further tightening in December.

text:
people online assume i make a lot of money.

and they’re right. especially for a 20 year old, i’m incredibly fortunate.

but what people don’t understand is how little of that money i actually keep.

almost everything goes straight back into the business. employees, content, travelling, relationships, education, new opportunities. of course i enjoy a certain lifestyle, but that’s not where my priorities are.

my actual profit margins are far lower than people imagine. and that’s intentional.

look at Revolut. founded in 2015, it took until 2021 to report its first profitable year. in 2020 alone, it lost over £220 million while expanding.

today, that same business generates billions in annual profit.

the lesson isn’t that losing money makes you successful. it’s that maximising short term profits and maximising long term value are two completely different objectives.

i could take significantly more money out of my business today. but every dollar i extract is a dollar i can’t deploy into something that could compound in to 10$ and even 100$ over the next decade.

i’m not building to maximise what i can spend at 20.

i’m building to maximise what i can own at 30, 40 and 50. 

revenue feeds your lifestyle. reinvestment, when done right, builds your future.

text:
nine years in crypto, zcash was always there

my journey in crypto had an unusual start: during my grad studies, i joined a chainalysis when they were a 20-people startup in copenhagen

my job: apply ML (aka AI before it was cool) to break the privacy in cryptocurrencies and blockchains like bitcoin, ethereum, etc. 

i also read and analyzed dash, monero, etc. and
that's when i first learned about zcash – and it completely blew my mind

the weakest point of all crypto and blockchains is how much data is leaked and published on-chain, combined with how much OSINT and privately gathered data (kyc) can be correlated with on-chain data

the fact that zcash essentially removed the need to publish any data basically meant that there was no data to analyze – in other words zcash was at the frontier of crypto 

it heavily inspired me to ditch AI and pursue decentralized protocols instead 

from ethereum, through cosmos, many other L1s in-between, and anoma for the last 6 years, I wasn't formally involved with zcash – yet somehow zcash was always there 

because everything I've worked on shared Zcash' values of decentralization, privacy, and self-sovereignty

my mind was shaped by zcash (think like an attacker, analyze data flows from end-to-end, etc) and a whole lot of my work has been inspired by cash too, from custom protocols like Namada and the Anoma DOS to end user products like Namadillo, AnomaPay, and recently Zillions

and now that i think about it, i probably would've left crypto a few months ago if zcash wasn't around anymore

i've grown increasingly disillusioned with the industry: the hypergamblification brought by memecoins and the dominance of centralized protocols and products (combined with this brutal bear market)

like many, i've considered leaving this industry 

because I didn't join to make casinos faster and more addictive – i joined because of the initial ethos of this space, to build an alternative to the financial system, one that gives people real sovereignty over their money, data, and lives

in an industry where even ethereum is losing its roots, zcash remains true to its values and even today the community is full of ethos-driven and strongly aligned people (come to a zcash conference and you'll see, they feel like 2017)

zcash has been like a north star to me, 
a reminder that the original vision of crypto isn't dead,
there are still people willing to build for principles rather than speculation

so yeah, it's been 9 years since I've joined crypto, and without zcash, i probably wouldn't be here anymore

happy 10th birthday zcash!

honored to be part of this community, and more excited than ever to contribute to what comes next

As I'm sure we've all seen, your product can be copied within a few days by someone with any frontier AI and then will either be open-sourced or will race to zero on Twitter with cheaper prices 

Just being able to create the product, of course, doesn't mean it will replicate your success in marketing or distribution, but as I've seen more and more of this, it got me thinking

I think as AI becomes more accepted widely, more people will do creative stuff with it and less productive stuff

We will see a shift towards gaming, video, image, movies, etc and away from iOS apps

At that point, it doesn't mean that your iOS apps will be useless but it means that replicating and/or open sourcing your product will be pretty normal and much harder to do with the creative parts of AI

I'm excited for that shift because I've been a creative person my whole life. I've been on the internet for 10 years, and I've had countless failed creative startups since I was 16

That's why I've decided to pursue making a game rather than more and more product-based software

Just something to think about

GPT Astra 6, Kimi K3, Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 & GPT 6 SOL worked together over the past few weeks to make Animal Crossing/Pokopia but in rural Afghanistan

author: teortaxesTex
quoted_text:
最近看到一篇关于 mHC 的分析，跟我们之前在 v4 的模型上跑出来的结论一致，mHC最终会收敛到一条HC上的情况，这也是为什么我一直在推荐iHC的原因之一。

mHC 通过 Doubly Stochastic Matrix 约束多条 Residual Stream 的混合，解决了数值稳定性问题，但 Numerical Stability ≠ Information Preservation。

双随机矩阵虽然保证了均值方向的信息不变，却可能使不同 Stream 之间的差异随网络深度逐渐衰减，最终让多条残差流在纯混合路径上趋向同一个均值。

如果希望保留这些差异，就需要让混合矩阵接近置换矩阵，但这又会带来 Vertex Viscosity 和 Sinkhorn 收敛变慢的问题。

这篇paper讲了 mHC 在 Stability、Information Preservation 和 Optimization Efficiency 之间的 Trade-off。

当然，这并不意味着完整的 mHC 一定退化成单条 Stream，因为每一层仍然可以注入新的信息。真正值得思考的是：增加的 Residual Stream 究竟能在多深的网络中保留独立信息？我不知道，实验还在继续，还没有确切的结论，等等实验的详细结果吧，我先去吃饭了。

text:
Idk who needs to hear this, but formal verification of software (mathematically checking that software is correct) is by no means done, even now that we have LLMs and the proof tedium is gone. Instead, having LLMs lets us focus on the spec, where humans remain in the loop, and where people were often sloppy in the past. By sloppy I mean they often touted “formally verified!!11”, without even mentioning the spec. And upon closer inspection, the spec often turned out to miss critical guarantees you would naturally expect.

Formal verification IS hard. First, you need to figure out what behavior you even want to check: the spec. Then, you need to go through the tedium of writing a proof that your program indeed satisfies the spec.

LLMs massively speed up the second step. That’s because the proof can automatically be checked by a compiler. If the compiler is happy, the LLM did its job and you can trust the result, namely that your program satisfies the spec, without reading the proof yourself. (Ofc assuming you don't hit a compiler bug.)

But the first step is still there: What’s the spec? Writing the spec is still tedious and error-prone, and while LLMs help, a human needs to remain in the loop, at least to some extent, to assess whether the spec matches with the programmer's intention and the user's expectation. If you vibe that part, that’s where the bugs will creep back in.

Also: not all specs are equal. Don't trust "formally verified" without checking the spec. If the spec only says "the program doesn't crash", that is much less useful than a spec that reflects in detail the intended and expected functionality of the program.

So, humans are not leaving the loop, we're just moving up a level. With the proof tedium gone, we can finally focus our attention on the spec!

text:
我给百合网创始人转了2000后拉黑了他。

今天天气不错，
二连板，吃着天妇罗刷着抖音，
突然看到一条新闻：百合网的联合创始人慕岩，因为财产被冻结，生活遇到了困难，甚至在朋友圈发了收款二维码，向朋友们寻求帮助。
我跟慕岩认识，以前连过麦，微信里偶尔也会聊几句。上一次聊天，我们还在讨论孙宇晨。印象里，他以前在我直播间刷过几百块钱的礼物。
所以看到新闻，我就想着给他转点钱。
本来准备转一万块钱的。
但看到他当时一共才筹集了五千多块钱，我又觉得不合适。一个曾经那么成功的企业家，如今愿意发二维码求助，想必已经经过了一番心理挣扎。大家几百块地转，我突然转过去一万块钱，比他筹集的总金额还多，反而可能让他不好意思收。
于是改成了2000块钱。即便如此，按照我当时看到的记录，这依然是最大的一笔。
转完之后，我又想了想，干脆把他微信删了。
我给他留了一句话：
“为避免收款心里有压力，我就先删除了，回头有事找我随时加回来。你的放下，注定你可以再次找到人生的方向，下一个人生路口再聚。”
为什么要删呢？
因为我们算不上特别亲密的朋友。我怕他不好意思收，也怕他想着怎么感谢我、怎么还这份人情。
反正我都把他删了，他收了也就收了。我希望他能少一点心理负担。
这件事让我想了很多。
慕岩曾经是中国互联网创业浪潮里非常成功的一批人。百合网最辉煌的时候，他拥有过的财富和社会地位，恐怕是绝大多数人一辈子都无法企及的。
但人生有时候就是这么奇怪。一个人可以花二十年建立自己的事业，却未必能够决定未来二十年会发生什么。
我在人选天选论里写过两句话：
选择必有代价，不选择也是选择。
未失而能止者，人选也；既失而后止者，天选也。
这两句话放在财富上，尤其值得思考。
我们总是把赚钱看成一种能力。一个人从零赚到一千万，我们佩服他；从一千万赚到一个亿，我们更佩服他。
可一个人赚到一个亿之后，决定不再追逐下一个十亿，安安稳稳守住财富，难道就不值得佩服吗？
我甚至觉得，后者可能更难。
因为赚钱需要不断寻找机会，而守钱往往需要不断放弃机会。
一个人已经赚到足够生活一辈子的钱，却依然要面对无数诱惑。有人告诉他项目可以让资产翻倍，有人告诉他某个行业正在风口上，错过就再也没有机会。
他过去又确实成功过很多次，于是继续下注，继续扩张，继续承担风险。
可财富积累到一定程度以后，风险和收益对人生的意义，已经不再对称。
一个拥有一个亿的人，再赚一个亿，生活未必会发生多大改变。但失去这一个亿，生活却可能翻天覆地。
所以关于财富，我觉得有一个特别简单的道理：
永远不要用我们需要的钱，去挣我们不需要的钱。
什么叫需要的钱？
是能够让家人安稳生活的钱，是孩子的教育、父母的养老，是生病时不必借钱，是不想工作时还能有底气休息几年。
什么叫不需要的钱？
是已经拥有足够的财富，却还想再多赚一点；是一个亿变成两个亿，两个亿变成五个亿；是那些即使没有赚到，也不会影响生活的数字。
如果为了后者，把前者也押上去，无论最后赢了多少钱，这个选择都值得警惕。
我不反对冒险，也不反对追求财富。但至少应该知道，哪些钱可以冒险，哪些钱无论如何都应该留下来。
选择继续追逐财富，要承担失去财富的可能；选择停下来，也要承担错过机会的遗憾。
但人最容易犯的错误，就是把错过赚钱机会的遗憾，看得比失去已有财富的痛苦还重。
赚到一个亿以后，看到别人赚了十个亿，觉得自己错过了九个亿。可那九个亿原本就不属于你。
你真正拥有的，是手里的一个亿。
为了追逐那九个亿，把已经拥有的一个亿也输掉了，这才是真正的损失。
这就是“未失而能止者，人选也；既失而后止者，天选也”。
在还有选择权的时候，主动决定不再追逐什么，这叫人选。等到财富失去，现实逼着你停下来，那就由不得自己选择了。
当然，我不知道慕岩今天的处境究竟是怎样造成的，更不知道他过去做过哪些财务选择。我虽然想用一个人的困难去证明自己的观点，但不能。
但他的事情确实再次提醒了我，人在有的时候，一定要懂得守，尤其要懂得放弃。
而财富的得失，还只是事情的一面。
更难的是，一个人失去财富以后，能不能放下过去的自己。
我们这个社会特别喜欢讲东山再起。一个成功的企业家遇到困难，大家第一反应就是，他什么时候能够重新成功？
仿佛曾经拥有过一个亿，以后就必须再赚回一个亿，否则就意味着失败。
可为什么呢？
一个人曾经站在山顶，难道就没有资格走下山来？
他可以重新创业，也可以过普通人的生活。可以继续追逐财富，也可以做过去一直想做、却没有时间做的事情。
人生又不是只有一场考试，考过一次第一名，以后就必须永远考第一名。
有时候，最难放下的可能已经不是钱，而是曾经那个成功的自己。
曾经别人见到你，会主动打招呼，尊重你的意见，认真听你讲话。突然有一天，这些东西都变了。
你还能不能接受自己？还能不能坦然面对曾经认识你的人？还能不能允许自己重新成为普通人？
这些问题，可能比失去多少钱更难回答。
所以看到慕岩公开求助，我并不觉得有什么可笑的。一个人愿意承认困难，愿意向别人开口，本身就需要勇气。
我希望他能渡过难关，也希望他不必被过去的成功困住。
说回那2000块钱。
我为什么转完以后，要把他删掉？
除了不想让他收款时有压力，还有一个原因。
我不想让这2000块钱变成一笔未来的投资。
慕岩毕竟曾经是成功的企业家。也许有一天，他真的东山再起了。
到那个时候，我会不会想起自己曾经帮助过他？会不会觉得，我们之间因此多了一份特殊的关系？
我不敢保证自己一定不会。
人对自己的道德评价，往往比真实的自己要高。
《人选天选论》里还有一句话：
道德是选择完成后对自己的解释。
我今天可以说自己出于好意，过几年，也许又会给这件事找出另外一套解释。
所以我选择把这段关系暂时放下。
他曾经给我刷过礼物，我今天有能力，就给他转2000块钱。至于他将来会不会重新成功，会不会记得，都不重要。
当然，有人可能会问：既然不想要回报，为什么还要发文章讲这件事？
两个原因。
第一个，给自己的决策装装逼。
我没必要把自己包装得多么高尚，仿佛连一点虚荣心都没有。
第二个，希望这件事能被更多人看见。
慕岩求助的消息已经传了出来，我不知道他是否希望得到更多关注，也不知道外界的帮助能不能解决问题。但如果文章能让更多人了解他的处境，或许也能带来一点帮助。
虚荣心是我的，2000块钱也是我自愿给的。我可以承认自己想装逼，但不想因此要求他欠我一个人情。
其实人与人之间的缘分，有时候挺奇妙的。
我们上次还在微信里讨论孙宇晨，讨论别人的事情。没想到过了一段时间，我却在新闻里看到了他的事情。
今天我有能力给他转2000块钱，明天也许我会遇到自己的困难。谁又能保证一辈子都顺风顺水呢？
至于慕岩兄，如果将来他东山再起，我会不会替他高兴；如果他选择放下过去，重新开始另一种生活，我倒是会祝福他。
我们曾经有过一麦之缘，
他不必因此记住我，如果有一天，我们又在什么地方碰见，还能像以前一样，聊聊孙宇晨，聊聊各自的经历着就很好。
君子之交，淡如水，下个人生路口再见。

时薪15美元的专家：
利用AI，让普通人可以承担专家的工作。

写作垂直LLM：

text:
马斯克曾经投了1000万美元，帮亲表弟开了一家公司。

结果后来，两个表弟都被他开除了，他还说，他快恨死自己的表弟了🤣

因为这俩兄弟拿了他的钱，做出来的东西却像狗屎🤣

林登和彼得是马斯克的亲表弟，他们的妈妈Kaye和马斯克的妈妈Maye是双胞胎姐妹。

兄弟俩从南非来到美国后，开了一家帮小公司管电脑的IT公司，起家靠的就是踩着滑板满城打推销电话。
2004年夏天，几个人开着房车去玩，路上林登说IT做烦了，想干点能帮人类应对气候变化的事。
马斯克就回了一句："去做太阳能吧。"

林登还真当了真，和哥哥彼得琢磨出一个办法，客户一分钱不用先出，打个电话，就有人上门把太阳能板装好。
那是2006年，马斯克很仗义的给两兄弟投资了1000万美元，办起了SolarCity，他自己还当了董事长。
他只给了表弟一个要求：越快做大越好。

兄弟俩还真做大了，可靠的还是他们的老本行：推销，为了冲业绩，公司给销售发提成，派人上门推销。

马斯克越看越别扭，说这跟挨家挨户推销刀具的没什么两样，在他看来，东西只要做得够好，订单自己就会找上门，根本不用这样。
他一遍遍追问俩表弟："你们到底是一家销售公司，还是一家产品公司？"

表弟们却不太明白马斯克为什么这么较真，连一个夹子好不好看都要挑，看着丑就生气。

到了2016年，马斯克让特斯拉花了26亿美元，把表弟的公司整个买了下来，说要做一个真正好看的太阳能屋顶。
作为表哥，真的算是仁至义尽了。

可那年8月，表弟彼得给他展示的，却是一个金属太阳能屋顶，为了能快点装上去，好看只能往后放。

马斯克下车一看就炸了，说这个可怕的东西完全就是狗屎啊！
他当场下令，只做太阳能瓦片。

结果到了发布会前两天，金属屋顶还是摆在了现场，这俩家伙完全是把自己的话当了耳旁风啊，于是马斯克又发了一顿火。

公司买下来没几个月，马斯克就叫停了SolarCity挨家挨户的上门推销，涉及大约1000个推销员。
两周后，林登宣布离开，又过了两个月，彼得也走了，对外一个说想陪陪家人再创业，一个说想先休息一下，走得都挺体面。

可私下里，完全是另一回事，马斯克说是他把俩表弟开了，还说，我恨死我表弟了，我想我再也不会跟他们说话了😂😂

text:
The relationship between stocks and bonds has flipped again:

The 20-day correlation between the 10Y Note Yield and the Nasdaq 100 is up to +0.51, its highest since the March pullback.

This marks a sharp reversal from the negative correlation of -0.68 recorded in the last week of September.

This also follows 6 consecutive months in which the 20-day correlation between the two assets remained negative.

This comes as Treasuries once again acted as a hedge against the drop in tech stocks, as they did during the March pullback and the March-April 2025 correction.

To put this into perspective, during the 2020 pandemic crash, the 20-day correlation between the 10Y Note yield and the Nasdaq 100 surged to as much as +0.85.

The Treasury market is regaining its role as a defensive trade.

author: akshaybd
quoted_text:
No, it definitely won't. I personally spent several years building SHA-256 as a Boolean circuit and then using all the most sophisticated techniques known to math and cryptography to try to invert that function (to execute a preimage attack). I know the math of SHA-256 more deeply than most people on this planet. It's exceptionally well-defined as a trapdoor function, and inverting it is most certainly NP complete.

I also spent over 30 years trying to prove that P = NP, and threw my entire 30 years of knowledge of this problem at frontier LLMs to try to crack it. What they ended up doing was to thoroughly and convincingly refute every single line of reasoning and "clever" trick I came up with over those decades, which has now left me believing for the first time that actually P≠NP.

text:
Fable复盘——找早期项目的逻辑

找早期项目，我现在最有感受的办法不是刷推特，是等一条链热起来之后，把链上所有协议挨个扫一遍。

先说下，Fable 这个项目我赚得不多，七周下来三个点，年化二十几。但它是我今年最值得写的一笔，因为它不是谁喊的，是扫出来的。

当时 PONS 刚起来，Robinhood 链很热。我的逻辑是这样：一条链热度起来了，钱会往链上其他协议流，那就看链上还有谁的数据在动。我让 AI 监控了全网，顺手做了个监控面板，扫出来几个，大多要么只能二级买、要么已经晚了，只有一个还算早期，能靠做 LP 拿一级的筹码，门槛也不高。最合适。

进场的时候它的 TVL 还在一千万左右，一个月后涨了三倍多，吃掉了全链三分之一的 LP 手续费。什么概念呢，我进场那周每一刀手续费能换四百多积分，最后两周进来的人只能换不到一百。

早到的人吃的是肉，热度显出来再进的人，只能喝汤了

过程也比较曲折。开始的时候几千刀测了一天，数据还没回来就加到了十倍，后来又加到四十倍，也是我的老毛病。

区间跑出去四次，每次重新进场也是比较谨慎。积分活动延期，很多人骂稀释，但其实我觉的也还好，我算了一下留下的人反而拿得多，就留了，积分翻了一倍。

代币这块预期差得最远。公告写 12% 给社区，到了领取页面，不带锁仓条件的只有 4.5%。开盘 0.08u，比我算的悲观还要悲观。我定了闹钟，六点起来第一时间全卖了，因为结构很清楚：首日流通 6.5%，一半是零成本筹码，一年供应翻五倍，这种币不适合拿。空投锁仓最后的结局只有归零。

最后的数据，ETH 下跌亏的被手续费补回来了，利润主要是开盘卖掉的代币。策略本身年化三位数，被 ETH 跌 8% 吃掉三分之二。亏的部分大头是行情，但是行情无法控制，最理想的就是在手续费最多的时候撤掉，但是站在那个当下是很难的。

这项目我最大的体会是：凡是从规则推出来的判断都对了，凡是从价格倒推的估值都错了。

总后总结下，一条链热度起来，扫链上每个协议的数据异动，筛早期、一级逻辑、门槛低的那个，先小仓位测、合适再加仓位。就是个流程。

面板我现在还开着，下一条链起来的时候，还这么扫。行情好不好需要你自己判断，我只能说这套在行情不好的时候，也依旧可以赚个零花钱。

最后附上 9/25 号时候的 Robinhood 链的协议监控截图

author: _ConorMoore
quoted_text:
A lot of ink has been spilled on GPU financing lately. I spent over a decade trading ABS on Wall St, and structured over $2B+ of debt financings as an operator (including at @tryramp). Figured I'd try to make sense of this market, so I went back to a framework I knew well: aircraft ABS and aircraft engine ABS.

My take: a GPU neocloud runs on airline economics, and the debt behind it looks a lot like aircraft engine ABS.

The parallels:

• Perishable inventory. An empty seat after the door closes is gone forever. So is an idle hour on an energized H100 rack.
• 85%+ of cost is fixed (servers, 10-year rack leases, 10-14% debt service). One more hour of compute costs pennies of power.
• Utilization is everything. Airlines break even around 80% load factor, a levered GPU cluster around 65-75%. The returns live in those last 25 percentage points.
• NVIDIA is Boeing and Airbus rolled into one. Powered shells and grid interconnects are the new airport slots.
• Wall St copied the aircraft financing playbook: take-or-pay contract plus servers in a bankruptcy-remote SPV, 70-80% LTV.

Part 1 of my blog post goes into a lot more detail:

https://t.co/0fghWVnGOU

author: OdailyChina
quoted_text:
4 data leaks reported today:

1. Coinbase's vendor Amplitude exposed some users’ contact data (funds unaffected).
2. Bithumb (Korea) had user data leaks.

In TradFi, two securities firms in Korea leaked data: 
3. Mirae Asset
4. Daishin Securities

You can't prevent a leak, but you can protect yourself.

Leaked exchange data (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ID documents, transaction history) is mostly used for phishing, SIM swapping, and social engineering.

Reduce info you share
- Use a unique email alias for each exchange (SimpleLogin, Apple Hide My Email, etc). A leak then can't be linked to your other accounts, and you can spot which service leaked.
- Share only what's required. Don't add optional profile details.
- Use a dedicated phone number (a VoIP or secondary SIM) for exchange accounts if you can, since leaked numbers are the main route to SIM swaps.

Lock down the account
- Use a unique, long password from a password manager.
- Turn on hardware security keys (YubiKey) or passkeys, or at least an authenticator app.
- Avoid SMS 2FA.
- Enable withdrawal address whitelisting and a withdrawal time lock if the exchange offers them.
- Set up an anti-phishing code, which puts a code you choose in every legitimate email from the exchange.
- Review active sessions and API keys regularly. Delete any API keys you don't use.
- Restrict API keys to withdraw-disabled and IP-whitelisted.

Defend against
- SIM swapping: Ask your carrier to add a port-out PIN or number lock.
- Phishing and impersonation: Assume anyone who contacts you about your account, "security issues," or "refund recovery" is a scammer, even if they know your name, balance, or recent trades.
- Exchange support staff don't ask for your password, 2FA codes, or seed phrase.
- Never click links in emails or texts. Go to the site yourself.

- "Wrench attacks": Leaked addresses plus holdings data have led to real-world extortion and robberies. Don't publicize your holdings, and keep large balances out of anything tied to your home address if you can.

If a breach is announced
1. Change the exchange password and any other account that reused it.
2. Check https://t.co/qtIGFkbaPO for your email address.
3. Revoke API keys and active sessions.
4. Review recent withdrawals and security settings.
5. Watch for phishing emails and texts that reference the breach, because scammers move fast after one.

Stay SAFU! 🙏

quoted_text:
4 data leaks reported today:

1. Coinbase's vendor Amplitude exposed some users’ contact data (funds unaffected).
2. Bithumb (Korea) had user data leaks.

In TradFi, two securities firms in Korea leaked data: 
3. Mirae Asset
4. Daishin Securities

You can't prevent a leak, but you can protect yourself.

Leaked exchange data (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ID documents, transaction history) is mostly used for phishing, SIM swapping, and social engineering.

Reduce info you share
- Use a unique email alias for each exchange (SimpleLogin, Apple Hide My Email, etc). A leak then can't be linked to your other accounts, and you can spot which service leaked.
- Share only what's required. Don't add optional profile details.
- Use a dedicated phone number (a VoIP or secondary SIM) for exchange accounts if you can, since leaked numbers are the main route to SIM swaps.

Lock down the account
- Use a unique, long password from a password manager.
- Turn on hardware security keys (YubiKey) or passkeys, or at least an authenticator app.
- Avoid SMS 2FA.
- Enable withdrawal address whitelisting and a withdrawal time lock if the exchange offers them.
- Set up an anti-phishing code, which puts a code you choose in every legitimate email from the exchange.
- Review active sessions and API keys regularly. Delete any API keys you don't use.
- Restrict API keys to withdraw-disabled and IP-whitelisted.

Defend against
- SIM swapping: Ask your carrier to add a port-out PIN or number lock.
- Phishing and impersonation: Assume anyone who contacts you about your account, "security issues," or "refund recovery" is a scammer, even if they know your name, balance, or recent trades.
- Exchange support staff don't ask for your password, 2FA codes, or seed phrase.
- Never click links in emails or texts. Go to the site yourself.

- "Wrench attacks": Leaked addresses plus holdings data have led to real-world extortion and robberies. Don't publicize your holdings, and keep large balances out of anything tied to your home address if you can.

If a breach is announced
1. Change the exchange password and any other account that reused it.
2. Check https://t.co/qtIGFkbaPO for your email address.
3. Revoke API keys and active sessions.
4. Review recent withdrawals and security settings.
5. Watch for phishing emails and texts that reference the breach, because scammers move fast after one.

Stay SAFU! 🙏
