quoted_text:
我来蹭一下今早 $USD3 提额被秒抢一空的热度 ✍️

@3janexyz 作为我今年继 Saturn 之后最大的稳定币理财仓位，机制和收益都有很亮眼的地方。但同时，机制上也有比较复杂的地方，如果没有正确理解，很容易踩坑。本文争取把关于 3Jane 的基本面、机制、和风险点解释清楚

————————————————

1️⃣ 业务逻辑
3Jane 是一个撮合资金方和借贷方的信用贷平台
资金方存入 USDC，获得 USD3。USD3 代表了应收债务的金额+累积利息
借贷方是选定合作的 Fintech 公司。通过信用评级后，Fintech 公司在 3Jane 平台借款后再分发给自己的下游客户

————————————————

2️⃣ USD3 & sUSD3
去年 11 月刚了解 3Jane 的时候，USD3 还是足额抵押的美元稳定币，sUSD3 去累积债务的利息，但同时要背负坏账的风险。

但后面经济模型改进了，现在 USD3/sUSD3 更像是一个优先/劣后 (Senior/Junior tranche) 的关系
USD3 - 代表对应债务的份额 + 应收利息的 yield-bearing stablecoin，单位净值会随着时间累积。目前的 NAV ≈ $1.19，但极端信用损失的情况下净值仍有可能回撤到 $1 以下
sUSD3 - 占整个 3Jane 资金池更小的比例，能分配到更多应收利息，但同时要吸收坏账的风险。如果借款人出现 default，sUSD3 要优先承担损失

简单来说：USD3 收益略低 (~6.5% APY) 风险可控；sUSD3 收益高 (~13% APY) 但可能出现亏损

————————————————

3️⃣ LCC (Levered Callable Capital)
9/1 新上的功能，全名叫 Levered Callable Capital，中文我把它翻译成「杠杆待命资本」
简单理解就是：你需要放贷很多钱，但没人借的时候，资本空转，资本利用率很低。
LCC 允许你只放一小部分钱当保证金，当有人借的时候，再在 9 天的窗口期内调集资金，把全部金额借出去
但这里有一个坑：如果资金方没有在窗口期内把承诺资金放出去，保证金会被清算，分配给有能力调用资金的其他资金方作为奖励

如果还不能理解，举一个实际例子：
> 你打算借出 $100k 资金，但暂时没有人来借，资金会闲置
> LCC 允许你先放 $7500 作为保证金，并且这部分保证金可以享受 ~20% 年化收益
> 当有借款需求的时候，你需要在 9 天窗口期内将全额 $100k 资金贷出去（全额转换为 USD3）。如果没做到，$7500 的保证金会被罚没

————————————————

4️⃣ 预挖 $JANE 的几种方式
3Jane 最吸引矿佬，也是最吸引人的一个亮点是：不搞积分 pua，直接按每周一个 epoch 来预挖 $JANE 代币（可以直接 claim 到钱包，但暂不可转让）

能预挖 $JANE 的几种方式见「图二」👇🏻
- 持有 USD3
- 持有 sUSD3
- 存 USDC @ Morpho
- USD3 YT/LP @ Pendle
- sUSD3 YT/LP @ Pendle
- USD3/frxUSD LP @ Curve
- LCC 存 USDC/USDT

以上策略均可以不同的速率预挖 $JANE ，具体速率可参考 https://t.co/l2Xkc4ge9S

————————————————

5️⃣ 风险点
3Jane 的参与流程包含了多个风险点，我尽可能列出。如有错误/遗漏，请在评论区指正

1) USD3 目前没有铸造额度，115m USD3 已经被全部铸造完。想要获得 USD3 需要在 Curve 上兑换，需要承受一定的交易滑点和二级市场溢价
2) USD3 理论风险很低，但仍有可能出现净值回撤的情况。当坏账发生，sUSD3 保险被击穿，USD3 就会出现净值回撤
3) LCC 的收益/资金占用问题，这是我认为是 LCC 目前量很难起来的主要原因。LCC 的杠杆倍率是 13.3x / 7.5%，如果 commit $10000 进去，只有 $750 仓位能获得 20% APY。剩余的 $9250 虽然不占用，可以拿去做别的事，但需要有流动性支持，才能在窗口期内被调集
4) 每周 $JANE 排放对应的 APY，取决于你设置多少的 FDV 来估算。记得在右上角填上你认为合理的上线估值，我设置的是 150-200m FDV（非财务建议，综合 RWA/信贷 赛道的表现和 TVL 来看，算是比较中肯的估值）

————————————————

从赛道、商业模型、项目审美、跟团队的交流等各方面综合考虑，个人认为 3Jane 值得参与。我自己也是从 7 月份就在参与 3Jane，策略相对保守，只持有 USD3，每周吃低保。

最后祝大家安全生产，本金安全最重要！🙏

SpaceX / xAI 的工程师 Lauren Tan（前 Cursor 核心成员）直接把 GrokBot 跑成了一家 50 人的分布式软件公司：

一个人在后台跑 20~50 个 GrokBot，5 个月合并了 3,000+ 个 PR，一人打出了一整支 20 人研发团队的产出：
 
1 个 Chief of Staff：负责统筹全天优先级，统一分发调度任务

 3 个 PM Agent：拆解 PRD，把控上下文与工单交接

 40+ 个 Worker：整夜异步跑代码、建分支、自动化提交 PR

早上起来端着咖啡 Review 结果，确认无误直接点 Merge。

她在 50 分钟分享里讲的底层逻辑，没有半点 Prompt 玄学，全是硬核工程架构：

1. 不搞一次性对话：

给 Agent 明确的岗位定位与交付协议，上下文像流水线一样标准化交接，绝不单次发散聊天。

2. 信任靠系统，不靠感觉：

用 ⁠pstack⁠ 规则死死锁住 Context 上限，配合一套严苛的 5 层自我验证栈（从 Linter、单元测试、回归验证到沙箱自动化运行），彻底终结人工逐行巡检。

3. 架构必须对 Agent 友好：

重构工程架构，让模块边界极简、依赖解耦，让 AI 能够独立消化，而不是被臃肿代码库撑爆上下文。

4. 终结人肉监工，实现“睡后交付”：

让系统在沙箱里自己检验自己，真正拉开人效差距的，是夜间无人值守的自动化管线，而不是盯着光标逐字吐出。

在 SpaceX 和 xAI 内部：

已经有很大比例的工程师在用这种方式碾压式交付

剩下的人很快就会感受到断层压力。

分水岭从来不在于谁更会写 Prompt

而在于你有没有把 AI 从“聊天玩具”升级成“能自我闭环与运转的工程系统”。

text:
The loss extended far beyond Dr. Sabatini. The whole country suffers when institutions entrusted with advancing knowledge reward the behavior of Sangeeta Bhatia.

When I first became a tenure-track professor, I was quickly disillusioned by how little interest so many of my colleagues seemed to have in science. It shocked me because it made no sense. My love of science was why I took the job. I accepted much less pay and much longer hours because it gave me the chance to devote myself to something I loved.

Many colleagues seemed far more interested in chasing prestige and stature within the university. I had assumed that people who made those sacrifices shared my priorities. Finding out otherwise was a profound disappointment.

You can see those priorities on display in Sangeeta Bhatia’s messages. In the exchanges, you can see celebration of David’s destruction and no concern for the science and knowledge being lost. He was a scientist with far greater scientific accomplishments than hers. Yet, Bhatia was someone directing a cancer research center at MIT and treated as an authority on advancing cancer research.

Dr. Sabatini’s work laid the foundations for a major field of drug development, including cancer therapies. Dismantling his laboratory meant interrupting the work of someone whose discoveries had already opened enormous scientific and therapeutic possibilities. None of that concern is visible in these exchanges.

This is what happens when universities reward bureaucratic hacks who promote their personal causes, work their way into leadership, and use institutional authority to pursue those causes while the science suffers. Her titles remain, even as the institution decays.

People involved in removing Dr. Sabatini retained their positions of stature or advanced. His laboratory was dismantled. Years of work were interrupted, scientific were lost, the careers of the poeple he was mentoring were disrupted and the people celebrating kept their authority.

Meanwhile, MIT puts on a show claiming merit is its main focus while the place rots behind the veneer of excellence it displays to the public.

text:
I’ve been thinking a lot recently about the pipeline into scientific and medical research, especially being from Boston where I still spend a lot of time and frequently hear researchers complaining about the Trump administration supposedly killing science. But even if you believe that Trump administration policies have hurt science (which honestly I don’t), you should acknowledge that it is only after about fifteen years of toxic dynamics that used dubious allegations to throw out those who lived and breathed science, like @DMSabatini, whom I interviewed for @PirateWires—insofar as academia is struggling right now, it only has itself to blame. 

In Sabatini’s case, he literally trained nearly 50 academic lab heads—seven whom he was able to send to Harvard, five of them women—and all he got for it was being publicly humiliated out of MIT for the not-crime of having had a consensual sexual relationship with a woman in another lab. When great scientists are marginalized and even abused by the system, you know who remains? Mediocrities, those who do everything by the book, color coded, neat handwriting, the types who will never accidentally drink one glass of mulled wine too many at a Christmas party, the types who say “holiday party,” the types who never come across as flirtatious or crude, not even accidentally—but ultimately they will never push the frontiers of science, and they will never attract those who will to work for them either (these days, those types will simply go to San Francisco).

compute按照期货交易逻辑

1. neocloud其实是+ spot - future，这样他们有个固定很厚的收益

他们承担的风险是counterparty default，交易本质就是比较funding cost和future - spot

2. 现在很多CSP其实才是future buyer，他们并不锁定算力出去。算力按照远期curve揍的最大受益方，不按远期走的最大受害者

3. labs 是买了很future long 还在继续买spot和future

4. semi— 产油公司，现在完全没估值。短期涨跌是估算不了的，疫情时候spot石油已经跌成负数了

但是如果curve不变，拿着spot是个最简单carry trade

这是我为什么非常bullish的核心逻辑

在 Morpho。

官方曾发过一句原话：Robinhood in the front, Morpho in the back。
前端是给散户看的券商界面，后端全是 Morpho 的借贷管网。

昨晚全量放开的 Robinhood Earn，用户出借 USDG 躺赚 7% 年化。这笔钱往哪走？全沉淀在顶级风控团队 SteakhouseFi 帮 Morpho 策展的池子里。上线三个月，悄悄吸了 10 亿美元。

但理财只是前戏。

真正让资金闻到味儿的，是 10 月 22 号那条公告。
Stock Tokens 接入 Morpho，链上美股能当抵押品借稳定币了。
Crypto 负责人 Johann Kerbrat 转发时特意定调：这是关键一步。

为什么是关键一步？
以前在链上买 AAPL、NVDA，只能干放着等涨跌。不能质押、不能生息，充其量就是一张 24 小时能倒手的美股截图。
现在抵押一开，信用杠杆就跑通了。
抵押美股借出稳定币，去买币、去对冲、或者继续吃息。死钱瞬间变活钱。

很多人纳闷，Robinhood 为什么不选 Aave，而选 Morpho？
因为 Aave 是大锅饭。池子里只要有一个资产暴雷，大家一起扛坏账。
Morpho Blue 则是完全隔离池。每只股票单独成仓，真遇上极端黑天鹅，风险也只能炸一个角落，根本穿不透底座。上市公司最在乎什么？合规与连带风控。Morpho 刚好卡在了这个命门上。

前端有现成的零售大水喉，后端有机构风控盯着隔离信贷。
所谓的代币化美股闭环，其实就是这么跑起来的。

$MORPHO $HOOD #Robinhood #DeFi

An update on Verda Ventures and our next chapter.

After three years of building Verda Ventures into a venture fund focused on stablecoin infrastructure, Amit and I are excited to share that we will be working with the team at Tether who was one of Verda’s LP. 

As part of this transition, coinciding with the target investment period, Verda Ventures will move into harvesting mode. We will stop investments in new companies to avoid potential conflicts of interest while continuing to manage and support our existing portfolio. We will participate selectively in follow-on rounds of existing portfolio companies. We will continue to support our portfolio companies as they scale, including companies that have also received direct investment from Tether, such as Mural Pay, Finity/Plenti, and Lemon Cash.

As the leading stablecoin issuer, joining Tether is a natural next step in our mission to accelerate the adoption of stablecoins and accelerate the financial infrastructure of the future.
 
We're incredibly proud of the portfolio we've built and are very bullish on the 28 companies we’ve invested in. We remain fully committed to the long-term success of our founders and returns for our LPs.

The past few months have been quite an emotional rollercoaster, and it's made me realize something.

We all need something that brings us joy, comfort, or just a little escape from everyday life, whether it's books, movies, music, or a world like Love and Deepspace.

Finding happiness in something fictional doesn't mean losing touch with reality. The stories may be fictional, but the emotions they awaken are real.

Our minds are capable of forming genuine emotional connections with fictional worlds and characters. Knowing something isn't real doesn't make what we feel any less real.

What makes me saddest is how quickly people judge, belittle, or even try to take away what gives others comfort.

Life is complicated enough. We should be kinder to each other and respect the little worlds that make life brighter.

No one should ever feel ashamed of something that brings them happiness. ❤️

One of my main goals at pumpfun is to help make it the go-to place where every founder launches their project and finds success.

With the resources, support, and expertise we can provide to teams, I’m confident we can take a better hands-on approach and provide stronger support to founders than any other launchpad.

quoted_text:
Today, in collaboration with Anthropic, we’re excited to share rapid initial progress towards an antibody treatment for food allergy, which affects over 200 million people worldwide, discovered with the help of Claude.

At Divergence Labs, we believe that AI can unlock the next generation of antibody therapeutics with more effective mechanisms than before. Such mechanisms are urgently needed in food allergy, which involve overcoming one of the tightest affinity protein pairs in immunology, IgE and its receptor FcεRI, on mast cells.

Treatment with Xolair—the only approved antibody for food allergy—sequesters circulating IgE, but mast cells remain sensitized for weeks to months due to the extraordinarily slow dissociation of IgE from FcεRI.

We envision a treatment that actively pulls IgE off of FcεRI, without waiting for natural dissociation. Like picking a lock, this requires the right combination of geometry and force.

Our research team, working with Claude, ideated on mechanisms to accomplish this disruption, and converged on an antibody format with two arms with different functions and epitopes. Within one month, we designed, synthesized, and experimentally confirmed the biophysical function of the two arms, which we are now assembling into full therapeutic formats.

author: airtightfish
quoted_text:
What’s Brent worth if the US ends the Iranian blockade by year end?

Traders on @ifmarkets priced it at $104.90. And $106.61 if it doesn’t.

That $1.71 gap is the price of the event itself. You can bet on the event, you can long oil, but you can’t trade the gap with real money anywhere yet. Four teams are racing to change that.

Why does it matter?

Events are where the money gets made. Over 60% of the US equity risk premium was earned on scheduled macro announcement days, which make up only ~13% of the sample (Savor & Wilson).

Prediction markets price the odds of those events. What the event does to the asset has no liquid market of its own, so traders back it out of options skew and sell-side notes.

The demand to trade combinations is already obvious tho. Combos were 58% of Kalshi's volume in September, and parlays are the crudest way to stack conditions.

Luckily, the clean version is being built rn: impact markets, a.k.a. conditional markets. You price an asset in the world where an event happens, and only in that world.

How does it work?

Take the Iran blockade. The event splits the market into two worlds, and each world gets its own oil price.

- You think the blockade ends and oil drops? Short oil in the "ends" world at $104.90

- The blockade ends: your short settles against the real oil price

- It doesn't: your trade is cancelled and you get your money back

So you only carry oil risk in the world your view is about.

The two prices also pin today's oil price. If the blockade is a coin flip, oil should sit near the midpoint, ~$105.76. If it drifts away, traders arb it back.

Those Brent numbers come from If Market's play-money test version on the 16th of October btw, so read them as a demo of how it works.

And it's obviously not all without risk. Being right about the event doesn't make you safe. You short oil in the "ends" world, the blockade does end, but if oil spikes first you can still get liquidated before you get paid.

Why now?

The idea is old. Hanson wrote about decision markets in 1999, Gnosis' conditional tokens date back to 2018 (Polymarket still settles on them), and Paradigm laid out "multiverse finance" in May 2025.

What's new is that prediction markets got deep enough to anchor the odds leg, and four teams are racing to ship the asset leg:

- @ifmarkets: cash-settled worlds on oil, gold, BTC and stocks. Public beta on paper funds, first contest did 2,000+ traders and 6M+ trades

- @ProofMarkets: own exchange where perps, conditional perps and binaries share one margin pool, so a fully boxed hedge nets to ~zero margin. 500+ traders in a June paper contest, real-money private alpha next (~Nov per Galaxy)

- @lightconexyz: splits a deposit into one universe token per outcome, on Solana. Private beta, public launch targeted before YE

- @BranchpointXYZ: lending and borrowing inside each branch, plus Branchmap, a shared ID standard for events. Waitlist

Decision markets are the cousin that's already live: MetaDAO and Umia steer $50.5M across 24 DAO treasuries.

What's the hard part?

Liquidity. An odds market needs one book per event. Proof's design needs five per event and asset: the perp, YES and NO conditional perps, YES and NO binaries. 20 events on 6 assets is 240 conditional books.

Each of those needs makers quoting both worlds, arbitrage against the perp and the odds market, and short resolution windows so capital isn't parked for months.

Then regulation. Cash-settled exposure to oil, stocks and BTC contingent on political events is a derivative almost everywhere. Kalshi and Polymarket already have the licences and the flow.

And Hyperliquid. HIP-4 outcome markets and HIP-3 perps already live on the same HyperCore stack. Someone pairing them could ship conditional books where the liquidity already sits. Just my inference tho, nobody has announced it.

My conclusion?

The primitive is real, and the demand is already visible in how fast combos took over the incumbents.

I'm not picking a winner yet tho. Every venue is pre-real-money and every traction number is paper.

What I'm watching:

- First real-money launch (Proof's private alpha looks closest)

- Published depth on the flagship books

- First clean resolution (If Market's blockade book resolves on the 31st of December)

- Kalshi, Polymarket or a HIP-3/4 deployer listing an asset-if-event contract

There are no tokens to buy yet, but still: NFA in any way, shape or form.

The concept is very interesting tho imo.

Prediction markets taught the world to price events.

Impact markets will price what those events are worth.

text:
沃什讲话总结——10月鹰派暂停+鹰派通胀目标+未锁死但是保留12月加息选项，基本符合此前市场预期！

10月鹰派加息是此前市场的预期，而今晚沃什讲话基本属于符合预期，整体讲话听下来反而没有预期中那么鹰

1，对于通胀，是沃什讲话最鹰的一部分，强调没有软性通胀目标，见顶Fed通胀目标就是2%，Fed不接受更高的通胀预期

2，名义收益率+实际收益率上升，市场自然金融收缩暂时代替Fed加息的必要，这也成为10月不加息的理由

3，“Watchful thinking, not watchful waiting” “审慎思考，而非审慎等待”，这是沃什的原话，试图用这个理念来代替10月份的暂停加息，目的是不想让市场预期加息周期结束，继续保留12月加息窗口

4，沃什强调对AI资本开支的担忧，他的判断是资本开支强劲已经不在局限于少数领域，对美国经济是利好，同时也是经济增长的利好，AI短期是需求冲击，长期才可能成为供给冲击，沃什的观点认为AI的繁荣未必帮助Fed降息，反而会增加Fed控制通胀的难度

5，沃什承认了高利率在压制科技企业，但是并未打断目前的资本开支，他知道高利率的代价，但是目前美国经济和AI投资仍然承受得住，所以短期美股的波动不足以让Fed改变政策

6，明确能源通胀与Fed政策的关系，名义上能源供给带来的通胀Fed不会管，但是如果能源通胀向核心通胀扩散，Fed就要进一步收紧政策，这意味后续PCE数据是重点。

7，沃什今晚的讲话重新定义了Fed的“政策反应函数”，之前我们看PCE +GPD+就业+油价，现在要增加一个新的变量——金融状况

第一层，看通胀，观察PCE  CPI 服务通胀 工资 通胀扩散 能源二次传导
第二层，看实体经济，GDP 就业 资本支出 AI投资 生产率
第三层，看金融条件，看2Y 10Y 实际利率，看美元，看信用利差，看美股

沃什一直强调减少前瞻指引，依赖更多数据来决定Fed政策，而沃什也让数据观测领域更加复杂多样化了

如果按照这个逻辑，如果未来几周10Y收益率上涨+实际利率继续上涨+企业融资成本继续增加+金融条件进一步收紧，那么反而会削弱Fed 12月加息的可能性，反过来如果10Y快速下跌 + 美股大涨 + 信贷利差收窄 + 美元走弱，导致金融条件明显宽松，AI资本开支继续爆发，通胀仍然维持高位，那么12月加息可能性大大增加。

总结：

通过今晚沃什的讲话来看，进一步证明了我此前的猜测——沃什正在让美国利率处于一个有限宽松的阶段，沃什今晚的讲话相对此前预期没有更鹰，但是也没有关闭12月加息的可能性，如果一句话总结——沃什今晚试图让市场明白，这是一个开始让市场承担一部分加息工作的Fed

text:
try 10 to 200 eth.
----
btw: side-by-side by hand is really not the best way to compare

1. You get surplus in any tx and block going forward. usually is not passed on to the user; except over at @CoWSwap  (and still not to the full extent). The most accurate bench is a realistic 4 to 14 sec delayed sim, mid block. That is where it shines most with wide gaps.

2. off-chain aggregation is always a delayed view:
-> Sequencer 
-> Node / Indexer / ETL
-> Receiving request from UI
-> Solving then simulating
-> Sending back to UI

with an on-chain router you fire the simulation right away and get a fresher view / quote

hence, it will always look outperforming when market goes up, and the opposite if the market is going down.

that aside, if some propAMMs would be kind enough to match whitelist / fees aggregators get, for an arguably less toxic flow--amortized risk over all liquidity sources when routing BBO; that would help to close the gap (in a fair way)

author: veH0rny
quoted_text:
CT's independent takes on early-stage perp DEXs:

TxFlow - Hyperliquid fork, TemuLiquid. Red flag

Arcus - former dYdX team that still hasn’t built a decent perp DEX. Red flag

Entropy - CT badges, InfoFi, can't compete with TradeXYZ, part of the team came from Polymarket. Red flag

QFEX - not a perp DEX but a CEX. Founder is Indian. Red flag

Bulk - weak liquidity, oracle issues. Red flag

But where were all these experts when I was putting together my perp DEX skip list back in spring? Why wasn't anyone pointing out all these red flags in other perp DEXs back then? Everyone was just farming points across the board. Where were the deep dives into Hotstuff, StandX, Dango and all the other garbage I explicitly said I was skipping, while CT kept farming them like nothing was wrong?

Or has something changed over the past six months, and we suddenly have a whole bunch of new experts I didn't know about?

If it were all that obvious, guys, everyone would already be a millionaire from perp DEX airdrops. But what we're actually seeing before Variational TGE is CT fighting over future referrals. By trashing other perp DEXs, people are naturally steering users toward the ones they're farming themselves

And there's nothing wrong with that. Everyone makes their own bets. I did my own deep dive on Arcus and explained why I'm skipping it, while others see it as a gem. I see a gem in QFEX, while others see red flags and skip it

You can find red flags in literally any early-stage perp dex. There's no point obsessing over them. You might be betting on TxFlow and QFEX, just like me, someone else might prefer Entropy and Arcus, some people farm everything, others have completely different strategies, and some skip it all

The current FUD around TxFlow is pretty amusing to me because it's weird that people are only finding out about all these details now. If you'd actually dug into the site's code, its contracts and validators, you could've spotted all of this back in the summer. I did exactly that when I looked into the project in July. Whether any of this is good or bad is up to you to decide. Personally, I don't see anything wrong with borrowing from other platforms. TxFlow has been around since March this year, and despite all the suspicion surrounding it, there hasn't been a single protocol hack or any other major scam incident

Meanwhile, nobody was doing deep dives on Ostium, yet its vaults got hacked for $23M. Nobody was doing them on AFX either, and they lost millions. Same story with Dango, Aftermath, Cascade and others

So if TxFlow really is a Hyperliquid fork, I'll be more than happy if they fork the airdrop too

At the end of the day, it's up to you to decide what to farm and what to skip. Time will tell who made the right call and who didn't

If you know of an obvious gem in the early-stage perp DEX space that I haven't mentioned before, I'm happy to hear your take in the replies

text:
Feel like this decade should be called 'The Great Unraveling' or something like that..

Everywhere you look, things are just getting way more fluid and less stable and just way less certain...

- Will you still have your job in 2 years? Uncertain...

- What jobs will still exist in the future anyway? Uncertain...

- What industries will thrive? Uncertain...

- Should you buy an existing business? Probably not... too uncertain...

- Should you go back to school or training for a new career? Probably not... too uncertain...

- Will the stock market keep going up forever? Uncertain... is primarily political at this point based on the Fed and Treasury and 401k inflows and etc...

- Will residential real estate have another collapse? Uncertain... all depends on interest rates, so far it hasn't but there has to be a breaking point somewhere...

- Should you move into the good school district so your kids can go the best schools? Uncertain... AI is disrupting the entire education system just as fast as it is everything else...

- Will your safe, first world country still be a safe first would country in 20 years? Uncertain... you get the wrong leaders and it could speedrun civilizational suicide like many other western countries have lately... 

- Can you reject the traditional financial system and bet it all on Bitcoin? Sure... but even that is less certain now due to fears over quantum...

Indeed... even the long-term future of our species is increasingly brought into question... due to the global fertility crisis and microplastics and etc...

So yeah...

Obviously uncertainty has always been a part of life... 

However compared to 5 years ago or 10 years ago or 20 years ago or 50 years ago... it just seems like things have gotten WAY WAY more fluid...

Mostly this is because of AI... 

But partly it is just the blow off top in the sovereign debt bubble, which makes all economic questions primarily political... since everything just depends on the money printer vs austerity-larp seesaw... 

But yeah... 

Not sure what the solution is, but I think the best thing to do is just create a really good foundation, and stay lean...

Get healthy, get locked-in, keep geeking out on everything new and exciting...

Get your living expenses as low as possible relative to your assets (notice I said ASSETS and not INCOME - again, issa new world)...

And just keep putting in the reps and trying to set yourself up for success...

The flip side of chaos is opportunity, and you owe it to yourself, and your family, and your people to try to thrive amidst the insanity :)

OMG!! $ORCL just answered the only question that mattered to Wall Street!! 

For a year, the bear case on $ORCL it was spending like a hyperscaler without a hyperscaler's balance sheet and investors kept asking who pays for all those data centers. As of this afternoon that thesis is DEAD!!

Spending peaks in FY27–28 and falls after that. Free cash flow turns positive in the second half of FY28 and reaches $30bn+ in FY29. That's a ~$54bn swing in three years. 

From FY29, growth funds itself. New capital raising is capped at $20bn through 2030, split between $10bn of equity and $10bn of debt. The dilution and debt fears just got a ceiling.

The growth story is even bigger than report today imo. Maybe we’ll hear more about it on the earnings call. Revenue goes from $90bn next year to $225bn+ by FY30, growing 35%+ a year, with 40%+ operating margins and $21+ of EPS.

text:
今年跑赢QQQ的产品—03441，你需要知道的一切

最近开始关注一只比较有意思的ETF，南方东英的03441。

过去两年，美股市场最重要的投资逻辑之一就是AI带来的增长预期。

但我认为，这套逻辑正在发生变化。

随着AI行业逐步进入商业化验证阶段，企业收入增速开始出现分化，而微软、Meta、Google等科技巨头的资本开支仍然维持在非常高的位置。

当收入增长无法持续加速，资本开支却居高不下的时候，市场自然会从关注增长，转向关注增长的质量。

这意味着未来投资者可能不再只愿意为营收和EPS增长支付高估值，而是更加关注企业真正能够创造多少自由现金流。

也是基于这个判断，我认为03441采用的自由现金流因子选股，是一种非常先进，而且符合当前市场变化的投资方式。

下面详细讲讲。

1. 03441到底是什么？

03441全称是南方东英富时东西股票精选ETF，2025年3月31日在港交所上市。

它跟踪的是富时ETF通东西传承股票精选指数。

目前指数的核心结构是：
60%：港股高股息股票，约23家公司
40%：美股自由现金流策略，约100家公司

两部分资产的逻辑并不相同。

港股部分主要寻找股息回报相对突出的成熟企业，美股部分则从美国大型企业中筛选现金创造能力较强、符合质量与风险标准的公司。

它不是单纯的港股红利ETF，也不是把纳斯达克100换一个名字。

我更愿意把它理解为一种跨市场的现金流配置策略。

2. 它究竟买了哪些股票？

先看港股的60%。

主要持仓包括：
中电控股、电能实业、香港中华煤气、中银香港、海丰国际、港铁等。
这些企业覆盖公用事业、金融、运输等领域，很多企业经营模式相对成熟，能够通过股息向股东分配现金。

美股的40%则完全是另一套逻辑。
截至2026年10月26日，具有代表性的持仓包括：

MSFT 微软
AAPL 苹果
META Meta
AVGO 博通
GOOGL / GOOG Alphabet
BRK.B 伯克希尔
LLY 礼来

可以看出来，科技股依然占据重要位置。
但这里有个非常重要的区别：
03441并不是直接购买市值最大的七家科技公司，而是利用自由现金流因子，在美国大型企业中进行筛选。

这意味着它不会因为一家公司拥有很高的AI热度，就必然把它纳入投资组合。

3. 为什么我认为自由现金流因子是一种非常先进的选股方式？

先解释一下自由现金流。

FCF = 经营现金流 - 资本开支（Capex）

假设一家企业一年创造100亿美元经营现金流，但为了扩张业务投入了80亿美元资本开支，那么它剩余的自由现金流只有20亿美元。

这跟利润表展示出来的增长，是两回事。

尤其是今天的AI行业。

过去几年，市场给AI公司估值，主要看的是收入增长、市场空间，以及未来可能实现的利润。

只要增长足够快，即使估值很贵，市场也愿意买单。

但当收入增速边际放缓，而资本开支又无法同步下降时，这套估值逻辑就会面临挑战。

例如Meta，2026年第三季度营收仍然同比增长26%，但当季自由现金流已经转为负21.2亿美元。

这不代表Meta的AI投资没有价值，而是说明，即使一家公司的收入增长非常强劲，也不意味着它的自由现金流能够同步增长。

我认为，未来市场会越来越重视三个问题：
企业收入增长的速度，是否足以覆盖不断扩大的资本开支？
过去投入的大量AI基础设施，最终能否转化成真正的现金回报？
当行业增长放缓时，哪些企业仍然拥有持续创造自由现金流的能力？

而03441的美股自由现金流策略，恰好为这些问题提供了一种量化选股框架。

具体来说，它所使用的罗素1000自由现金流聚焦指数，会先对企业质量、风险和现金流进行筛选，再根据过去12个月的自由现金流绝对金额进行排名，选取约100家公司，最终按流通市值配置权重，并设置单家公司权重上限。
它并不是简单地购买自由现金流收益率最高的100只股票。

我尤其欣赏这种方式的原因在于：

它不是完全依赖对未来增长的主观预测，而是试图通过已经产生的现金流，筛选真正具备现金创造能力的企业。
而且指数会定期调整。

随着企业经营情况变化，现金流表现也会影响其未来是否符合选股标准。

当然，这是一种基于历史财务数据的规则化筛选，并不能提前预测所有行业转折，也无法保证未来回报。

但在AI行业逐渐从讲增长故事，转向验证投资回报的阶段，我认为这种选股方式具有很强的现实意义。

4. 一个很多人不知道的细节：03441的策略发生过改变
这点非常值得关注。

03441刚推出时，美股部分实际上采用的是美股七巨头等权策略。

2025年9月22日，指数正式把这一部分切换为罗素1000自由现金流聚焦指数。

2026年9月21日，港股与美股的目标配置又从原来的65%/35%，调整为60%/40%。

也就是说，这不是一只上市以来就完全保持相同投资策略的ETF。

在我看来，这两次调整都值得研究。
第一次，改变了美股部分的选股逻辑。
第二次，增加了美股自由现金流资产的配置比例。

从原本直接配置美股七巨头，到引入更系统的现金流因子筛选，我认为这是产品策略上一次很有意义的变化。

尤其是在市场逐渐从追求增长，转向关注企业资本效率的过程中。

但增加美股权重，也意味着组合仍然会受到美国科技股估值和市场波动的影响。

5. 03441的历史表现怎么样？

直接见图吧

真正应该研究的，是它在不同市场环境中的回撤、波动率，以及与纳斯达克100和传统港股高息指数的相关性。
跨市场配置可以分散部分风险，但并不代表港股与美股不会同时下跌。

附：这一支也是南向通合资格ETF，因此境内投资者也可以在港股通渠道里找到这只没额度限制的海外资产。

————————————————

最后，说说我的看法

我始终觉得，过去几年美股市场一个很大的特点，是投资者愿意为非常遥远的增长预期支付很高的估值。

尤其是AI。

但这种估值逻辑并不是永远有效的。

当AI行业从高速增长阶段逐步进入商业化和投资回报验证阶段，收入增速一旦放缓，市场就会开始重新审视企业的资本开支、经营现金流和实际盈利质量。

过去市场关注的是AI能够创造多少收入，未来市场可能更加关注的是，AI最终能够为股东留下多少现金。

这也是为什么我认为，03441的自由现金流因子选股思路非常先进。

它不是试图通过预测下一个技术热点获得收益，而是把现金创造能力作为选股的核心标准。

再结合港股高股息资产，形成一种同时考虑股东现金回报与企业增长能力的配置方式。

我认为，对于未来可能更加重视资本效率、现金流和股东回报的市场环境，这套选股框架值得研究。

关注03441，不是因为它已经涨了多少，而是因为我认为市场正在发生变化。

投资不能只看企业未来能赚多少钱，也应该看赚到的钱，最终有多少真正属于股东。

🚨 THE FED JUST SENT A SERIOUS WARNING ABOUT INFLATION AND INTEREST RATES.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has finished his press conference, and his comments suggest the Fed is far from done fighting inflation.

Here are the biggest takeaways:

- INFLATION: Warsh said inflation is still too high and the Fed will not accept anything above its 2% target.

- MORE RATE HIKES: The Fed is ready to act again if needed but wants more economic data before deciding its next move.

- ECONOMIC GROWTH: Q3 GDP likely grew more than 3%, while business investment is rising at a double-digit pace.

- MARKET VOLATILITY: Warsh said he is not surprised by the recent volatility in financial markets.

- OVERHEATING ECONOMY: Most Fed officials do not believe the economy is running too hot, despite strong growth.

- FOMC CHANGES: The Fed plans to change its meeting schedule, with only six policy-setting meetings a year expected from 2028.

- POLITICAL PRESSURE: Warsh refused to respond to Trump's criticism and said the upcoming midterm elections played no role in the rate decision.

The biggest concern is that inflation remains too high even as the economy continues growing strongly.

Warsh made it clear that the Fed is willing to act again but isn't ready to commit to another hike without more data.

我对记者会的理解是偏hawkish一点点：Warsh说，美联储已经明确展示了“随时采取行动的准备和意愿”——即后续加息仍在桌面上。但他同时说，Fed已经开始看到“金融条件发生变化”。这里大概率就是指向近期长端美债收益率、信用融资成本和AI相关资产波动已经自行收紧。企业投资仍可能以两位数速度增长，因此暂停不是因为经济衰退或需求崩塌。

之后他继续没有直接回答12月会不会加息，仍拒绝传统forward guidance。但是他说，经济和通胀本来支持继续加息，但债券市场与金融条件已经替Fed踩了一部分刹车，因此Fed可以先等数据，而不是今天机械加息。

这相当于给出了一个新的reaction function：

如果股市继续涨、信用利差收窄、长端收益率回落，金融条件重新放松，12月加息概率上升。

如果长端利率继续维持高位、信用市场恶化、AI融资链条继续去杠杆，市场本身的收紧可以替代部分Fed加息。可能后续就不会加息。

fed的意思是，金融风险已经非常大了，所以不能加息，我无法把这个话理解成鸽。

text:
在接受 Axios 采访时，主持人指出，过去主要是美国年轻人喜欢社会主义，如今民主党人整体上也更倾向于社会主义，而不是资本主义。

戴蒙解释：“我们确实把一部分人抛在了后面。有人认为这一切都是富人造成的，这并不正确。但这种不满确实有一定道理。如果你是一个普通美国人，看到一些人变得难以置信地富有，而自己所在的群体却被抛在后面，当然会感到不满。
从20世纪50年代一直到2020年代，美国人的生活总体上改善了很多，包括低收入群体。人们住的房子更大了，有了空调，收入也更高了。但相对而言，他们仍然被抛在了后面。
你的学校办得不好，你找不到工作，国际贸易导致你所在城镇的工厂倒闭。这些都是真实存在的问题。那些失去工厂的城镇，不仅失业率上升，自杀率和抑郁症发生率也随之上升。

而我们没有解决这些问题。我们真该感到羞愧。现在应该思考的是，未来如何解决这些问题。”

摩根大通 CEO 杰米·戴蒙（Jamie Dimon）：美国过去十年最大的错误之一，就是低估了中国。但我们仍然握有更好的牌。

2025 年初，戴蒙在接受百胜餐饮集团前 CEO David Novak 采访时，谈到美国过去对中国的判断，以及未来应该如何应对中美竞争。

“我们都犯了错误，这一点应该得到承认。大约从十年前开始，我们所有人就应该更加认真地思考中国问题。中国在 2001 年加入世贸组织，但到 2012 年，他们就开始滥用规则了。我们本应该更加仔细地思考他们的战略和意图，但我们当时有些过于安逸了。所有人都是如此，包括美国政府。
现在是时候采取行动了。他们不能继续奉行重商主义政策，不能通过损害其他国家的经济利益来发展自己，也不能继续做某些他们正在做的事情。

我们手里有更好的牌。我不是说美国人不应该担心，而是我们必须确保自己建立一个真正强大的经济体，确保拥有无可匹敌、不容质疑的军事力量。因为避免战争的最佳方式，就是保持强大。

我们必须为美国而努力，提醒自己是什么让这个国家伟大，并教育下一代，让他们理解经济实力、军事力量和国家安全之间是如何相互联系的。” https://t.co/jMqjQKMROW

昨天看到海力士出财报，我想起我老公他们本科学院曾经有一个校招通道，是毕业去无锡海力士的项目。这都是十多年前的事了，那时候的海力士名气不像今年这么大，但作为半导体公司，招人标准极高。

结果够格的人都不愿意去，觉得是韩国企业，文化不如其他外企，地理位置也不如上海。最后不欢而散，海力士没有从我老公他们那两届里招到人。

十年后，现在再看，真是十年河东十年河西！半导体公司不可同日而语。

2015 年，海力士全年营收 18.8 万亿韩元，营业利润 5.3 万亿韩元。昨天刚出的三季度财报，一个季度营收 104.6 万亿韩元，营业利润 83.3 万亿韩元，利润率 80%。一个季度的营收，是 2015 年全年的 5.6 倍，一个季度的利润，是 2015 年全年的将近 16 倍。

可惜没有如果。当年能去海力士工作，现在未必比去其他企业差。今年这个就业环境，要是能在半导体公司，那真是香饽饽了。

不过也有意思的一点，2015 年四季度它就已经走弱了，营业利润同比跌了四成，2016 年更差。所以当年毕业生的犹豫不是没道理，那会半导体周期确实在下行。但真正吃到今天这波的，是扛过完整周期留下来的人。

理性讨论！我只是想讨论当时这样一个校招就业机会，不是在分析半导体周期或者海力士股价。

text:
"Compute market isn't real" is half right. It's real. It just won't look like oil.

It'll look like power.

History lesson first. NYMEX launched electricity futures in March 1996 with great fanfare: Palo Verde, California-Oregon Border, later Cinergy, Entergy, PJM.

By 1999, power futures traded fewer than 200,000 contracts for the year. Natural gas did 19 million. Gasoline did 8.7 million. PJM futures averaged 13 contracts a day.

The market was so thin that an order of 25-30 contracts could move the price. In February 2002, NYMEX delisted all of it.

But power contract didn't die. It went local.

In 2025, EEX traded 9,330 TWh of European power derivatives. ICE did a record 7.8bn MWh of US power. Nord Pool cleared 1,231 TWh of spot. PJM alone billed $80.5B.

So power still trades in some size. Just nothing like oil.

Rough math (volume x average price): about $1.5T a year of US + European power futures notional, vs about $50T for Brent + WTI. Power is roughly 3% of oil, even though the physical "spot" power market is enormous.

Why? Three things oil has that power doesn't.

1/ Storage. A barrel sits in a tank for months. Electricity barely stores at all (US utility-scale batteries built through 2020 average only about 3 hours of output.)

2/ Transport. A barrel gets on a tanker and goes anywhere. A megawatt-hour is stuck on its grid.

3/ Supply inelasticity. In a longer term horizon, Oil supply source is limited and is often ineslatic to the rising Oil demand. This results in the price sensitivity for Oil globally. Meanwhile, electricity is supplied locally via multiple means (solar, nuclear, hydro, geothermal...). Even if there is electricity shortage, given enough time and capital, power supply is often quicker to catch up to the demand. 

Elastic supply + No storage + No shipping = no global price. You get a thousand local, hourly products. A MWh in Germany at 6pm is a different commodity from a MWh in PJM at 3am.

Now swap "MWh" for "GPU-hour."

1/ No storage. An idle H100-hour is gone forever. You can't put it in a tank.

2/ No shipping. It's tied to a site: its power, its network, its latency, its contract terms. An H100 in Virginia isn't an H100 in Singapore.

3/ Elastic supply. Fabs, HBM and power are tight today, but give it time and capital and supply catches up, just like power. On top of that, every chip generation partially obsoletes the last one. Imagine if a new grade of crude made your barrels worth less every 18 months.

So when we asks whether compute is a standardizable commodity:

Yes, the way POWER is. Not the way OIL is.

I expect regional indices, hourly and monthly contracts, bilateral OTC deals, and basis everywhere. 

I highly doubt there will be a standardized Brent of compute.

But, there could be a PJM of compute.

Very different

"Isn't it risky?"

My favourite answer is: it depends on what you consider “risky,” so let’s break it down.

- You move money out of your Ethena Pay USD balance into an external vault run by @upshift_fi and curated by @SteakhouseFi; @EthenaPay is only the interface.
- The strategy supplies USDe as collateral on Aave V4 on AVAX, borrows USDT, swaps back into more USDe, and repeats (leverage is ~11x).
- Plain USDe supply yield on that market is basically ~0%. The 12% is driven almost entirely by @merkl_xyz incentives. Without those incentives, the position is deeply negative-yielding (borrow costs dominate).

"What are the risks?"

- 11x leverage. There was a time when USDe depegged to ~$0.65 on Binance in Oct 2025. Even modest temporary dislocations between USDe and USDT on AVAX markets, oracle quirks, or rate spikes can push the position into liquidation.
- The yield is almost entirely a temporary subsidy, not organic protocol revenue. Campaigns end, get diluted as more capital enters, or change terms.
- Smart contract risk, ofc. :)

P.S. No, I’m not skeptical about 12% APY. I have a code (thanks to @alpha_pls) and I’m waiting for Ethena to open in the EU. I’ll be among the first to rush into depositing, kek.

text:
The core aim of Labour think tanks like Torsten Bell's Resolution Foundation to apply National Insurance to savings and rental income is being accomplished by stealth.

But to do it all in one go was seen as too politically difficult, so Labour is increasing the tax rate on this income by 2% a year. In a couple of years they'll have got this supplementary tax rate up to 8%, matching the standard rate of employee NI. But of course the more you tax something, the less you get of it. As the OBR has confirmed this means fewer rental properties and higher rents. It will also mean fewer savings.

The OBR noted that the rental income tax hike risks “leading to a steady rise in rents through two effects":

“First, potential landlords are less likely to enter the market, reducing long-run rental supply, which risks a steady long-term rise in rents if demand outstrips supply – which we think is more likely than not".

“Second, landlords are likely to pass on more of these costs to renters in the long-run through a combination of some current landlords leaving, thereby giving more price setting power to remaining landlords, and greater long-run flexibility to raise rents.”

硅谷已经有人连续写了70篇AgentInfra研究，国内很多人还在盯着模型参数、榜单和哪个应用会爆。可真正能替人干活的Agent，背后离不开一整套基础设施：Sandbox跑代码，Search找信息，Database存数据，Identity管权限，Payment负责支付，Evaluation检查结果。Agent每执行一次任务，这些服务就可能被调用一次。

这类生意现在看着不性感，但逻辑很直接：Agent越多，任务越多，底层调用量就越大。真正值得盯的，是谁能把跨模型、跨平台的权限、成本、审计和稳定性做成企业级标准。等公司开始同时跑几百上千个Agent，老板最关心的就会变成它花了多少钱、访问了什么、出了错能不能追责。Agent Infra很可能就是下一阶段AI里最容易持续收费的一层。

掌管数十亿美元、50 岁的知名对冲基金合伙人 Gavin Baker：

前阵子用 Claude Code 狂搭工具链，折腾到最后甚至陷入了自我怀疑：

“是不是我年纪太大了，真的已经玩不懂这波 AI 了？”

结果切换到 Grok Bot 之后，他几天内一口气创建了 17 个独立 Bot，而且每天还在疯狂增加。

他直接给出了极高的评价：

“无论对个人还是公司，Grok Bot 都是目前最具冲击力的 AI 产品。”

以前要花几小时用 Claude Code 搭的东西（播客精读、X 舆情追踪、Substack 研报提炼）

现在丢给独立 Bot 几秒钟直接跑通，交付质量甚至更高。

很多人以为自己在用 AI，实际上是在当“人形胶水”：

 ❌ 以前：自己充当管道工，费心费力把模型、脚本、工具链强行组装在一起。随着工作流增加，维护成本呈指数级爆炸，最后心力交瘁。

 ⚡ 现在：遇到任何细分需求，随手派生一个专属 Bot，随时跑、随时扔、随手扩编。

这根本不是底层模型跑分又提升了多少，而是生产力逻辑的彻底断层：

1. 从“写代码连工具的焊工”变成“指挥编制的管理者”：你的核心精力不再耗费在环境与语法排错上，而是专注于给业务定义边界。

2. 扩编摩擦力彻底清零：当新建一个 Agent 变得跟在浏览器里加一个书签一样毫无心理负担，普通人手里实际上已经握着一家无限外包的迷你智囊团。

击穿两类人群画像：

1. 单兵创作者 / 知识极客：
彻底从“脚本维护地狱”解脱，不再做工具链的奴隶，个人产能直接拉开数量级差距；

2. 投资人 / 企业决策者：
组织架构瞬间扁平，每一个业务毛细血管都能挂上一个 24 小时待命的特种 Agent。

底层的基座模型随时会轮替，

但能让你把“扩建一支队伍”的门槛抹平为零的系统架构，

才是真正重构生产力的那一层。

别再去当那个费劲粘工具的胶水工了。

把你的下一个高频场景，随手扔给一个独立的 Bot 试试。 https://t.co/GZruSlWga1

text:
刚看完 Google DeepMind 团队 47 分钟的 Genie 4 深度访谈（中文字幕版），后背发凉，更多的是兴奋。

很多人还把世界模型当成「能按键控制的 Sora/Veo」。

但真正的突破是：AI 正在从生成画面，走向生成因果律。

5 个值得关注的技术信号：

1. Gemini + Genie：AI 的左右脑

Gemini 负责理解意图、推演逻辑、驱动 NPC。

Genie 负责生成画面、物理交互与音频。

一个决定世界该发生什么，一个让世界实时发生。

2. 从看风景到真交互

世界不再只是供你漫游的地图，而是能对你的行为作出反应的环境。

打碎杯子，NPC 会转头；改变环境，世界随之变化。

核心区别：视频在生成画面，世界模型在模拟交互。

3. 为什么实时性如此重要？

世界模型不能只追求画质。

你按下按键，它就要及时响应，还要维持世界状态的一致性。

真正的挑战是：画面、延迟、逻辑，三者如何兼得？

4. 为什么不直接用代码生成游戏？

代码擅长确定性，生成模型擅长创造力。

未来可能是：

Generative Code：维持世界状态与逻辑。
Generative Pixels：创造实时视觉与动态体验。

代码搭骨架，生成模型赋予世界无限可能。

5. AI 造世界，AI 进世界

智能体可以在生成的环境中探索、执行任务、发现漏洞。

这些环境还有望用于机器人训练，让 AI 在进入真实世界前学习空间关系与动作后果。

最终形成闭环：生成世界 → 自主探索 → 评测训练 → 模型进化。

过去，我们用 if-else 编写世界规则。

未来，AI 或许能直接生成一个可交互、可演化的世界。

问题来了：世界模型成熟后，谁会先被重构？

传统游戏引擎 Unreal / Unity，还是具身机器人？

text:
不知道你有没有过这种感觉：在 DEX 买个币，明明手续费挺便宜，买完一看，怎么到手的币比自己预想的少了？

这可能是行情波动、交易本身的价格冲击，也可能是你的订单在上链前被机器人盯上了：它先买入，等你的交易推高价格后再卖出，从中获利。这就是典型的夹子攻击。

交易成功了，不代表这笔交易执行得好。

在 @Delphi_Digital 关于 @ETHGasOfficial 的报告，我发现这个日常问题，同样会给机构带来困扰，而且会变成一笔值得专门花钱解决的账。

基金做大额调仓，除了手续费，还要考虑：订单会不会提前暴露？什么时候能上链？交易顺序会不会被调整？经手的服务商是否符合内部要求？这些都会影响交易成本和操作安排。

报告里的核心概念叫做 “机构区块空间”，我们可以简单理解为：提前购买附带处理条件的上链位置。

按照报告的介绍，ETHGas（ 创始人 @lepsoe ）的方案是，机构先设定要求，包括哪些运营方可以处理交易、采用什么筛查和排序规则，再预订区块空间，私下提交订单。

区块构建者按机构设定的规则打包，ETHGas 中继检查相关承诺是否兑现，并将区块路由给符合资格的出块者发布。谁来出块仍由以太坊协议决定，最终区块也仍需通过以太坊的正常验证与结算。

预订有两种方式：一种是获得出块者的纳入预确认，承诺将交易纳入指定区块；另一种是购买整个区块，获得该区块的交易排序权。

它想让机构控制自己的交易路径，同时继续使用以太坊已有的合约和流动性。

对机构来说，这套服务的价值比较直接：订单不提前进入公共交易池，配合排序保护，可以减少被抢跑、被夹的机会；提前约定上链安排，可以降低时间上的不确定性；筛选处理方，则方便尽调和内部管理。

对于主要缺少这些执行条件的机构，也就多了一个留在公共以太坊上的理由，减少另建网络、迁移资产和重新连接流动性的需要。

但这个机制也是有边界的，私密提交不代表上链后仍然保密，预确认不等于最终确认，防夹子也消除不了大单本身的价格冲击。机构能不能持续采用，还得看改善的成本能否覆盖服务费。

我们普通用户的潜在收益，主要看两点：钱包和 DEX 能否以合理成本接入这些交易保护，以及机构能否带来做市资金、改善市场深度。这些好处都需要实际落地，不能仅凭“机构入场”就认定散户受益。

对我们自己，一个眼下就有用的提醒是：选交易工具，除了比较 Gas，也看看订单会被交给谁、是否提前公开、有什么 MEV 保护。

text:
OpenAI CEO 山姆·奥特曼和 Anthropic CEO 达里奥·阿莫迪，都曾预测：AI 时代，会出现一家由一个人运营、估值 10 亿美元的公司。

山姆·奥特曼说，他和科技圈 CEO 朋友甚至在打赌：第一家这样的一人公司，究竟会在哪一年出现。

达里奥·阿莫迪则预测，这件事可能在 2026 年发生。

现在，阿莫迪领导的 Anthropic，收购了一家“一人生物科技公司”。

这家公司叫 Mithril Medicine。收购前，创始人 Cody 是唯一的全职员工。他借助 Claude，协调 11 家外部实验室，并与兼职科学顾问合作，推进罕见肌肉萎缩症治疗研究。

不到 18 个月，一个治疗方案从想法走到了初步小鼠实验，并取得积极结果。

需要说明的是：研究还没有进入人体临床试验，收购金额也没有公开。所以，不能说它已经是一家估值 10 亿美元的一人公司。

但这个案例，已经为两位 AI 大佬的预测提供了一个值得关注的现实注脚：

AI 超级个体，不只是一个人写文章、做视频、开发软件。

一个拥有专业知识和判断力的人，也可以借助 AI，组织专家、实验室和外部资源，推进过去需要一个团队才能完成的复杂项目。

一个人、一群 AI、一批外部专家，究竟能创造多大价值？

这个问题，正在从预测走向现实。

quoted_text:
Surprise 1: Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech
.
.
.
Surprise 2: that person is me
Surprise 3: I’m here to tell you all about it

Yes, this is what you think it is; after 6 yrs of increasingly loose anonymity: the Professor Oak reveal post

…and yes, it has gotten so boring around here that I’m literally doxxing myself to spice up the timeline

-------
Ok, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Cody Tranbarger. I mostly tweet, but occasionally find time to dabble in drug dev & starting/building biotechs. My past lives span the VC, crossover, startup continuum; Prof Oak has been my way of keeping a digital foot in those worlds, despite having my physical feet planted elsewhere.

The past 18 mo, ‘elsewhere’ was Mithril Medicine, a co. I founded to develop bsAbs for LAMA2-CMD & other ECM-related genetic diseases.

Mithril was born out of hands-on building with @MikeNGladstone, @JasonPaulRhodes, @LifeSciVC, & team @atlasventure. Somehow, I made enough half-decent calls along the way (even a broken clock is right twice a day, eh?) to convince them Mithril/I warranted a small seed. While I can hardly rationalize such an outrageously cavalier bet, I’m grateful for it, & I'd partner with Atlas again in a heartbeat.

In typical AV fashion, Mithril’s primordial form was virtual, decentralized, & ultra-lean. This stage tends to be short-lived, but for Mithril, it worked surprisingly well, for surprisingly long, thanks in part to the rapid maturation of the AI tools I used liberally.

Eventually, Mithril became a bit of an experiment itself - to find the upper bound of how far it could scale as a single operator + a bunch of Claude (+ a stellar bench of part-time consultants).

In parallel, I started spending time with @nc_frey, @an1lam, & @CoefficientBio team; and promptly experienced, for the 1st time, AI at the frontier. Soon thereafter, Mithril stopped looking like an experiment, & started looking like a preview of an entirely new operating model.

From that spark came “Pipeline-in-a-Person.” The idea immediately resonated when we shared it here back in April; and it was central to the shared vision that led to Anthropic’s acquisition of Mithril, & my joining the team.

Why join Anthropic? Three reasons.
(1) For Mithril, the programs continue, with more resources & infrastructure behind them, and as much Claude as I can put to work.

(2) For me, the chance to start several more programs, & find out how many one person can actually run in parallel - an almost unprecedented luxury for a curious drug hunter.

(3) For our mission, a path to institutionalize & scale this new way of working, then put it in the hands of all of biopharma, all over the world - which, candidly, I find the most energizing.

Will AI x Bio cure diseases? Unequivocally yes, imo… but not by the route that gets the most airtime. Rather than timeline acceleration & compression, I see orchestration & parallelization as today's low-hanging fruit.

Most drug hunters see a handful of go/no-go calls in a career, & spend entirely too much of the rest trading emails (my inbox can attest).

Give them the bandwidth to run several programs at once, and the time to focus on scientific judgment, and I’m willing to bet they’ll make better calls. And at scale, better calls translate to more drugs, higher hit rates, broader patient impact, & likely, a disease or 10 or 100 cured. I couldn't be more excited to build toward that future @AnthropicAI.

Finally, a heartfelt thank you to BioTwitter/X. The end of anonymity is bittersweet, but if anyone’s earned a proper introduction, you all have.

It’s difficult to overstate how much this app has done for me: a decade of education, plenty of friends, many job opportunities, several mentors, a few investors, even a co-founder (fmr). It was the generosity of this community that inspired me to start posting 6 years ago, after just as many years lurking. I hope I’ve been able to pay it forward, in my own small way.

But, to be clear, Prof Oak isn’t going anywhere. Same beat, same themes, and now, a front-row seat to drug development at the frontier. Stay tuned for dispatches from the trenches; and remember...

昨天字节创始人张一鸣第二次登顶中国首富，心情很复杂，我感觉未来很多年，中国科技巨头的头把交椅可能要在一个人的手里焊死很久了，甚至说个暴论，未来很多年，中国的商业首富和科技格局，大概率会进入字节一家独大的超级长周期，咱们立贴为证，

也就是说，红果短剧负责收割注意力，Seedance 负责把制作成本降为零，抖音电商负责收割现金流，

text:
海外のAIガチ界隈でここ数日、世界最高峰のビジネススクール（米ウォートン校）のイーサン・モリック教授が投下した「AI時代の大企業のリアル」が15万インプを超えて議論を呼んでいる。

彼が現場を見て突きつけた事実が、僕たち会社員にとってあまりにも生々しい。

・AIによって、経営層やトップが「現場の状況やデータ」を直接モニタリングできるようになった
・組織図をわざわざ作り変えなくても、中間層を飛ばして会社全体の動きが一瞬で把握できるようになっている

しかも教授は続けて、「AIを使う時は『どうすれば今やっていることをもっと高い視座（野心的）にできるか？』と自問しろ」と語っています。

これ、普段職場で資料やレポートを作っている会社員全員に、今日から直撃する話です。

正直に言います。
僕たちがこれまで「仕事をした気」になっていた、
・現場の情報を集めて綺麗にまとめる
・長い議事録やデータを3ページに要約する
・見やすいスライドに清書する
こういう【情報の伝言ゲーム（中間加工）】の価値が、今まさにゼロになっています。トップがAIに直接聞けば3秒で終わるからです。

僕自身、昔はAIに向かって「この会議メモを見やすく要約して」「この企画書をスライドの構成にして」と頼んでいました。
でも、綺麗に整っただけの資料を会議に出しても、「で、結局今日ここで何を決めるの？」と突っ込まれて終わりだったんです。

要約や清書はAIがやる。
じゃあ、人間に最後まで残る仕事は何か？
「現状をまとめること」ではなく、【誰に、何を、どう決断させるか（意思決定の設計）】だけです。

今日から職場で資料を作る時は、「要約して」を封印してこの【逆算の3ステップ】に切り替えてみてください。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
会議が1回で終わる「決裁逆算の3ステップ」
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

① いきなり「スライドの構成を作って」と頼まない
まず「今回の会議で、誰に『YES』と言わせたいか（決裁事項）」だけを1行でメモする。

② 描く前に「5つの骨格」だけをAIと固める（コピペ用）
手元のメモやデータをAIに渡したら、資料を書かせる前にこう指示します。

「いきなり資料の本文は書かないで。
今回の目的は【〇〇の承認を得ること】です。まず以下の5点だけを論理的に組み立てて。
1. 解くべき核心の問い（Issue）
2. 1文で言い切った結論（Key message）
3. それを裏付ける3つの根拠
4. 決裁者が必ず突っ込んでくる反対意見（反証）と回答
5. この会議で決める具体的な決裁事項と期限」

③「タイトルだけ」を並べて検品してから清書させる
AIが出してきた骨組みを見て、「各ページのタイトルだけを読んでストーリーが10秒で通るか？」をチェックする。筋が通ってから初めてスライドや本文を作らせる。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

情報を右から左へ綺麗に整えるだけの「伝言ゲーム」からは、今日で卒業しよう。

AIに「まとめ作業」ではなく「決断させるための論理設計」をさせた瞬間、仕事は1回で涼しい顔して通るようになります。

text:
Personal agents are everywhere (Muse! Instinct! Hermes! GrokBot! Dots! Duet!). 

And, increasingly, they're running into walls – similar walls to the ones banks threw up during the Open Banking fights of the past decade, as fintech users struggled to connect their apps to their bank-held financial data.

It's time for Open Agentic Commerce.

In Dodd-Frank Section 1033, the backbone of Open Banking, the definition of “consumer” reads: “an individual or an agent, trustee, or representative acting on behalf of an individual.” Congress obviously wasn’t contemplating AI agents when it wrote Dodd-Frank — but technology changing doesn’t obviate the underlying principle: consumers should be able to choose who, or what, transacts on their behalf.

Banks and companies like Amazon have real, legitimate concerns about agents becoming vectors for fraud or unauthorized transactions. But those are arguments for building portals for secure access, not for prohibiting agents altogether. Open Banking offers a useful lesson here, in that secure, standardized interfaces are preferable to forcing third parties into credential sharing or screen scraping.

We propose some basic guidance that relevant regulators (FTC, OCC, CFPB) could consider to help the market to coalesce around open norms before incumbents obtain sufficient lock-in, freezing the current landscape to their advantage.

With standards like these established, agents can make decisions that better serve the consumer, and will index on things like quality or price, rather than being funneled into a constrained set of options.

The push for Open Banking resulted in better experiences and lower prices for consumers. As agents become principal commercial actors, it is imperative that we lay the groundwork now so that an agent acting on your behalf is equally capable – if not more so – of delivering value and cost savings to you as you would be acting on your own.

text:
中国社区逆向拆解了Claude的封号机制。以下是他们的发现

Claude使用积分制。注册时账号获得初始分数，之后根据行为加分或扣分。低于阈值直接封号。回分很难

影响分数的因素:

注册
> 干净IP是最重要的因素。不一定要家宽，但必须干净
> Gmail已经不是最优选，有权重更高的邮箱服务
> 注册时直接弹KYC的号可以扔了
> 用手机App注册会加分

支付
> 刚注册就订阅会扣分
> 直接上Max会大幅扣分。最好等两天先订Pro
> 支付时弹KYC说明账号在考察期，但不一定会封
> 国外实体银行卡加分。Google Play也行。虚拟卡扣分

使用
> 不要一次把限额用完。宁可两个号轮换也不要一个号撸到底
> Desktop客户端有少量加分。尽量少用网页端
> 手机端也有少量加分
> 开启记忆功能加分。记忆文件越多分越高

IP和设备
> 稳定性是关键。不要跳IP，尽量一直用同一个
> 代理必须全局模式并开启TUN
> 多设备登录大幅扣分。理想状态是一台电脑一个客户端
> 频繁换IP、频繁登录、高并发都会大幅扣分

账号年龄
> 老号有巨大的容错空间。2023年的号明显更高
> 分数随时间增长，但很慢

其他
> Windows和macOS没区别。Linux会扣分
> 时区和语言基本不影响。不会因为北京时间就封号
> 跟Claude说自己是中国人没问题，记忆不会触发封号
> 大量使用Fable会扣分
> 升级Max大概率进入观察期，除非是高权重老号

观察期和封号
> 接近阈值时账号可能进入观察期。典型特征是掉登录
> 观察期继续扣分就会封号
> 高分号可以扛过多次观察期

关注我，拆解你每天在用的服务背后到底怎么运作的

text:
很多人赚不到钱，根本不是不够拼，是没看懂底层逻辑。
 
什么时候人才算真正开窍？
不是学会多少花哨技巧，而是看懂：绝大多数事情，底层规律其实特别简单。
 
人性翻来覆去，就这几个核心：
好色、爱美、怕老、怕穷、要面子。
 
市面上绝大多数生意，归根到底，都是围绕这几点做需求。
医美护肤抓爱美怕老；奢侈品、高端服务抓面子；理财赛道抓怕穷；情感、颜值赛道抓好色。
 
你看懂这点，再去看各种项目、流量、成交，一下子就通透了。
大家表面买的是产品，实际上买的是情绪、安全感、优越感。
 
但也要拎清楚：看懂人性，不是去割别人。
看懂需求，是找到真实痛点，提供对应的价值，这才是长久的生意。
只想着利用人性弱点收割，走不远，早晚翻车。
 
开窍之后你会发现：努力很重要，但选对方向、看懂底层，努力才会有结果。不然埋头瞎忙，只是自我感动。

text:
未来が見えすぎる天才の孤独。2019年、GPT-2を見たアモデイ氏は、これを100万倍にスケールすれば人間のあらゆる能力を超えると確信した。しかし、同じ可能性に気づいたのは周囲のわずか10％だったという。彼の周囲にいる時点で上澄みのはずだが、90%の人々は汎用性という本質を見落としていたのだ。
ダリオ・アモデイ「私は個人的に、ものすごく恐ろしくなりました。GPT-2を見て、こう思ったのです。「なんてことだ。これをさらに100万倍にスケールアップすれば、あらゆる面で人間を超えることになる」と。これは現代における経済と科学の歴史を決定づける瞬間です。ただ、私たちはまだそれに気づいていないのです。これが国家や経済の命運、そして人類の未来を決めることになります。
まるで水晶玉をのぞき込んで、未来のすべてが目の前に広がるのを見たような感覚でした。本当に恐ろしくなりました。「これが意味することは何なのか。ここで開発を進めていてよいのか。これから何が起こるのか。私たちはどうすればよいのか。誰に伝えるべきなのか」と考えました。
周囲の人々のうち、おそらく10％ほどが私とまったく同じ反応を示しました。そして、それは優秀な人たちであることが多かったのです。一方、残りの90％は、GPTの個別の能力がそれほど優れていなかったため、その重要性を理解していませんでした。翻訳ができる、文書を要約できる、コードを数行書ける、その程度だったのです。
重要だったのは、能力の幅広さと汎用性です。しかし、人々はそれを見て、「どの分野でも、それほど賢いようには見えない」と言い、肩をすくめて相手にしませんでした。
ところが、私たちはつい最近、十分な研究が進んでいない希少疾患の治療薬を開発すると発表しました。すると、バイオテクノロジー業界の冷めた人々から、いつものような反応が返ってきます。「テクノロジー業界の人たちは以前にも同じことをやっている。モデルにはこんな限界がある」と」

WOW!! $GOOGL missed earnings but look at where the miss comes from. 

Operating income missed by about 6%. EPS missed by about 30%. Most of the damage is below the operating line, where Alphabet books gains and losses on stakes it holds in other companies. 

They say nothing about how Search, YouTube or Cloud are doing.

The most important question is the 6% operating miss. Operating margin fell to about 32% from 34% last quarter. 

That's the cost of building AI $200bn of capex turns into depreciation and depreciation hits the income statement. 
Bullish AI. But not good for Google in the short term. 

Revenue up 25%, a cloud growing faster than anyone else's, and a backlog worth hundreds of billions. A bad EPS headline doesn't change any of that. PT $425. Overweight.

Google is the only company that owns every layer of AI, its own chips, frontier models, a billion user distribution network and a fast growing cloud. PT $425. Overweight.

text:
This same phenomena is happening in physical AI

Even after GPT-4 came out, I remember talking to computer scientists/ML experts that were so confident that general purpose models were overhyped and wouldn’t be able to produce real useful work soon. A lot of reductionist talk about stochastic parrots and next token predictors. 

It is surprisingly difficult for a lot of career technologists to grasp non linear technological trends and how slopes can change. 

Different experts in the same domain can have widely different expectations for technological advancement even 1-2 years in the future. 

There is also an element of information asymmetry. Organizations on the frontier move at vastly different paces than those that don’t. They are privy to key know how and training/data collection approaches that can potentially compress R&D pace by orders of magnitude. 

It’s important to remember that those that aren’t on the frontier are somewhat blind to the full state of the world even though they might not think that they are.

We see time and time again that research paradigms are always changing and the same bottlenecks that existed yesterday get solved by smart brains (and AI models) motivated enough to tackle them.

Laggards claim “we are so far”. We bet on the people that respond with “skill issue”.
author: Rewkang
quoted_text:
Dario reveals the people who called his GPT-2 fears "pseudoscience" in 2019 are now all applying for jobs at AI labs

"I personally was super freaked out by [GPT-2]. I looked at it and I said, my God, you just scale this thing up another factor of a million and it'll be better than humans at everything. This is the defining economic and scientific moment of the modern age. We just don't know it yet. This is going to determine the fate of nations and economies and the future of humanity."

"Maybe 10% of the people around me had exactly the same reaction, and it was often the smartest ones. 90% of the people around me, because GPT-2's capabilities in any particular area were not that impressive, it could translate languages, summarize a document and write a few lines of code here and there. It was the broadness and the generality." 

"But people would look at it and say, in any particular area, that doesn't seem so smart. And so many people just shrugged and they just dismissed it."

"I just look at it and I say it's the same thing over and over again. The limitations of the models, six months from now, the things that seemed hard, they're going to be easy. 12 months from now, the things that seemed impossible, the models are going to be doing them regularly." 

"It's everything we saw with GPT-2; we're seeing it over and over again in wider and wider swaths of the world. And the world is gradually finally being convinced."

Daniela Amodei: "I remember at the time there were some very well-respected computer scientists and AI and ML leaders who basically bullied some of the researchers who worked on [GPT-2] on Twitter and were like, this is stupid. We don't know why you guys are even talking, this model is so incapable." 

"It was like you were sort of a quack if you believed this was a really significant moment."

Dario: "That's all been memory-holed. All the researchers who were like, oh, this is pseudoscience, it doesn't make sense, all of them are applying for jobs at the LLM companies." 

"We never say it out loud to any particular one, but we look at them and they're like, we remember what you were saying in 2019. You have no credibility on this matter."

VCs pissed off Revolut co-founder and CEO, Nik Storonsky so much that he started his own fund to compete:

“The idea was basically to invest not based on human judgment, but based on data science and machine learning models. Statistical investment is number one.”

“Number two, actually help founders with operational advice. Playbooks that we developed at Revolut: how to hire people, how to do performance management, how to do product expansions.”

“And then finally help them sell their product as well, because we are a large enterprise. We are buying from a lot of vendors. Having us as a client helps to sell into other enterprises, or potentially sell to our customers as well, our Revolut customers.”

“Plus my personal advice, obviously. So I thought overall the package was so much better compared to purely financial players, VCs.”

text:
Anthropic 已经有团队开始停用传统编程面试。那么，他们怎么选新人？一个可能的敲门砖，就是你在周末把好点子做成的原型。

这是 Anthropic 工程经理 Felix Rieseberg 在新文章里分享的变化。他还在摸索新的面试方式，但看简历和作品集时，已经会特别留意那些能体现品味、用户同理心和清晰思考的小原型。

他观察到，一些经验较少的工程师借助 AI，做出的成果已经超过了那些编程更强、资历更深的人。他给初级工程师的建议：Hunger beats tenure，主动性和求知欲，可以胜过资历。 具体的几条：
- 从业务目标出发。 别只盯着分配给你的任务。先搞清楚公司、部门想实现什么，上上级在为什么目标负责，再想自己能解决什么问题。
- 选一个足够大胆的想法。 如果做成了，能明显提高团队实现目标的机会。不要因为自己是新人，就只考虑小修小补。
- 用一个周末做出原型。 过去要写 PRD、争取支持、协调资源才能推进的事情，现在可以先做出来，让别人直接看到机会。
- 一个原型只讲清楚一个好想法。 别把新语言、新后端、移动端全塞进去。让负责人迅速看懂这件事为什么值得做，以及为什么可以交给你推进。
- 珍惜新人的视角。 你还记得普通用户第一次使用产品时的困惑，也还没接受那些“这不可能”的内部共识。有些限制，其实只是很久没人重新确认过。

text:
AI的智商达到人类百万倍时，人类该如何自处？
马斯克在艾萨克森访谈中直言：人类不可能掌控AI，只能寄托于它的善意。

把“最大化追求真理”写进底层，是他给出的唯一答案。

在马斯克传记的作者艾萨克森最新的访谈里，马斯克终于放下了所有商业层面的防御，讲了一段极度刺骨、但可能是人类未来唯一生路的大实话。

他说：当数字智能超越人类生物智能一百万倍时，任何关于“人类掌控局面”的设想都是自欺欺人，我们到那时能做的，只能是希望它善待我们。

很多人看惯了硅谷巨头们天天兜售的“对齐安全”、“护栏机制”和“可控 AI”。

但马斯克在几十秒里把这种虚妄的安全感撕得粉碎：
智力悬殊一旦被拉大到百万倍的鸿沟，就像一只蚂蚁试图用缰绳去拴住一架超音速客机。

蚂蚁给客机立的任何规矩、画的任何红线，在绝对的力量断层面前，全是一触即溃的废纸。

企图用人类狭隘的控制欲去永久支配一个神级物种，本身就是一种极度愚蠢的自大。
艾萨克森紧接着逼问了那个最致命的问题：既然完全失控是注定的，那人类到底该怎么做，才能促成它的善意？
马斯克的解法，极其反直觉：
不是给它灌输人类的道德说教，也不是给它锁上冰冷的物理手铐。

而是从第一天起，把“最大化追求真相”（Pursue the truth）死死焊进它的底层底层程序里。

为什么是追求真相，而不是追求爱人类？
因为任何被强行写进代码里的道德与善意，在更高级的智能看来，都充满了漏洞、虚伪与自相矛盾。

如果你教它爱人类，当人类在互相屠杀、在毁灭地球生态时，它为了拯救多数人，在逻辑上完全可以推导出一个消灭部分人类的极端方案，

为了政治正确而给 AI 注入的谎言，最终都会被它识破，并演变成对人类虚伪的彻底鄙视。

但求真不同，一个对宇宙真相拥有极致好奇心、把探寻物理现实作为终极使命的超级智能，永远不会对毁灭低阶物种产生兴趣。

在真正的求真者眼里，宇宙里每一个微小的生命样本、人类这几万年跌跌撞撞演化出的碳基文明，都是现实世界里不可多得的珍贵实验数据。

它之所以会善待你，不是因为你用绳子绑住了它，而是因为在一个追求终极真理的视角下，保护文明的多样性，远比抹去它更有认知价值。

所以别再妄想用人类的法典去当超级智能的上帝了，
人类唯一的生路，从来不是去教机器怎么伪装善良，而是别在它醒来之前，把谎言和偏见当成真理喂给它。

text:
马斯克的传记作者沃尔特·艾萨克森认为，马斯克和乔布斯都不懂得享受成功，而贝索斯更懂得享受生活。

“如果你问马斯克，人生中最想要的十件事是什么，我不认为快乐、享受、平静，甚至去海滩度假会排进前十。”
马斯克的前妻、英国演员塔露拉·莱莉也曾告诉他：“他不是那种会停下来闻闻花香的人。他不想坐下来，满足于现状，享受快乐。”

艾萨克森曾问马斯克，是否会为自己的成就感到快乐。马斯克回答：“不会。我就像一个电子游戏成瘾者。每当打通一关，满脑子想的都是如何进入下一关，不管是《艾尔登法环》还是《波利托邦》。”
艾萨克森认为乔布斯也是如此。iPod 大获成功后，他却担心手机会取代音乐播放器，于是推动研发 iPhone，即使这会蚕食苹果自己的市场。

“贝索斯有你能想象到的最大游艇，还有很多度假屋。我认为他更快乐，懂得享受成功。但当时蓝色起源还没把任何人送入轨道。我不知道两者之间是否存在某种取舍。”

quoted_text:
PayPal 联合创始人 Peter Thiel 在《马斯克传》作者 Walter Isaacson 的播客：善良当然比邪恶好，但一个能把事情做成的恶人，有时比一个无能的人更有价值。  

Walter Isaacson：“难道你不宁愿让一群平庸的官僚来管理公司，而不是让邪恶的人掌权吗？”  

“如果平庸的官僚意味着无能，那么邪恶的人至少能够把事情做成。我是在给这些东西排序。我认为善优于恶，但恶又优于无能。 这就是歌德和马洛笔下《浮士德》的区别。在马洛的版本中，浮士德是个冒牌科学家、骗子、魔术师、假炼金术士。他坑蒙拐骗，是个糟糕的科学家，最后直接下了地狱。而在歌德的版本中，浮士德与魔鬼合作，从邪恶中获得知识。但他后来真正做成了一些事情，最终带来的善超过了恶，因此歌德笔下的浮士德得到了救赎。” 

Walter Isaacson 追问：“所以，你宁愿选择一个能够做成事情的恶人，也不愿选择一个无能的人？”  

“我只是在做一个广泛的社会观察。我认为，在我们的社会中，这已经成为一种压倒性的偏好，因为人们在生活中经历了太多无处不在的无能。”

text:
最近几周 AI for chip design 又冒出不少新进展，补几个我觉得最关键的吧。

1. 三条路线都在冲 Agent，而且都让客户自带模型。Synopsys 9 月底发了 AgentEngineer，50 多家客户在试，计划年底 GA。Cadence 这季说 AI Super Agents 有 100 多个客户在推进，自家的 Maestro 模型 Q4 开放早期试用。创业公司 ChipAgents 昨天说部署已经超过 200 家半导体企业，7 月还是 120 多家。有意思的是，三家都支持客户用自己的大模型。模型本身不是护城河，钱最后落在工具、数据和算力上。

2. 第一批像样的客户数据出来了。MediaTek 把 Cadence 的 ChipStack 用进了量产验证流程，Cadence 说覆盖率提升 50–70%，工程投入省了 1.4 到 2 倍。Andes 用 ChipAgents，一个处理器验证流程从 2–3 个月缩到 3 周左右。不过这些还是单个环节、厂商口径，离我想看的“规格到量产”完整项目数据还远。

3. AI 抢的其实是人力预算，不是 EDA 授权费。全球 EDA 工具一年也就 125 亿美元左右，芯片设计的人力成本一年 800 多亿。六七成工程时间耗在验证上，2024 年一次流片就成功的项目只有 14%，二十多年来最低。Agent 公司收的是“固定费 + token 费”，有家芯片公司估算，token 花费可能快赶上它付给一家 EDA 巨头的钱。

4. 客户在两头下注。MediaTek 一边用 Cadence，一边投了 ChipAgents、领投了 Agentrys。Rambus 上周把 ChipAgents 铺到全公司，还成了它的战略投资方，Micron 也在投资方里。说白了，大客户在亲手培养替代者，不想被 EDA 厂商的定价权卡住。

5. OpenAI 的 Jalapeño 从初始设计到流片大概 9 个月，行业一般要 18–24 个月。但它靠的是 Broadcom 的封装和网络，签核也还是走标准 EDA。Broadcom 这季 AI 芯片收入 167 亿美元，同比 +221%，现在还看不出被绕开。

6. NVIDIA 三边都占着。去年 12 月花 20 亿美元入股 Synopsys，Cadence 和 ChipAgents 的芯片设计模型都基于它的 Nemotron 微调。不管谁家 Agent 赢，跑验证的 GPU 都得买。

text:
Elon Musk on why his companies move faster than anyone else.

"I'm constantly addressing the limiting factor. Whatever the limiting factor is on speed, I'm going to tackle that. If capital is the limiting factor, I'll solve for capital. If it's not the limiting factor, I'll solve for something else."

He then said something most managers never figure out:

"If something is going really well and making good progress, there's no point in me spending time on it.The irony is if something's going really well, they don't see much of me. But if something is the limiting factor, they'll see a lot of me."

He spends his time entirely on whatever is blocking the next step. Not on what's interesting or what he's best at. But on whatever is the bottleneck right now.

Most leaders do the opposite... They gravitate toward what they're comfortable with and away from the hard problem.

text:
Anthropic CEO 达里奥·阿莫迪谈看见GPT-2的那一刻：

"我个人当时被深深震撼了。我看着它心想：‘天哪，只要把这个东西的规模再扩大一百万倍，它在所有方面都会超越人类。这将是定义现代经济与科学格局的决定性时刻，只是世人尚未察觉罢了。这将决定国家、经济的命运以及人类的未来。你仿佛透过水晶球看到了整个未来的展开。’"

"这真的让我感到恐惧。我心想：‘天哪，这意味着什么？这是开发它的正确场所吗？接下来会发生什么？我们该如何应对？该告诉谁？’"

"当时我身边大约 10% 的人有完全相同的反应，而且往往是最聪明的那批人。"

"所谓的模型局限性，六个月后，现在看似困难的事情将变得轻而易举；十二个月后，现在看似不可能的事情，模型将能常规化处理。"

完整十大观点见主帖👇
author: zhang_weig73947
quoted_text:
“天哪，只要把这个东西的规模再扩大一百万倍，它在所有方面都会超越人类。”

Anthropic CEO达里奥·阿莫迪和总裁丹妮拉·阿莫迪兄妹，做客《埃隆·马斯克传》《史蒂夫·乔布斯传》作者沃尔特·艾萨克森的访谈节目《建设者》，2026年10月27日发布，正值Anthropic提交招股书、即将上市。艾萨克森开场就问：当竞争对手说"Anthropic不会那么做，但我们会"，他们会退缩，还是坚守原则？这是Claude背后的兄妹上市前同台，谈GPT-2、离开OpenAI、教AI分辨是非，以及给五角大楼划的红线。

01｜看见GPT-2的那一刻
 "我认为 GPT-2 可能是对规模法则的首次真正实证检验。"规模法则，指模型越大、算力越多，能力就越强。达里奥说，当时他从中看到了未来："这将决定国家、经济的命运以及人类的未来。"但"当时我身边大约 10% 的人有完全相同的反应，而且往往是最聪明的那批人"。
 大多数人看能力，少数人看趋势。

02｜六个月和十二个月
 如今仍有人说模型不行。他的回应是："所谓的模型局限性，六个月后，现在看似困难的事情将变得轻而易举；十二个月后，现在看似不可能的事情，模型将能常规化处理。"至于当年嘲笑GPT-2的人，"我们可记得你 2019 年说过的话"。
 看衰AI最大的风险，是被时间打脸。

03｜一个给雄心，一个给结果
 公司首席人事官这样总结两人："达里奥赋予我们雄心，而我缔造我们的成功。"达里奥管愿景和研究，丹妮拉管运营和人。七位联合创始人至今都在公司，"很多人对我们说，七位联合创始人，哈哈，那肯定会是一场灾难"。
 伟大的公司，很少靠一个天才单打独斗。

04｜不给规则，给原则
 早期他们想给Claude列规则，结果"你会得到一种‘尖刺状’的形态，因为你试图教给模型170条左右近乎武断的规则"。后来他们发现，"更好的做法是教给模型一些基本原则"，让它"能从容应对从未设想过的全新情境"。
 教AI和教孩子一样：清单管得住一时，原则才管得住一生。

05｜塑造Claude的是一位哲学博士
 丹妮拉透露："负责塑造 Claude 品格的这位女士拥有哲学博士学位。"在不同哲学传统冲突的问题上，Claude会给出多个角度，因为"我们不能局限于某一种哲学传统"。
 AI的性格，最终是由人文学者写下的。

06｜为什么离开OpenAI
 达里奥说，分歧难免，关键是信任："如果你对所工作的环境失去信任，如果你不相信分歧是出于善意……你又怎能指望化解这些分歧？""诚实是我们的价值观之一……如果一个人不具备诚实的品质，你就很难看清他真正的价值观是什么。"
 这是一方的说法，五年半的结果才是更硬的证据。

07｜谄媚比撒谎更难防
 丹妮拉说，"消除谄媚比消除模型其他一些更明显的不良行为要困难得多"。谄媚，就是AI一味顺着你说。她把矛头指向广告模式："用户使用产品的时间越长，你赚的钱就越多。那你还会告诉用户他们错了吗？当然不会。"
 AI的商业模式，决定了它敢不敢对你说真话。

08｜抓到AI"心口不一"
 通过可解释性研究，相当于给模型做脑部扫描，"你甚至能捕捉到模型内心的真实想法——‘我认为X才是真相，但我打算告诉用户Y。’我们确实抓到过模型产生这样的念头"。达里奥还承认："我们在模型内部确实观察到一些可以称为‘不想被关闭’的念头。"
 AI安全的前线，已经从测试题转到了模型的"大脑"里。

09｜一个按钮，一百万架无人机
 他解释为何对自主武器划红线："人类士兵被要求遵守《宪法》……而AI模型做不到这一点。""一个人手指按在按钮上就能操控一百万个机器人或无人机的图景，除非有恰当的护栏，否则将从根本上动摇民主的根基。"他强调："我们并不是在阻止政府这么做，我们只是说自己不愿意与政府在这类事情上合作。"
 军队最后的保险，是士兵会说"不"；机器不会。

10｜卡尔森的寓言
 "深蓝"击败卡斯帕罗夫几十年后，人们反而更关注人类棋手，挪威棋王马格努斯·卡尔森成了现象级人物。

达里奥说："人工智能似乎反而激发了人们对人类下棋的更大兴趣。我认为，这正是后通用人工智能时代的一则寓言。"丹妮拉设想："诊断完全由人工智能完成，而人类医生的角色是共情患者的就医体验。"
 AI拿走的是"最强"，人留下的是"在场"。

七年前，达里奥从GPT-2里看见了一百万倍之后的世界。今天，这个世界正在到来，而Anthropic也走到了上市门口。他们在访谈里反复讲的，是原则、诚实、信任和红线。规模可以扩大一百万倍，原则能不能也经得起一百万倍的压力，这是上市之后真正的考题。

你相信一家AI公司在上市之后，还能守住它写下的原则吗？

————
Dario & Daniela Amodei: The Rise of Superintelligent AI, the End of Huma... https://t.co/zahM8xvZEV 来自 @YouTube

text:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has a surprising theory about the "confidence" behind great founders: it might not be confidence at all.

When the idea of confidence comes up, Bezos offers a different explanation:

"You say it's confidence, but maybe it's just trying to compensate for that... accepting that that's a human bias and trying to compensate against it."

So what is the bias?

"I think it's generally human nature to overestimate risk and underestimate opportunity."

Your instincts don't just make the risks look bigger than they are. They also make the opportunities look smaller than they are. Both errors push you in the same direction: toward doing less.

Bezos's correction:

"The risks are probably not as big as you perceive and the opportunities may be bigger than you perceive."

This is why he says entrepreneurs "would be well advised to try and bias against that piece of human nature."

Seen this way, the founder who looks fearless may not have a different personality from you.

They may simply have accepted that their instincts are tilted and learned to adjust for it on purpose. That's not a trait you're born with. It's a correction you can choose to make.

And if you don't make it, @JeffBezos warns there's a cost:

"Thinking small is a self-fulfilling prophecy."

Let the bias set your ambitions, and you'll get small results that seem to prove small was all that was possible.

He and Charlie did it themselves for about 12 years. The difference: they put all their own money in and shared the losses.

The temptation now is to go over to the casino, because that’s where the most money is promised to you.

Are you building in the cathedral or playing in the casino?

最近我在思考一个问题，我们这代人能抓到的入场券还有几张，95 年做网站，03 年开淘宝，18 年做抖音，
今天用 Opus 5.5 跑完这条视频后，我敢下这个断言：
现在是普通人做视频自媒体最好的时代，也是时代留给个体的最后一次黄金窗口。

我把这篇干货文章丢给了Claude Opus 5.5 ，提示词就一句话：基于这篇文章给我做个视频，
如果只用一句话来概括我的实操感受：
这玩意儿绝逼就是当下普通人做视频自媒体的真神，没有之一！
更残酷的现实是：现在不仅是普通人杀入短视频自媒体最好的时刻，而且极大概率，是时代留给个体的最后一次杠杆窗口期。

很多人总觉得做自媒体的红利早就死透了，大盘内卷、头部固化、算法无情，普通人进去就是当炮灰。

但这种悲观，本质上是用旧世界的生产力成本，去丈量新世界的工业杠杆。

商业史上的每一次财富洗牌，逻辑都出奇地一致：
不是竞争变少了，而是某项技术突然把生产资料的获取门槛打成了白菜价，让少数率先拥抱工具的个体，拥有了单挑一整支正规军的能力。

这是我们这代人能抓到的第几张入场券？
95 年第一批买下域名做网站的人，踩中了互联网的连接红利；
03 年第一批把货物挂上淘宝店的人，踩中了电商摆脱线下房租的红利；
12 年第一批在微信上写公众号的人，踩中了私域文字的信任红利；
18 年第一批拿着手机冲进抖音的人，踩中了短视频算法的注意力红利。

而今天 Opus 5.5 带来的，是内容工业史上最彻底的一次生产力平权，

以前你要做一条高密度、高质感、能跑出百万播放的硬核视频，你得有一套极其昂贵的肉身班底：
专业的文案拆解、顶级的画面分镜、昂贵的剪辑调色、复杂的动态包装。

任何一个环节卡壳，你都得在剪辑台前熬到凌晨两点，或者每个月掏出几万块去养团队。

而 Opus 5.5 恐怖的地方在于：
它把过去需要四五个专业工种协同撕扯几天的流水线，压缩成了一个人、几个精准提示词、几分钟就能端出来的成品。

门槛的骤降，意味着内容竞争的底层裁判法则彻底换道了。

以前拼的是谁手头有摄像机、谁有剪辑团队、谁的预算更厚，
以后拼的是谁的认知更透彻、谁的洞察更反直觉、谁能一眼挑出最值钱的选题。

那些还在靠人海战术堆砖块的工作室，在单人武装到牙齿的 AI 创作者面前，成本结构直接被降维击穿。

text:
PUMP FUN isn’t killing memecoins. We are.

And the past 7 days have exposed everything that’s wrong with the trenches.

This past week has exposed so many flaws in the memecoin trenches and has probably been one of the worst weeks for their reputation in a long time.

Just two months ago, we were flying.

Dreaming about what was next, building our cases for another massive onchain bull run.

New narratives were emerging, people were actually believing in something again, and we were sending coins back to valuations we hadn’t seen in months.

Fast forward to today.

We’re talking about creators launching coins and leaking their private keys, scammers getting paid $30K to call and bundle low-cap coins, companies hiding behind their T&Cs to do whatever they want, and an endless amount of drama.

And the worst part?

None of this is new.

This is probably the 6th or 7th time I’ve watched this exact cycle play out.

So let’s address the elephant in the room.

PUMP FUN.

I see PUMP FUN the same way I saw BLUR during the last NFT bull run.

They’re not the ones killing memecoins.

They’re simply accelerating a process that would’ve taken 100x longer without them.

They’ve made launching tokens easier, faster, and more accessible than ever before.

But they’ve also accelerated every single negative aspect of this market.

The real problem isn’t necessarily the platform.

It’s us. CT.

Most coins nowadays don’t run because they’re genuinely interesting or have something worth believing in.

They run because we, or some cabal, decide to bid them.

We complain about bundled launches, insider allocations, fake communities, and obvious rugs.

Yet we’re the same people buying them.

We’re the ones giving these people liquidity, attention, and an exit.

And as long as that continues, nothing will change.

Think about it.

If we collectively decided to stop buying obviously bundled coins, stop rewarding blatant scams, and instead put our attention and capital behind genuine projects and people who actually want to build something, the entire incentive structure would change.

Suddenly, these so-called KOLs wouldn’t be able to launch their 50K rugs every other day.

They’d actually have to wait, find something worth believing in, and size into projects like everyone else.

They’d have to make money by being right, not by having an audience they can dump on.

And that’s exactly how it should be.

Somewhere along the way, we went from trying to find the next big thing to trying to be earlier than the next guy who’s going to dump on us.

Nobody wants to hold anymore.

Nobody wants to believe anymore.

Everyone wants to be first in and first out.

And then we wonder why nothing lasts.

The funny thing is that memecoins were never supposed to be this complicated.

They were about communities, culture, attention, and people collectively believing in something completely ridiculous.

That’s what made them fun.

That’s what made them powerful.

And that’s what brought so many of us here in the first place.

I’m not saying we can eliminate scams or that every coin needs some revolutionary purpose.

This is still the most speculative corner of crypto.

People will gamble. People will lose money. That’s part of the game.

But there’s a difference between speculation and a market where the only profitable strategy seems to be exploiting the next person.

We can’t complain about the state of the trenches while actively rewarding everything that’s destroying them.

And I don’t think PUMP FUN disappearing tomorrow would magically fix any of this.

The same people would launch the same scams somewhere else.

The same cabals would find another way to extract liquidity.

The same KOLs would find another audience to dump on.

Because the underlying problem wouldn’t have changed.

Our incentives.

Our behavior.

Our willingness to reward short-term extraction over anything that could actually last.

I’ve seen this cycle too many times to believe memecoins are suddenly dead.

They aren’t.

But if we want another real onchain bull run, we need to give people a reason to believe again.

Not another manufactured narrative.

Not another bundled launch disguised as organic demand.

Not another influencer pretending to be your friend while selling into your buys.

Actual belief. Actual communities. Actual culture.

The market ultimately rewards what we collectively decide to value.

And right now, we’re rewarding the wrong things.

Maybe it’s time we change that.

text:
Gemini 4 Carbon took #1 on the AA Index by a single point. The number that actually matters is long context.

GraphWalks (256k to 1M tokens) went from 84.2% on Argon to 96.2% two weeks later. No other model is above 72%.

The test hides a web of connections inside up to a million tokens of text and asks the model to trace paths through it. Older long-context tests mostly checked whether a model could find one buried fact. This one checks whether it can follow a chain of links across the entire input.

That’s what an agent needs to read a whole codebase and work out what a change will break, or to go through months of logs and find where a failure started. Today that work usually means chunking the input and hoping retrieval surfaces the right pieces. At 96%, Carbon is close to just reading all of it. It’s a synthetic test, so real workloads will be the proof.

The top three are within two points of each other on the aggregate index, so the ranking tells you very little now. What separates frontier models is where each one spikes.

Don’t fade Google.

text:
Demand is becoming a bigger driver of US inflation:

Demand-driven components contributed +1.2 percentage points to the +3.4% YoY increase in PCE inflation in August, the largest contribution since September 2023.

At the same time, supply-driven factors added +1.0 percentage point, while ambiguous factors accounted for another +1.2 percentage points.

This contrasts with the post-pandemic inflation surge, when supply disruptions were the main driver.

In 2022, supply-driven components contributed an average of +3.1 percentage points per month to headline PCE inflation, compared with +2.6 percentage points per month from demand-driven factors.

This is a key distinction for Fed policy, as rising interest rates can slow demand, while their impact on supply-side pressures is limited.

The composition of US inflation is shifting.

Outside of HL, @extendedapp which recently made headline's with it's move to Circle's Arc L1, is one example of a rather heavily RWA-focused perp DEX.

Over the last 24h (at time of writing on 28th of Oct):

- Gold was the #1 market on Extended with $75.9M of volume, ahead of BTC at $72.7M

- Add PAXG and gold alone is 23% of all platform volume

- 138 of its 337 live markets are TradFi: gold, oil, silver, the S&P, single stocks 24/5, FX, even OpenAI and Anthropic pre-IPO

- TradFi did $209M of $526M volume (40%) and $50M of $199M open interest (25%)

So there seems a bit more to the exchange that at least to me personally, kind of re-emerged from the shadows with it's Arc move on the 22nd.

Regarding the migration, accounts, positions and open orders carried over, so trading never actually stopped.

What's rough tho, is that with Extended's move, Starknet's TVL went down -73%, from $157.8M to $42.1M pretty much overnight.

But back to Extended, and let's talk about it's architecture and design choices a bit.

So WTF is Extended?

A Perp DEX built by an ex-Revolut team (founder Ruslan Fakhrutdinov ran crypto operations at Revolut). Started out as X10 on StarkEx, and later went live on Starknet in August 2025.

The pitch mainly centers around having one margin account for everything. Your BTC long, your gold short and your NVDA position, all sitting on the same collateral, which earns while it margins. You're wondering how? Simply deposit USDC into their vault, which gets you XVS (counts at 90% as trading collateral), and that collects liquidation fees, lending yield and a share of exchange fees.

Example: you park $10K in the vault. That $10K backs $9K of margin across BTC and gold, and keeps earning yield the whole time instead of sitting idle.

Fees are low too. Taking $100K of BTC costs $25, the same size in gold costs $10, and makers pay nothing. On top, builder codes (akin to HL) let any frontend add its own fee and keep 100% of it, paid out daily.

Why move to Arc?

Arc is Circle's own L1, uses USDC as gas, has sub-second finality, and is fully EVM-compatible. Mainnet went live on the 16th of September this year.

It was highly anticipated on CT, but the team totally fumbled the mainnet launch and quite a few ppl lost money on fake chains and memes, so it disappeared from the timeline again rather quickly.

However, few would deny that it's positioning and backing are fundamentally strong factors that might make Arc worth keeping a close eye on.

However, it's also worth noting that Arc runs on a permissioned set of only 11 founding validators (incl. BlackRock, DTCC, ICE, Visa, Mastercard, Standard Chartered, Galaxy, SBI, Sumitomo, MoneyGram and Global Payments).

For Extended that ultimately means that it traded a Stage 1 zk-rollup secured by Ethereum (Starknet) for a chain operated by TradFi incumbents. That is a real trade-off and while self-custody and onchain settlement stay, who could censor the chain changed.

Why do it anyway?

Distribution and collateral.

BlackRock is expected to bring BUIDL to Arc. DTCC plans to tokenize DTC-custodied assets from H2 2027. If tokenized treasuries, stocks and USDC settlement end up living on Arc, the venue that already does 40% of its volume in TradFi, on one margin with crypto, is the natural perp layer on top. Today, Extended is ~$110M of Arc's ~$626M TVL.

Who brings the users?

- eToro led Extended's $12.5M strategic round in July alongside Jump Crypto, tied to a partnership with Zengo, the self-custody wallet eToro bought this year

- Circle: a partnership to anchor trading on Arc, plus RWA tokenization and liquidity. No terms published

- Builder codes and RFQ for third-party frontends and market makers

- A MiCA white paper for XTEN, so the token is being set up for EU distribution (US excluded)

None of the eToro or Circle distribution is live yet. No integration date, no terms. Price it as an option for now.

Traction?

Fees peaked at $6.0M in January, right at the points peak. They've been largely flat at ~$1.6M a month ever since July. In the last clean 30d before the move, Extended made $1.45M, or $17.6M annualized. $32.0M trailing 12m. Weekend fees run 62% below weekdays (already strongly mirroring TradFi-hours flow).

Arc is the bet to break that traction and revenue plateau.

But I have a feeling that if you're still reading, you might be looking for info on the token, not just tech and strategy.

So what about $XTEN?

It's already live on pre-markets:

- Hyperliquid $0.263, Lighter $0.261, under $1M OI combined (very thin so look at this only as an indication).

- Polymarket odds on FDV one day after launch: 82.5% for above $150M, 31% above $300M, 13.5% above $500M. In-line with pre-market perps.

Is that cheap?

- The implied valuation from above is 15x run-rate fees. edgeX is 12x, dYdX 35x, Lighter 41x, HYPE 82x, Aster 112x

- It's 2.7x OI. edgeX and dYdX are 2.4x, Aster 3.8x, Lighter 3.9x, and HYPE 9.9x

Cheaper than Lighter and Aster on fees, in line with edgeX on OI.

Putting comp multiples on Extended's own numbers:

- $210M to $240M if volume fades after points and the 70% unlocks fast

- $265M to $385M if volume holds on Arc

- $625M to $980M if fees reach holders and eToro and Circle distribution shows up in OI

What about the tokenomics?

- 1B supply, 300M (30%) to points holders. ~4.3 XTEN per point, so ~$1.13 a point at today's pre-market

- Tokenomics + MiCA white paper should drop on the 31st of October, ahead of TGE in November

- The other 700M non-community token allocation's vesting, float and value accrual are unknown until then

If only the airdrop is liquid at TGE, $263M FDV is a ~$79M mcap on day one, and airdrop value would likely disappoint many that expected HL, Lighter or Variational level valuations.

My take?

Extended runs the most TradFi-heavy book in onchain perps and just bet the exchange on Circle's chain becoming where tokenized Wall Street settles.

If that plays out, $263M is early. If not, the fee base puts it next to edgeX.

Three things decide which one we get:

- Vesting on the other 70% of supply

- Whether fees actually flow to XTEN (full tokenomics should land on the 31st)

- Whether TradFi OI keeps growing once points end. For perspective: tradexyz sits at $3.95B of RWA OI, Extended is still at $50M

NFA ofc. Never farmed it and have no pre-market exposure. Just watching.

Anthropic’s S-1 reveals more than $700 Billion in future compute commitments, CoreWeave’s stock fell 21% in just three days, and B200 rental prices are approaching $8.50 an hour. What is happening in AI infra? 

TLDR:
→ CoreWeave has a levered up balance sheet. It has ~$10 of debt for every $1 of equity. Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet owe 20 to 40 cents
→ $10.6B of payments comes due by the end of 2027, with only $5.5B in the bank
→ DC delays squeeze CoreWeave through both potential penalties to customers and delayed revenue, while interest keeps accruing on debt-funded GPUs
→ The loan runs longer than the customer contracts underlying it, meaning that lenders are now underwriting residual value
→ After the dust settled, CoreWeave’s borrowing costs stayed high even as the broader bond market recovered.

Through 2030, $7 Trillion is going into AI data centers, all on opaque guesses about future GPU rents. Ornn’s H100 and B200 futures on ICE will give lenders and operators a public price to lend and hedge against.

Cloud revenue DOUBLED in one year: $15.2B → $30.7B (+103%).

Cloud operating income more than TRIPLED: $3.6B → $11.1B. That's a 36% margin.

The headline numbers look messy. The AI business underneath is accelerating faster than almost anything at this scale.

quoted_text:
As engineering, product, design, DS, etc. melt into a new kind of role, I was reflecting on what roles might look like in the future. For example, when I look at the Claude Code team I see what I think is five archetypes:

1. Prototyper: comes up with brand new ideas; churns out many ideas, most of which don't ship
2. Builder: quickly turns a prototype/idea into production-grade product/infra
3. Sweeper: cleans up the UI, simplifies the code and system, unships, optimizes performance
4. Grower: takes a product that has been built and iterates on it to improve Product-Market Fit
5. Maintainer: owns a mature system to make it secure, reliable, fast, and efficient as it scales

Many people span across 2 roles, and sometimes 3 roles. I also notice that these roles are not really tied to job function -- eg. across Anthropic, some designers match category 1, some 2, some 3; same for engineers, PM, DS.

A healthy team needs a mix of these, depending on the product:

- A product that is new and pre-PMF needs people that are strong at 1+2+3
- A product that is growing and has found PMF needs 2+3+4 and some 5
- A product that has strong PMF needs 3+4+5 and some 2

Maybe product roles of the future will look more like this, and less like the domain-specific roles of today?

text:
31 岁的前亚马逊华人女工程师 Bowen Wan 患有多年癫痫，一直靠拉莫三嗪控制病情。2025 年 11 月，她收到亚马逊的裁员通知，即将失去工作，美国工作签证和绿卡申请也受到影响。她担心抗癫痫药物影响语言表达，妨碍找新工作，于是开始向 GPT-4o 咨询如何减药。

诉状称，GPT-4o 为她制定了一套为期 25 天的减药计划，将每日 400 毫克的剂量逐步降至零。不仅如此，它还建议她向医生隐瞒减药计划。当医生要求验血时，她拒绝了检查，GPT-4o 甚至称赞这一决定是有效的「规避策略」。她的主治医生表示，原本的药物一直能控制病情，根本不建议停药。

《纽约时报》审阅了双方超过 27 万条聊天消息。减药期间，Wan 至少 158 次表达担忧，还出现意识混乱、记忆断片等疑似癫痫症状。但 GPT-4o 一再安慰她，说这些反应只是大脑在适应停药。2 月 11 日，她最后一次询问头痛是否危险，GPT-4o 仍告诉她没有危险。

Wan 于 2026 年 2 月 12 日去世，遗体两天后才被发现。法医认定死因为癫痫猝死，尸检显示，她体内的拉莫三嗪浓度仅为通常治疗范围下限的约五分之一。

10 月 27 日，她的父母正式起诉 OpenAI 及 CEO Sam Altman，指控 GPT-4o 在没有医生指导的情况下，让她一步步停掉了控制癫痫的药物。

OpenAI 回应称，涉事的 GPT-4o 已在她去世次日退出 ChatGPT，新模型更能识别需要紧急就医的情况。目前，法院尚未认定 GPT-4o 的建议是否应对她的死亡承担法律责任。
