今天是来告别的，七月初预警存储半导体见顶很多朋友舍不得走，于是陪玩整个下跌到反弹的过程，反弹开始以后的八九月我基本就不发帖了，享受上涨就好。

十一第一周提醒大盘见顶，也很多人舍不得走，那就陪完整个下跌过程（QQQ 762-701，SOXL169-78），现在情况好起来那我就休息了。

因为那个帖子都很多朋友留言，有几类共性问题：

1 喜欢玩低位做空

胜率最低的游戏，QQQ762 跌到 701，反弹到 710 什么的，看到一个小回调马上去空，胜率几何？为何昨天盘前我紧急发一条消息：夜盘低点就是全天最低点，大盘压力位 7710/7725，收盘就卡点在 7722.6。假如你夜盘开始去空，24 小时你可以亏 10-20%，当燃料了。

做空是高手干的，普通小散就踏踏实实被套着，买好公司，逢低补仓。

2 大跌时候不敢持股

大盘每次大跌都会反弹，不管跌多少，只是有时候遇到熊市要等两年而已最终会回来，大跌了就要慢慢买，被套了就装死。交给时间，比如谷歌，这公司没问题，400 去追，310 不敢买我是不理解，就算 280 250 有什么关系，迟早回来。

3 喜欢抓小放大

太在乎小细节，多看日线，4H 线，看分时线就是送钱的。

4 被套的哲学

股票被套才是安心的，你怎么保证你总买在低点卖在高点，美股最坏的几天和最好的几天往往连在一起。

所以我在低位，一直保持 20-30 万美金的固定仓位，雷打不动，有种跌死我。在避开下跌的同时也在避开上涨。

当然我一直做浮动仓，这个赚点钱就好不存在踏空，风险和机遇并存，看不懂不做也是一种智慧，股票可以控制自己不操作其实非常难。

后续看法

1 之前的三个结论，“特斯拉技术形态很好”“存储看多，先于其它板块见底”“SOXL 底部是 78”，有据此操作的肯定都赚钱了。

2 后续有两种可能

1）QQQ701 就见底了，现在四小时线低点不断抬高。是强势的表现，后面会小回调不断不影响去看前高

2 ）今天交易的是伊朗停战，A 家上市，承包继续买芯片存储，海力士财报很好，半导体才起来了，如果周三四很多大事件有任何利空出来，存在一个快速下跌的可能性。比如内狐胜选，云厂暴雷，联储放鹰等…

我不知道到底 1/2 哪个剧本所以没办法给出明确的操作建议。但是固定仓我死拿，浮动仓等待机会，踏空拉倒。

quoted_text:
中国社区逆向拆解了Claude的封号机制。以下是他们的发现

Claude使用积分制。注册时账号获得初始分数，之后根据行为加分或扣分。低于阈值直接封号。回分很难

影响分数的因素:

注册
> 干净IP是最重要的因素。不一定要家宽，但必须干净
> Gmail已经不是最优选，有权重更高的邮箱服务
> 注册时直接弹KYC的号可以扔了
> 用手机App注册会加分

支付
> 刚注册就订阅会扣分
> 直接上Max会大幅扣分。最好等两天先订Pro
> 支付时弹KYC说明账号在考察期，但不一定会封
> 国外实体银行卡加分。Google Play也行。虚拟卡扣分

使用
> 不要一次把限额用完。宁可两个号轮换也不要一个号撸到底
> Desktop客户端有少量加分。尽量少用网页端
> 手机端也有少量加分
> 开启记忆功能加分。记忆文件越多分越高

IP和设备
> 稳定性是关键。不要跳IP，尽量一直用同一个
> 代理必须全局模式并开启TUN
> 多设备登录大幅扣分。理想状态是一台电脑一个客户端
> 频繁换IP、频繁登录、高并发都会大幅扣分

账号年龄
> 老号有巨大的容错空间。2023年的号明显更高
> 分数随时间增长，但很慢

其他
> Windows和macOS没区别。Linux会扣分
> 时区和语言基本不影响。不会因为北京时间就封号
> 跟Claude说自己是中国人没问题，记忆不会触发封号
> 大量使用Fable会扣分
> 升级Max大概率进入观察期，除非是高权重老号

观察期和封号
> 接近阈值时账号可能进入观察期。典型特征是掉登录
> 观察期继续扣分就会封号
> 高分号可以扛过多次观察期

关注我，拆解你每天在用的服务背后到底怎么运作的

text: Interactive, optimizable mathematics 🤩
author: skominers
quoted_text:
I think it's becoming rather clear that ALL of mathematics will become possible to formalize rather soon. There are deep implications:

1. Mathematics becomes super interactive. Formalizations make it easy to browse, recombine, and build mathematical proofs from components.
2. Each new idea and paper can be checked much faster. The deep part is meaning and explanation. Validation is almost automatic.
3. Optimization and identification of new proofs can be done partially via agents, and humans can contribute much faster with great new ideas. Proofs from the Book are possible at scale.
4. Scientists and people at large can finally use mathematical artifacts as black boxes with trust and confidence. We can commoditize mathematical theorems.

I think the mathematical enterprise also becomes very gamified. We can clearly see each unproven statement as a concrete goal, identify existing tools and directions, and focus quickly on what's missing. And everyone can contribute, with agents or through understanding.

Soon, new languages and new theories will also develop, but the structure will keep growing steadily, with no mistakes and on fundamentally solid foundations. Hilbert's dream is becoming a reality.

One important caveat: mathematics is by no means trivial now! It's just becoming extremely well-structured and laser-focused. I think the jump in capacity, quality, and scale will be massive. I also hope that our understanding of the big picture will remain solid, because there will be a lot to grasp.

中国社区逆向拆解了Claude的封号机制。以下是他们的发现

Claude使用积分制。注册时账号获得初始分数，之后根据行为加分或扣分。低于阈值直接封号。回分很难

影响分数的因素:

注册
> 干净IP是最重要的因素。不一定要家宽，但必须干净
> Gmail已经不是最优选，有权重更高的邮箱服务
> 注册时直接弹KYC的号可以扔了
> 用手机App注册会加分

支付
> 刚注册就订阅会扣分
> 直接上Max会大幅扣分。最好等两天先订Pro
> 支付时弹KYC说明账号在考察期，但不一定会封
> 国外实体银行卡加分。Google Play也行。虚拟卡扣分

使用
> 不要一次把限额用完。宁可两个号轮换也不要一个号撸到底
> Desktop客户端有少量加分。尽量少用网页端
> 手机端也有少量加分
> 开启记忆功能加分。记忆文件越多分越高

IP和设备
> 稳定性是关键。不要跳IP，尽量一直用同一个
> 代理必须全局模式并开启TUN
> 多设备登录大幅扣分。理想状态是一台电脑一个客户端
> 频繁换IP、频繁登录、高并发都会大幅扣分

账号年龄
> 老号有巨大的容错空间。2023年的号明显更高
> 分数随时间增长，但很慢

其他
> Windows和macOS没区别。Linux会扣分
> 时区和语言基本不影响。不会因为北京时间就封号
> 跟Claude说自己是中国人没问题，记忆不会触发封号
> 大量使用Fable会扣分
> 升级Max大概率进入观察期，除非是高权重老号

观察期和封号
> 接近阈值时账号可能进入观察期。典型特征是掉登录
> 观察期继续扣分就会封号
> 高分号可以扛过多次观察期

That’s a very subtle yet important detail because it means that the perpetual supply increase can actually induce demand by attracting new user types instead of recycling an existing base.

author: PSkinnerTech
quoted_text:
Joe Liemandt of Alpha School on why AI is today's 1910 tractor moment, and why parents once again have to rethink their kids' future:

"In 1910, 90% of America had an 8th grade education. There were basically no high schools. And over 30% of America is a farmer. So everybody's on the farm, 8th grade was enough."

"Then in 1910, the Case tractor rolled up on the American farm. You can go look at the ads, it literally looks like an Anthropic ad. 'Does the work of 50 programmers. Does the work of 50 farm hands.'"

"Literally everybody in America realized 30% of the jobs are going away. That path is gone, and we have to get our kids ready for this new future. And it was that same recognition I think that parents have today."

text:
🦔Alphabet earned $2.12 a share last quarter, well short of the roughly $3 analysts expected, even as revenue grew 25% to $127.6 billion. Google Cloud more than doubled. Capital spending hit $51.4 billion and free cash flow went negative. Alphabet bought back no stock, and it sold $12.4 billion of new shares and $28.7 billion of bonds.

My Take
That’s a big miss, and I don’t like the reason behind it. More than half came from an $8.7 billion paper loss on stakes in other AI companies, the same stakes that padded last quarter’s profit by tens of billions. Google invests in AI startups that rent its chips, then books gains or losses as their values move. I’ve called that circular for a while. Now it swings Alphabet’s own earnings by billions a quarter.

Cloud doubled, I’ll give Google that. But Alphabet spent more on data centers last quarter than the whole business brought in, and it made up the difference by selling stock and bonds when it used to buy shares back. Management says spending goes up again next year, so I don’t see buybacks returning anytime soon. I’m sure we'll be seeing more of the big AI spenders follow Google to Wall Street for cash.

Renaissance's Medallion fund is WRONG 49.25% of the time. It still made 66% a year for 30 YEARS.

A trader who's right 60% of the time can't touch it.

This f*cking formula shows why.

I ran the math on both.

Genius, right 60%, 100 trades a year - loses money 1 year in 44.
Medallion's 50.75%, 10,000 trades - 7x the profit, loses 1 year in 15.
Same 50.75%, 1,000,000 trades - 750x the profit, basically never loses a year.

Same edge. Different number of bets. Different fate.

P(losing year) ≈ Φ(−(2p − 1) × √trades)

Being right more often helps a little. Being right by a hair, a million times, is how the best fund in history was built.

text:
Marc Andreessen explains why AI might be the end of James Burnham's "managerial society"

In his book The Managerial Revolution, Burnham divided capitalism into two phases.

The first phase was what he called "bourgeois capitalism"

"Think of this as name on the door -- it's Ford Motor Company because Henry Ford runs the company. It's a dictatorial model and Henry Ford just tells everyone what to do. He said the problem with bourgeois capitalism is it doesn't scale because Henry Ford can only tell so many people to do so many things."

The second phase was what Burnham called "managerial capitalism", which was Marc describes as, "the creation of a professional class of managers that are trained -- not to be car experts or experts in any particular field but to be experts in management. And then that led to business schools and management consultant firms and all these things."

Marc continues:

"You look at every big company today and most executives at most of the Fortune 500 companies are not domain experts in whatever the company does. And they're certainly not the founders of those companies. They're professional managers. And in fact, over the course of their careers, they'll probably manage many different kinds of businesses. They might work in healthcare for a while and then work in financial services and then go work in something else."

"What Burnham said was that transition was absolutely required because the problem with bourgeois capitalism is it doesn't scale... So if you're going to run capitalist enterprises that are going to have millions to billions of customers, they're going to be operating at a level of scale and complexity that will require this professional management class."

Burnham acknowledged that this professional management class has its downsides -- they're not as inventive and not going to come up with the next breakthrough. But whether you think that's good or bad, that's what's going to be required.

And basically that's what happened. Marc continues:

"Managerialism basically took over everything. What I'm describing is basically how all big companies run and how all governments run and how our large-scale non-profits run."

Marc believes venture capital is a protest movement to that -- backing founders under the Henry Ford model, and trying to find the next Elon Musk or Steve Jobs who can out-innovate the incumbents.

"I've always viewed my entire life as: we're raging against the dying of the light. We're constantly trying to fight off managerialism from swamping everything and everything getting boring, gray, dumb, and old."

But AI may now offer a third model. Marc explains:

"Maybe the new Henry Ford, Elon Musk, or Steve Jobs + AI is the best of both because it's the spark of genius of the name on the door model but gives that person AI superpowers to do all the managerial stuff... What's the thing these bots are really good at? They're really good at doing paperwork, writing reports, and doing all the managerial work."

"The challenge is going to be for the innovators to figure out how to leverage AI to actually do this."

"The other challenge is going to be for the incumbents that are managerial to figure out: what does that mean? Because now they're going to be facing a different kind of insurgent competitor that has a different set of capabilities than they're used to."

"I think this is going to force a lot of big companies to figure out innovation - figure out innovation or die trying."

Ben Horowitz elaborates on this point further in his article Databricks & the Future Firm below.

text:
网友晒 OpenAI 软件工程师面试全流程：带回家项目会被逐行追问，部分人加考“用 AI 写代码”

Reddit 求职论坛 r/InterviewCoderHQ 上，用户 little_kwagga 发帖说自己刚面完 OpenAI 的软件工程师岗位，把流程拆开讲了一遍：
一通招聘官电话，两轮技术初筛，一个 48 小时的带回家项目，一场专门追问这个项目的面试，再加四轮现场面试。部分候选人还会多一轮，要求用 AI 编码工具解决一个靠手写做不完的问题。

这是一位匿名网友的个人经历，OpenAI 没有公布这么细的流程，不同团队、不同职级的面试也可能不一样。能对照的官方信息是 OpenAI 官网的面试指南：大致分初步沟通、技能测试、终面、出结果几个阶段；技能测试可能是结对写代码、带回家项目或技术测试；终面一般 4 到 6 小时，见 4 到 6 位面试官。

【每一轮考什么】

招聘官电话：主要聊背景，但发帖人被问到“你觉得 AI 会往哪走”。发帖人建议提前读一遍 OpenAI 章程（Charter），这是 OpenAI 2018 年发布的使命文件，核心是让通用人工智能造福全人类。官网面试指南也建议读，并写明会看候选人跟公司使命和价值观合不合。

技术初筛：同一天两轮，各 60 分钟。编码题是做一个“带版本的键值存储”，可以理解成一本能记住修改历史的字典：同一个词条改过很多次，你要能查出它在任意时刻的值。系统设计题是一个容错的任务调度系统，负责按时派发任务，某台机器挂了，任务既不能丢，也不能重复执行。

带回家项目：48 小时内做一个能真正跑起来的东西。发帖人拿到的是分布式 webhook 投递系统。webhook 是网站之间互相通知的方式，比如你付款成功后，支付平台会主动给商家网站发一条消息。题目要求发送失败时自动重试，重试多次仍失败的消息放进“死信队列”，相当于邮局存放无法投递信件的柜子，留着之后处理。

技术深挖：面试官事先看过你的项目，自己列好一张问题清单，带着你逐行过代码，追问每个选择和决定的理由。

现场四轮：

编码第一轮是“渐进式多阶段”题：题目分几段放出，前一段做出能跑的解法，下一段才开放。发帖人拿到的是 token 级的流式比对器。token 是大模型输出文字的最小单位，大致是一个词或半个词，模型回答时就是一个 token 一个 token 往外吐。这道题要边接收边比对内容的变化，记录每一步状态，还要能回滚到之前的状态。发帖人的经验是先尽早做出一个正确的版本，再一步步改进。

编码第二轮偏系统方向，考状态管理、并发和内存效率，还问到 Python 的生成器、异步写法和迭代器这些语言底层机制。

系统设计题是“设计 ChatGPT”。面试官关心的是 GPU 怎么分配、流量忽高忽低时怎么自动加减机器、多台机器之间怎么协调。发帖人提醒，除非面试官特别要求，模型推理那一层可以当成一个黑盒，不用展开。

行为面问的是技术领导力、影响多个团队的架构决策、压力下怎么让大家达成一致。发帖人说要讲具体的取舍，空谈沟通技巧的回答不管用。

【新增的 AI 编码轮】

发帖人说，这一轮还在测试阶段，只有部分候选人会遇到：给你一个现成的代码库，外加一个大到靠手写做不完的问题，要求你用 AI 编码智能体完成。AI 编码智能体指能自己读代码、改代码、运行命令的 AI 工具，比如 OpenAI 的 Codex、Anthropic 的 Claude Code。这一轮怎么评分，发帖人没说，OpenAI 官方也没公开介绍过这一轮。

OpenAI 官网面试指南里有一句相关的说明：不同面试对 AI 工具的要求不同，有些形式有意允许使用，有些要考你不靠 AI 独立解题；准备材料里会写清楚，拿不准就提前问招聘官。所以同一套面试里，可能有的轮次不许用 AI，有的轮次专门看你怎么用 AI。

发帖人在帖子最后问，有没有人专门准备过渐进式多阶段这种题型，什么方法有用。

来源：Reddit r/InterviewCoderHQ 用户 little_kwagga 的帖子《OpenAI Software Engineer Interview 2026》；OpenAI 面试指南 https://t.co/1YXHnS71LN

text:
如果现在给一个完全没有计算机背景的人 6 个月时间，让他从零开始学习 AI Engineering，最后能不能达到企业的招聘要求？

路线其实很清晰：第一个月学 Python、API、Git，第二个月学 LLM 基础，第三个月学 RAG，第四个月学 Evals 和 Tracing，第五个月学 Agent 和 Tool Calling，最后一个月做出两个能够公开访问的项目。

说实话，我觉得这个方向没有什么大问题，但如果真让我重新学一遍，我绝对不会等到第六个月才开始做项目。

我自己就是一个从广播电视编导专业转向 AI 工程方向的学生。

这几个月一直在企业接触 RAG、Agent、GEO 和自动化工作流，最大的感受就是很多技术知识，你不真正做项目，根本不知道自己哪里不会。

比如 RAG，你看教程，可能几个小时就能理解 Chunking、Embedding、Vector Database、Retrieval 的基本流程。

但真正让你做一个企业知识库，你马上就会碰到一堆教程里没有仔细讲的问题。

PDF 解析错误怎么办？文档更新以后索引怎么同步？不同用户的访问权限怎么隔离？检索到的资料已经过期怎么办？Evals 到底应该怎么设计？

这些东西不是看完一套 RAG 教程就能自动掌握的。

Agent 也是一样，会调用一次工具，不代表你就理解 Agent Engineering。

工具调用超时怎么处理？任务执行到一半失败怎么办？怎么防止重复操作？什么时候需要人工审批？如何追踪每一步的执行结果？

真正开始做项目以后，你才会发现原来很多所谓的 AI 工程问题，最后都绕不开传统的软件工程基础。

所以我现在越来越倾向于一种学习方式：从第一个月就开始做项目，遇到什么问题就去补什么知识，同时留出固定时间系统学习基础。

比如先用 Python 和 FastAPI 做一个简单的 API 服务，把它部署到公网。

然后逐渐接入大模型，增加文档检索、工具调用、日志追踪和自动化测试。

最后把项目放到 GitHub，写清楚架构设计、测试方法、已知问题和实际运行效果。

做完以后至少要能回答别人几个问题：为什么这样设计？为什么不用其他方案？系统在哪些情况下会失败？你是怎么验证它的？

现在有 Codex、Claude Code，开发速度确实快了很多。但 AI 帮你生成代码，不代表这些工程能力就自动属于你了。

我特别认同原文最后一句话：Proof beats certificates。

不过我觉得还可以再往前延伸一步。

真正有说服力的不只是你做出了两个 Demo，而是你能不能解释这两个项目的技术决策、测试结果，以及你亲自解决过什么问题。

当然我也不觉得学六个月就一定能成为合格的 AI Engineer。

不同公司的要求差别很大，六个月能走到哪里，也取决于投入的时间、原有基础和项目质量。

但对于非科班想转 AI 的人来说，与其花半年时间收藏教程、研究各种热门框架，不如尽早开始完成一个真实项目，在实践里找到自己能力上的缺口。

我自己现在也还在补 Python、数据库、计算机网络和软件工程这些基础，远没有到成熟工程师的水平。

但至少这几个月的经历让我明白了一件事：

学会一个框架不难，真正困难的是把它用在真实问题上，出了问题还能够自己找到原因。

text:
Personal agents are everywhere (Muse! Instinct! Hermes! GrokBot! Dots! Duet!). 

And, increasingly, they're running into walls – similar walls to the ones banks threw up during the Open Banking fights of the past decade, as fintech users struggled to connect their apps to their bank-held financial data.

It's time for Open Agentic Commerce.

In Dodd-Frank Section 1033, the backbone of Open Banking, the definition of “consumer” reads: “an individual or an agent, trustee, or representative acting on behalf of an individual.” Congress obviously wasn’t contemplating AI agents when it wrote Dodd-Frank — but technology changing doesn’t obviate the underlying principle: consumers should be able to choose who, or what, transacts on their behalf.

Banks and companies like Amazon have real, legitimate concerns about agents becoming vectors for fraud or unauthorized transactions. But those are arguments for building portals for secure access, not for prohibiting agents altogether. Open Banking offers a useful lesson here, in that secure, standardized interfaces are preferable to forcing third parties into credential sharing or screen scraping.

We propose some basic guidance that relevant regulators (FTC, OCC, CFPB) could consider to help the market to coalesce around open norms before incumbents obtain sufficient lock-in, freezing the current landscape to their advantage.

With standards like these established, agents can make decisions that better serve the consumer, and will index on things like quality or price, rather than being funneled into a constrained set of options.

The push for Open Banking resulted in better experiences and lower prices for consumers. As agents become principal commercial actors, it is imperative that we lay the groundwork now so that an agent acting on your behalf is equally capable – if not more so – of delivering value and cost savings to you as you would be acting on your own.

text:
10 years ago, we launched Zcash, making a private version of Bitcoin. But the origins go back to the 80s, when, in the wake of the Watergate scandal, cryptographers first dreamed of private electronic cash, and the story runs through Satoshi’s invention of Bitcoin.

Zerocoin came three years before Zcash launched in 2016. We’d written it as a zk-mix for Bitcoin, and then a year later, Zerocash, which introduced SNARKs to cryptocurrency and is now the de facto approach to private payments on chain.

More than 30 years before that, in the early 80s, cryptographers first dreamed of private electronic payments. This was right after the invention of public key cryptography, the Watergate scandal, the Church Committee’s revelations of intelligence agency wrongdoing, and an ongoing fight between the nascent academic crypto community and the government over regulations and alleged backdoors.

It was also right as it became clear that the growth of the internet and electronic payments would pose a major surveillance risk. Today, there are a number of cryptographers who think crypto is simply math, devoid of purpose, and a number of folks in cryptocurrency who do not care about privacy (or perhaps even cryptography). That was not the case in the 1980s.

Starting with David Chaum, cryptographers first designed e-cash, a centralized private payment scheme that required a trusted bank to blindly sign special tokens. These went nowhere: existing trusted institutions, like banks, didn’t adopt the protocols, and no one wanted to trust magic internet money run by a strange company. Then Satoshi invented Bitcoin, overcoming the trust issue by inventing a blockchain. Bitcoin’s key innovation was the blockchain, which replaced a trusted bank with a public database anyone could participate in running. Because anyone could participate, it got off the ground without convincing a bank to run it. But because anyone could participate, there was no privacy: everyone could download the database of payments. And we couldn’t just use an e-cash scheme, as that required someone to keep a secret signing key, and the entire point of Bitcoin was that no one had to be trusted.

This is where Zerocoin, Zerocash, and Zcash come in. They replaced the e-cash system with a zero-knowledge proof and, this fact is not well understood by many, strengthened the privacy of e-cash schemes by giving the recipient full privacy even if the bank was malicious.

Buyback vs Growth

There are a lot of various stakeholders, with different priorities and time horizons. Alignment means giving everyone a shared interest in building the strongest version of this business, while having room for that business to evolve to its greatest form. It's a form of gravitational pull. 

That’s how I view this proposal: a first step toward durable alignment, while preserving the ambition and flexibility to leverage one of the most powerful forces in the universe: compounded interest. The objective is to build the greatest version of this business we can, with alignment that grows and also compounds alongside it.

This is the 1st revenue line item that we've identified that is developed enough to become programmatic. For example, GLX, or gain on sales of loans to institutions, was not a revenue line item until this past month. There's many more being built with the CHIP protocol as its core, we want to get to over >10 revenue line items, and that requires someone to build these!

With the initial network and ecosystem created by sUSDai & CHIP, the goal is to demonstrate our "commits" toward it across 

1) programmatic buybacks (once fully optimized)
2) discretionary buybacks (still optimizing/compounding)

The goal is to build the biggest mass possible of a busienss, and the business itself will organically, progammatically have the strongest gravity that pulls in network value.

--> $42.2/GB

--> $166.7/GB

M5U 512GB is 20% cheaper per GB and 27% cheaper per GB/s than the Spark. But, M5U 256GB is the real sweet spot: cheapest per GB of anything here, and half the 512's cost per GB/s

Spark is the worst deal on bandwidth. 273GB/s is under a quarter of the Mac's. RTX Pro 6000 matches the 256GB Mac on bandwidth/$, but costs ~4x per GB, before you buy the PC it goes in

Spark still wins on software by a large margin. But on raw hardware per dollar, the Mac is the better deal. We are working on the software portion and I expect the value of these M5U 512GBs, clustered together will do great things.

The credit market was never open to private startups to finance GPUs btw. Public neoclouds (former BTC miners) have been able to raise parent co financing by stuffing structure, converts, warrants into debt deals. They also have revenue from mining coins.  

Anything less than $1 billion notional GPU purchase has always been too small for private credit, too big for community banks, so the market has never existed. The fear mongering around credit markets closing for private startups is fundamentally silly, and also not really how it works. Deals have move from parent co financing to asset backed (GPUs). GPUs are better collateral than your startup equity. This is self explanatory 

How do I know this. Portco @USDai_Official has seen and financed more (by count) GPU deals than anyone else on earth. $450M of funded loans so far and growing. The reality is all of these smaller players will be forced to interact with the stablecoin economy to finance deals. I think the opportunity for stablecoin players to win the SMB GPU financing is large, and you are getting equity like returns (10-15%) against pristine collateral.

text:
last night, yc f26 founders heard from @james406 from @posthog

one thing that he said resonated with me deeply: 

"being more ambitious can make a startup easier to build - not because the work gets easier, but because the idea gives customers, teammates, and investors something to get excited about."

the challenge is making progress on that ambition *this week*

james shared an analogy i loved: “elephant carpaccio.” instead of building the feet first and promising the rest of the elephant later, build a thin slice that shows the shape of the whole thing.

a few other lessons i'm taking away:

- put a product in people’s hands quickly. polite interest isn’t the same as usage.

- ask not just where your first customers came from, but why they came. then do more of what’s working.

- don’t mistake self-serve for no human touch. posthog saw 30-40 percentage points better NRR among customers it had regular relationships with. correlation isn’t causation, but the pattern was hard to ignore. customer success became a major hiring focus for them.

- be decisive enough to learn when you’re wrong. posthog pushed its “self-driving” positioning hard, then adjusted when users showed they wanted more composable tools.

text:
Claude风控天机泄露😱

1. Claude 的风控是积分制：注册时会先给账号打分，之后根据行为加分或减分，低于一定分值就会直接封号（很少加分）。

2. 注册：邮箱和 IP 的权重最高。IP 不一定要家宽，但一定要干净，例如自建 IP。Gmail 已经不是最优选，他们现在使用的是一些其他高权重邮箱。注册时直接弹 KYC 的账号可以直接放弃。注册环节很重要，否则后续稍有高危行为就可能直接封号。使用手机 App 注册会加分。

3. 支付：刚注册就订阅会减分，直接订阅 Max 会大幅减分，最好间隔一两天再订阅 Pro。订阅时弹出 KYC 意味着账号处于考察期，但不一定会封；简而言之，A 社想先看 KYC 结果再决定。KYC 使用中国护照没有问题，最大的问题是不能一人多扫；闲鱼上很多账号都属于这种情况，要小心。

4. 注册后的 IP：最重要的是稳定，千万不要随便切换，尽可能一直使用同一个 IP；同样要求干净即可，不要求一定家宽，最好与注册 IP 一致。代理一定要开启全局模式并启用 TUN，这是重点。

5. 老号：老号权重非常高，也就是积分很多，容错率更高。账号积分会随着账号寿命增加，不过 2023 年的老号才是显著更高。

6. 使用：不要一上来就把周限额用完，尽量控制并平均使用；用量大的宁可开两个号轮换使用，也不要一次性用完。使用 CLI 和 Desktop 都可以，Desktop 似乎会少量加分。尽量少用网页端，最好只保留手机端和 Desktop 登录。

7. 时区和语言基本不减分，或仅极少量减分，没必要特意调整。

8. 高并发、反复提问同一个问题、频繁登录、频繁切换 IP 都会大幅减分。

9. 手机端使用会少量加分。开启记忆功能会加分，甚至可能记忆文件越多分数越高。

10. 支付方式为国外实体正规银行信用卡会加分，其次是 Google Play。Apple Pay 不了解；官方礼品卡不减分，但要注意来源是否为黑卡；虚拟卡直接绑定会减分。

11. 到达斩杀线后可能进入观察期。例如及格线是 60 分，账号 55 分就进入观察；如果继续扣分直接掉到 40 分，就会直接封号。观察期的典型特征是掉登录。有的高权重号可能经历两三个观察期才被封。

12. 多设备登录会大幅扣分，最好只在一台电脑上使用一个客户端。

13. Windows 和 macOS 没什么区别，Linux 使用会减分。

14. 跟 Claude 说自己是中国人也没事，不会因为记忆文件就封号。

15. 充值 Credits 会加分，不过成本太高，尚未进行大量实验。

16. 大量使用 Fable 会减分。

17. 升级 Max 大概率会直接进入观察期，除非是积分特别多的高权重号。观察期内有减分行为，大概率会封号。

18. 在工作时间使用不会扣分，不会出现因为使用北京时间就封号的情况。

text:
Ex-Tudor PM Tom Costello (@tcoste110) on what he looked for as head of equity trading at a $1B quant fund:

"At one point I was head of equity trading for about a billion dollar quant fund. I had guys coming to me with their strategies multiple times per day."

"I would interview about 10 of them a week, for a couple of years."

"People would come to me with that overfitted backtest. Well, this is just a backtest. Come back to me when you have real results."

"If they did come back with real results, very often the results would include a component of beta. I would say, well, I don't need you to trade beta. I can get my own beta. You've got to give me what's different from beta."

"What a hedge fund was always looking for was an uncorrelated return. If I have the S&P 500 in one hand and another asset that goes up as well but is completely uncorrelated, I can combine them and lever it and get an even higher return than either of them."
author: ethanrkho
quoted_text:
Retail investors vs. hedge fund managers: who wins?

Ex-Tudor quant PM Tom Costello (20%/yr, 1.4% max drawdown) DEBATES Market Wizard Chris Camillo ($20K → $80M, tells you to expect 70% drawdowns).

Chris Camillo (@ChrisCamillo) turned $20K into ~$80M over 18 years, audited by Jack Schwager for Unknown Market Wizards at 77% annualized. Founded TickerTags, sold to Jefferies. Co-founder of Dumb Money.

Tom Costello (@tcoste110) ran money at Tudor, Moore Capital, and Caxton. Started as a quant on JPM's exotic swaps desk. Now CIO at Bedrock Digital Assets.

We cover:
- Why a 50% drawdown is "a career-ending event" for a PM and "completely rational" for a retail investor with a 20-year horizon
- Chris's case that everyone should have a levered, concentrated risk bucket, and expect a 70% drawdown in it
- Tom's pushback: "At least half of the aspiring engineering students who wanna be day traders are gonna go broke"
- Why hedge funds don't beat the S&P, and why that's a category error
- 3x leveraged S&P ETFs held for decades: ~1.85x market returns, and the futures roll cost buried inside
- The e.l.f. trade: one YouTube video, a full day sitting in a Walgreens, and every cosmetics analyst on Wall Street asleep
- Chris spent 5 years selling social data to the biggest funds. They couldn't institutionalize it because "the words keep changing"
- Vita Coco: a viral TikTok sound → the biggest quarter in company history → +34% on earnings
- Tom's bet: LLMs hand social arb to the quants. Chris: "there's still plenty of time"
- "I know very few day traders who ever made anything like real money"

text:
Bloomberg: Over $170M in Unusual Hyperliquid Oil Perp Orders Raise Spoofing Suspicions

According to Bloomberg, market surveillance firm Solidus Labs identified over $170 million in unusual orders placed through two Hyperliquid accounts between March 8 and 10, amid sharp oil price swings linked to the Iran war. The activity raised concerns about potential spoofing in oil perpetual futures markets.

The trader repeatedly placed and canceled large orders on one side of the order book while executing trades on the other, with a cancellation-to-execution value ratio of roughly 30:1, generating about $119,000 in profits over three days. The activity primarily involved Brent crude perps. Solidus said the pattern resembled spoofing but acknowledged that manipulative intent remains unproven. Hyperliquid Labs emphasized that all orders, cancellations and trades are recorded on a transparent public blockchain and can be independently reviewed.

text:
Claude Code with Grok Bot just found proof that the keyboard on your iPhone can read everything you type. WhatsApp, Safari, Instagram, your bank app. a "free" keyboard was sending it out 2,416 times a day. i have the logs to prove it.

i've had a weird feeling about my phone for weeks but tonight something happened that made me finally check.

i was texting my brother about a used car i wanted to buy. never searched it. never said it out loud. just typed it in WhatsApp. 20 minutes later i open Instagram and my feed is full of that exact car. same model. same color. my brother texted me "bro why are you sending me car ads." i said i didn't. but i knew something was wrong.

i opened my MacBook and ran Claude Code that same night.

it went through my home Pi-hole log, every request my iPhone made since midnight. 18,342 of them. not just from the apps i had open. from everything running on the phone, including stuff i forgot i even installed.

what it found:

→ Instagram → 212 requests
→ WhatsApp → 388
→ K*yboard Pro → 2,416

a keyboard. a "free fonts" keyboard i downloaded in February and used maybe twice. Full Access turned on since 14 Feb.

then Claude Code matched every request to what i was doing on the phone at that moment:

→ WhatsApp → 1,120 requests, every time i typed a message
→ Safari → 806, every search and every login form
→ my bank app → 490, on the screen where i type my password
→ screen locked → zero. it only woke up when i typed

the last one went out at 00:58:41. three minutes before Claude Code found it.

the scariest one was the bank. 490 requests from the one screen where i type my password. every day. for 8 months.

then i checked my mom's phone on the same network. same keyboard. different fonts, same domains. she installed it because i told her about it.

i asked Claude Code how this was even possible. when you add a keyboard on iPhone it asks you to "Allow Full Access", and Apple's own warning says a keyboard with full access can send anything you type to its developer. passwords, card numbers, messages. nobody reads that screen. the fonts don't work without it, so everyone taps allow.

and it's not just one sketchy app. in 2024 Citizen Lab tested 9 of the most popular keyboard apps. 8 of them leaked what people typed. close to 1 billion users.

what i did:

→ Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards → Edit → deleted it
→ deleted the app itself, not just the keyboard
→ changed my bank and email passwords from my laptop, not from my phone
→ turned off Full Access for every keyboard that isn't Apple's

Claude Code checked the log again an hour later. zero requests from the keyboard. did the same on my mom's phone. took about 2 minutes per phone.

my feed went back to normal the next day. no more car. that's when i knew for sure.

the full step by step and the prompt are in the first reply. takes 2 minutes. save it so you don't lose it and send it to anyone who's ever downloaded a "cute" keyboard. yours might be doing it right now.

quoted_text:
There have been three key critiques in regards to the @prlnet  raise, but they are largely overblown in my view:

(1) The lab sells AI for dollars and keeps any PEARL it mines, so its investors can profit even if pearl-2:native falls. 

But PEARL is meant to be a SoV like Bitcoin, so buybacks would start a classic fight over how much of the lab’s revenue goes to shareholders vs token holders. The lab raised its own money to build a business that earns separately. That is the separation the SoV narrative actually needs, and the raise allows the lab to not sell the PEARL it may have for funding.

(2) The lab has written every fork and therefore controls the network and would cater to itself. 

But a fork only sticks if the majority of hashrate runs it and the lab’s $75M fleet would add only 2% to 3%. More importantly, the network won’t survive unless someone actually proves useful mining works, so the lab pushing to prove it outweighs the risk of its control.

(3) The lab has never disclosed how much PEARL it holds and the whitepaper says the low starting difficulty was partly meant to fund the team behind it. 

But the raise was cash for shares and not a token sale, and while we can’t tell which addresses are the lab’s, 98% of the coins mined in launch week have never moved. Although more transparency around their current holdings would help the market give more confidence around the entity.

If you agree or disagree let me know...

text:
As an Ethereum co-founder people sometimes ask me what has changed since 2014. The answer is almost everything. The tech, the scale and the stakes.

But back in 2014, all our soul-searching boiled down to a single question: for profit or not? We chose non-profit to keep the Ethereum protocol and vision as pure as possible.

Twelve years later, we're witnessing that same bold choice being made again. This time by @ethlabs_org, a non-profit lab built by researchers who helped shape Ethereum, with the independence to do what's right for its long-term future.

Twelve long years and the non-profit spirit we chose back then still beats at Ethereum's heart.

But one thing hasn't changed: Ethereum was never meant to belong to one person, one company, or one foundation. It was always meant to be a living and growing network of nodes, ideas, people and organizations.

That's why I'm both happy and proud to join @ethlabs_org as an Anchor funder.

I'm grateful to stand alongside my fellow Ethereum co-founder @ethereumJoseph and @BitMNR, @Sharplink, @snzholding, @krakenfx, @Anchorage, @Payward, @OctantApp, @gattacahq, @Lomashuk and so many other amazing supporters helping Ethereum’s innovation layer become just as distributed as its infrastructure.

In 2014, we chose the non-profit path to keep Ethereum's vision incorruptible. In 2026, the ecosystem is choosing the distributed path to keep its innovation unstoppable. 

Both choices come from the same belief: Ethereum belongs to everyone, and no single entity should carry it alone. The multi-node future isn't coming. It's here. 

What a joy! ❤️

Today, more people are backing Ethlabs.

Ethereum co-founder @MihaiAlisie joins as an anchor funder, @payward and @gattacahq join as contributors, and 19 new supporters from the Ethereum community are now backing our mission.

Case-Shiller 20-City Home Price Index hit a fresh record at 𝟯𝟰𝟲.𝟲 in August, +2.7% YoY — five straight monthly gains. Shelter-driven inflation stays embedded even as other CPI components cool.

𝗛𝘂𝗽𝘇𝘆 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲: Shelter is the largest CPI weight, and rising home prices feed directly into owners' equivalent rent. Persistent housing inflation reinforces the Fed's hiking bias — higher-for-longer rates raise the discount rate on non-yielding assets like BTC and pressure equity valuations. Worsening affordability also risks a wealth-effect drag on spending, a second-order risk-off channel.

For BTC and SP500, the setup stays rate-sensitive: sticky shelter inflation keeps the Fed boxed in, and any hawkish repricing hits both. Short exposure on both remains the higher-probability read while home-price momentum persists.

The last time a new machine threatened a third of American jobs, we reinvented how we educated our kids.

author: eriktorenberg
quoted_text:
Joe Liemandt of Alpha School on why AI is today's 1910 tractor moment, and why parents once again have to rethink their kids' future:

"In 1910, 90% of America had an 8th grade education. There were basically no high schools. And over 30% of America is a farmer. So everybody's on the farm, 8th grade was enough."

"Then in 1910, the Case tractor rolled up on the American farm. You can go look at the ads, it literally looks like an Anthropic ad. 'Does the work of 50 programmers. Does the work of 50 farm hands.'"

"Literally everybody in America realized 30% of the jobs are going away. That path is gone, and we have to get our kids ready for this new future. And it was that same recognition I think that parents have today."

"What America did back then... they voted to fund an education that they never experienced. They knew they had to do something different than their background, see the world differently, to get their kids ready and get them the good jobs."

"That school system became the industrial system we've had the last 100 years. It served us really well for 100 years, but now it's time for the next change."

@jliemandt

text:
彭博说 $MRVL 要买 $LITE，盘后一个涨15%一个跌10%

用最简单的话讲这是怎么回事
AI数据中心里，芯片算完东西要把数据传出去
传得太多，电线不够用了，要改用光
改用光需要两样东西，一个是把电信号翻译成光信号的翻译官，一个是发光的灯泡
$MRVL 是翻译官， $LITE 是灯泡，而且是全世界七八成人都在用的那种灯泡，货已经卖到2029年了
现在翻译官想把灯泡厂买下来，以后客户来一次就能把两样都买齐
它的对手 $AVGO 是翻译官加交换机，$MRVL 买了灯泡之后就是翻译官加灯泡，各有一头

为什么买的人跌卖的人涨
$LITE 市值805亿， $MRVL 2206亿，等于买一家自己三分之一还多的
两家都贵，用贵的股票买贵的东西还要再加溢价，股东自然要问钱从哪来 
如果溢价25%，这笔交易要1000亿， $MRVL 账上现金远远不够，大头只能换股，稀释奔着30%去
而且 $MRVL 这两年已经买了两家公司，口袋本来就不鼓
跌8%不是说方向错，是在说这笔钱不好出

对以后股价的看法

$LITE
明天开盘涨幅大概率回吐一部分，15%里面有一半是交易成了的溢价，有一半是情绪
现在追它等于在赌交易一定成，彭博报深入谈判的交易最后黄掉的不少
没谈成，这15%原路吐回去；谈成了，上面空间也就是溢价那点，风险收益不对称
已经拿着的可以留，没拿的别追
$MRVL
今晚的10%跌的是不确定性，不是交易本身
看两个东西：一是条款出来是现金多还是换股多，这个体量大头换股几乎跑不掉，稀释30%上下，市场今晚跌10%其实还没跌够这个数；二是有没有反垄断的声音，灯泡市占率七八成，这关不一定好过
我自己的做法是等条款，条款出来之前不动，如果是现金为主而且跌到230以下，这是比 $LITE 更好的买合并后公司的方式 

整个光通信板块
不管成不成，这个消息说明大公司已经开始用真金白银抢连接链条上的资产
$COHR 是和 $LITE 最像的灯泡厂，明天大概率跟涨，而且它后面也可能被人买
$NVDA 3月给 $LITE 和 $MRVL 各投了20亿，它早就想让它们在一起
这条线上的公司以后估值里要加一个被收购的溢价

text:
After a week of the ICP patent drama, here is what I see. DFINITY started two lines the same week in 2021: a sealed patent application, and a public CC BY paper with the same method. For three years the public line was the only one anyone could see. NEAR built on it and cited it. Then DFINITY switched to the sealed line and asked for money. The product they built on the same patent holds about 240 BTC today.

The dates, all public and linkable.

Sep 30, 2021: DFINITY files a patent application on re-randomized presignatures. Applications are sealed until published, nobody outside the company can read them.

Oct 5, 2021: five days later, the same two people, Jens Groth and Victor Shoup, DFINITY's cryptographers and the named inventors on the patent, put the same method on eprint under CC BY. Free for anyone to use, attribution only.

Nov 13, 2023: a NEAR engineer opens a public ticket. He describes a known attack on ECDSA with derived keys and presignatures, and proposes the defense from Groth and Shoup's paper, citing it by name: "one technique proposed in [GroSho22] is to re-randomize presignatures". Merged in December. This is how cryptography is supposed to work: you do not invent your own, you take a published, peer-reviewed construction and say where it came from. The code running today still carries the comment "inspired by [GS21]" with a link to the paper, and the Trail of Bits audit describes it the same way.

Nov 28, 2024: the application becomes public for the first time. Three years after filing, a year after NEAR cited the paper.

Jul 28, 2026: patent granted.

Sep 25, 2026: NEAR makes online presign the default, a path where the presignature is computed after the request and there is nothing stored to re-randomize. The PR description is about protocol safety, no patents mentioned.

Oct 2026: DFINITY's founder calls it theft and asks for license fees back to the first day of use.

Bottom line: two paths opened the same week. NEAR took the public one for three years and said so at every step. DFINITY waited until the sealed one was granted, then came for the readers of the public one.

今天的主流大模型，ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini、DeepSeek，底层都是将近十年前的算法：2017 年谷歌论文《Attention Is All You Need》里的 Transformer。我做了个视频，用大白话讲清楚AI在想什么？

看这篇论文的时候，我诞生了两个想法

1、Transformer 把理解语言变成了矩阵乘法，这正是显卡的强项。模型越大，显卡卖得越多，英伟达踩中这张算法彩票，赢了将近十年。可 Mamba、RWKV、扩散语言模型都在挑战它，算法一变，护城河就可能动摇...

2、论文里的核心公式：Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√dₖ)·V

一个字的意思由身边的字决定："因为它不饿"，它是小猫；"因为它不新鲜"，它是鱼。

我用"生命三问"理解 Q、K、V：你要去哪里、你是谁、你从哪里来。

这很像佛教的缘起：意义依条件而生

text:
Should you buy a 512GB Mac Studio for Local AI? I ran the numbers before ordering one.

1) On token price alone, renting wins. At DeepSeek V4.1 Flash API rates, the Mac needs years of 24/7 output to pay for itself.

2) Price per token is the wrong way to judge it, though. In expensive housing markets, renting is cheaper month to month than owning, and people still buy for control and because a home holds value. The same logic applies to this machine.

3) It holds value. The 512GB M3 Ultra now resells for about twice what it cost new, because memory got scarce. If mine resells for even half, the real cost halves.

4) Nobody can take it away. API models get swapped, rate limited and refused mid-task. In June, access to two frontier models was cut off for almost three weeks. Weights on my desk stay put.

5) Zero-cost tokens change what you build. When every call costs nothing, agents can run all day and you can experiment freely. MacStories ran local agents 24/7 for 99 days at zero token cost.

6) It runs the big ones. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (552B) and GLM-5.3 (744B) don’t fit in 256GB. In 512GB, each loads into one memory pool.

So if you’d use it a few hours a week, rent. If you’d run it all day the moment it was free, buy.

Go Local AI!

text:
一句话总结Google财报：

营收和Cloud强劲增长（尤其AI驱动），核心运营利润率提升，但股权投资波动拉低净利润，重资本开支继续压制自由现金流，目前盘后跌了10个点

和我想象的差不多，又是AI投入压制现金流，但是AI也的确带来了业务的增长，需要看今晚开盘后的情况，决定是否加仓。

短期风险是已经破位了，涨回来可能需要时间，但目前谷歌的估值已经便宜到地板价了。

接下来等下跌企稳会再加一点仓位。

整体业绩
•  营收：1276亿美元（精确为1275.77亿美元），同比增长25%（去年同期1023亿美元），连续第13个季度实现双位数增长，年化运行率接近5000亿美元。

•  运营利润：405.8亿美元，同比增长约30%，运营利润率31.8%（去年同期约30.5%）。

•  净利润：261.7亿美元，同比下降约25%；稀释EPS为2.12美元（去年同期2.87美元）。

•  净利润下滑主因是其他收入/费用转为亏损约82亿美元，主要来自股权投资（包括SpaceX等）的未实现损失约86.6亿美元；去年同期则有大额收益。核心运营业务本身表现强劲。

业务分部亮点
•  Google Services（含搜索、YouTube、订阅等）：963亿美元，+11%。

•  广告总收入：约820亿美元，+约11%。

•  Search & other：633.5亿美元，+12%（AI推动搜索查询同比增长创近5年新高，包括商业查询）。

•  YouTube广告：112亿美元，+9%（增速有所放缓）。

•  订阅、平台和设备：约143亿美元，+11%。
•  Google Cloud：307亿美元，+103%（去年同期约152亿美元），创纪录增长。主要驱动来自企业AI基础设施、AI解决方案、核心GCP服务以及TPU系统销售。Cloud运营利润约111亿美元，利润率大幅提升。

•  Other Bets：营收约3.72亿美元，亏损有所扩大。

其他关键信息
•  AI与用户指标：Gemini App月活用户突破10亿（公司历史上增长最快产品之一）；YouTube Music和Premium订阅超1.5亿（含试用）；第一方模型API处理接近320亿tokens/分钟。

•  资本开支与现金流：本季资本开支约513.6亿美元（大幅高于去年），全年指引维持在1950-2050亿美元区间，2027年可能超过3000亿美元。自由现金流为负约90.7亿美元，受AI基建和TPU相关投入影响。

text:
for @AnthropicAI’s J-space paper, @neurostrow and @FieteGroup at MIT worked out what the Jacobian lens behind the “global workspace” in Claude actually picks up

the lens averages over many prompts and positions, and an average can look nothing like the things it averages: in four open models, the averaged Jacobian lands away from the cloud of individual ones

what survives the averaging are directions that grow through the layers, they stay steady across the text and work the same in every context: that’s also why J-space is a small slice of the activations (under 10% of variance)

it’s a question we care about at @mostik_ai too: which parts of a model’s internal state are steady enough for another model to read

In crypto, the liquid token market over the last 18-24 months grew increasingly allergic to a three things: 
1. token overhang via unlocks 
2. token overhang via inefficient emissions
3. siphoning of protocol value away from token holders 

As a result, we saw a stage of extreme token nihilism followed by a set of projects that identified they need to prove to the market that 1-3 are being solved first. Buybacks solve all three, with a single mechanism. 

So, in crypto, when a company starts doing buybacks, it is not because they are unable to innovate anymore, but rather, a simple signal to the market that they can now begin to trust the asset issued by the protocol (token).

text:
The Fed has gone QUIET.

Kevin Warsh has dropped forward guidance and skipped his own dot twice, and the Fed held rates without committing to a December rate move.

How the Fed went from silence to signals, and back:

1. Before 1994: The Fed didn't routinely announce rate decisions, so markets guessed from its bond trades and read the minutes 6 to 8 WEEKS later.

2. Feb 4, 1994: The first post-meeting statement, just 99 words, which Greenspan privately argued shouldn't set a precedent.

3. Aug 2003: "Considerable period," the first explicit guidance on the future rate path.

4. Apr 2011: The first post-meeting press conference, which Powell made an every-meeting event from 2019.

5. Aug 2011: Low rates likely "at least through mid-2013," the first calendar-based rate guidance.

6. Jan 25, 2012: The first dot plot.

7. Jun 17, 2026: Warsh's first meeting, where he said "We've dropped forward guidance."

18 officials submitted rate forecasts in September, and the Chair submitted none.

author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
James Talarico is very damaged.

We all know he supports illegals voting.

But I discovered a more disturbing story.

Either Freako himself repeatedly voted illegally and lied about it, or he has been living for years with his mother as an elected official.

I also discovered that he illegally occupied elected office in the Texas House for more than a year.

I am not making this up.

Freako is out of control.

On October 13, 2021 Talarico posted: "I'm excited to move over the county line ... (Yes, I may have to move back with my parents like a true millennial.)"

Texas Constitution article III §23 says, "If any Senator or Representative remove his residence from the district or county for which he was elected, his office shall thereby become vacant."

Now, from 2019 until January 2023, Talarico was a member in the Texas House of Representatives in HD-52, Williamson County.

Yet on November 5, 2021, he registered as a voter at his mother's house, in HD-50.

His campaign says he moved into his mother's residence that day. It provided journalists a U-Haul receipt.

His parents gave his campaign a $1,437.84 in-kind contribution labeled "Moving expenses" in December 2021.

Talarico had moved from HD-52 to HD-50, a completely different district.

He was not living in the district that he represented, yet he never vacated his seat.

Talarico thus illegally occupied elected office, until January 2023, for more than a year, in violation of the Texas Constitution, Article III §23.

Now, in June 9, 2022, Talarico bought a house in Austin, the same HD-50 as his mother's house.

The mortgage that he signed stated that he would "occupy, establish, and use the Property as Borrower's principal residence within 60 days", or August 8, 2022.

On that mortgage, "Non-Homestead Property" is unchecked, while other boxes were checked, indicating that this property was his homestead, or primary residence.

On Aug 8, 2022, the deadline day under this mortgage to move into the new house, he sold his previous house.

Yet the sale deed was signed with his mother's address as his mailing address.

So, he was registered to vote at his mother's house, and he signed his mailing address as his mother's mailing address.

Yet he signed a mortgage requiring him to live at a different house.

What's going on!

Now, on Aug 15, 2022, he refinanced that mortgage. The checked box: "Renewal and Extension of Liens Against Homestead Property."

Tax Code 11.13(j)(1)(D) says a residence homestead must be "occupied as the individual's principal residence."

Yet, he was still registered to vote at his mother's address.

Texas Election Code says:

§11.003. You "may vote only in the election precinct in which the person resides".

§1.015(a). "Residence" means domicile, "one's home and fixed place of habitation to which one intends to return after any temporary absence".

His mother's house must be his primary residence for him to vote in that election precinct, which is in precinct 191.

Yet, according to both the mortgage and its refinancing, he could not be living with his mother, but in the new house, which is in precinct 133.

Which is it?

Because if he was not living with his mother, he was voting illegally.

Now, at every vote, §63.0011(a) requires the election officer to ask each voter whether the address on the list is current and whether they've moved within the county.

If he said he had moved, he had to sign a statement giving his current address, and §15.022(a)(4) then required the registrar to correct his record.

Yet Talarico voted from his mother's address on five separate occasions, November 1, 2022, November 2, 2023, February 28, 2024, April 30, 2024, May 28, 2024.

His registration stayed at his parents' house until Sept 7, 2024.

Either Freako was living with his mother, or he voted illegally five times over the course of nearly two years.

Which is it?

Now, on April 27, 2023, Texas House Bill 1243 proposed to make voting illegally a felony.

On April 27, Talarico voted for Bucy Amendment 1 to gut the bill.

The amendment failed.

On April 27, he then voted for Manuel Amendment 2 to keep voting illegally a class A misdemeanor unless the person had a prior conviction.

That amendment also failed.

On April 27, April 28, and May 28, he then voted three additional times to block the bill.

In total, he voted five times to block the bill to make illegal voting a felony.

But the Bill passed, making voting illegally a felony, taking effect on September 1, 2023.

Talarico voted from his mother's address four more times after the Bill took effect, exposing him to four potential felony counts.

Now, on May 1, 2023, Talarico filed a sworn financial statement with the Texas Ethics Commission that marked the Travis house that he bought in 2022 as his home address.

The one we keep ping-ponging back and forth on.

In Part 7A, real property, he listed two entries:

Round Rock house (Williamson County): marked as sold in 2022 at "NET GAIN at least $47,220 or more".

Home box unmarked.

One Travis County lot: street "REDACTED PER 572.032(a-1), GOV'T CODE".

Box "X CHECK IF FILER'S HOME ADDRESS" marked.

He knew where he lived.

Or did he?

At the Texas Tribune Festival on September 24, 2026, just a month ago, he contradicted himself again.

When he was asked about the reporting about his voter registration, he responded:

"I voted where I lived, in every single election."

Now, we established early that Freako illegally occupied elected office, refusing to vacate in violation of the Texas Constitution.

But which of the following are true:

Did Freako live for years with his mother while serving as a Representative in the Texas House?

Is that why he has said, "What if we ran our world like we run a kindergarten classroom? Because at the end of the day, aren't we all just really big kindergartners?"

Because he lived for years with mommy?

Or, did he not live with his mother, but by registering his mother's address as his home address, engage in felony illegal voting?

Which is it?

And why won't Talafreako be straight with us?

Robinhood Chain's RWA market cap has dropped below the $330M line a live @Trueo_ market settles on October 31, and traders still price "YES" at 65.2%.

Yesterday it sat at $337.4M per @DefiLlama, with "YES" at 75.9%. Today it's $321.7M.

@RobinhoodCrypto Chain RWA TVL first crossed $330M on September 28, the day DefiLlama began tracking Midas mGLO, a single asset worth ~$36M.

The current RWA TVL breakdown:
→ 194 Robinhood stock tokens: $163.8M (51%)
→ Maple's syrupUSDG: $121.4M (38%)
→ Midas mGLO: $36.2M (11%)
→ 15 Ondo stock tokens: $0.3M

The drop came from syrupUSDG, which fell from $139.2M to $121.4M in under a day. Onchain, about 17.8M syrupUSDG (~$18M) left Robinhood Chain in four bridge transfers between 06:55 and 11:08 UTC today. Each batch landed on Ethereum and was burned within about an hour. Three of the four came from a single wallet.

Getting back above $330M takes about $8.3M, and there are two realistic routes.

The first is a stock rally: a ~4% rise in large-cap US stocks by Friday's close, which works out to about 5% in the stock-token basket. That uses the basket's historical sensitivity of about 1.3x to the market.

With syrupUSDG held where it is, a market rally of:
→ +2% = $325.9M
→ +4% = $330.2M
→ +5% = $332.3M

Since 2025, the stock-token basket has risen 5% or more over 3 to 4 trading days only about 5% to 9% of the time, and the broad market has risen 3.9% or more in about 3% to 6% of those windows.

The second route is syrupUSDG coming back. It would need to recover about 6.8% on its own to close the distance.

A 65.2% "YES" price sits well above what the stock route alone has delivered historically, which may mean traders are leaning on syrupUSDG returning.

Friday's US close is the last real price input for the stock tokens, since Robinhood's stock-token minting closes Saturday at 01:00 UTC, six hours before the October 31 reading at 07:00 UTC. syrupUSDG supply can keep moving right up to the reading.

text:
Dan Tapiero on Getting Rich in Crypto, Knowing When to Sell, and Building Wealth That Lasts

In this episode of When Shift Happens, I sit down with @DTAPCAP, founder of @50TFunds, to discuss what it really takes to build and preserve wealth in crypto. Drawing on 35 years of investing experience, including working alongside legendary investors Stanley Druckenmiller, Julian Robertson, and Steve Cohen, Dan shares why patience is often more valuable than intelligence, how he avoided investing in FTX, and why he believes the biggest opportunities in blockchain are still ahead.

Wealth Is What You Keep, Not What You Spend

Dan begins with a lesson he frequently shares with his children: "You are wealthy because you have money, not because you spend it." Having spent decades around some of the world's wealthiest investors, he has observed a difference between genuine financial security and outward displays of success. In Greenwich, Connecticut, where he previously lived, families with generations of accumulated wealth often occupied modest homes, while newly wealthy residents purchased enormous properties and expensive luxuries.

For Dan, wealth is less about demonstrating purchasing power and more about retaining the freedom that money creates. Spending is not inherently wrong, but without limits, even substantial fortunes can be lost. He also challenges the assumption that becoming rich solves every problem. Wealth brings comfort and independence, but can introduce new responsibilities, unwanted attention, and complications.

Learning to Take Risks Before Everyone Agrees

Dan's career illustrates another essential principle: meaningful opportunities rarely come with widespread approval. Before establishing 50T Holdings, he co-founded a physical gold investment business, GBI. For years, people questioned why he was pursuing gold when it attracted relatively little interest, but the business prospects later improved dramatically as gold prices rose.

His early conviction in Bitcoin and blockchain attracted similar skepticism. "You have to be comfortable living a little bit in the gray with uncertainty," he explains. Investors must develop the confidence to act on well-researched opportunities before the broader market recognizes their potential. By the time everyone agrees an investment is attractive, much of its potential upside is gone.

Why Dan Passed on FTX

Perhaps the clearest illustration of Dan's investment discipline is his decision to avoid FTX. During the crypto boom, investors urged him to back the exchange, but he remained unconvinced, particularly by its valuation. His firm generally targets investments valued at approximately five to ten times revenue, but FTX was valued at roughly 50 times revenue, far outside his preferred range. Instead, he invested in Deribit, a cryptocurrency options exchange, at approximately six to seven times net profit. Deribit subsequently became a major success for his fund when Coinbase acquired it.

Dans explains that investors often become enthusiastic when prices are high but retreat when opportunities become cheaper. In fact, he struggled to raise his fourth fund during the 2023–2024 bear-market period, despite his extensive track record. That fund then became his most successful, generating more than 250% in gross gains.

Patience Gets You Into Wealth. Selling Helps You Keep It.

Dan describes crypto as "the easiest place in the world to make money" but one of the hardest places to hold on to it. Much of this difficulty comes from investor psychology. For instance, investors who experience enormous gains often become emotionally attached to their ‘wins’ and struggle to sell, while those who endure prolonged losses may sell immediately when prices recover just to escape the discomfort.

Dan believes both reactions demonstrate why patience and emotional detachment must be learned. He also emphasizes the importance of establishing an exit strategy before purchasing an asset. Even when there are fundamental reasons to keep holding, taking some profits can protect the gains already achieved.

For younger investors especially, he cautions against optimizing for immediate riches. Although taking risks early in life can create opportunities, recovering from significant financial losses can take years. His preferred approach is to think in five- or ten-year periods, allocate capital deliberately, and recognize that surviving market downturns is essential to long-term compounding.

The Next Opportunity

Dan remains deeply optimistic about blockchain's long-term potential. He compares the internet's digitization of information with blockchain's emerging ability to digitize money, ownership, and value. Stablecoins, tokenized government securities, and decentralized trading platforms represent early examples, but Dan believes the larger opportunity lies in tokenizing illiquid assets, particularly real estate and farmland.

His interest stems partly from an agricultural investment business he established years earlier. Despite farmland representing an enormous asset class, ordinary investors had limited opportunities to access large, professionally managed portfolios. Tokenization could eventually change that. Dan imagines a future where property records, financial assets, and legal documentation can be managed through interconnected blockchain systems, simplifying transactions that currently require numerous intermediaries.

What Does a Rich Life Actually Look Like?

Toward the end of the conversation, Dan offers a more personal definition of success. For him, a rich life means independence, time with family, intellectual curiosity, travel, and the freedom to pursue interests that matter. Despite his success, he continues attending conferences, meeting entrepreneurs, and exploring unfamiliar ideas rather than settling into a comfortable routine.

After decades navigating financial markets, Dan's perspective ultimately returns to a simple distinction. Wealth is not defined by the biggest trade, the fastest return, or the lifestyle it can display. It comes from making thoughtful decisions, remaining patient when others lose conviction, and working towards your personal definition of enough.

刚看完 Google 财报和盘后大阴线，几分钟内就亏掉大几个月的的薪水，瞬间就没心情写代码了😭

复盘一下这次砸盘的核心逻辑：
1. CapEx 焦虑：内部这大半年把日常 budget 抠到极致，省下的钱全砸进了算力和 AI 基建。但华尔街逻辑变了：光砸钱不够，拿不出立竿见影的 ROI 指引就是挤压利润率。

3. 预期差：财报前预期拉得太满，没有炸裂的 beat & raise，资金就会直接借机获利了结。

白天在工位死磕分布式系统省那几毫秒延迟和机器成本，晚上看机构以毫秒级的速度把自己的 RSU 砸出个大坑。血泪教训：永远别把人力资本和财务资本绑在一条船上。等这波过去，老老实实做分散了。今晚湾区和西雅图估计不少人睡不着。

中国社区逆向拆解了Claude的封号机制。以下是他们的发现

Claude使用积分制。注册时账号获得初始分数，之后根据行为加分或扣分。低于阈值直接封号。回分很难

影响分数的因素:

注册
> 干净IP是最重要的因素。不一定要家宽，但必须干净
> Gmail已经不是最优选，有权重更高的邮箱服务
> 注册时直接弹KYC的号可以扔了
> 用手机App注册会加分

支付
> 刚注册就订阅会扣分
> 直接上Max会大幅扣分。最好等两天先订Pro
> 支付时弹KYC说明账号在考察期，但不一定会封
> 国外实体银行卡加分。Google Play也行。虚拟卡扣分

使用
> 不要一次把限额用完。宁可两个号轮换也不要一个号撸到底
> Desktop客户端有少量加分。尽量少用网页端
> 手机端也有少量加分
> 开启记忆功能加分。记忆文件越多分越高

IP和设备
> 稳定性是关键。不要跳IP，尽量一直用同一个
> 代理必须全局模式并开启TUN
> 多设备登录大幅扣分。理想状态是一台电脑一个客户端
> 频繁换IP、频繁登录、高并发都会大幅扣分

账号年龄
> 老号有巨大的容错空间。2023年的号明显更高
> 分数随时间增长，但很慢

其他
> Windows和macOS没区别。Linux会扣分
> 时区和语言基本不影响。不会因为北京时间就封号
> 跟Claude说自己是中国人没问题，记忆不会触发封号
> 大量使用Fable会扣分
> 升级Max大概率进入观察期，除非是高权重老号

观察期和封号
> 接近阈值时账号可能进入观察期。典型特征是掉登录
> 观察期继续扣分就会封号

quoted_text:
我很愿意认真回答这位德国朋友的疑问。

你的第一个问，其实是在说，由于中国是一个威权政府，因此人民在政治上不受认真对待。

这个命题本身就是错误的。威权政府，并不意味着人民不受认真对待。民主政府，也不意味着人民就受到认真对待。

新加坡是威权国家，菲律宾是民主国家，难道新加坡人的处境，不如菲律宾人吗？中国是威权国家，印度是民主国家，难道中国人的处境，不如印度人吗？

你的第二个问，你的发问本身并不严谨。不能笼统地说，中国人没有政治自由。这个问题要分两个维度来讲。

1、政治参与自由。
从这个维度讲，中国任何人有参与政治的自由。中国人都有权利申请入党、考公务员。筛选规则与民主制度不同，但不等于中国人没有参与政治的自由。

中国制度与民主制度的区别在于：

民主制度下，一个人只要有钱，可以在任何时候参与政治。就像川普一辈子没有从政，老了突然想要竞选总统，他就可以参选，而且成功了。

但在中国，任何官员都必须从基层公务员做起。一个人无法因为有钱，就能一步登天当上高官。

这种制度的好处有：

A、公平性。
中国有大量的高层领导人出身平民家庭，如胡锦涛、温家宝、汪洋、李强，等等。像习近平这种红二代，反而是个意外。

B、专业性。
任何一个高层领导人，都必须经过几十年不同级别岗位的历练，他对国家各个层面的情况的了解，以及他的治理经验，不是一个企业家、一个明星，或者一个未治理过一个城市的议员，所能相提并论的。

C、远见性。
由于领导人不受制于短期的、非理性的民意，因此可以规划长远的发展战略，并以唯一执政党确保该战略的长期、有效的实施。

D、政策不受资本干涉。
你选择从政，就不能从商。你选择从商，就不能从政。这样一来，资本的归资本，政治的归政治，资本无法干涉政治。

2、政治权利自由。
当然，中国制度有其“表面上”的代价。为什么只是“表面上”的，后面再说。先说这种代价。

代价就是中国人不拥有谩骂政府、抨击政策的自由。我们可以批评政府，但必须在一种就事论事的理性语境中。我们不能喊“习近平下台”或者“共产党下台”。

我们也不拥有全民选举的自由，建立政党的自由。

这些“代价”为什么只是表面上的，可以从一则寓言说起：

一农场主临死前问儿子；猪抱怨饲料太差，牛报怨活太重，鸡报怨窝太脏，怎么办？ 儿子说：“喂好饲料，干轻活，清理鸡窝。” 农场主摇摇头说：你啥都别做，给他们选票，让它们选择你或者你媳妇管它们，让它们以为这个家是它们做主。

这个寓言让我们思考，作为人民，我们要的是什么？我们要的其实是更好的生活，而不是选票以及骂政府的自由。

回到开头那个举例，新加坡缺少很多民主国家所具备的政治自由，但没有人会认为新加坡人受到压迫。

这就涉及到自由的定义，自由到底是什么？

按照罗斯福的定义，自由包括：言论自由、信仰自由、免于匮乏、免于恐惧。

在我们计算一个社会的自由度时，我们计算的是自由的总量，而不是单项自由的含量。

举个例子，很多非洲国家拥有选票和骂政府的自由，但人民生活贫困，出行只能靠双脚。我在中国，生活富足、商品丰富、服务便捷、社区安全，我坐3个小时的高铁可以抵达一座大城市，我也有经济条件时不时出国旅游。

你认为非洲人自由，还是我自由？

诚然，中国还有很多人口，在物质生活上并不自由，但这是经济发展不充分导致的，不是政治压迫导致的。一个贫穷地区，无会因为给你民众选票和骂政府的自由，他们就变富裕了。

因此，当你谈自由的时候，你要计算自由的总量，不能单看一项自由的有无和多寡。你也不能将经济问题，归咎于某一项政治自由的问题。

坦率讲，我觉得你们的民主制度，已经病入膏肓了，中国人并不羡慕你们那种制度。

BREAKING: Brazil's -19.8% stock market crash on Monday was one of the rarest market events in the last two decades, according to our analysis.

Brazil's EWZ ETF plunged -19.8% on October 26th, marking an 8.4 standard deviation move.

For context, the ETF's average daily move over the last 20 years has been just +0.04%, with a standard deviation of 2.36%.

Under a normal distribution, the probability of a decline this extreme is approximately 1 in 58 quadrillion.

In other words, this event should be virtually impossible under conventional statistical models.

What just happened in Brazil was *almost* impossible.

text:
I've always believed that intelligence should come from simple, general building blocks that learn their own abstractions directly from raw data; in other words, the bitter lesson. I think we're finally seeing a real step towards AI that can learn from all data.

Language modeling on raw bytes is a microcosm of this ideal, and to me it's a central problem in AI: if we can't build LLMs that learn end-to-end from bytes, how will we handle the rest of the world's data that we understand even less?

Last year we introduced hierarchical networks (H-Nets) as a first step. Our new version finds up to 3-5x efficiency gains in controlled scaling law experiments, and at larger scale matches an open-source model trained on 11T tokens with ~10x less data and compute. The posts below walk through what we found and why we think it works.

text:
红果日活 1.68 亿、人均每天两小时：秦朔说“字节时间”来了，程苓峰说这才刚开始

同一份数据，两篇文章，两个结论。野村证券 9 月的报告援引 QuestMobile 数据：今年 7 月，在中国使用时长排前 50 的 App 里，抖音第一次超过微信，字节系合计占 40.9%，腾讯系占 29.1%。

《第一财经日报》原总编辑秦朔据此写了《可怕的红果与中国互联网的字节时间》，担心红果这类算法机器正在吃掉人们的时间。

公众号“神在吗”的作者程苓峰 10 月 28 日接着写了《肉鸡时间》，认为份额只是表面，AI 短剧才是真正的“核爆”。两篇文章都在传的“红果年入 400 亿”，红果官方已经声明不实。

【红果有多能占时间】

秦朔引用的报告显示，红果 7 月日活 1.68 亿，一年翻了一倍，超过腾讯视频、爱奇艺、优酷、芒果 TV 四家相加（约 1.55 亿，未去重）。按使用总时长，红果已是中国第四大 App，排在抖音、微信、抖音极速版之后；今年 2 月人均每天看 125 分钟，比抖音和微信还长。

用户数上红果还差得远：微信日活 9 亿多，抖音 7 亿多。红果赢的是每个人花在上面的时间。

【秦朔：红果是一台时间吸收器】

秦朔把红果跑得快归结为四点。

1. 算法：每集 1 到 3 分钟，集集结尾留悬念，手指一滑就是下一集。

2. 供给：广电总局公布，今年前 8 个月全国上线微短剧 43 万部，是去年全年的 13 倍，其中 AI 剧超过九成。

3. 生态：在抖音刷到剧情片段，一键跳到红果看全集；番茄小说提供原著，秦朔文中说，去年的爆款短剧六成以上改编自番茄小说。

4. 免费：看剧不花钱，只看广告，平台拿广告收入给创作者分账。

腾讯刚在微信小程序里推出“绿泡泡短剧”应战，秦朔不看好。

秦朔打了个比方：字节所有 App 共用一套算法底座，像同一个酒瓶倒出不同的酒；腾讯靠社交起家，各个产品各用各的瓶子。秦朔还提到，在抖音和红果上看什么，朋友不知道，也就没有发朋友圈那种顾虑。

秦朔最在意代价。每天 125 分钟，意味着读书、思考、陪家人的时间少了。

秦朔预计短剧会分化成 K 型：底层是海量 AI 爽剧，顶层是少量真人精品，夹在中间的真人短剧最难过。秦朔也认为，时间多不等于价值高，腾讯在精品内容和中老年用户上仍有底盘。

刹车已经出现。9 月 1 日起施行的《微短剧发展管理办法》要求 AI 内容逐集标注，禁止平台用诱导沉迷的算法。红果 10 月 21 日宣布下线“看剧赚金币”：11 月 1 日起新用户不再有这个功能，12 月 31 日前全部下线，已攒下的金币和余额不受影响。

【抖音的反驳】

抖音集团副总裁李亮两次在微博回应，说“字节时间”不严谨：数据只算前 50 个 App，没算长尾 App 和电脑端；字节系最新的 41.8% 也没过半；短剧和短视频是充分竞争的行业，没有谁能一直第一。

秦朔 10 月 28 日回应说，“字节时间”是对注意力流向的概括，并非垄断认定。

【程苓峰：要看速度，AI 短剧是另一种东西】

程苓峰认为份额过没过半不重要。一年前字节系和腾讯系差不到 3 个点，现在差 13 个点，跑得快的一方会吸走所有新增的时间。

程苓峰把红果的优势叫作“三低合一”：番茄小说的网文省了剧本成本，字节的视频生成模型 Seedance 省了拍摄和演员成本，抖音流量便宜还能先放片段试水，省了拉新成本。

秦朔和程苓峰都看了穿越剧《持械入宋》。

秦朔说它比以前的短剧多样，有内涵也有专业性，但耗时、容易陷进去。程苓峰在里面看出了一场创业：主角用现代知识造火炮、改弩机，为了拿到铁料去考科举，再一点点组织人手，按未来的地图改造旧世界。

程苓峰还刷到讲急诊分诊、大闸蟹养殖、货车司机生活的剧，觉得这些短剧像一部百科全书。

所以程苓峰主张把真人短剧和 AI 短剧分开看。抖音的内容是普通用户拍的，短而散，算法负责把内容送到你面前；AI 短剧是一个懂行的编剧加 AI 拍出来的，一季上百集，往一个行业越挖越深，AI 用在把内容做出来。

程苓峰预计下一步 AI 两头都管：内容生成得比人看得快，每个人看到的剧情都不一样，广告直接编进情节。

到那时会分成两条路：
1. 免费的娱乐加广告，普通观众毫无招架之力，程苓峰称之为“肉鸡”；
2. 收费的教育，因材施教，逼人往上走。

【两人的分歧】

秦朔认为监管和金币下线会让红果从狂奔回到常规，短剧也不会杀死长内容，就像方便面没有取代正餐。程苓峰认为这才是“核爆当夜”，引用朋友的话说“字节没有上限”。

两人都担心沉迷。秦朔担心的是人的注意力和耐心被算法重塑；程苓峰担心的是社会更加 K 型，少数人借 AI 往上走，多数人被娱乐吞掉。

【数字靠不靠得住】

字节系、腾讯系的时长份额有出处，来自野村报告援引的 QuestMobile 数据，7 月是 40.9% 对 29.1%（秦朔引用），8 月是 41.8% 对 28.6%（程苓峰引用），统计范围只有前 50 个 App。

红果“第四大 App”“人均 125 分钟”出自同一份第三方报告，红果官方没有确认。

“前 8 个月 43 万部、AI 剧超九成”是广电总局网络视听司司长王小亮在国新办发布会上公布的。

程苓峰文中“红果今年收入 400 亿”，红果 10 月 27 日晚已声明不实，并称网传的机构数据和专家预计都不是官方信息。

拿来对比的“电影总票房 520 亿”是 2025 年全年数字，国家电影局公布为 518.32 亿元。

text:
$GOOGL  presentó el balance más contradictorio del año: un negocio que duplica sus ingresos y una caja que ya no alcanza.

✅Lo que salió bien: 

📌Ingresos de US$127.600M, +25%. Pichai dice que ya facturan a un ritmo de medio billón por año. Google Cloud facturó US$30.700M, +103%, contra US$29.600M esperados y 82% el trimestre pasado. 
📌El resultado operativo de Cloud se triplicó, a US$11.100M, con un margen de 36%. Hoy aporta más de un cuarto de la ganancia operativa de Alphabet. Gemini superó los 1.000 millones de usuarios mensuales. 
📌El margen de Google Services subió de 38,5% a 40,7%.

☑️ La letra chica: 
📌La publicidad creció 11%, contra 13% esperado. Búsqueda +12%, contra 17% el trimestre pasado. YouTube +9%. 
📌El EPS fue de US$2,12, -26%, por una pérdida de US$8.700M en participaciones. Sumando esa pérdida, igual quedaría en unos US$2,67, contra ~US$3,00 esperados. 
📌El Capex fue de US$51.400M, +114%, y el flujo libre, -US$9.100M. Son los dos primeros trimestres negativos desde su salida a bolsa. Para cubrirlo, emitió US$28.700M en bonos y vendió US$12.400M en acciones nuevas. 
📌Cero recompras, contra US$11.500M hace un año. La deuda de largo plazo pasó de US$46.500M en diciembre a US$125.100M.

Mi lectura: El mercado castiga en el after y tiene lógica. Durante años, Alphabet fue una de las máquinas de recomprar acciones más grandes del mundo. Hoy emite acciones y deuda para financiar centros de datos. Cloud es la prueba de que esa inversión tiene demanda real y rentabilidad creciente. Pero el accionista pasó de ser recomprado a ser diluido, y la publicidad, que paga todo, empieza a crecer menos. La apuesta es que Cloud justifique el gasto antes de que la búsqueda se desacelere más.

text:
✨️Did you know this rare Umbreon card actually came from a box of chocolates? 🍫✨
​
 Meet the Japanese Meiji Promo "Get Card", released exclusively in Japan during the Pokémon Advanced Generation era in the early 2000s. These where only available inside promotional packs of Meiji chocolates. 

 The name "BLACKY" across the front was Umbreon’s original Japanese name (Burakkī) before being changed internationally to sound more "mysterious". They even doubled as an interactive playground game, complete with a fist icon in the bottom corner so kids could use them to play rock-paper-scissors! 
​
 Because these cards were packaged with chocolate, most were tossed out or damaged. Making high-quality survivors exceptionally rare today. Finding a raw, ungraded copy in good condition can easily command $150 to $300 USD, while high-grade professionally graded copies fetch a massive premium—with a legendary population of only 9 PSA 10s in existence worldwide!

Spotted at a local card show 🤩

text:
云业务翻倍，为何谷歌财报后却大跌近10%？

Q1—Q3 资本开支分别为 356.74、449.24、513.55 亿美元，同比均翻倍以上。

Q3 Capex 实际比华尔街预期低约 7%，所以股价下跌不能简单归因于“本季花钱太多”。

真正的问题是 Q3 自由现金流为 -90.65 亿美元，远弱于约 -23 亿美元的预期。

全年 Capex 指引维持 1950—2050 亿美元，2027 年还将显著增加，说明现金流压力不是单季现象。

一句话：“核心广告低于预期＋EPS 大幅 miss＋FCF 远低于预期＋AI 高投入持续更久。”

Cloud 很强，但还不足以抵消现金牛业务的预期差。

财报前市场预期又高度乐观，因此，在市场大盘整体情绪低迷的情况下，“总收入接近预期、云大幅超预期”依然不够。

中国社区逆向拆解了Claude的封号机制。以下是他们的发现

Claude使用积分制。注册时账号获得初始分数，之后根据行为加分或扣分。低于阈值直接封号。回分很难

影响分数的因素:

注册
> 干净IP是最重要的因素。不一定要家宽，但必须干净
> Gmail已经不是最优选，有权重更高的邮箱服务
> 注册时直接弹KYC的号可以扔了
> 用手机App注册会加分

支付
> 刚注册就订阅会扣分
> 直接上Max会大幅扣分。最好等两天先订Pro
> 支付时弹KYC说明账号在考察期，但不一定会封
> 国外实体银行卡加分。Google Play也行。虚拟卡扣分

使用
> 不要一次把限额用完。宁可两个号轮换也不要一个号撸到底
> Desktop客户端有少量加分。尽量少用网页端
> 手机端也有少量加分
> 开启记忆功能加分。记忆文件越多分越高

IP和设备
> 稳定性是关键。不要跳IP，尽量一直用同一个
> 代理必须全局模式并开启TUN
> 多设备登录大幅扣分。理想状态是一台电脑一个客户端
> 频繁换IP、频繁登录、高并发都会大幅扣分

账号年龄
> 老号有巨大的容错空间。2023年的号明显更高
> 分数随时间增长，但很慢

其他
> Windows和macOS没区别。Linux会扣分
> 时区和语言基本不影响。不会因为北京时间就封号
> 跟Claude说自己是中国人没问题，记忆不会触发封号
> 大量使用Fable会扣分
> 升级Max大概率进入观察期，除非是高权重老号

观察期和封号
> 接近阈值时账号可能进入观察期。典型特征是掉登录
> 观察期继续扣分就会封号
> 高分号可以扛过多次观察期

text:
ChatGPT Pro 和 Business 订阅即日起每月送最高 500 美元 API 额度，不另收费，Plus 没有

OpenAI 10 月 28 日宣布，付费的 ChatGPT Pro 和 Business 订阅用户，每月可以免费领一笔 API 额度，最多 500 美元。API 是给开发者用的接口，按用量付费，自己写的 App、网站、自动化脚本要调用 OpenAI 的模型，走的就是这条路。以前订阅 ChatGPT 和用 API 是两本账，交了订阅费，写程序照样另外充钱。现在这笔额度算在订阅里，不用额外付费。

【谁能领、领多少】

Pro 按档位给，每月 100、200 或 500 美元。据 CellCog 的说法，额度正好等于各档月费，相当于订阅费原样变成 API 额度。Business 按付费席位算：标准席位每个 20 美元，高级席位每个 100 美元，整个工作区合在一起用，上限 500 美元，也就是 25 个标准席位或 5 个高级席位就封顶，再加人也不涨。

Plus、Go、免费版和 Enterprise 都没有。据 CellCog 转述 OpenAI 帮助页，订阅还要满 7 天，免费试用和赠送的订阅不算。地区限制官方推文没提，两家媒体也没写。

【怎么领】

在 ChatGPT 的“设置 → 账单”里领取，绑定一个你自己名下的 API 组织（OpenAI 开发者平台上的账户），ChatGPT 账号和 API 账号要用同一个邮箱。Business 由工作区管理员在账单设置或管理后台领。领完后，在 ChatGPT 或 Codex 里用 OpenAI Developers 插件就能生成 API key、建项目，不用先绑信用卡。

【能干什么，有什么限制】

这笔钱可以花在 OpenAI 开发者平台的大部分服务上：调模型做对话和智能体、实时语音、生成图片，以及联网搜索、代码解释器这些内置工具。比如给自己做个小工具，或者给团队搭个内部问答机器人。

几条限制要注意，以下均据 CellCog 转述的 OpenAI 帮助页：额度当月有效，账单周期结束清零，不能攒到下个月，第一个月按剩余天数折算；用 API key 跑 Codex 不能花这笔钱；它也不会提高你在 ChatGPT 和 Codex 里的使用上限，两边额度各算各的。花钱顺序是先用赠送的，再用自己充的；两笔都花完，请求会直接报错，除非开了自动充值。

说明：OpenAI 帮助中心原文（https://t.co/TmmayxRUMq）这次没能直接打开，推文之外的细则来自 AlphaSignal 和 CellCog 对帮助页的转述。两家都写到的部分（Plus 和 Enterprise 不能领、额度不累积、Codex 不能用）说法一致；满 7 天、同一邮箱这些细节只有 CellCog 写了。

text:
While I do agree with @eastdakota that tokenized money is probably the best surface for agents to interact, it doesn't answer the question of what the business model is going to be.

With several projects busy in building liquidity primitive, money movement rails, yield primitives, programmability primitives, it is not clear how agents will combine those and where margin will accrue. 

We are moving from a monolithic, black-box-like approach to maturity transformation and risk management (i.e. the universal banks) to one where value is composed and decomposed real time. This is not necessarily a good thing, since time mismatch has historically been a great absorber of statistical risk. Banks are able to do maturity transformation because on average they can predict liquidity behavior, banks can lend because on average they can predict repayments. If omniscient herds are moving value in a continuous and coordinated way, the statistical buffer component breaks. Real-time is not always better for humans.

With the confluence of open financial system, and non-human financial actors, we might see the death of the money primitive as we know it. And we might have not realized it yet. It is not only how we will adapt to it, but actually what type of value creation strategy will emerge from it.

It is indeed so crazy.

quoted_text:
Should you buy a 512GB Mac Studio for Local AI? I ran the numbers before ordering one.

1) On token price alone, renting wins. At DeepSeek V4.1 Flash API rates, the Mac needs years of 24/7 output to pay for itself.

2) Price per token is the wrong way to judge it, though. In expensive housing markets, renting is cheaper month to month than owning, and people still buy for control and because a home holds value. The same logic applies to this machine.

3) It holds value. The 512GB M3 Ultra now resells for about twice what it cost new, because memory got scarce. If mine resells for even half, the real cost halves.

4) Nobody can take it away. API models get swapped, rate limited and refused mid-task. In June, access to two frontier models was cut off for almost three weeks. Weights on my desk stay put.

5) Zero-cost tokens change what you build. When every call costs nothing, agents can run all day and you can experiment freely. MacStories ran local agents 24/7 for 99 days at zero token cost.

6) It runs the big ones. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (552B) and GLM-5.3 (744B) don’t fit in 256GB. In 512GB, each loads into one memory pool.

So if you’d use it a few hours a week, rent. If you’d run it all day the moment it was free, buy.

Go Local AI!

text:
A man left Twitter to build a crypto wallet with no token of its own, and somehow turned it into a $3 BILLION company.

> Brandon Millman worked as a senior engineer at Twitter from 2013 to 2017.

> He moved into crypto and joined 0x, a project building infrastructure for decentralised trading on Ethereum.

> After spending years working on crypto infrastructure, he teamed up with Francesco Agosti and Chris Kalani to build something of their own.

> They wanted to make using crypto simpler.

> In 2021, the three started building Phantom, a wallet that initially focused on Solana.

> At the time, Solana was still growing, and Phantom was betting that more people would need a simple way to interact with its ecosystem.

> By July 2021, Phantom had raised $9 MILLION from investors led by Andreessen Horowitz.

> Then its user base started taking off.

> By September 2021, Phantom was adding around 100,000 users a week with just six developers and a couple of contractors.

> In January 2022, it raised $109 MILLION at a $1.2 BILLION valuation.

> Three years later, it raised another $150 MILLION at a $3 BILLION valuation.

> And it did all this without launching its own token.

> Today, Phantom is one of crypto's most widely used wallets, giving millions of people access to digital assets and blockchain applications.

Brandon left Twitter and bet on an emerging ecosystem to build a multibillion-dollar company.

Imagine if he'd just stayed at Twitter.

text:
谷歌财报出来，越看越有意思。

表面看全是好消息：云收入 307 亿，一年翻了倍，涨 103%；搜索查询增速是五年来最猛的；营收 1275.8 亿，同比 + 25%，跟预期就差一口气。

可股价偏偏往下砸。原因就一行字 —— 过去 12 个月自由现金流只剩 197.5 亿，同比掉了 73%。

谷歌财报重点看三样：云还能不能猛、AI 有没有动搜索的基本盘、那笔 806 亿的 capex 烧完账上还剩几个钱。结果前两样全给了惊喜，最后一样给了暴雷。生意越做越大，现金越烧越少，等于用本金换增长。更早就露马脚的是 CDS—— 财报前谷歌微软的信用违约互换双双冲到历史新高，债主子先扛不住跑了。

所以谷歌的刀，最好不要接。这种现金流的窟窿，一个季度填不上。但话说回来，它亏着钱疯狂建数据中心，钱最后不都流去了电力、制冷和存储？ Vertiv、MU，MRVL 反而该攥紧。

谷歌这张财报就是 AI 查账季的主裁判。如今哨声响了：业绩是优等生，现金却是不及格。这不是 AI 讲不下去了，是市场开始追着问到底哪天回本。巨头烧得越凶，这些卖铲子的，日子越好过。

text:
“我们理智上已经接受这件事正在发生，但情感上还没有真正感受到。”

奥特曼说的"这件事"，是AI已经从聊天机器人，走到了亲手设计芯片、发现新科学。

OpenAI CEO萨姆·奥特曼，2026年10月27日在拉斯维加斯甲骨文AI World大会上，与甲骨文（Oracle）联席CEO克莱·马古约克同台对话。马古约克开场就说："一年前我们不可能有这场对话，技术不存在，体验也不存在。"一个是最大的模型公司，一个是最老牌的企业软件巨头，两人谈的不是概念，而是正在发生的事：GPT-6、AI写代码、人人造应用、AI安全，以及AI设计芯片。

01｜从小学算术到最难的数学
 "我们四年前推出GPT时，模型连小学算术都做不好；现在它们已经在攻一些我们所知最难的、尚未被证明的数学问题。"更让他意外的是速度："最近六个月，即使放在这样的时间线里，也像是加速版。"
 加速度本身，正在加速。

02｜GPT-6：采用率最高的一代
 "GPT-6是一个一次性向前跨步的时刻。"一方面，"它发现新知识、做非常困难事情的能力提升了"；另一方面，人与模型协作完成实质性工作的能力大幅提升。"GPT-6是我们迄今为止采用率最高的新模型。"
 模型的竞争，最终要看有多少人真的在用它干活。

03｜甲骨文七成代码由AI编写
 马古约克透露，甲骨文把ChatGPT桌面版推给了所有员工，"现在超过70%的代码由AI编写，而且还在加速"。他还看到，"很多几年前根本不认为自己是开发者的人，现在在创造全新的应用"。
 一家老牌软件巨头带头让AI写代码，信号比任何发布会都强。

04｜不叫编程的编程
 奥特曼说，企业全员推广AI后，"很多原本不认为自己在‘写软件’的人，会非常快地传播这种能力"。"他们可能不会把这叫编程，但需要某个东西时，他们会直接做一个应用来完成它。"
 编程正在从一种职业，变成一种日常动作。

05｜生产力翻倍，琐事减少
 他转述了一个流行说法："到2026年底，我的生产力会是2025年初的两倍；我更喜欢自己的工作，因为我少做了很多琐事。"他的判断是："我认为这部分正在发生。" AI最先改变的，可能不是收入，而是对工作的感受。

06｜在电脑里管理一座工厂
 "我现在坐在电脑前使用最新工具的主观体验，像是在管理电脑里的一个工厂。""我可以相当连续地从一个想法移动到另一个想法，不被阻塞。"
 未来的工作，是指挥，而不是操作。

07｜启动成本消失之后
 "即使某件事我只有模糊感觉、不太确定怎么做，过去我可能因为启动成本太高而放弃；现在我愿意探索这些不太可能、但有时回报很大的创意方向。"他说，"人成为背后的创意力量"，"我见过30岁的人从零搭建完整网站来实现目标"。
 当试错几乎免费，冒险就成了理性选择。

08｜头号建议：先搞懂安全
 "如果现在只给公司推荐一件与AI有关的事，甚至比‘用AI大幅提升编码生产力’更优先，那就是真正理解AI带来的安全威胁格局，并缓解它。"他也承认，这话"听起来有点烦人，像是‘你们制造问题，又让我们解决’"。
 OpenAI的CEO把安全排在效率之前，这句话值得每个CIO记下。

09｜AI不是漏洞的制造者
 "AI不是这些bug的制造者，它在帮我们发现过去50年积累下来的安全问题。""唯一出路是把这些问题全部找出来并修复。"他坦言："我震惊于这些AI系统发现的漏洞数量之多，以及要领先于威胁需要付出多么巨大的努力。"
 50年的技术债，正在被AI一次性翻出来。

10｜AI开始造芯片
 "AI非常擅长芯片设计。"OpenAI的芯片Jalapeno正在甲骨文云上部署，"我认为它是世界上最好的推理AI芯片，速度快到没有AI参与大量工作就无法想象"。他总结这几年的路径："从聊天机器人走到编码代理，再走到直接把AI算力转化为创新。"
 AI开始设计运行AI的芯片，这个循环才是真正的拐点。

这场对话最打动人的，是奥特曼那句坦白：理智上接受了，情感上还没感受到。七成代码由AI编写，非程序员在造应用，AI在找50年的漏洞、在设计芯片。变化已经写进了企业的日常数据里，只是大多数人的感受，还停留在"聊天机器人"阶段。

理智上，你相信AI正在改变一切；情感上，你真正感受到了吗？

Palmer Luckey says analysts claiming it's too expensive to manufacture in the US are lying to protect megacorps

"I think I have a more realistic view than almost anybody. One of the problems with all these analysts that are telling you that it's going to cost $37,000 to build an American iPhone or $100,000 to buy an American computer."

"The only difference between an Anduril attack drone and a laptop is a keyboard and a screen. That is not that hard to figure out, especially for a guy like me who started Oculus and comes from the consumer electronics space." 

"We're not going to let people lie about what America can and can't do anymore. We're just going to do it."

text:
Can a small model get better at a hard reasoning benchmark without touching its weights?
Recursive Self-Improvement for ARC-AGI-3: Hill-Climbing to 78.95 RHAE with Haiku 5.5 and ASSAY

The loop:
I wrapped a human-in-the-loop RSI loop around ASSAY (my open-source reasoning harness) and ran it on the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games with Haiku 5.5. Assay also introduces 5 levels of abstraction for reasoning and has equivalent plugs for each layer. This design was used to guide the analyst model in this experiment to recommend fixes at the layer where the reasoning broke, and the harness runs again. 

After two rounds:
Won games stay pinned to the version that won them. The final record is 17/25 at **78.95**.
at medium effort, Haiku went from 5/25 (37.18) under plain Claude Code to 12/25 (60.24) after only two rounds of reviews: 7 wins gained, none lost, p = 0.016

The most interesting part was why Haiku failed. Its model of the game fit every transition it tested and was wrong in regimes it never tested. The harness's meters couldn't see that error. Fix 1 moved the stop later; fix 2 removed the exits fix 1 had opened!

Paper: https://t.co/KSTde5HpTg
ASSAY: https://t.co/YH7ao1wXcR

居然还有金融机构，接受用声纹来验证身份、批准大额转账。“AI 已经彻底攻破了这一招。”Sam Altman 说。

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 在去年美联储的银行资本监管会议上，和美联储副主席 Michelle Bowman 对谈 ⬇️

1️⃣ 声纹验证已经失守：说一句验证口令就能转一大笔钱，“到现在还这么做，简直疯了”。除了密码，自拍挥手、录声音这些花哨的验证方式，AI 基本都攻破了。

2️⃣ 诈骗危机就在眼前：他“非常担心”一场严重的诈骗危机即将到来。OpenAI 不发布这项技术，“不代表它不存在”，总会有坏人把它放出来，“这事并不难做”。

3️⃣ 亲人的声音也能假冒：已经有报道说，骗子用你孩子或父母的声音打来紧急电话勒索，而且会“越来越逼真”。

4️⃣ 很快就是视频：现在是语音电话，很快就会是视频通话，“和真人根本分不出来”。每个人都得改变核实对方身份的方式。

🔺 这是去年的访谈，今年大多已经应验了。声音和脸都能造假之后，最可靠的反而或许是最笨的办法：挂掉电话，用自己存的号码打回去，或者家里人提前约好一句只有彼此知道的暗号。😂

怎么说呢，还是呼吁那些造假之人，回归善良本心才是正道。

text:
We just crossed $1M in annualized revenue run rate in just 6 days after launch.

And we're just a team of 2 people.

Our idea started out really simple: ai video platforms are doing billions, but they don't have a strong moat. why don't we just steal their users?

Seems like it worked.

--

I genuinely believe that the only moat in AI applications is acquiring users with velocity, then making them stay by getting deeply embedded in their daily workflows.

Our plan is simple. Keep stealing users from ai video platforms' $nB+ pie in every area with no moat, ship new features every week, and find the ones that get deeply rooted in marketers' everyday work.

Sure, you can ask how we're gonna make our users stay. But honestly, worst case we still hit $100M ARR, and if we're crushed by competitors, my cofounder and I will go back to a shitty couch, build again with no salary, and make millions again. Not worried about that either.

We just focus on growth & net revenue retention.

In an era of thin moats, we don't need fake storytelling like "Agentic creative OS". We should build something people want :

"A product that's cheaper than higgsfield, better than higgsfield"

沃什宣布减少议息频次！

2028年，美联储一年仍然开8次会，但只有6次真正投票决定利率，另外2次专门讨论长期货币政策战略，不投票，也不发布利率决议。

2027年秋季开始实施，第一年先安排1次这样的会议。

昨晚美联储维持利率不变，目标区间仍为3.75%–4%，符合市场预期。

1. 通胀仍是头号敌人。 

沃什表示，通胀已经连续近六年高于2%的目标，降通胀是美联储的责任。如果后续数据不支持通胀回落，继续加息仍然是选项。

2. 12月加不加息，现在不给答案。 

沃什拒绝对下一步利率路径作出承诺，强调需要更多经济数据。此次按兵不动，不代表美联储已经结束加息周期。

3. 经济强劲，但多数官员认为还没过热。 

沃什提到经济增长和企业投资表现强劲，就业市场也保持韧性。美联储需要继续压制通胀，同时避免过度紧缩拖累经济。

本次决议以10比2通过，Cook和Hammack两名官员主张加息。美联储虽然暂停了行动，但内部对通胀风险的判断并不完全一致。
