text:
Strap in and consider this my official update on the kinetiq:native thesis, specifically regarding @Enter_Elysium.

Best way to do this is to refute some arguments I've seen:

1. "L2's are parasitic"

It's very lazy to compare Elysium to other L2s from the past. Robinhood Chain has generated a little over $50m in fees, of which $5m went to Arbitrum, and a whopping...$70k went to $ETH blob fees.

HyperEVM hyperliquid:native fees are burnt, whereas sequencer fees on Elysium go to kinetiq:native buys and builders (more on this later), but HyperEVM fees only account less than 1% of Hyperliquid total revenue. Papertrade is actually much more directly parasitic to hyperliquid:native; HyperEVM fees are peanuts even if Elysium vamped them entirely.

An under appreciated dynamic that a lot of people don't know is that HyperEVM USDC applies to AQAv2 hyperliquid:native revenue too, and USDC on Elysium will as well. Assuming the HyperEVM burns around $25k of hyperliquid:native a day, every additional $1b USDC that Elysium onboards in TVL would burn 4x that same amount due to AQAv2. 

For reference, Solana has ~$7.5bn USDC and Base has $5b. Robinhood chain is predominantly USDG, which they monetize on, and ETH obviously gets nothing from. Imagine if Base contributed to $175m (3.5% of $5b) of value accrual to $ETH via their USDC TVL...maybe my $5k/7k $ETH calls would actually hit then 🙃

Beyond this, the entire selling point of Elysium is that it sits adjacent to HyperCore. propAMM's are functionally impossible on HyperEVM now due to the 1s block time (amongst other reasons). Additionally, on the HyperEVM, you can only read Hypercore price, not order book depth. 

As a result, Solana does 25-50x the spot trading volume that Hypercore/HyperEVM handle. If Elysium can eat even a moderate chunk of on chain spot volume from Solana, especially in tokenized RWAs, the implications for corresponding hedging flows to Hyperliquid are enormous. 

Elysium explicity enables net new flow and TVL to Hyperliquid, both of which are very accretive to hyperliquid:native itself. I would not be surprised if Elysium directly contributes an additional low 9 figure ARR for hyperliquid:native in 2027. 

2. "L2's are bad investments and down only tokens"

As stated above, $ARB made about $5m so far from Robinhood Chain. Of that amount, a whopping...zero dollars made it to tokenholders. No buybacks, no burns, nothing.

50% of Elysium sequencer fees are directed at kinetiq:native buybacks. Even if you assume that Elysium only generates half the current sequencer fees of the current ghost town that is the HyperEVM, that'd still more than double their current revenue. 

Currently, kinetiq:native buybacks as a % of market cap are about 1.5%, compared to 4-5% for hyperliquid:native. If Elysium generates only half of the sequencer fees of the current HyperEVM ($5m/yr), they'd be retiring token off the market at the same rate that hyperliquid:native does relative to market cap.

If Elysium can do closer to 50-75% of Base annualized sequencer fees ($30m), they'd be doing kinetiq:native buybacks at double the rate of hyperliquid:native as a % of market cap.

This is completely negating a likely increase in kHYPE TVL and other revenue streams (which there are numerous), like from launchpads like @AscendLaunch.

Ascend actually deserves their own section because they've commited to doing 30% of gross revenue as kinetiq:native buy/burns (50% to buys, 60% of that to burn). $PONS has generated $200m revenue in the last 2 months, but is currently only annualizing about $125m revenue, so we'll use a very conservative ~10% of the more conservative number. That'd add another $4m of kinetiq:native buybacks, which brings buyback yield/mcap well into the double digit %, over double hyperliquid:native.

3. "Why would there be activity on Elysium if there wasn't on the HyperEVM?"

Probably because the HyperEVM operates at the speed of smoke signals and has 0 support from Hyperliquid. 

You have @Uniswap, @fomo, @Pumpfun etc all announcing integrations and deployments on Elysium day 1 after ignoring the HyperEVM all this time. @0xOmnia and the @Kinetiq_xyz team is putting on a master class in distribution, and you're seeing it play out this week. 

Jeff and company are focusing on building the best perps platform in the world, and that's great, but this hands off approach has come at the expense of any support or curation of an on chain ecosystem. 

That's left a massive gap that other chains have filled, but Elysium can bring all that activity back into the "house of all finance". Having a team that's fully dedicated to making this a reality will look nothing like the lack of attention the HyperEVM received.

4. "It'll be a flash in the pan memecoin chain and die out just like RHC activity has"

This is more speculative and it's hard to say. Elysium could have an epic and unsustainable PvElysium memecoin season by inheriting some of the wealth effect from both hyperliquid:native and kinetiq:native. Obviously this would absolutely moon kinetiq:native from sequencer fees/Ascend revenue, but that's shortlived.

Lively trenches aren't mutually exclusive with a real and innovative DeFi ecosystem though. As I mentioned before, Elysium will be uniquely able to plug in with, leverage, and read Hyperliquid orderbooks and liquidity. DeFi applications that couldn't be built anywhere else are made possible here. 

A performant general purpose blockchain adjacent to HyperCore is the natural home to propAMM and HFT arbitrage against HIP3, which incentivizes deeply liquid spot RWA markets, which enables much higher LTV lending, which enables unique structured products and DeFi primitives to be built.

I do imagine that the trenches are built before more serious innovation comes about, but an important note here is that builders are getting 25% of sequencer fees as well. What builder wouldn't want to deploy on a new ecosystem, adjacent to the most successful app in crypto history, with a built in rev share agreement with the chain itself? Based on my conversations with Ascend and Montra, lots of serious teams want to build, not just memecoin deployers.

TLDR: It's not that complicated guys. kinetiq:native is a $120m mcap token that has a very clear path to buyback % yields multiples higher than hyperliquid:native, with an unprecedented ecosystem flywheel. It's both beta to hyperliquid:native and enhances the hyperliquid:native bull case. It might be the most asymmetric bet in crypto right now, and it's not conditional on some long shot thesis, just that there will be a large on chain ecosystem for the most important app in crypto. 

Maybe it's a flop and a sell the news event on launch...or maybe it's all the best parts of Base/Hood sequencer fees combined with the revenue streams of $PUMP, $CAKE, solana:jtojtomepa8beP8AuQc6eXt5FriJwfFMwQx2v2f9mCL, ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 etc and heads towards billions of TVL and 9 figure annual revenue.

If you pattern match too hard to "L2 bad" or "HyperEVM sucks", it's from a place of being too 🏳️‍🌈🐻-pilled and/or lazy research.

author: nic_carter
quoted_text:
As someone who has personally spent $500k / mo+ on Google Ads for years, I can tell you with certainty: 

This revenue growth in Search is artificial & extremely unhealthy for Google’s business long term

Search volumes are declining as legacy search is being increasingly cannibalized by non-monetized LLM queries

Google’s response? 

Manufacture revenue growth via short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics. I.e. charge advertisers more for lower quality clicks, including clicks they do not want and explicitly did not approve Google to charge them for

A few examples to illustrate: 

For all of its history until recently, Google operated on a 2nd price auction model

I.e. if you bid $5 CPC and the next highest bidder bids $1 CPC, Google charged you $1.01 for the click (one penny more than the 2nd highest bidder) rather than the $5 you bid

This was a genius move by Google early on as it incentivizes advertisers to input their true maximum willingness to pay rather than trying to play the game of bidding low and constantly adjusting to try to stay just ahead of the next highest bidder while still not paying too much

However recently, Google silently deprecated the 2nd price auction and began charging advertisers as much as their bid and budget caps allow, regardless of what anyone else is bidding

It’s a short-sighted cash grab at the expense of the long term health of the  advertiser ecosystem

Making thing worse, Google also recently nerfed keyword targeting precision

Google previously had precise keyword targeting settings that allowed advertisers pick individual search phrases to bid on, defined down to the character w/ exact match or phrase match targeting 

This was one of the core features that made search advertising magic, enabling advertisers to run extremely precise campaigns based on exactly what their target customer typed 

But now, even if you bid on a specific term or phrase using the strictest exact 
-match targeting settings, Google will show your ad across 1000’s of unrelated keywords, labeling them as as “exact match (close variant)” 

The definition of “close variant” means whatever they want it to and changes constantly. The result is advertisers get billed for clicks that are totally irrelevant to their business and that their targeting settings explicitly forbid Google from targeting. Google does it anyway and there’s no ability to turn this off

So now exact match is broad match, and broad match is just meaningless spam

This is all very bad for advertisers, but for Google, it allows them to show your ad and bill you for clicks across 1000x more searches that were previously going unmonetized (mainly because they’re garbage queries no one wants) 

This is how you grow revenue atop declining search volumes 

Lastly, and perhaps most egregiously, Google quietly stopped respecting budget caps by a factor of 2x. For example campaigns we’ve been running for years with $1000 daily budget caps suddenly began spending $2000+ per day 

And the extra spend is entirely on the garbage keywords Google arbitrarily throws in as “exact match (close variants)” which have no value to our business, but can’t be turned off

Google offers no refunds nor any recourse for overspend or spend on keywords you explicitly did not target

These are not the actions of a healthy business. These are the actions of company whose core business is in decline but desperately needs to pump quarterly earnings so Wall Street will continue to fund insane capex while hopefully looking through their rapidly deteriorating negative free cash flow 

Google operated a benevolent monopoly for the better part of 25 yrs

Meaning the value Google captured from Search was but a small fraction of the value it created, and that spread produced a potential energy that justified expectations of high earnings growth far, far into the future 

This is now no longer the case

At the alter of AI capex, Google is sacrificing the golden goose

20 岁加国少年盗币 1300 万美元炫耀后仅获刑 7 个月

20 岁的加拿大人 Trenton Johnston 近日被美国迈阿密联邦法院判处"以羁押期抵扣刑期"，实际只关了约 7 个月。他承认共谋洗钱，电信欺诈的指控则在认罪协议中被撤销。

Johnston 从 17 岁开始作案，冒充谷歌、Trezor 等公司的客服，以"账户被盗"为由骗取受害者的钱包访问码。

今年 3 月，他和同伙骗走一名加州受害者的 185 枚 BTC，当时约值 1300 万美元，是对方的全部积蓄。得手后，他向同伙炫耀"今天搞定一个 185 BTC 的目标"，还在 Discord 上共享屏幕演示作案手法。

赃款被他用来买兰博基尼、宝马和珠宝，租私人飞机，在迈阿密夜店挥霍，同月，他坐在一辆劳斯莱斯 库里南 里被警方截停并逮捕。

他目前已交出约 380 万美元的加密货币，后续将被遣返加拿大。认罪协议原本建议判 51 至 63 个月，法官考虑到他协助调查其他案件，最终从轻判决。

text:
Apollo CEO Marc Rowan explains how Jon Gray and Ken Griffin can both be right about AI

“They can both be true. We are seeing unbelievable demand for compute, particularly in a supply constrained market in the short term. And to the extent we get regulation and we have anti-data center sentiment, those people who hold existing powered assets are going to see their assets go up in value because what they’re able to provide is something that’s in short supply. Jon can be right, and I think Jon is right on that, at least for the foreseeable future.”

“At the same time, I think Ken can be right. The valuation at which someone is willing to pay reflects their bet, not only of what’s happening currently, but that this will continue in the future. We now have a Treasury which was hovering around 5%. We have interest rates, the cost of capital going way up. And yet we have not seen what we historically see, which is equity market correction following increases in cost of capital. And on that side, I think Ken is stating the obvious. We have not seen the normal economic behavior associated with this.”
author: firesidealpha
quoted_text:
Chamath explains how VC funding circularity is giving AI the diffusion problem Ken Griffin is picking up on

“So the cycle here, just to be very precise, is VCs raised from pension funds and LPs and foundations and family offices. They put money into a startup. That startup takes that money and invests in growth. Part of growing is by consuming other people’s AIs. And so that company then starts to show revenue traction. Those folks then say, hey, look how well we’re doing, raises a bunch of money from the same VCs. And it’s just this circularity.”

“Why that’s important is what Ken is pointing out is that for AI to really scale as a predictable driver of long term earnings, it has to diffuse out of the startup ecosystem. And so you can’t be in a situation where on the one hand, you’re talking about breathtaking valuations. But we’re 75 cents of every dollar is actually just a startup sending it back and forth so that they can mark themselves up. That’s, I think, a structural problem.”

“But the difference there is that AWS was abstracted from Amazon retail, which was already then a roughly breakeven profitable business, at least on a free cash flow basis. So what’s different here is you have a bunch of money losing entities just spinning a bunch of money around and it has to diffuse more broadly.”

“They said, we have decreased our spend on AWS and GCP. We now have six completely independent ground up data centers that we’ve built from scratch for ourselves. And I was like, what is going on here?”

“AI has a diffusion problem. It is too concentrated and ripping around in a small little ecosystem. We need to diffuse out. But as it diffuses out, people are picking open source is what I would tell you.”

text:
Need a Criminal Record / Police Certificate from Italy?

Has a prospective employer, immigration authority, or another institution asked you to provide an Italian Police Certificate or Criminal Record Certificate, but you're not sure what document they actually mean or how to obtain it?

In most cases, they are referring to the Italian Certificato del Casellario Giudiziale (Criminal Record / Police Certificate).

This official certificate is issued by the Procura della Repubblica (Public Prosecutor's Office) and shows whether a person has any final criminal convictions recorded in Italy.

It is commonly requested for:

✅ Employment abroad (for example, in the UK, France, and many other countries)

✅ Immigration and visa applications (for example, Spain, Luxembourg, and other jurisdictions)

✅ Citizenship or residency procedures (for example, Greece and others)

⚠️ One important thing to know:

Some foreign authorities, especially for immigration purposes, generically refer to "Police Certificates" when they are actually referring to more than one document, not just the Casellario Giudiziale.

For example, some immigration authorities (such as those in New Zealand and Australia) require both:

• Criminal Record Certificate (Casellario Giudiziale)

• Certificate of Pending Charges (Carichi Pendenti)

The U.S. immigration authorities require a third document as well, called the Visura del Casellario Giudiziale.

I'll explain the differences between these certificates in a future post.

📄 Here you can see a Criminal Record Certificate (Casellario Giudiziale) we obtained for a client, so you can get an idea of what it looks like.

text:
🚨 BLACK OCTOBER: HACKERS PARALYZE MAJOR U.S. HOSPITAL NETWORK

A massive cybersecurity attack on the University of New Mexico Health System forced hospitals to divert ambulances, cancel surgeries, shut down appointments across 30+ clinics, and temporarily leave an entire state without access to its ONLY Level 1 trauma center.

Here’s what happened:

At approximately 11:30 AM on Monday, October 26, employees across the hospital network began experiencing a bizarre cyberattack.

According to reports, computers were suddenly taken over, broadcasting messages warning employees:

“You have been compromised.”

The attackers claimed to have stolen highly sensitive information, including:

• Student and employee personal data
• Social Security numbers
• Confidential patient information
• Private documents
• Email accounts and other sensitive records

These claims of stolen data have NOT been independently confirmed.

According to KRQE, internal communications instructed employees to immediately SHUT DOWN and UNPLUG their computers.

Staff were reportedly forced to revert to PAPER-BASED processes.

The disruption quickly escalated into a healthcare emergency.

🚑 All ambulance traffic was diverted to other hospitals for approximately two hours.

🏥 Outpatient surgeries and appointments across more than 30 clinics were canceled.

🚨 Patients were instructed NOT to come to UNM Health facilities.

🎓 Medical, nursing, pharmacy and other health sciences classes were canceled.

And here’s the most concerning part:

The University of New Mexico Health System handles approximately 900,000 outpatient visits and 100,000 emergency room visits EVERY YEAR.

It also operates New Mexico’s ONLY Level 1 trauma center, the facility responsible for treating the state’s most critically injured patients.

For a period of time, the entire state was left without its highest-level emergency trauma facility operating normally.

Think about that.

A cyberattack on computer systems was enough to disrupt critical medical services relied upon by millions of people.

The FBI became involved, and the incident remains under criminal investigation.

UPDATE (October 28):

UNM reports that hospitals and clinics have resumed normal operations. Officials say some end-user devices were affected, but the attackers did not penetrate core systems or servers.

The alleged theft of sensitive personal information has not been confirmed.

This is an enormous wake-up call about the vulnerabilities of our increasingly digitized infrastructure.

We’re connecting everything to networks: hospitals, banking systems, energy grids, communications and transportation.

But are we building the security and resilience necessary to protect them?

Cybersecurity is no longer just an IT problem.

It’s a national security and public safety issue.

Sources: Associated Press, KRQE, University of New Mexico Health System.

text:
谷歌云业务收入翻倍，股价盘后却跌了 10%。Alphabet 第三季度营收同比增长 25%，但每股收益只有 2.12 美元，比市场预期低了近 30%。

不过，拆开来看，这次 EPS 暴雷有很大一部分来自非经营性损失。谷歌持有的其他公司股权产生了约 87 亿美元的亏损，单这一项就拖累了 EPS 约 0.55 美元。

真正值得担心的还是经营层面。

营业利润比预期低了约 6%，营业利润率从上季度的 34% 降到了 32%。谷歌今年预计投入近 2000 亿美元建设 AI 基础设施，这些投入会逐渐变成折旧成本，持续影响未来几个季度的利润。

而且，谷歌的自由现金流已经连续两个季度为负，这个季度净流出了约 90 亿美元。

有意思的是，需求端却非常强劲。Google Cloud 营收同比增长 103%，达到 307 亿美元，未履约合同额已经达到 5610 亿美元。

但另一方面，搜索广告收入低于预期，AI Mode 的广告变现还在摸索。

所以我觉得，这份财报最值得关注的地方，是谷歌正在面临一个很现实的矛盾。

AI 需求越旺，它就越需要建设更多数据中心、购买更多芯片，而这些投资的成本已经开始实实在在地反映在财报里。

EPS 的大幅不及预期，并不意味着谷歌的核心业务突然出了大问题。但自由现金流的恶化，也很难再被简单解释成暂时性的投资。

过去市场一直在奖励科技巨头的 AI 资本开支，谁花的钱多，谁就被认为更有机会赢得下一轮竞争。

现在，投资者可能终于开始认真算另一笔账了，每年砸进去 2000 亿美元，到底什么时候才能赚回来？

WOW!! $GOOGL missed earnings but look at where the miss comes from. 

Operating income missed by about 6%. EPS missed by about 30%. Most of the damage is below the operating line, where Alphabet books gains and losses on stakes it holds in other companies.

That's the cost of building AI $200bn of capex turns into depreciation and depreciation hits the income statement. 
Bullish AI. But not good for Google in the short term. 

Revenue up 25%, a cloud growing faster than anyone else's, and a backlog worth hundreds of billions. A bad EPS headline doesn't change any of that. PT $425. Overweight.

text:
AI 基建的钱，华尔街快借不动了。

彭博社最新报道，美国信贷市场已经开始出现明显的承压迹象。至少 18 笔 AI 数据中心相关的债券和杠杆贷款，收益率已经升到了两位数。

摩根大通和高盛最近为了推销一笔 50 亿美元的 AI 基建贷款，不得不提高利息、折价出售，最终收益率超过了 11%。

更麻烦的是，银行发现，想把这些贷款的风险转移给保险公司和其他投资者，正在变得越来越困难。

对于那些依赖持续融资来扩张的新云厂商来说，11% 的融资成本已经相当沉重。尤其考虑到 GPU 的折旧速度，以及未来算力租赁价格的不确定性。

股价可以靠未来的增长预期维持很久，但债务需要实实在在的现金流来偿还。

一旦融资成本持续上升，AI 基建的扩张速度就可能被迫放缓。而这会进一步影响上游芯片采购、数据中心建设，以及整个行业对未来算力需求的预期。

text:
有人把一整套拥有 9600 张英伟达 A100 GPU 的 AI 超级计算机，挂到 eBay 上卖了，标价 5970 万美元。

这套设备规模相当夸张，300 个服务器机柜、1200 台 GPU 计算服务器、384TB GPU 显存，以及约 1.4PB 系统内存。

卖家 Core 4 Solutions 称，这批设备来自一家大型云服务商退役的计算集群。A100 是英伟达 2020 年推出的产品，已经有六年历史，但仍然可以用于 AI 模型训练和推理。

算下来，平均每张 A100 连同配套服务器、CPU、内存和机柜，售价约 6200 美元。

最搞笑的是，eBay 页面甚至提供免费 FedEx 陆运，隔夜配送也只需要 50 美元。300 个机柜，50 美元隔夜送达，估计快递员看了都得辞职。

但我觉得这件事还有一个很值得关注的地方。

过去几年，整个 AI 行业都在讨论 GPU 短缺、算力军备竞赛，以及科技巨头动辄数百亿美元的数据中心投资。

现在，六年前还代表全球顶级算力的 A100，已经开始以整套集群的形式流入二手市场。

而且这些 GPU 依然有使用价值。对于不需要最先进芯片的推理任务，以及预算有限的 AI 公司来说，二手算力仍然有市场。

AI 基础设施正在呈现出传统重资产行业的另一面，设备折旧、技术淘汰、资产转售，以及越来越复杂的投资回报计算。

text:
SK 海力士一句话，直接带着全球存储芯片股集体暴涨，未来三年的 DRAM 和 HBM 产能，基本已经卖到 2029 年了。

消息公布后，美光隔夜一度上涨约 32 美元，日本铠侠涨超 10%，三星电子也一度上涨约 7%。

市场的逻辑很简单，如果连 SK 海力士未来三年的产能都已经供不应求，那么美光、三星这些竞争对手自然也会受益。

更值得关注的是，这轮存储芯片的短缺正在从 HBM 蔓延到传统 DRAM。过去，存储行业是典型的周期性生意，价格一涨，厂商扩产，随后就可能迎来产能过剩和价格崩盘。

但这一次，AI 数据中心持续扩张，科技巨头开始提前数年锁定芯片供应。存储厂商获得了过去很少见的长期需求可见性，定价权也随之增强。

当然，所谓「卖到 2029 年」，还包括正在谈判的采购需求，并非全部签约。但仅仅是这个预期，就足以让资本市场重新评估整个存储行业的价值。

AI 基建的钱，正在越来越多地流向卖内存的人。

text:
Romantic Realism

Imagine telling peasants in feudalist France there will one day be no kings and the masses of peasants will elect all their leaders to represent them.

Imagine telling a founding father of America that black people & white people would live, love, & go to school together; and work side by side in every state.

Imagine telling women in 1900 they would, within 3 or so generations enjoy complete equity with men (at least legally) in all regards: voting, ability to access banking and the financial system, property rights, etc.. And that more women would be getting a college education than men.

At the time, each would have seemed like silly unrealistic dreams; and not for lack of technology.

Yet it is easy to imagine Romantic futures where humanity has achieved even greater heights. Technologically but also Socially: the elimination of poverty, astroid mining, near 100% voter participation, micro fission reactors, high quality education for all, AI intelligence for all too cheap to meter, greater civil rights.

The hard part is finding Realistic paths to build that Romantic future. Is there really a path to infinite world peace? Is there really a path to deep space mining? What silly unrealistic dreams we have today. We know from history many of our most silly and most unrealistic dreams will be obvious in hindsight.

The progress of the past 100 years is great to romanticize, because it inspires a realistic future.

text:
微软和谷歌最新财报后的市场反应，提供了一个很好的观察样本。

微软当季Azure 收入增长 48%，经营现金流 580 亿美元，购置不动产及设备的现金支出约 394 亿美元。自由现金流仍然为正。

Google的Cloud 收入增长 103%，但当季经营现金流约 423 亿美元，低于约 514 亿美元的资本开支，自由现金流为负91 亿美元。

但这次分化也不能简单概括成“同样的 Capex，只差现金流”。

两家公司的资本开支口径并不完全一致，微软还有融资租赁等因素；谷歌当季还受到搜索收入预期、股权投资损失和后续资本开支指引的影响。

更准确的说法是：

市场开始奖励“增长超预期，同时现金投入没有失控”的公司；开始惩罚“增长很强，但核心现金牛、资本开支和外部融资需求同时上升”的公司。

需求仍然重要，但需求本身已经不够了。

接下来，判断 AI 公司的质量，要看两笔。

第一笔，资金来源账。

不是只看公司发了多少债，而是看自由现金流、租赁承诺、SPV 担保、供应商融资和债务到期结构。

季度自由现金流为负，不代表马上发生危机；但如果负自由现金流、外部融资和表外承诺持续一起上升，估值问题就可能逐渐变成信用问题。

第二笔，增量回报账。

新增 AI 投入带来的回报，能不能覆盖新增折旧、电力、运维、利息以及股权资本成本？

随着美债利率市场的高位震荡，市场可能出现的，是分层出清：

最弱的 neocloud 和项目 SPV 先遇到再融资压力；
随后项目融资收紧、股本要求提高；
再往后，融资约束传导为实际 Capex 和采购订单下降；
最后才是巨头之间根据资产负债表、客户质量和现金兑现能力重新分化。

text:
没想到大家对这个讨论还挺热烈，评论区也推荐了一些工具，但是我看了基本都没满足我说的这几个点。
以前的代码编辑器/IDE的首要任务是写代码，其次才是看代码，这意味着很多设计是围绕写展开的，像VS Code、IntelliJ IDEA、Cursor甚至是Zed。

然而围绕写这个功能需要完成大量相关的工作，例如文本编辑引擎，代码解析，调试系统，构建与运行等等，这些功能不仅使软件变得臃肿，也会导致运行时耗费大量的资源。

例如 VS Code 采用 Electron，涉及 Chromium、Node.js、扩展宿主等进程；语言服务器又可能独立运行。打开大型项目后，索引、文件监控、插件和语言分析都会增加资源消耗。

Vibe Coding时代，代码更多的是围绕看而设计，激进点我甚至觉得可以在UI层面把编辑功能都去掉，但是需要拓展AI基本的聊天功能，例如选中代码让AI解释。看似一个优先级的改变，却可能需要对整个产品的设计做一次重大的重构。首先一切都得为更好更高效更沉浸的阅读代码而设计，这就包括代码高亮，字体设计和排版，主题，快速函数跳转响应，Git Diff与历史变更等。此外可能还需要添加一些当前没有的功能，例如自动生成模块关系、核心抽象、架构概览，点击概念就能回到对应的真实源码等。

总之我们需要用新的思维来设计一款新时代的代码阅读器，我也打算自己Vibe一款，大家有很好的思路也欢迎分享。

中国社区逆向拆解了Claude的封号机制。以下是他们的发现

Claude使用积分制。注册时账号获得初始分数，之后根据行为加分或扣分。低于阈值直接封号。回分很难

影响分数的因素:

注册
> 干净IP是最重要的因素。不一定要家宽，但必须干净
> Gmail已经不是最优选，有权重更高的邮箱服务
> 注册时直接弹KYC的号可以扔了
> 用手机App注册会加分

支付
> 刚注册就订阅会扣分
> 直接上Max会大幅扣分。最好等两天先订Pro
> 支付时弹KYC说明账号在考察期，但不一定会封
> 国外实体银行卡加分。Google Play也行。虚拟卡扣分

使用
> 不要一次把限额用完。宁可两个号轮换也不要一个号撸到底
> Desktop客户端有少量加分。尽量少用网页端
> 手机端也有少量加分
> 开启记忆功能加分。记忆文件越多分越高

IP和设备
> 稳定性是关键。不要跳IP，尽量一直用同一个
> 代理必须全局模式并开启TUN
> 多设备登录大幅扣分。理想状态是一台电脑一个客户端
> 频繁换IP、频繁登录、高并发都会大幅扣分

账号年龄
> 老号有巨大的容错空间。2023年的号明显更高
> 分数随时间增长，但很慢

其他
> Windows和macOS没区别。Linux会扣分
> 时区和语言基本不影响。不会因为北京时间就封号
> 跟Claude说自己是中国人没问题，记忆不会触发封号
> 大量使用Fable会扣分
> 升级Max大概率进入观察期，除非是高权重老号

观察期和封号
> 接近阈值时账号可能进入观察期。典型特征是掉登录
> 观察期继续扣分就会封号
> 高分号可以扛过多次观察期

关注我，拆解你每天在用的服务背后到底怎么运作的

author: thedefiedge
quoted_text:
Feel like this decade should be called 'The Great Unraveling' or something like that..

Everywhere you look, things are just getting way more fluid and less stable and just way less certain...

- Will you still have your job in 2 years? Uncertain...

- What jobs will still exist in the future anyway? Uncertain...

- What industries will thrive? Uncertain...

- Should you buy an existing business? Probably not... too uncertain...

- Should you go back to school or training for a new career? Probably not... too uncertain...

- Will the stock market keep going up forever? Uncertain... is primarily political at this point based on the Fed and Treasury and 401k inflows and etc...

- Will residential real estate have another collapse? Uncertain... all depends on interest rates, so far it hasn't but there has to be a breaking point somewhere...

- Should you move into the good school district so your kids can go the best schools? Uncertain... AI is disrupting the entire education system just as fast as it is everything else...

- Will your safe, first world country still be a safe first would country in 20 years? Uncertain... you get the wrong leaders and it could speedrun civilizational suicide like many other western countries have lately... 

- Can you reject the traditional financial system and bet it all on Bitcoin? Sure... but even that is less certain now due to fears over quantum...

Indeed... even the long-term future of our species is increasingly brought into question... due to the global fertility crisis and microplastics and etc...

So yeah...

Obviously uncertainty has always been a part of life... 

However compared to 5 years ago or 10 years ago or 20 years ago or 50 years ago... it just seems like things have gotten WAY WAY more fluid...

Mostly this is because of AI... 

But partly it is just the blow off top in the sovereign debt bubble, which makes all economic questions primarily political... since everything just depends on the money printer vs austerity-larp seesaw... 

But yeah... 

Not sure what the solution is, but I think the best thing to do is just create a really good foundation, and stay lean...

Get healthy, get locked-in, keep geeking out on everything new and exciting...

Get your living expenses as low as possible relative to your assets (notice I said ASSETS and not INCOME - again, issa new world)...

And just keep putting in the reps and trying to set yourself up for success...

The flip side of chaos is opportunity, and you owe it to yourself, and your family, and your people to try to thrive amidst the insanity :)

text:
过去一段时间，跟创业者聊天，总会听到一句话：「现在 VC 只投共识。」

他们觉得投资人越来越看赛道、看背景、看谁已经投了。

但转头去问投资人，听到的又是另一种抱怨：「真正的好项目太少了。」

我一直很好奇，这两拨人到底在抱怨什么。

过去几年，从新消费到大模型，再到具身智能、世界模型，每一轮风口都有大量资金涌进去，也总有人在泡沫退去之后说，自己早就看出了问题。可下一轮风口来了，大家还是会做出差不多的选择。

所以我们找了一些创业者做长谈，又在 10 月底办了一场匿名 Meetup，请一线投资人聊聊平时不方便公开讲的事。

聊完之后，我最大的感受是，很多看起来荒诞的行业现象，背后都有一套非常现实的逻辑。年轻投资人要考虑考核，合伙人害怕错过下一代平台，创业者需要下一轮融资，基金要向 LP 交代，而所有人最终都得面对退出。

每个人都有自己的难处，也都有一套能说服自己的理由。可这些选择叠加起来，整个行业就会反复走向同一个方向。

我想把这些声音放在一起，让牌桌两边的人互相解释，也互相印证。很多事情在公开场合被包装成判断力、远见和勇气，私下聊起来，其实还有很多无奈、妥协和身不由己。

我想弄清楚的就是，为什么一个几乎所有人都能看出问题的游戏，却很少有人能够不参与。

text:
不得不说微软是这次云厂商的绩优生，基本上都超出了我前瞻框架的上沿，聊聊个人角度今天微软财报里的亮点：
1、Azure本季收入331.65亿美元，比上年同期增加107.81亿美元。按重列后的可比口径计算，Azure贡献了微软集团收入同比增量的约74%。 一个单季收入超过330亿美元的业务，还能从上季42%的增速加快到48%，对整个公司的影响已经很大。而且工程优化释放了更多GPU可用容量，这相当于已上线产能会有更多的业绩。

积压订单6770亿，官方确认约30%预计在未来12个月确认收入，营收的能见度还是很高的。

2、自由现金流有186亿美元，在云厂商里算是一枝独秀了。2026自然年的资本开支预期从约1750亿美元调整为约1700亿美元，一部分交付移到了2027财年下半年，也就是2027年1月至6月。官方再次确认了2027财年全年自由现金流为正。

3、业务与客户
1）Foundry收入达到上年同期的三倍以上；Fabric有4.4万家付费客户，同比增长超过50%，超过1.9万家客户同时使用Foundry和Fabric。

2）微软披露，活跃使用按量计费credits的Copilot客户数，季度内增长超过75%；GitHub的Agent功能，credits消费自按量计费实施以来已经超过翻倍。
前一个数字说的是客户数量，后一个说的是消费量，都能表明微软开始把更多用户的实际工作量纳入收费。

4、微软给出的下一季度总营收指引是960亿至971亿美元，同比增长18%至19%；Azure固定汇率增长49%至50%。两组数字放在一起，可以看到Azure继续加速，云业务仍有很强的收入动能。

整体来说这一季微软的财报也是AI商业化在加速的一个有力支撑。

关乎微软此次财报的深度拆解看OKX星球全文https://t.co/EHy8JMsYmb
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
怎么看微软下周四凌晨最新一季财报？倾向于微软这次会交出一份超预期的财报，核心逻辑：企业云需求有支撑、Copilot开始有更清楚的收费路径、新增算力也有机会转成收入。财报里最值得关注的几个点则是：
1、Azure云业务增速能否超过官方自己给的指引，并进一步靠近市场最乐观预期的上沿？

2、未履约订单RPO的增长情况和前沿模型之外的客户订单占比，要知道上一季度官方明确表示RPO环比增长全部来自前沿模型公司以外的客户，如果这一季继续的话说明AI需求有更多来自终端企业经营活动的支撑。

3、Copilot要开始回答：客户愿意为实际使用多付多少钱
微软上一季披露，Microsoft 365 Copilot付费席位已经超过3000万。接下来需要知道，这些客户用得有多深，续约时愿不愿意继续付费。按照员工数量收费，收入空间终究与组织规模有关。Agent如果能持续处理工作，收费就有机会进一步与使用量挂钩。

4、资本开支和自由现金流
微软对本季资本开支的指引超过500亿美元，其中包括融资租赁。要把现金购建设备、融资租赁与经营租赁的影响读清楚。

微软自由现金流仍为正是更合理的基准情景。因为7月29日的FY2026第四季度财报电话会上，CFO Amy Hood在介绍FY2027全年展望时说：
“we expect to remain free cash flow positive in FY27.”意思是：“我们预计FY2027自由现金流将保持为正。”

对微软最新财报预测超预期是大概率的、关键是超预期的程度，自由现金流的情况值得关注，而下一季指引则更有分量。

前两天这里https://t.co/8VfgH4bpQ8还聊到：微软、亚马逊和谷歌既向前沿大模型卖算力，又向数百万家企业卖云算力、开源和中等模型的高性价比token、还有企业采用AI进程的一系列消费。这三家的业绩才是衡量AI商业化最核心的指标，对市场的影响权重是要高于spacex和meta的。

Google计划推出加密资产托管/安全系统，主要面向机构和银行。

总结来说，是加密资产的MPC 密钥管理与签名服务。

这意味着，可以帮助银行/金融机构更安全地托管和转移加密资产及代币化资产（包括它们为客户持有的资产）。

解决了安全和托管问题，利于增加加密资产的渗透率。

具体来说，

它采用了多方计算（MPC）模式：

把私钥拆成分片，分散存在不同环境，

比如自家硬件 + Google Cloud + 其他云，

签名时不需要把完整私钥拼在一个地方，

降低单点被盗风险。

也支持在交易前加机构规则，

比如限额、白名单地址、多部门审批等。

银行或机构保留对密钥分片的控制权，

Google 看不到明文私钥。

目前处于 private preview，多家大型金融机构在测；

Alphabet（Google母公司）已经在用它保护自家在以太坊上的数字资产等。

计划 2027年初正式商用，快了。

text:
中国社区逆向拆解了Claude的封号机制。以下是他们的发现

Claude使用积分制。注册时账号获得初始分数，之后根据行为加分或扣分。低于阈值直接封号。回分很难

影响分数的因素:

注册
> 干净IP是最重要的因素。不一定要家宽，但必须干净
> Gmail已经不是最优选，有权重更高的邮箱服务
> 注册时直接弹KYC的号可以扔了
> 用手机App注册会加分

支付
> 刚注册就订阅会扣分
> 直接上Max会大幅扣分。最好等两天先订Pro
> 支付时弹KYC说明账号在考察期，但不一定会封
> 国外实体银行卡加分。Google Play也行。虚拟卡扣分

使用
> 不要一次把限额用完。宁可两个号轮换也不要一个号撸到底
> Desktop客户端有少量加分。尽量少用网页端
> 手机端也有少量加分
> 开启记忆功能加分。记忆文件越多分越高

IP和设备
> 稳定性是关键。不要跳IP，尽量一直用同一个
> 代理必须全局模式并开启TUN
> 多设备登录大幅扣分。理想状态是一台电脑一个客户端
> 频繁换IP、频繁登录、高并发都会大幅扣分

账号年龄
> 老号有巨大的容错空间。2023年的号明显更高
> 分数随时间增长，但很慢

其他
> Windows和macOS没区别。Linux会扣分
> 时区和语言基本不影响。不会因为北京时间就封号
> 跟Claude说自己是中国人没问题，记忆不会触发封号
> 大量使用Fable会扣分
> 升级Max大概率进入观察期，除非是高权重老号

观察期和封号
> 接近阈值时账号可能进入观察期。典型特征是掉登录
> 观察期继续扣分就会封号
> 高分号可以扛过多次观察期

关注我，拆解你每天在用的服务背后到底怎么运作的

text:
加拿大一个工程师大哥，卖掉房产，几乎把全部身家都押在了软件公司Palantir的股票上。

买完之后股价最低跌到过6美元，他也照样加仓。

到今年10月，他持有的Palantir股票价值已经逼近300万美元，2000万人民币，大哥47岁就辞职退休了。

递辞呈那天，他发帖说，这周日就能提保时捷了🤣

大哥叫Etienne Breton，在加拿大魁北克当机械工程师。
20多年前他也炒过股，9·11之后股市大跌，他吓得全卖了，之后再没碰过。
2020年疫情股灾，他看到有人恐慌，把股票全卖了，他反倒去开了个账户。

他在工作中天天被乱七八糟的数据和供应链问题折磨，后来在YouTube上刷到Palantir，一家给美国军方和大公司做数据分析的公司，专门解决的就是这些问题。

经过一番分析之后，大哥认定Palantir是个好公司，没有竞争对手，有护城河，比别人好10倍，于是决定梭哈。

2020年底，他卖掉房产，在10美元左右开始买，把所有身家押在了Palantir上。

结果买完股票先涨了一段，就开始一路狂跌，2022年底跌到了6美元。
大哥一点不慌，还是照样买，每买一次就记在车库墙上，到2023年1月，墙上记到了9544股。

2023年年中，股价回到10美元，他手里已经有1万股，均价8.83美元，算下来成本不到9万美元。
这几年他又借钱多买了几千股，再靠卖期权收钱，收到的钱接着买股票。
后来AI热潮来了，Palantir一路涨，今年10月最高冲到了212美元，他手里的Palantir股票一度值到近300万美元。

去年11月，他递了辞呈，今年4月30日正式退休，那天他发帖说："47岁退休，就在今天，Palantir做到了。"

现在他还是一股不卖，日常开销都靠卖期权收的钱。

2、找到新东西比交易本身更加重要，没有时间的情况下就要借助团队和流程的力量，这里的流程很重要，信息采集、交流、汇报、执行要最终形成一套sop ，否则只是丢个ca或者信息到群里，只是团伙不是团队，目前团队由 @something_labs 和 @10UWINA8 组成，我们也在开发团队内部使用的监控+流程产品；

3、二级一定要借助AI的力量，而且要有取舍，如果专注二级的话可以关注一些优质博主比如 @luge517 @nine_DeFi @lijiuer1 @Arya_web3 ，但是我觉得二级也是需要盯盘的，虽然没有链上那么p，但盯交易信号也是无法离开屏幕的，所以我只选择AI股、BTC/ETH和低市值埋伏这三个品类，加上AI工具辅助（这里特别推荐 @MojoAI_HQ 这个产品，数据很全，非广）；

用人与人之间的沟通降低信息差；

以趋势收益替代喊单收益；

text:
As someone who has personally spent $500k / mo+ on Google Ads for years, I can tell you with certainty: 

This revenue growth in Search is artificial & extremely unhealthy for Google’s business long term

Search volumes are declining as legacy search is being increasingly cannibalized by non-monetized LLM queries

Google’s response? 

Manufacture revenue growth via short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics. I.e. charge advertisers more for lower quality clicks, including clicks they do not want and explicitly did not approve Google to charge them for

A few examples to illustrate: 

For all of its history until recently, Google operated on a 2nd price auction model

I.e. if you bid $5 CPC and the next highest bidder bids $1 CPC, Google charged you $1.01 for the click (one penny more than the 2nd highest bidder) rather than the $5 you bid

This was a genius move by Google early on as it incentivizes advertisers to input their true maximum willingness to pay rather than trying to play the game of bidding low and constantly adjusting to try to stay just ahead of the next highest bidder while still not paying too much

However recently, Google silently deprecated the 2nd price auction and began charging advertisers as much as their bid and budget caps allow, regardless of what anyone else is bidding

It’s a short-sighted cash grab at the expense of the long term health of the  advertiser ecosystem

Making thing worse, Google also recently nerfed keyword targeting precision

Google previously had precise keyword targeting settings that allowed advertisers pick individual search phrases to bid on, defined down to the character w/ exact match or phrase match targeting 

This was one of the core features that made search advertising magic, enabling advertisers to run extremely precise campaigns based on exactly what their target customer typed 

But now, even if you bid on a specific term or phrase using the strictest exact 
-match targeting settings, Google will show your ad across 1000’s of unrelated keywords, labeling them as as “exact match (close variant)” 

The definition of “close variant” means whatever they want it to and changes constantly. The result is advertisers get billed for clicks that are totally irrelevant to their business and that their targeting settings explicitly forbid Google from targeting. Google does it anyway and there’s no ability to turn this off

So now exact match is broad match, and broad match is just meaningless spam

This is all very bad for advertisers, but for Google, it allows them to show your ad and bill you for clicks across 1000x more searches that were previously going unmonetized (mainly because they’re garbage queries no one wants) 

This is how you grow revenue atop declining search volumes 

Lastly, and perhaps most egregiously, Google quietly stopped respecting budget caps by a factor of 2x. For example campaigns we’ve been running for years with $1000 daily budget caps suddenly began spending $2000+ per day 

And the extra spend is entirely on the garbage keywords Google arbitrarily throws in as “exact match (close variants)” which have no value to our business, but can’t be turned off

Google offers no refunds nor any recourse for overspend or spend on keywords you explicitly did not target

These are not the actions of a healthy business. These are the actions of company whose core business is in decline but desperately needs to pump quarterly earnings so Wall Street will continue to fund insane capex while hopefully looking through their rapidly deteriorating negative free cash flow 

Google operated a benevolent monopoly for the better part of 25 yrs

Meaning the value Google captured from Search was but a small fraction of the value it created, and that spread produced a potential energy that justified expectations of high earnings growth far, far into the future 

This is now no longer the case

At the alter of AI capex, Google is sacrificing the golden goose

The hidden tax measure in the Budget is huge for people paying tax under self-assessment - sole traders, partners, landlords, retired investors.

For 6th April 2028-29, you currently pay 50% of your income tax late in the tax year in question (in January 2029), 50% just after the year end (in July 2029) with any make-up payment in January 2030.

text:
社区空投预期落差过大及分配信息的不透明，个人认为是当前Predict问题的主因

先说下个人情况吧，参与的早，虽然自己有点菜，没撸多少分，但一直都在参与。好在早期写了几篇详细教程，获得了一些邀请分，不太多，跟大佬们比不值一提。另外也是Predic大使，前期写的多些，因为前面自己参与多，最近几个月写的少了，主要是后面亏了不少，就有点佛系了，没怎么实际参与的我一向是不太写的。所以也算是利益相关吧，下面是纯个人观点，如有不对，欢迎指正。

一、社区空投预期落差大

先说下社区空投预期落差大的问题吧，首先就是团队给的预期是真的高，且不说前期Ding老板各种放话拉升预期的事，现在都作为传播梗图了。

我们单看昨天发布到这份简单的（有点过于简单了😂）代币经济学。

第一个上来就是社区最关注的-生态与社区 占比51.95%，这里确实非常诱人，也就是说给到社区的分配会有大半，至少从愿景上来说算是特别大方的项目了。

但问题就在这了，前面定调的这么高，实际TGE时社区直接能领到的空投份额上限是多少，7%*35%=2.45%，注意这里的2.45%还只是上限，如果一些人选择锁仓，到时候社区空投占比连2.45%都没有。

如果以上看着还没什么感觉，再做一个比较，前面经济学中设定给生态与社区的分配是超过50%的，再看下本次社区的分配占整个TGE首次流通的占比是多少，很简单，首次流通16%，社区空投的哪怕按顶格2.45%算，就是2.45/16=15.3125%.

这么一对比是不是就比较明显了，首先给人立的预期是超过50%占大头的，实际打算发的才15.31%，这种落差感就很明显了。而且甚至都没法未来会分配来填补，用户都知道，TGE时候对于社区来说就是最大的一次分配，如果连最大的一次分配都差距这么大，应该很难说服用户再去相信后续会有更好的分配。

其次，还有一个比较产生的落差，这也是昨天公布至今项目DC中用户一面倒开骂的主因之一，也就是积分空投和币安Alpha的对比。有时候给的少不要紧，如果大家都一样少，似乎也能忍受，现在社区很多人的感觉就是，辛辛苦苦撸半年一年，付出手续费、本金压力前提下，也就比币安Alpha撸15天多可怜的0.45%。

虽然团队解释（见图一）说给币安的份额他们怎么分配团队没法控制，但有一点是可以控制的，给出去多少，剩下的又怎么分配是否能够控制，我认为这些是能体现出团队是否真的在乎社区用户关键点。

二、代币分配信息不透明

这个点我看大家说的似乎很少，不管是DC还是推特上，我们这里就稍微展开下吧。

首先来看看总的分配，直接看代币经济学的分配图（图二）
不知道大家发现问题没有，5个分配板块中，除了最下方的流动性是明确知道TGE时时用于添加流动性的之外，其他四块大伙是否真的能理解每个对应给什么群体了么。
什么是早期支持者、核心贡献者，是团队？投资人？早期顾问？，占了大头的生态与社区究竟含有哪些？营销费算在这里面吗？本次给的币安的算生态吗？国库又是什么？

几乎都没有解释，当然，我相信团队肯定是有一版足够详尽清晰的白皮书，但是现在币安都马上要Pre - TGE了，是不是应该公布出来给大家具体看看。

另一个巨大的不透明我甚至没看到人提，想想也是有点恐怖。我们再回想下本次TGE总流通16%，已知几个明确的分配如下，流动性4%、币安Alpha2%、社区空投按顶格2.45%，这些加起来是多少，8.45%，那么剩下的7.55%在哪，反正我查了各种信息都没有查到剩下这些是怎么分配的，可能有些信息我还不知道，如果有知道的朋友欢迎提醒我。

如果确实没有公布，那就可以理解为剩下将近一半的份额分配未明，这些是属于什么的呢，做事商么，应该不至于这么大，而且理论上流动性的部分含了做市商的，还是说这些也给到了币安老爷们？或者投资人的兑现？

昨天看到一些KOL说本次TGE是个高控盘玩法，实际流通只有2%，总感觉他们似乎高兴的太少了，真正的大象在房间里一直不看是吧。

希望团队能尽快公布这些详情吧，作为一个热度这么高的项目，真没必要藏，没啥意义。当然，最希望看到的是一个相对合理的分配  @dingalingts

也希望两位大老板能关注下此事  @cz_binance ，@heyibinance ，我认为当前 @predictdotfun 已经不能算的Yzi投资的一个项目这么简单了，作为已经深度接入了币安交易所、钱包的一个项目，基本上算是币安本身的一部分了。这么一个直系项目，在马上TGE的时刻，应尽的信息披露义务我觉得还是有必要，当然社区的分配情绪问题也请关注下。

以上仅个人看法，如有不对的地方欢迎指正，个人还是很看好Predict的，今年基本没参与什么项目，长期参与的核心项目就3个，Predict是其中之一。

所以也无比希望Predict能跑出来，我以及很多看好Predict的朋友都是把它比作预测市场的hyperliquid，前面的发展也大有这种势头。只是目前这波TGE情况有显著开倒车的趋势，甚至说从云端排入泥潭都不为过，希望能重新起飞吧。

author: _FORAB
quoted_text:
As someone who has personally spent $500k / mo+ on Google Ads for years, I can tell you with certainty: 

This revenue growth in Search is artificial & extremely unhealthy for Google’s business long term

Search volumes are declining as legacy search is being increasingly cannibalized by non-monetized LLM queries

Google’s response? 

Manufacture revenue growth via short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics. I.e. charge advertisers more for lower quality clicks, including clicks they do not want and explicitly did not approve Google to charge them for

A few examples to illustrate: 

For all of its history until recently, Google operated on a 2nd price auction model

I.e. if you bid $5 CPC and the next highest bidder bids $1 CPC, Google charged you $1.01 for the click (one penny more than the 2nd highest bidder) rather than the $5 you bid

This was a genius move by Google early on as it incentivizes advertisers to input their true maximum willingness to pay rather than trying to play the game of bidding low and constantly adjusting to try to stay just ahead of the next highest bidder while still not paying too much

However recently, Google silently deprecated the 2nd price auction and began charging advertisers as much as their bid and budget caps allow, regardless of what anyone else is bidding

It’s a short-sighted cash grab at the expense of the long term health of the  advertiser ecosystem

Making thing worse, Google also recently nerfed keyword targeting precision

Google previously had precise keyword targeting settings that allowed advertisers pick individual search phrases to bid on, defined down to the character w/ exact match or phrase match targeting 

This was one of the core features that made search advertising magic, enabling advertisers to run extremely precise campaigns based on exactly what their target customer typed 

But now, even if you bid on a specific term or phrase using the strictest exact 
-match targeting settings, Google will show your ad across 1000’s of unrelated keywords, labeling them as as “exact match (close variant)” 

The definition of “close variant” means whatever they want it to and changes constantly. The result is advertisers get billed for clicks that are totally irrelevant to their business and that their targeting settings explicitly forbid Google from targeting. Google does it anyway and there’s no ability to turn this off

So now exact match is broad match, and broad match is just meaningless spam

This is all very bad for advertisers, but for Google, it allows them to show your ad and bill you for clicks across 1000x more searches that were previously going unmonetized (mainly because they’re garbage queries no one wants) 

This is how you grow revenue atop declining search volumes 

Lastly, and perhaps most egregiously, Google quietly stopped respecting budget caps by a factor of 2x. For example campaigns we’ve been running for years with $1000 daily budget caps suddenly began spending $2000+ per day 

And the extra spend is entirely on the garbage keywords Google arbitrarily throws in as “exact match (close variants)” which have no value to our business, but can’t be turned off

Google offers no refunds nor any recourse for overspend or spend on keywords you explicitly did not target

These are not the actions of a healthy business. These are the actions of company whose core business is in decline but desperately needs to pump quarterly earnings so Wall Street will continue to fund insane capex while hopefully looking through their rapidly deteriorating negative free cash flow 

Google operated a benevolent monopoly for the better part of 25 yrs

Meaning the value Google captured from Search was but a small fraction of the value it created, and that spread produced a potential energy that justified expectations of high earnings growth far, far into the future 

This is now no longer the case

At the alter of AI capex, Google is sacrificing the golden goose

➡️“Arcus —  RBH Lighter / Entropy”对冲控制台的主要功能：
▪️找到共有代币，计算资费差的回本周期
▪️创建代币任务，程序自动按照“开仓时会能吃到资金费差的那个方向开仓”
▪️程序会一直盯着两边离强平还有多远，太近了就两边同时平掉
▪️你可以设定持仓的「轮换周期」，程序会在这个周期内持有随机时长然后后两边一起平，冷却后再开新的仓位（纯是想增加交易量的功能）
▪️你可以设定“持仓金额范围”，程序会在这个范围内随机找金额开仓

Should you buy a 512GB Mac Studio for Local AI? I ran the numbers before ordering one.

1) On token price alone, renting wins. At DeepSeek V4.1 Flash API rates, the Mac needs years of 24/7 output to pay for itself.

2) Price per token is the wrong way to judge it, though. In expensive housing markets, renting is cheaper month to month than owning, and people still buy for control and because a home holds value. The same logic applies to this machine.

3) It holds value. The 512GB M3 Ultra now resells for about twice what it cost new, because memory got scarce. If mine resells for even half, the real cost halves.

4) Nobody can take it away. API models get swapped, rate limited and refused mid-task. In June, access to two frontier models was cut off for almost three weeks. Weights on my desk stay put.

5) Zero-cost tokens change what you build. When every call costs nothing, agents can run all day and you can experiment freely. MacStories ran local agents 24/7 for 99 days at zero token cost.

6) It runs the big ones. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (552B) and GLM-5.3 (744B) don’t fit in 256GB. In 512GB, each loads into one memory pool.

So if you’d use it a few hours a week, rent. If you’d run it all day the moment it was free, buy.

A memecoin launch platform built on Raydium LaunchLab, with a core feature: every launched coin is paired with real tokenized stocks.

Users trade with SOL, and the platform automatically converts SOL into the paired stock token before buying the coin. Users don't need to hold the stock tokens themselves.

quoted_text:
仔细读了Google的财报全文以及问答，又查看了热门的对于Google的评论，我尽量摈弃了干扰的一点个人感受。

你说这份财报很差，我觉得没有。虽然miss但是miss的不多。但是你不是别人，你是Google，你是全村的希望。

这次最大的问题有两个：
1️⃣广告/搜索业务的不及预期。要知道搜索是公司最核心、利润率最高的业务。
管理层电话会上明确指出，AI Mode（AI聊天式搜索界面）使用量快速增长，查询量创五年新高，但其变现效率低于传统搜索，拖累了广告收入增长。
说大白话，就是AI用的人很多，但是愿意付费的人很少，典型的叫好不叫座。
更严重的是，公司不断推广AI MODE的代价也正在显现——“自我蚕食”。市场担心高利润传统搜索被自己的AI产品侵蚀。更重要的是，我们看不到AI明确的变现时间点。

2️⃣Capex和自由现金流
结合最近的下跌行情看更有感。最近半导体又迎来了一波剧烈下杀，市场本还在刚因为Anthropic的招股书稍微缓过劲来的修复期。
Google的财报讲了一个怎样的故事？公司为建数据中心、TPU等AI基础设施大举支出，自由现金流连续为负，并大幅举债（长期债务升至约1251亿美元）。2027年Capex还将显著上升，市场质疑在搜索增长放缓的背景下，这些投资何时能转化为足够回报，是否存在过度支出或AI泡沫风险。

其实财报不是没有亮点，只是摇摇欲坠的市场期待的是大大的狠狠的Beat，而不是这样的miss。

目前这类设备更多被当作取暖器，或者当成"买彩票"玩。

昨晚到今天上午，Pons 官方（@ponsdotfamily）和创始人 Ozzy（@MEADGod）密集发声，很多人可能只当成普通的喊单，但仔细看推文会发现，Pons 的战略定位发生了一个非常关键的质变。

先看他们刚刚发的核心动作：

Pons 国库正式向 Robinhood 链上的 PayPal 股票代币（$PYPL）注资提供流动性。
随后 Ozzy 直接转推定调：Pons 不仅要做发射台，更要调配国库资金，成为 Robinhood 链上所有美股代币对（Stock Token pairs）最大的流动性提供者（LP）。

结合昨晚官方那句意味深长的 gm，他们已经把 Pons 生态正式拆成了四块：AI Agent、DeFi、Memestock（美股代币）、Meme。

这件事的核心逻辑在于：

1. 摆脱纯土狗内盘的内卷
如果只做发土狗的 https://t.co/sbUzPCXgan 仿盘，在 Robinhood 链上根本打不过 Solana 的高频 PVP。但 Robinhood 链唯一的降维打击优势，就是美股上链和合成资产流动性。Pons 官方亲自用国库做市美股代币，等于直接跳过了空气盘阶段，去卡位全链最核心的交易路由。

2. 承接官方流量与资金
前两天 Pons 刚刚被内置进最新版的 Robinhood Crypto 官方钱包，昨天 Vlad Tenev 又公开表示加大对 RH 链扶持。Pons 紧接着下场做大 $PYPL 这类合规科技股的流动性，完全是在顺着官方最希望看到的方向走。

3. 飞轮模型形成
发币抽水积累国库资金，再把国库资金拿去当美股代币的最大做市商，赚取全链资产沉淀和交易费，最后反哺给 $PONS 本位。今天 $PONS 单日成交干到了 2300 万美元，持币地址破了 10 万，显然大资金已经开始认可这个美股做市商的估值逻辑。

接下来在 Robinhood 链上找机会，单纯的土狗 Meme 赔率正在边际递减，重点盯紧能跟美股对冲或者把美股代币当底池的标的，这才是官方国库和流动性真正会去倾斜的地方。

text:
This chart is exactly the daisy chain I always worry about! One Amazon share reaches investors through 5 jurisdictions and 6 different legal claims: security entitlements, contractual claims, debt notes, certificates, beneficial interests, and a "digital asset" out of El Salvador. Same ticker, but very different answers to the only question that matters when something breaks… who actually owes you what? 

I agree with @LorenzoARK that this consolidates like stablecoins did, and my bet is it consolidates around the entitlement model. That's why today is huge news and a big advanced. DTCC's Tokenization Service went live, the shares stay registered with Cede & Co., DTC stays the legal intermediary, wallets are permissioned, and you hold the same entitlement you'd hold today, just on a new rail. It's less decentralized but it's clear about who owes you what and that's key. Hugeeeee congrats to everyone who built toward this, I see you! 

Contrarian view here though: 24/7 trading of large-caps isn't the ultimate prize. That's a better casino not a better society. My eyes are on collateral mobility. Earlier this month BNY and Citadel Securities settled a tokenized Treasury in minutes and used it for overnight repo and in July JPM posted tokenized QQQ as margin at CME. Settlement speed has been behind some of the scariest margin events in market history, from the 2020 dash for cash to the 2022 LME nickel squeeze. Collateral that moves at 2am on a Sunday when the clearing member is asleep takes real pressure out of the system. The bigger prize is markets where ownership has always been murky like commodities in transit, trade finance, and emerging markets, where fraud thrives because no one can see if an asset has been pledged twice. If we can trust that a token really represents the asset, backed by real evidence and an immutable record of who owns it and who has a claim on it, we've delivered the transparency and trust Bitcoin created, but for the real economy.

We're not there yet. Under the SEC relief DTCC launched on, tokenized shares don't count toward collateral in DTC's own settlement risk controls, even though they're supposed to be a digital twin of the exact same securities. So the real test is whether a clearinghouse's risk engine, in the middle of a margin crisis, gives a token the same haircut as the asset it represents. Today is an exciting first step but semper paratus.

On the OKX/ICE issuer refusal, people need to understand how confusing this market is right now. We have 5–10 different wrappers for the exact same equity.

As things stand, it’s hard to see how this improves liquidity, let alone composability or programmability. 

I think we will run the same playbook as stablecoins: platform-neutral equities will win and the market will consolidate. 

But today, the value proposition is weak. You basically need a PhD in wrapper archaeology just to buy one share.
